reviews.text: An unforgettable experience. The Sunday service at Abyssinian Baptist Church is truly inspiring—filled with powerful gospel music, heartfelt preaching, and a warm, welcoming atmosphere. On your website, the “New Here” section does not state anywhere that attending the gospel service requires a mandatory reservation. This lack of clarity is extremely misleading, especially for international visitors.

Three months before our trip, I sent an email asking how to attend the service. I never received any reply, nor any delivery failure or error message. Today, we were simply told that our email was “never received,” despite the fact that I had evidence showing I followed the correct process.

When we arrived, despite our good faith, preparation, and explanations, no solution was offered, no empathy, no attempt to help — just a blunt refusal.

This trip was carefully planned, and this experience meant a lot to us. Seeing my partner in tears because of this situation is something I will not forget.

As I tried turning to enter to sit downstairs a man tried directing me to sit in the balcony. I pointed out to him that there were seats downstairs and that is where I wanted to sit. He allowed me. 2 minutes after I was told that I was sitting in a reserved area and that I had to move. I tried to move immediately but before I could get away, 2 other persons around starting poking me to get up. I moved further down front in an empty pew. About 10 minutes later a well dressed man came over and started talking to me. He told me that persons in the church complained to him that tney were concerned for their safety because I had a small backpack with me. I take this backpack everywhere I go, especially if I am taking public transportation.  I was dressed in a clean t shirt, a clean pair of jeans and I had on clean socks and underwear. My sneakers were also clean and I wore my best cologne that day. I did take a shower that morning. The man asked me to walk outside with him so that he could search my bag. I told him he could search it right there and proceeded to show him my fruits and nuts and reading material. I walked out 10 minutes later because I could not stand the embarrassment any more. I hopped on the train and walked into a predominantly white church and it was smooth sailing. I enjoyed the service, felt totally at home and as I worshipped I did not for a second feel that my attire mattered. I am writing to express my profound disappointment and concern regarding the treatment my mother and I received from Mt. Neboh during the planning and execution of my father, Michael Anthony McPhee, Sr.'s Homegoing service on July 7, 2025. I waited to write this review to ensure I could provide a clear and objective account of our experience.

My father was a longstanding member of this church, and my brothers were all baptized here. One of my brothers (Malik McPhee) passed away 5 years ago and his homegoing service was here as well. Despite my father's long history and the fact that he consistently praised and respected Pastor Johnnie M. Green Jr. as a mentor, Pastor Green inexplicably deemed my father not a member due to his inability to attend regularly or pay tithes, attributing this to his severe health issues, including multiple back surgeries and esophageal cancer. We were charged $1300 for the service and informed that payment was required within 48 hours, or the service would not proceed. This was particularly upsetting given my father's consistent hospitalizations and battle with cancer over the years. During his final months, my family and I tried to reach Pastor Green without success; it was Deacon Jones and another Deacon who ultimately visited and prayed with my father.

The process of scheduling the service was fraught with difficulty. My initial contact, Ms. Jannette, displayed a dismissive and condescending attitude, lacking compassion for a grieving family. Subsequently, I received a call from Ms. Sally (also known as Tish) from a blocked number, who then added Pastor Green to the call. They introduced the "small fee" which quickly escalated to the $1300 demand relayed by the funeral home, to be paid within 48 hours. Communication then shifted to email, resulting in significant delays. I had questions regarding what the $1300 covered, expecting a choir or singers, but we only had a piano player who sung a beautiful song. We also observed what appeared to be a church recording without our permission. Additionally, a video tribute my uncle wished to play was denied without prior review, yet no details were discussed regarding what was permitted or what required pre-approval. Neither Sally nor Pastor Green was reachable by phone (private and blocked phone numbers), which meant I paid the $1300 without clear information and answers.

During the service, Pastor Green's eulogy included a comment stating my father was not an active member. This was heartbreaking and contradictory, especially given that other church members present remembered my father and confirmed his attendance to even where he sat. His petty comment was noted by many attendees and was later talked about. It deeply offended us, particularly given my father's prolonged illness. Whatever tithes my father owed for not attending service I wish I had in all one-dollar bills to throw in face as he spoke. However, I do understand God doesn’t like ugly but, that’s how I feel. I believe that pastors are servants to the Lord, and this experience, driven by what appeared to be a focus on money, has left us with profound disappointment.

Within a week after the service, Sally emailed me requesting a phone call, which felt like a belated attempt at a supportive comforting call that should have occurred before the payment.

Based on our experience, I cannot recommend Mt. Neboh. We rate our experience 0 out of 5 stars and strongly advise others to seek another church home.

Owens Funeral Home has stated they have never seen a family treated this way.

In response to the review by the McPhee family, unfortunately, Mr. Michael McPhee, after joining Mount Neboh and prior to becoming sick was never an active member.  Yes, he did attend several services, maybe 3 to 5 at the most, but he never was consistent in his membership, nor in his financial support of the church.  Second, Deacon Steve Dawkins did check on him often on behalf of the church.  Last, this family didn’t like the church’s protocol with regards to making funeral arrangements, and they were unhappy with having to pay fees to staff and security for the service for a none active members.  Long before Mr. McPhee became sick, he was not an active member.  Joining the church and not supporting the church does not equate to active membership.  I am appalled that this family would make such disparaging comments about our church.  Also, the funeral home, Isaiah Owens, did not properly communicate the funeral policy of our church with this family when they made funeral arrangements.  This is what happens when people do not go to church or support the church, but when someone in their family dies, they want the church to be there for them.  You have to attend church and support the church, if you want the church to be there for you in your time of need.  The church owes people nothing but Christ.  Yes, I liked Mr. McPhee.  I thought he was a nice person, but he was never an active member of Mount Neboh.  I remember only baptizing his youngest son and eulogizing his oldest son.  Our church accommodated this family every way possible.  Mount Neboh owes the McPhee family nothing but Christ.  I wish them well, and I hope that they will find a church home where they truly become active members so that the next time they need a church to funeralize a love one, they will not have superficial expectations.

Mount Nebo is a significant biblical and historical site located in Jordan, approximately 10 km northwest of the city of Madaba. It is believed to be the place where Moses first saw the Promised Land before he died. According to the Bible, Mount Nebo offers a panoramic view of the Holy Land, including the Jordan River Valley, Jericho, Jerusalem, and the Dead Sea.

Today, Mount Nebo is one of the most popular tourist attractions in Jordan, attracting millions of visitors annually. The site is well-maintained and features several noteworthy structures, including the church of Moses' Memorial, which was built in the fourth century AD. Inside the church, there are beautiful mosaics that represent scenes from the Bible, including the Ark of Noah and the Red Sea miraculous crossing.

Additionally, visitors can explore the outdoor area around the church, which includes monuments, ruins, and stunning views of the surrounding landscape. The weather at Mount Nebo is relatively temperate, making it a comfortable place to visit year-round.

Overall, Mount Nebo is a fascinating and awe-inspiring site for anyone interested in biblical history, archeology, or natural beauty. It is highly recommended to visit Mount Nebo while traveling to Jordan, as it offers a unique opportunity to connect with one of the most important religious and historical sites in the region.

A Transformative Experience at Christian Cultural Center (New York)

If you’re seeking a vibrant, inclusive community with uplifting worship, practical teaching, and a bold vision for faith in action, Christian Cultural Center in New York is a standout choice. From the moment you step through the doors, you’re welcomed into a dynamic worship environment and a supportive church family.

What makes it special
Energetic worship and ministries: The praise team leads with passion, blending contemporary energy with soulful gospel elements that lift the spirit and set a positive tone for the service.
Clear, relevant teaching: The messages are biblically solid and practically applicable, tackling everyday life challenges with actionable insights and hope.
Diverse, welcoming community: The center draws people from all backgrounds and ages, creating an inclusive atmosphere where everyone can connect, belong, and serve.
Broad program spectrum: From youth and family ministries to outreach initiatives and small groups, there are ample opportunities to grow in faith, build relationships, and engage with the community.
High-quality facilities and hospitality: The campus is well-maintained, with thoughtful seating, friendly volunteers, and a climate of hospitality that makes visitors feel at home.

Experience and vibe
The church as a catalyst for change: Beyond Sunday services, CCC emphasizes community impact, social outreach, and practical faith in action—appealing to those who want their faith to meet real-world needs.
Energetic yet accessible: The atmosphere is lively and inspiring, but approachable for newcomers or faith travelers exploring a new city.

Practical tips
Arrive early for a good seat and a moment of quiet reflection before worship.
Check service times and events: CCC frequently hosts guest speakers, concerts, and workshops—great to plan around.
Explore small groups or volunteering opportunities to deepen your involvement and friendships.
Bring friends or family for a meaningful, shared experience that can spark conversation afterward.

Bottom line
Christian Cultural Center in New York offers a bold, community-focused, biblically grounded worship experience with a heart for service and social impact. It’s ideal for individuals, couples, and families seeking inspiring teaching, vibrant worship, and opportunities to live out their faith in the city. Highly recommended for anyone looking to connect with a welcoming faith family and make a positive difference in their community.

There was a band, gift bags for the kids in the neighborhood, to keep them safe on a rowdy night, and, there was just warmth. formatted_address: 5th Ave, New York, NY 10022, United States
name: St. Patrick's Cathedral

reviews.text:
St. Patrick’s Cathedral is always a stop for us- every single time we’re in the city. No matter how busy or chaotic New York feels outside, walking through those doors instantly slows everything down.

We always light a candle. It’s just something we do. Something is grounding about that quiet moment- the glow, the stillness, the intention, especially in a city that never stops moving.

The cathedral itself is breathtaking in the most classic way. The architecture, the height of the ceilings, the details you notice more each time you visit, it’s beautiful, timeless, and somehow unchanged, no matter how much the city around it evolves. It doesn’t chase trends. It doesn’t need to. It simply is.

St. Patrick’s is peaceful, humbling, and familiar all at once. A place to pause, reflect, and reset before stepping back into the noise of New York. Some places become traditions for a reason, and this is one we’ll always come back to. 🕯️✨

This is quite possibly the most beautiful church besides St. Peters.
I have been going here since I was a kid but I had the opportunity recently to have an after hours  tour with a small group.
The tour started on the back side of the church at the residence of Fr. Enrique Salvo who is a total gentleman and one of those priests who just gets it.
He is incredibly intelligent and personable and you can feel the love that he has for the cathedral when he speaks about it.
We were taken into the church via an underground walkway which brought us to the robing room that is used by the priests prior to mass.
Then we walked up the large staircase that the celebrants use when entering the church. I was awestruck to think of the people who had walked up these stairs like St. Pope John Paul II and St. Mother Theresa and one of my favorites, John Cardinal O:Connor.
No matter how many times I am in the cathedral I can't help but be amazed.
There is so much to learn like the fact that there are pieces of bones of the Apostles in the alter. That in an of itself is absolutely amazing.
Each statue and side alter is more beautiful than the next.
I have an affinity for St. Mother Theresa, St. Sharbel Maklouf and Blessed Fr. Mcgivney as well as the Divine Mercy Image of Jesus.
There are side alters and statues and pictures to each of there people and images and there is even a first class relic of St. Sharbel at his shrine in the cathedral.
I understand that during the day that it's tough because it gets filled with tourists and tourists in New York can be very annoying and non Catholics don't treat it as reverently as we do but we are a welcoming faith and when I'm on the cathedral I feel so close to God and the Saints and nobodys poor behavior will stand in the way of that.
If you have never been, so yourself a favor and visit St. Patrick's but when you are there remember where you are. Keep your selfie sticks  to yourself and before you do it, realize how silly you look taking a selfie for your social media in the Cathedral.
Jesus I trust in you !

Attended mass on New Years Day 1/1/26. It was a great Homily. Staff were very organized and friendly.  There were too many tourists not there to attend mass but staff gave ample friendly reminders to be mindful of ongoing mass.  The interior is equally majestic as the church's exterior.

The cathedral is of course beautiful. I highly recommend getting tickets to tour ahead of time as you get to see areas that are roped off. A guest pass is not needed to enter although the website states so. Simply wait in one of the many lines around the cathedral and you will enter. There is a quick bag check and men are not allowed to wear hats. I also recommend doing the guided tour as in order to see all parts of the Cathedral without this you need to wait in each individual line outside which each line was about 30-45 min long when I had gone. Also without the guided tour tickets there are parts roped off that you cannot see. The audio tour is being your own headphones and listen via your cellphone.

This is my favorite Roman Catholic church in the city. It even has a chapel dedicated to Our Lady of Guadalupe, where I’ve always found spiritual comfort, along with other saints to whom I’m devoted, like Saint Anthony. It’s a truly beautiful place, and I highly recommend that everyone visit.
The Christmas Mass is especially lovely—I attended last year as well. Whenever friends or family visit the city, I make sure to bring them here. If you’re planning to attend Mass on holidays or major feast days, you should arrive about 1–1.5 hours early to get in line; people usually start entering through the side doors.
There is now increased security inside, which I appreciate, and the overall organization keeps improving as this landmark continues to welcome more visitors. Architecturally, it’s stunning. I really love this church

reviews.text:
I visited the Brooklyn Tabernacle for the morning service, and it was such a powerful and uplifting experience.
The atmosphere was warm and welcoming—no matter your background or beliefs, you immediately feel at home here.

The gospel music was deeply moving, filled with soul and genuine passion. It wasn’t just a performance; it felt like something that touched everyone in the room.

I also came here with a personal purpose. One of my childhood friends had a lifelong dream of singing gospel at the Brooklyn Tabernacle. She couldn’t be here herself, so I came on her behalf. Standing in this space and hearing the choir felt incredibly meaningful, almost as if I was sharing the moment with her.

Whether you're spiritual, curious, or simply looking for a memorable experience in New York, this is a beautiful place where anyone can walk in and leave inspired.

My family and I visited this church, and could not have been more encouraged, edified, and refreshed. The worship was amazing. The presence of the Lord was there, which is what brought the refreshment to the soul. Also, the message was straight from the Bible. I learned a lot. The choir is another level. I could listen to them all day! Loved each, and every song they sang, and even more… Loved the passion with which they sang the songs. I am so thankful that Brooklyn has this amazing church. What a beautiful “light on a hill” this church is, shining for Jesus.

Furthermore, they were all extremely welcoming and kind to us. They even have a room specifically for visitors to come get prayer after the service, which my family utilized and was blessed by. I definitely hope to come back!

We went for Sunday Worship service at 9am. It was a beautiful service and I felt the presence of God . The congregation was so friendly. The music was just spectacular and not just the Brooklyn Tabernacle choir but the whole congregation singing was so good!!! The pastor and sermon was directly from scripture and I left feeling blessed and grateful for the experience! I wish I could attend every Sunday in person but I can Live Stream it. The Tabernacle itself is a beautiful building as well! The paintings upstairs were so beautiful as well.

I attended the morning service at Brooklyn Tabernacle, and it was a truly powerful and uplifting experience. The atmosphere is incredibly warm and welcoming; no matter your background or beliefs, you immediately feel at home.
The BT Choir is exceptional—their music is heavenly, soulful, and filled with a genuine passion that touches everyone in the room. It is far more than a performance; it is a deeply moving experience. This spirit-filled environment is led by Pastor Cymbala, whose sermons offer incredible depth while remaining gospel-oriented and accessible for first-timers.
Having also visited the related tabernacles in Chicago and Philadelphia, I can testify to the strength of this ministry. If you are in New York and looking for a church, this is a beautiful place to leave feeling inspired. We now attend online, but I highly recommend experiencing it in person if you can."

During that visit, an usher was very rude to me, which made the church feel like an unsafe space at a time when I was already deeply vulnerable. In addition, after the same service a woman who was soliciting information (on behalf of the church) about the very breast cancer I was battling at 31 year old  responded rudely when I asked for an information packet, stating, flatly. “You are under 40.” This was particularly painful given that the guest I invited for the first time had lost her mother to breast cancer at as a young child.

The church offers only one service, and the lines have become excessively long. During my most recent visit, the line wrapped around the block, yet there was no communication when the church reached capacity. Many people were left outside in 20-degree weather, watching the livestream on their phones while waiting in line -- At that point, I left.

I’ve noticed tourists inside the church observing the worship rather than participating, which has makes  the environment feel more like a bit of a spectacle than a sacred space.

Altogether, it has become an accumulation of negative experiences that has made it increasingly difficult to feel safe, welcomed, or spiritually grounded in this setting.

What struck us most during the service was the true concept of "community" developed around and together with this church: a new faithful was baptized, public service announcements were given about the distribution of free meals and the schedules of volunteer activities, on how to be part of the choir, online meetings to deepen the Scriptures, and other useful information ... two large screens projected the images, videos and even the texts of the prayers, so as to allow everyone to follow the celebration. reviews.text: Judson is one of my favorite places in the city. It’s beautiful inside - it’s a Stanford White building with 13 La Farge stained glass windows (the most in any one location anywhere). In the meeting room, across from the La Farges there are murals of our “queer saints of color”: James Baldwin, Bayard Rustin,  Marsha P, Octavia Butler, etc. I burst into tears the first time I walked in there. You don’t have to be any kind of religion to go there (I’m super Pagan, and a member of Judson). They welcome everyone at Judson, and make you feel safe and at home the minute you walk in the door. There’s just so much love and support. Many of the offerings outside of service include meals. Wednesday nights there’s delicious soup - among other offerings - which accompanies some amazing performance art pieces. Judson has a loooooong history of supporting art and artists (modern dance was birthed at Judson). Judson also has a looooong history of social justice campaigns (“happenings” began at Judson). Judson is such a special place. I feel both accepted and loved exactly as I am when I’m at Judson, and also called to be my better self there. I would encourage anyone to peak in. I like to say, “I don’t go to Judson in order to get into heaven in the afterlife. I go to Judson to learn to be my better self in this life.” Simply put, there’s just so much divinity at Judson. I feel love and loved every time I’m there.

On Wednesdays there is spectacular FREE art programming. It’s called Judson Arts Wednesdays. I found it through the dude door (small sign advertising but also had seen a post on IG) They served vegan chili and cake then I saw a dance performance that included a sound bath at the end. Incredible.

reviews.text: As someone who has not been to Church is many years- Yesterday was my second Sunday.  Pastor Mitchell is a very sound biblical teacher with a practicality that is uncommon. reviews.text: My husband and I were both convicted to leave mid service. Bottom line up front, The pastor was being political and using race to divide. People were literally clapping after he said “78% of people on snaps are white.” Why did that deserve an applause? Had I been a white family to have walk in I would have felt embarrassed and shamed. We should pray for the government (which let’s not forget is established by God) and those leader in charge. And  get back to His will. A pastor’s role is to help raise ppl spiritually. Black,white, Caribbean, American it doesn’t matter.  Talking about worldly things with an “amen” there, and then a general comment about God here.. is not church. It’s a distraction, and time is running out y’all, Jesus is coming back. I trust that God will still use this church for His good. So, if you’re a new believer, ask for discernment but know the Word. This wasn’t the church for us.  (I say this all in love)

name: Lafayette Avenue Presbyterian Church

reviews.text: The most welcoming, non-judgemental, diverse church community I've ever found. Inside a historic structure surrounded with stunning Tiffany windows and a 1970s mural celebrating the community, this stop on the underground railroad has nevet forgotten it's abolitionist roots, providing an old-school Presbyterian service with a modern, progressive outlook, filled with Music and a ministry of "radical" love.

We saw Candle light music with three violinists and a cellist playing Queen and Abba songs. It was wonderful live music, and the seating was comfortable. You do have to walk up a couple flights of stairs, so it is a mobility challenge.

Visiting this church was a delightful visit down memory lane with my dad who had worked there as an intern for Reverend Knight 60 years ago. Thank you to Amir (sp?) for taking time to fill in some of the recent history of the church and assisting us with bringing my dad to visit and share in both “The Witnesses” (large scale paintings on the second floor) and the Tiffany window, equally glorious in their own right.
If you have not taken time to see these paintings on the upper level in between the stain glass windows please treat yourself and be in good company with those who are the community of LAPC.

Great place to worship, awesome parishioners. Remember to stop by for some coffee, juice, and a little snack before you go (after the service). Great way to meet the pastor and the church folk in an informal and relaxed setting. Also check out what's going on at the church on the bulletin boards.

It is a wonderful and diverse group of people who attend LAPC. All are welcome, be you Christian or not. Reverend Telfort is an amazing orator, the likes of MLK Jr. He is young & brings much needed perspective to the Bible and gospels. My family has been attending services here since the 1980’s. The church has always focused on inclusion and justice. It was at one point part of the Underground Railroad. That spirit is still present within the walls. The church features talented musicians that bring such life to the services. There is also a huge presence of children and families. LAPC is a warm, inviting, safe place. A true sanctuary from this hard world.

reviews.text:
The constant off track in service, the constant interruption durning worship for them to just ask for money and say some prayer about generosity!

Now let’s get personal! I tried to get baptized by them literally 6 months ago! I did a follow up email and nothing I did attend the baptism class and wrote my testimony but of course! They didn’t care to reply!

The people who pray for you don’t even know what to pray for or don’t use scripture and I had al day say she couldn’t pray for me because she thinks I need to talk to someone more experienced since I was dealing with bouts of depression.

This place only care about money! The place itself has weird faces on the edges of the walls and it’s old dirty and run down!

A church built around emotional health, spiritual growth, and life in fellowship. Connected to CDC community development program which supports the homeless, the underprivileged, and those in need of basic health needs. The leaderships run a great ship. Can’t wait for services to allow congregants to return!

We truly wanted to find a place of peace and inspiration after a difficult week, but unfortunately, our experience here left us feeling uncomfortable and unwelcome. The service was led by Minister Sharon and the entire plus hour service was focused wholly on her personal stories of racial injustice and political commentary. While we understand the need to speak truth and share lived experiences, the message included repeated negative references to white people and political imagery like the Berlin Wall and civil rights protests.

My husband and I came hoping to feel uplifted and spiritually connected, but instead felt alienated by what came across as a one-sided, divisive message. We looked around and realized we were among the only white people present, which only heightened our discomfort as the sermon continued. We are not political people and were not expecting to be part of a space that seemed to promote a strong racial and political agenda. It felt more like a lecture than a service.

We believe in unity, healing, and mutual respect, and we were truly hoping to find that here. Sadly, we did not. We won’t be coming again.

Haven't been to church for years because I think all churches are the same. They are run by human beings and human being always have their own agenda, and will try to push theirs onto you. This weekend at this church has proven this theory again.  First time coming here to try to find my way back to God and  want to find my way back to some churches to be surrounded by loving Christians, but it reminds me why I stay away from church in the first place. The guy tried to casually push his agenda onto you and thinking it would not be noticed. Dude, keep your political agenda to yourself and just preach what's in the bible.

This was my first time coming to this church. I came with my son, as soon as I step foot into the church I felt comfortable. As soon as I walked in where the sermon took place the music had such a presence. I felt as if I was being hugged by Jesus spirit and it brought me to tears. My son loved the music and was just taking all the energy in. It felt great as a first experience to be welcomed in such a way.  Pastor Rich, began the sermon with an ice breaker to build community within the members introducing oneself to another member and a member named Russell introduced himself and explained a little about the church and about the Sunday school for kids. He later introduced me to the teacher Ms Brenda so I can go and take a look at the Sunday school. I loved that everyone treated my son and I with much kindness. I’m glad I made the decision to come visit this church. I will definitely be returning next Sunday.

reviews.text: Been going to Ignite for almost year now and it has been nothing short of amazing. It’s a great church for people who are really into dissecting the Word, are seeking genuine community, and are into getting serious about their faith.

Ignite is really my home away from home. I’m thankful to be part of such a warm community of believers who have always pushed me to step into my identity as a child of God. The different initiatives at Ignite touch on service, fellowship, leadership, etc. The doctrine here is also very sound; you learn the word of God and learn how to grow in it as you live it out. Serving on teams here has also blessed me beyond measure! Grateful for the opportunity to keep coming back each Sunday.
Ignite Church NYC is where you need to be. I’ve grown spiritually, emotionally, and I’ve built so many great friendships.
Ignite is family. I'm so blessed God led me here. The first time I walked in, I knew I belonged in their community. God is using the pastors in so many ways!!
Amazing church with amazing doctrine and community!

formatted_address: 418 E 11th St, New York, NY 10009, United States
name: Hope Church NYC - East Village

reviews.text: I've been attending Hope for a few years now, and I am so grateful to have found such a fantastic community here in NYC. The Hope pastors deliver great sermons every Sunday, and we have had some amazing guest speakers visit us from all over as well. The people I've met here at church are not only people I see on Sundays for service, but I genuinely consider them great friends. We do plenty of things together throughout the week as well, including meeting for small groups / bible study and volunteer opportunities throughout the city to not make church a once-a-week, passive activity. I also appreciate the resources Hope provides everyone with, from bible study to financial literacy and marriage courses. I feel truly blessed to be a part of this church and highly recommend it to others.
Humble, young, Bible-centered non-denominational church. Really love the community here and feels like home!

My first time at Hope was memorable. I left telling my hubby, “this is our soon to be church home”. Warmth and friendliness from the people, worship is amazing and I just fell in love with the flow of Hope Church EV! All my friends and family i invite, come back. ❤️

I've been actively attending since Spring 2017. It's been my church home and community. We believe in the following and hope these values resonate with you as well. 🙂 Stopby and visit!

Living Deeply - We are committed to living out of the depth of our union and communion with Christ.

Living Neighborly - We are committed to joining God in loving and living intentionally for the well-being of our neighbors, both locally and globally.

Living Communally - We are committed to being shaped by, and living out, the gospel of Jesus Christ through life in authentic community.

Living Justly - We are committed to doing justice, living justly, and speaking prophetically for the sake of all who are oppressed in our neighborhood, in our city, and in our world.

Living Generously - We are committed to giving of all that we are and all that we have in response to God's abundant grace that has been poured out on us.

Living Restfully - We are committed to living lives of rest in the midst of a chaotic world.

Living Beautifully - We are committed to living lives that witness to the beauty of God by creatively generating beauty in our neighborhood.

Living Delightfully - We are committed to living lives full of celebration and joy.

Friendly family feel church that takes the time to know your name and ask how you are doing. First Sundays every month are reserved for food and fellowship which is a good place to meet other people interested in growing in faith.

formatted_address: 234 W 42nd St, New York, NY 10036, United States
name: The Journey Church NYC

reviews.text:
My NYC friends—this one’s for you! 🗽❤️

If you’ve been searching for a church that truly feels like home, I highly recommend The Journey Church NYC. When we lived in New York, we couldn’t find that connection and ended up traveling to NJ to attend Liquid Church, which became our home church.

But now—my cousin, who lives in NY, finally found a place that feels like family. We visited Journey, and from day one, they went out of their way to make us feel welcomed. We even shared how far the trip was for us, and guess what? They surprised us with a MetroCard so we could come back and serve alongside our cousin. 🥹🙌

That’s the kind of love and intentional care that makes this church so special. 💒✨ If you’re looking for a church that feels like home—and people who feel like family—I highly recommend Journey Church NYC. ❤️ From the moment you walk in, you’re welcomed with open arms. It’s a place where you can grow in your faith and feel truly connected. Don’t just take my word for it—come and experience it for yourself!

I have been to this church (2) and I really like their Sunday service when they start with worship. I have even decided to get Baptized on my own. Everyone is super supportive of your presence being there. There’s always so much activity and it seems like a very loving community from different backgrounds. Love it!!! Will recommend to all ages and they are very family oriented and flexible to your schedules.

The best church in NYC hands down ~ HOLY SPIRIT FILLED ; TJC is all about GOD — sermons are Bible based using scripture (sound doctrine) including our professional breakfast (always inspirational leadership; men and women of God / authors like Henry & Richard Blackaby) , growth groups , servant evangelism groups, feeding the homeless, visiting prisons providing clothing..(Rikers Island), 🎶WORSHIP🎶, last but definitely not least BAPTISM & JOURNEY KIDS (what a delight) during each Sunday service you get to experience God in a way that will make you desire to come back again and again. Here at the Journey Church we are taught practical lessons to help us find grit/ passion in order to achieve all that God has planned for our lives !! You are not alone here, this church is a home away from home “ a place to be yourself (come as you are) and because of the welcome team ; you just know in your heart of hearts GOD IS HERE!!! Pastor Kerrick, his wife Lorie & their three children and staff are great examples of mini Christ, truly set apart, they make it their business to always be of good service to everyone who enters TJC!! I have been attending TJC since 2014 became a member in 2015 with a burning desire to continue to grow and be more like Christ I will continue to serve and join every way possible; gimper for God!! The Journey Church has a servant spirit and allows you to pick and choose this day which path you will take … TRUE “ CHRISTIANS! I pray to see God’s living WORD , GRACE, hope , love and forgiveness expand and reach the world via THE JOURNEY ~ PS. This is a praying Church, prayer meetings are on Wednesday’s at noon, Sunday morning before service and via email (our pastors are always ready and willing to pray) #INJESUSNAMEAMEN📖❤️‍🔥🎶🤲🏼🙌🏼🪽🔥🩸🎶😇🫶🏻☀️🎁💪😇 🌎

The most beautiful and humble church and group of leaders to ever exist! They are out doing God’s work. This church feels so safe , welcoming and warming. They do so many great things for their community and people in general. I am so pleased with every single member of this church and the wonderful work they are doing in Jesus name. God Bless

Great church to go to! It brings comfort for those who are going through a tough situation in life such as health, finances and even the loss of a loved one. I too have experience that situation and the Journey has helped me a lot. This is considered a second home for me and it brings me closer to god and heaven. Pastor Kerrick teaches the message in a straightforward way!

formatted_address: 145 W 84th St, New York, NY 10024, United States
name: Trinity New York - Upper West Side

reviews.text: At Trinity New York I found community and friendships with amazing girls, who pray for me and have become my best friends. I love everything about this church from the worship to the preaching, and I’m so blessed to have found my church home.

I absolutely love this place—it’s the best church I’ve ever been a part of. It’s truly changed my life and strengthened my walk with God. I found a genuine sense of community here, made friends and even got baptized. What makes it even more special is that it’s local and led by millennial pastors who come from a strong lineage of ministry. Their teaching is rich, deep, and rooted in biblical truth. Every Sunday, I feel welcomed, seen, and excited to be there.

This has been my home church for the past three years, and what a glorious journey it has been. I can share my own testimony and it’s one filled with gratitude and awe. I’m so deeply moved that these two young people chose to come to the busiest, wildest city on earth and bless us with their unwavering obedience to God. Church often feels like a hospital a place full of broken, hurting people seeking healing. But here, in this sacred space, we are not only mended ..we are restored, renewed, and reminded of our purpose in Christ. It’s where grace meets growth, and where faith takes root in community. I’m genuinely overjoyed to be part of this body, this journey, and this move of God.

This is a Church for everyone. The lost who are seeking God for the first time, and the mature in their faith. This Chruch sticks to the word of God and pursues people who are far from God with love, grace and truth! 🙌

I love this church so much. I was baptized here. I gained friends that prayed for and with me. It’s a church that you can come alone and leave feeling seen. It’s a great church to build a community in. Equally important, I was able to further my love of God and understanding of the Bible. The children ministry truly cares about their wellbeing and so many kids become bestfriends . From group studies, to social gatherings and prayer meetings, this church knows how to feed what you’ve been lacking. Couldn’t recommend this church enough.

reviews.text: Strong community of Biblically minded believers fed with expository preaching of Scriptures and a beloved sister church from my own local Grace Bible Church Plantation in South Florida. Looking forward for visiting!

My husband and I looked into getting married at Grace Bible Church NYC. Unfortunately, we were  denied because we aren't "members" of the church. In my opinion marriage is a universal human institution ("common grace") that should be accessible to all couples, regardless of their specific affiliation with that particular congregation. If you are believers such as us and you desire to get married under God; in the house of God look into Manhattan Bible Church. You must meet with the pastor and are required to take marital classes before your ceremony. This is something Grace Bible Church NYC could have offered us. Unfortunately at the time my husband and I wanted to get married Manhattan Bible Church was being renovated. We never got to get married in the house of God which broke our hearts as believers! And as fellow Christians!

What a church! These guys are rare find. If you want to know God, find forgiveness, understand the Bible, grow spiritually, check this place out! So rare, sadly, to find people like this who are just committed to preaching the Bible as it is. Real food.

reviews.text: Love Epiphany! What  blessing to be led by leaders who are so rooted in the word and who make sure every message is centered around Jesus. Pastor B and Pastor Caleb are the best. The church is youthful and mostly millennials, and it’s great to see young people who love Jesus. Make sure you get there on time though, seats fill up quickly.

Not here to judge but it’s quite questionable to have people up front representing the church and kingdom of God in a such a way there should be a certain standard but overall service was great!

The church is a trendy church. A lot of people go there to get motivated. Many times I sit there I hear the pastor brush on things without really getting too deep, it’s almost like he doesn’t want to offend his young crowds of followers. Last Sunday preach was about newness. He kept saying that grace will save you from your sin; which is true. however, he made it seem that grace will always save you and that you can continue to fall without making the effort to really live for Jesus and like Jesus. Modesty is just not one of this church strength. It gives club vibes. The pastor always quoting drakes and other rappers with their dirty lyrics. I get it he just wants to make the new generation feel better and motivate them with offending them. Good luck with true spiritual growth.

reviews.text: Friendly staff and members.  When I went there, they don’t discriminate on appearance or ethnicity.  The congregation has a very diverse background.  They even have many people coming and driving from New Jersey and upstate. However, most members spoke to me to try to make me feel welcomed.  They also have complimentary breakfast, which is very nice, and communion.  Their service is in a school auditorium, which has these annoying concrete stubs on the floor behind the chairs that I tripped on.  I like the pastor’s way of preaching (he is from the south and more aligned to my Southern Baptist roots).  The service is very short (about an hour), so that’s nice in my opinion.

I've been going to this church fairly regularly for a few years. I have always found the congregation to be friendly, supportive, and spirit filled. Pastor Jeff's sermons are practical, inspirational, and sometimes pretty funny. His messages are based firmly on scripture, yet remain compassionate and non-judgemental. Newcomers are welcomed warmly and encouraged to explore the various programs and classes the church offers. The congregation is richly diverse and  gloriously reflects the melting pot that is New York. I think this church is a great place for spiritual nourishment, and they have great bagels too!

Awesome congregation! Pastor Jeff is an excellent leader who does feed the flock. The members are very welcoming and I love the idea that he leads Bible studies. Thank you for embracing us in His love 🙏🏼

I recently decided to visit Community Christian Church.   The welcome was so warm and loving.  This is what my grandson with special needs needed.At first he attended Sunday school and was doing his own thing. The next time he really was participating with the other children The 3rd time the teacher said he lead the pray in the class.  I must say thank you to these teachers of God.  He begs to go to Sunday school now, and I am so grateful for there patience and tolerance with my baby boy.  LOVE children know LOVE . Especially GODS Love.  See  you Sunday.

When my wife and I moved to New York, we were looking for a church that was more than just worship songs and a sermon. When we visited CCC, we were welcomed warmly and found a small yet diverse congregation of good people doing their best to follow Christ. We don't all agree on everything, but that's kind of the point -- anyone can come and be who they are, from where they are, in community with other believers. And the music turns out to be pretty good anyway.

There was a time of prayer to close out. Then, refreshments and visiting after. Such a great vibe for a church downtown. We would totally return to this great church!

I’ve visited Living Hope on so many occasions and every time the presence of God exceeds my expectations. If you’re looking for a place where you feel God’s presence every time, then Living Hope is the place to visit or make your church home. The pastor, his wife, and the church family are warm and welcoming. I can’t wait to visit again the next time I’m in NYC. Continue to let God shine Living Hope, our world needs the Jesus and the HOPE you are preaching about. God bless you all!
We LOVE visiting Living Hope NYC! We always feel so welcome and leave feeling loved and at peace. You will not regret visiting and experiencing amazing worship and dynamic biblical teaching.
Living Hope is an amazing church. The leadership is top notch and care for everyone.

A Spirit-Filled Church with a Strong Sense of Mission and Community

PMCC (4th Watch) of New York is more than just a place of worship—it is a vibrant and spiritually grounded community that truly lives out the teachings of Christ. From the moment you walk in, you’re welcomed with warmth, love, and sincerity. The members are united in faith, and there’s a strong sense of fellowship that makes you feel like family.

The church remains deeply rooted in the apostolic doctrine, guided by the leadership of Apostle Jonathan S. Ferriol and the local ministry of Ptr. What sets PMCC (4th Watch) apart is its commitment to evangelism, discipleship, and service. Whether through local outreach, prayer gatherings, or community events, the church actively seeks to fulfill its mission in the “4th Watch” of God’s timeline. It’s a place where your faith can grow deeper and your walk with God can become more purposeful.

If you’re looking for a church that teaches sound doctrine, promotes genuine fellowship, and lives with spiritual urgency, I highly recommend PMCC (4th Watch) of New York.

In every service they explain prophecies, end-times, and true worship with such clarity. What truly opened my eyes was their teaching about apostolic leadership - just like Paul was called through voice and light (Acts 9:3-6), God still calls His sent ones today. The church helped me understand why we need a true apostle in these last days (Ephesians 4:11-13) and how to identify God's messenger (Matthew 24:45). Their teachings about the Goodman of the House and God's times and seasons are eye-opening and completely biblical. The presence of God here is powerful through the preaching of unadulterated Words of God. What sets them apart is their unwavering commitment to pure biblical doctrine. If you're searching for truth and tired of watered-down teaching, this church will transform your understanding of God's Word.

After searching for truth and having so many questions about faith, I found answers here at PMCC (4th Watch). What struck me was how every teaching is backed by Scripture - not just opinions or traditions. The apostolic leadership here reminds me of the early church in Acts. They explained water baptism in Jesus' name (Acts 2:38), the Holy Spirit baptism (Acts 2:4), and end-time prophecies in ways that finally made sense. Unlike other churches I've visited, they don't shy away from deep biblical truths. If you're seeking genuine biblical teaching and a church that follows the apostolic pattern, this is where you'll find it. My faith has grown stronger through their clear, Scripture-based teachings.

reviews.text: This was such a terrible experience that it actually took me a few years to recover from the interaction I had one of the pastors feom Church @ The Rock. Approximately 3 years ago my husband and I was looking for a non-denomination church to have our daughter’s  dedication ceremony. We lived in NJ at the time, but we wanted to have the dedication done at a church in Brooklyn closer to our parents in Canarsie. I called the church to make an appointment to meet with one of the pastors. We went for Sunday service and right after service we were told to go to the building next door and upstairs in a room where my husband and I sat with pastor Nick and another member at the church. We spoke for over an hour in this room and one of the questions they asked us was if we died tomorrow would we go to heaven. They pretty much spoke to us in a judgmental way and insinuated we would have to join their church before they even considered doing a dedication ceremony for our daughter. I felt interrogated and confused upon leaving the church office. At first I thought maybe it was just me because I was still in my postpartum stage, but after my husband stated he felt the same way I knew I was not overreacting for feeling the way I felt.  The following week we found another church downtown Brooklyn with a wonderful pastor that did the dedication ceremony for our daughter. I waited over 3 years to write this review, because I wanted to choose my words wisely and to be sure I still felt the same way I did 3 years ago. I felt like upon making the appointment if they knew part of their protocol for us to have the ceremony done at their church that we had to become church members that should have been mentioned to us over the phone when I spoke to pastor Nick especially since they knew we lived 3 hour away coming from another state. To this day it still bothers me how we were treated and my husband and I felt like we were violated.

I attended the Candlelight Concert Halloween Music last night, and it was a beautiful experience.

The church setting was perfect for this performance. Hundreds of candles flickered throughout the space, casting soft shadows on the walls and creating an atmosphere that felt both intimate and mysterious. The lighting struck exactly the right tone—serene rather than spooky, which made the entire evening feel elegant.

The acoustics were excellent. String instruments resonated beautifully through the vaulted ceilings, and the Halloween-themed music balanced eerie moments with sophistication. Everything came together seamlessly: the venue, the candlelight, and the performance created a cohesive experience that felt special.

If you’re looking for a refined way to celebrate the season, I highly recommend this concert. It offers something far more memorable than typical Halloween entertainment.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

I also emailed the worship director about auditioning. He responded right away that they're always looking for vocalists for choir and worship leaders, but when I responded back with my audition video and why I left my previous church's worship team (due to the director yelling at volunteers which is now being investigated), he never responded for 2 months. I followed up last week with no response. Today, I finally got a generic email response today declining my joining the team.

The Lord told me it had nothing to do with my voice because I've served in worship choir and as a vocalist before. Instead of being compassionate toward a person who's struggling through church hurt, they added to the pain by ignoring.

I served on One's lighting/production and social media teams in 2012-2013 and visited on and off through the years. I'll keep listening to the sermons, but I won't be visiting the church again. This whole experience left a bad taste in my mouth.

reviews.text: This place is for genz, young people. The church has so many members, about 400-500 people per each service.  But it's spiritual place. I can eat donuts and coffee every Sunday. I love this church. Praying team is awesome and spiritual.

This is the perfect church if you are looking for:

1. Experience. The main worship area is very dark to set the right mood. No lights for you to read your Bible. In fact, I was the only one with my Bible (paper kind) and I could not read it because it was so dark. I should have traded down my Bible for an iPad since that seems to be what everyone else had or their phones. Actually there was no need for your Bible since every passage was displayed on the big screen. Also right when you walk in, you're greeted by a huge coffee area giving you the feel that you're not at stuffy/traditional church but a hip coffee shop with cool merch. But hey, the proceeds go towards missions so it's all good.

2. Emotion. This church charges you up with great emotion. From the moment you enter their building music is blaring and you can't hear anyone singing. There is also skits and dancing before the sermon comes. An emotionally charged ballet dancer weeps off the stage as they try to visibly display the Philippians 4 passage about not being anxious. People around me were crying from watching the ballet performance. The crowd also got into the break dancing moves by the male ballet dancer. I just love it when there is break dancing at church!  Nothing gets me close with God like break dancing! Woot, woot!

The songs were also very emotionally driven by talented singers and band members. The songs were very generic about God and feeling. It could have been songs about any god since no mention of Christ or his atoning work for sin is mentioned. In fact, the songs seem to be vetted and carefully chosen to give you an emotional experience. Perfect for those who are looking for a pure emotional experience.

3. Eloquence. The pastor, Aaron Kim, was incredibly eloquent. He quoted Andrew Sullivan and Henri Nouwen, two openly homosexual Roman Catholics, waxing eloquent on their views about being still and quiet. The pastor spent more time quoting theologians and philosophers instead of explaining the meaning of the biblical text. Very impressive!

If you are looking for a place which will preach the Word of God, the gospel as the remedy for sin through faith in Christ alone according to the Word of God alone to the glory of God alone, look elsewhere. If you want the Bible with context, exegesis, and biblical exposition you will not like this church. Instead the sermon drips with worldly eloquence!

But if you're looking for emotionally charged, experientially inviting, and eloquent speakers - this is the church for you! They are very open and do not want you to be offended. They will make you feel very welcome and feel great.

i go to another church nearby but had heard great things about tapestry so i checked it out.

if you are looking for a congregation is largely younger (high school, college, and a big demographic in the 20s and 30s), then you will probably like tapestry.  no church can be all things to all people but i found the people welcoming.  the church is definitely on the modern side with modern worship, big production and a modern space.

if i had any criticisms or concerns for people who are looking to check it out, it would be the following.  bear in mind that these are preference issues and fundamentally i think very highly of the church, but these may be dealbreakers for you.

1.  pastor tends to speak very long...frequently over 60 minutes.  i didn't find the pastor to be very dynamic, but again, this is a preference issue.  as far as theology and content, the messages are very much on point.

2.  congregation is on the young side, and the demographic is largely asian.

3.  parking can be a little difficult in this part of DTLA and it's a little more run-down but then again, so is my church's area (i go to newstory LA).

if this appeals to you, check out their services on youtube for a sense of what they are like.  their channel is "tapestry LA church."

reviews.text: Eagle Rock Baptist Church is a great place to call home. The church is very Bible-based, and the preaching is engaging without feeling stuffy. You can really tell they care about families and building strong relationships. The kids’ and teen ministries are awesome—fun, welcoming, and focused on helping kids grow in their faith. There are also solid ministries for both women and men, so everyone has a place to connect. ERBC is a friendly, down-to-earth church with people who genuinely love God and each other.

Eagle Rock Baptist Church has been a second home for me. I’ve been in attendance at this church for now going on 7 years. From the first day up until now I’ve grown spiritually-through life group, mental-through understanding the word, intellectually-through the importance of community, and financially-through understanding how money works when God’s word is applied.

I’m alway eager to return to church on Sunday’s & Wednesday’s to learn more about the word with like minded people. Though I’ve become like family to many of the members at ERBC. I can’t help, but to think about how difficult life would be without a covering of Christ while doing life.

I believe that we the people are the church, and God is within us. From the first time I attended ERBC I was able to see that same model duplicated throughout all the members, pastors and other individuals attending sermons.

ERBC has made coming to the house of the Lord a safe and friendly environment for families to grow together in Christ while striving to be exceptional at loving people. If you have a family & your interests in growing not only a community, but knowledge and understanding of the word with your children & God ERBC Is most definitely the place for you!

Hope to see you there!

More people, More like Jesus.

5 years ago, in the darkness of COVID, God led us to this little church. We were searching for a Bible-based community where we could hear God’s Word and where our children could put down roots.

We live in days where “due to the increase of wickedness, our hearts have grown cold.”  It’s all too easy to align ourselves with churches that fit our preferences or political views. (I confess this sin right here!) But this is not that kind of church. ERBC is Jesus-focused. Only in the presence of Jesus can our stone hearts truly melt—and here, our hearts melted.

Pastor Rick is a gifted speaker with a sense of humor that appeals to everyone—think dry, British-style humor—while Pastor Andrew takes us deep into the Bible with thoughtful, challenging teaching. We love them both, and we are so grateful for all the servants here at ERBC.

In just five years, reading and hearing God’s Word has transformed us—and continues to transform us every single day.

If you are looking for validation of who you voted for, this is not the place. But if you want Jesus—more of Jesus—this is exactly where you need to be.

I have been attending ERBC for almost 2 years now. The first thing that I experienced was how welcoming and friendly everyone is. The leadership in the church is very supporting and knowledgeable. In all the times that I have attended church in my life, this is the first time that I felt so close to a church, where I have joined a couple of Life Group bible studies and have volunteered for various things within the church. I am thrilled to announce that I was baptized in June 2025 on Fathers Day. I would recommend ERBC to anyone who is looking for a church to call home.

Eagle Rock Baptist Church and Sr. Pastor Rick Mandl have been instrumental in my spiritual and social life and for my wife. I had the good fortune of being involved at ERBC for 18 years, until shortly before moving from LA County. My relationship with Pastor Rick has been more instrumental and friendly than with any other pastor in my now-60+ age life. And the social connections forged with others I met at ERBC are far and away the most significant factors in my life compared to any other church or organization I have been involved with.

reviews.text:
Mt Sinai is a very interesting church, not perfect just interesting.

Recently Pastor Hurtt preached a sermon on gossip.   The sermon was helpful but it also reminded me that its important to know my bible and have a good understanding of it for myself.   Often ministers preach about various topics and I feel if something is bothering them that they can't control like gossip in the church, then its preached on, possibly to control what the congregation talks about regarding the church politics and issues/finances.

It was very interesting on that Sunday,  Pastor Hurtt provided a definition of gossip, which appeared to be his own definition of gossip.  He never stated if his definition came  google or the Webster dictionary or any other authentic legit source.   Instead  he just provided a definition with no reference point of where he got that definition.  He used some excellent scriptures to back his definition of  regarding gossip.

Often things (situations, issues etc.) go on in an organization and there should be legit discussions of what is going on.  Noone should be lying, exaggerating, or adding to or putting in there own assumption and then spreading it to others, however it is really important to discuss the facts about a situation and also often people's behavior regarding how they provide information or lack of it.   Its good to have an awareness of your surroundings and talking to others about the situation and finding they may have similar concerns is very important.    What goes on in the daily news should be discussed, and God will give you the wisdom to discern right from wrong without gossiping.   If people are contributing to an organization, they have the right to know what is going on and ask questions.  None one owns the church, yes there leaders and they should be held accountable and open about what goes on within a church.   Often when leaders decide what they want people to know, this causes problems.  45/47 is the same way, he wants citizens to do as he says without questions or commentary.   That's ridiculous and its not working.

The same for the church, people are going to talk, and if you are doing the right thing, it won't bother you.  Being transparent and open with others, keeps gossip down.

God is not pleased with Mt. Sinai and there will be accountability on earth and in heaven.   Everyone will be held accountable for there actions and everyone will reap what they sow.   Respect goes two ways.

Praise God!  I love to worship and exalt the Lord, sing His praises and study the Word.  I've  found the church after God's own heart and that stands on a Foundation of giving, love, studying the Word and fellowship.

reviews.text:
As a Los Angeles wedding photographer, I recently had the pleasure of photographing a ceremony at this incredible church — and it was such a memorable experience. The space is LGBTQ+ friendly, warm, and welcoming to all couples, which makes it even more special.

The church itself is stunning, with beautiful gothic architecture, tall arches, and elegant details that give every photo a timeless look. The light inside is soft and atmospheric, creating a perfect mood for wedding ceremonies. For professional photographers, I’d recommend bringing some additional external lighting, especially near the front section of the church, where natural light can be limited.

Couples should keep in mind that the time allowed for photography inside is limited, since the venue charges per hour spent there. In my case, we didn’t have much extra time for portraits inside, but we still captured some incredible moments before heading outdoors.

Overall, I truly enjoyed shooting here — it’s a one-of-a-kind location that blends classic architecture with inclusivity and heart. Highly recommend it for couples looking for a Los Angeles church wedding venue that’s both elegant and welcoming.

— Nem, Wedding Photographer | NZ Wedding Studio

I was referred to the Celebrity Centre after visiting another Scientology church in Los Angeles, and from the moment I arrived, I was welcomed with open arms. The staff are attentive, thoughtful, and consistent with follow-up—checking in on my progress and making sure I had what I needed to grow.

This place has changed my life for the better. If you’re looking for clarity, structure, and a welcoming environment filled with positive, focused people—this is where you’ll find it.

Their courses and counseling are some of the best in the, catered to people in the arts, business professionals etc..  I felt as if I was among family.  They have courses for any area of life you are having difficulty with or just want more information including How To Be a Successful Parent, and they even have an Art Course which is based on cutting edge technology on how to be a top artist.  It is all denominational so it does not matter what is a person's religion or belief.  This center will help your life prosper and help you reach your goals faster and more effectively.  These are some of the most ethical, highly trained professionals in the world.  THIS IS AN ADVENTURE OF YOU!!!

I really don’t like this church and its fake seminars. They attract artists under the name of acting seminars, but the seminar has nothing to do with film or acting. Then their staff approach participants one by one, isolate them, and ask for money. It’s truly a scam.
What’s worse is that before the seminar started, we filled out a form with our contact info, and now they harass us every day with texts and phone calls.
Be more cautious about this church and its seminars.

This church advertises acting seminars to attract artists. But when you attend, you quickly realize that their real goal is to sell you their own class packages, which have nothing to do with the actual film industry.

The seminar itself is just ten minutes of irrelevant talk by two unknown individuals who introduce themselves as a director and a producer. Then, the church staff took us to another floor and locked each of us alone in separate rooms. For an entire hour, they tried to brainwash us into signing up and paying for their classes.

I didn’t want to register, but two people stayed in the room with me, repeating the same things over and over—that I was a miserable and troubled person, and that I needed emotional healing. I was extremely frightened. When I said I would leave or call the police, they finally opened the door, and I ran away.

The staff of this church are suspicious and strange people. They try to use amateur psychological tactics to brainwash those who attend their seminars. They aim to bring out a broken and mentally unstable version of you from within, and then pressure you to pay and register for their classes.

Be cautious about the seminars they offer. Also, they only admit three people per seminar so they can more easily isolate and manipulate them.

I want to extend a sincere thank you to every single staff member... each of you plays a vital role, and this message is meant for all who contribute their dedication, time, and intention to the mission.

I will never forget how I first came across this path, through one of the devoted individuals who is part of the mission “Zarek“. What felt like something I “randomly” stumbled upon became the greatest birthday gift I could have received. Looking back, it’s clear it wasn’t by chance at all, but something that was meant to be part of my journey in this lifetime.

Discovering Dianetics has been truly life-changing. For so long, my reactive mind had been influencing what I believed to be truth, shaping my perceptions and reactions in ways I wasn’t fully aware of. Through the opportunity to participate in courses, seminars, and to begin using the tools. I’ve come to recognize what was hidden and to better understand myself and life with greater clarity. This has shifted the way I view my experiences, my purpose, and my potential.

I had intended to send this message sooner, but I found myself so deeply drawn to the mission that missing even a single day feels heartbreaking. Every time I am there, I feel a strong sense of purpose, as though I am exactly where I am meant to be. Being part of the environment, the learning, and the people has become something I genuinely value and hold close.

Thank you again to everyone who makes this possible. Your commitment does not go unnoticed, and it has made a meaningful difference in my life.

I recently attended a seminar where we watched a film about the cause and mechanism behind negative thoughts, emotions, and ineffective actions. We studied tools that help address these and improve life by removing the source of negativity, becoming happier, thinking more positively, and acting more effectively. We practiced these tools in pairs, and it became easier for me to cope with the loss of my grandfather. Thank you. This is a meaningful result for me.
I also helped a woman who had been in a car accident. She had been in pain for 2.5 years, and the pain went away.

Visiting the Church of Scientology felt unwelcoming. Security was very strict, closely watching anyone walking nearby. I tried taking a photo of a lion statue and security rolled up on a bike, and it felt like I was immediately under scrutiny. Overall, the place doesn’t feel very open or inviting to visitors.

Curious?
Go look for yourself.
Never rely on Negative Nellies who have never been there or done that.
It sure changed my life for the better!

When I made the decision to visit NAC, the only expectation that I had was to receive a Word that would minister to my needs. The emotional state that I was in at the time was very confusing and consuming. Prior to joining I had this encounter that ultimately awaken me to, the power and love of God. I was already an Evangelist and was already living a life aligned with the Word of God,- but what I experienced was life altering. This may sound a little weird, but have you ever been in search of something and had not a clue of where to look because in all honesty you didn't know what to look for? Well, in one service, I was thinking about the things that happened to me in my life and suddenly Pastor Jeff said, "some of you have gone through some things that you should have sought therapy for." At the moment that he said therapy, I felt the intense emotional pain hit my chest so hard that my knees literally gave out. I felt the overwhelming surge of emotions that was present when the Detectives informed me that my mother was murdered. My soul took up this wailing of a cry and the pressure I felt in my heart left. Needless to say I went down to the alter and when I walked away- I felt something detach from me. I didn't know what it was, but I felt so different.

The next day I called a few of my therapist friends to talk about this encounter. Everyone was so eager to learn what had left. I closed my eyes and shared the experience and before I knew it- I was in the parking lot at work crying. I realized that the emotional pain from my Mom's death had attached to me and just became a part of my way of life and when I recognized that the pain was gone; I couldn't believe that I was not aware that it became a part of my identity. From that day in August 2013 to now I have not felt that sense of gloom or pressure in my heart. I still cry but God transformed my perspective!!!!!!

reviews.text: Salvation army should not allow loitering and camping outside their building. This neighborhood community was PROMISED that allowing Salvation Army into the area will not negatively impact the community, but it has. Many businesses surrounding have closed because of the increased crime, the Salvation Army attracts. Drugs, overdoses, deaths, harassment, assaults..... all happening outside the Salvation Army in Hollywood.

I visited the Hollywood Salvation Army on Sunset to inquire about Homeless services. There are two buildings so I didn’t know which one to go into. Thankfully somebody from the kitchen immediately greeted me and asked if I needed help, and directed me where to go.

After checking in with their staff at the Access Point, I waited in a short line for a case worker. I went around 1pm on a Tuesday and there was only one person in front of me. While I was waiting, a gentleman in line informed me, first, that he wasn’t gay. More importantly, he let me know that they were handing out sack lunches, so I went to grab on.

The same gentleman in the kitchen from before (tall, tattoos, unfortunately I didn’t get his name) gave me a tomato & cheese sandwich because they were out of the packed lunches. The sandwich was honestly pretty good, definitely stop here if you are in emergency need of food.

After a few minutes, the case worker named Catherine came out to help me. They ran through the protocol of the steps I’d need to take to get housing through them. Ultimately they didn’t have the services I needed, which to me seems like false advertising so that’s why I gave them the 4 stars.

I made an appointment was told to come back the next day at 9am. Cam back the next day at 9am and was told to come in at 2pm. I came back at 2pm and was told to come back the following day at 9am. At 9am I received a call to come at 2pm. Came at 3pm and was told to wait outside. Waited for 2 hours outside and was ignored. I spent money to get here. And not to mention time. I am recently homeless and these people do not care about anyone. The lady at the front desk is ignorant and mean. I cant belive the wasted 3 full days attempting to get help.

Please fire the lady at the front desk she literally does everything in her power to avoid providing helping!

Survival wouldn't exist for many people in the heart of Los Angeles if it wasn't for such an amazing group of hardworking men and woman in our community that come together EVERYDAY and EVERY NIGHT to ensure the health and welfare of OUR people. The ones keeping the economy secure and our lands from being overtaken. The ones doing the jobs that are so dangerous that many lock themselves inside their home instead of getting involved. Security and connectivity. Bringing each other together for the longevity of it. For community resources and the help of coalitions the Salvation Army goes above and beyond to ensuring that those without a home are still protected and are still able to survive until the resources they need to get on there feet become available.

Perfect for helping the community and establishing a connection with a helpful hand and assisting getting our unhoused and in need people the safe and secure help they deserve. Amazing group of people work here.

I wanted to be in the sanctuary for each of the services I attended so I was in line 4 hours before each service. I was able to sit in the main sanctuary for each service including Easter Sunday. This is a real present day Jesus is walking on earth church. In Jesus' days people came from afar to meet him, to be healed, to be delivered. That is what is happening at Revelation Church.

We came from Florida in March 2025 for Spring Break, we were going to go to Universal Orlando but I was convicted to not waste money on that and instead spend it to go see Prophet Lovy since my son needed healing of a spinal tumor they found out of no where. Service was great both Thursday and Sunday! Thursday night Prophet Lovy was going to pray for me and as time went on and service was almost done I ripped a paper from my book and wrote Spinal Tumor. We got on stage and received prayer and then I ripped up my paper on the stage. The next week at his repeat MRI it was read as NEGATIVE, they have no idea what it even is and said due to no symptoms he can repeat an MRI in a year. Since then my son has asked me to go to church with him so I know God’s plan is bigger. I asked God “why did it not disappear I thought it would since his MRI was rescheduled to after we saw Prophet Lovy” (keep in mind I am a board certified Nurse Practitioner who believes God heals). God said “what makes you think he won’t be healed? It won’t always be done the way you think it will be done for my ways are not your ways”. Not only was I convicted but I was joyful knowing He beard me and answered me and I can see Him in action. Once we become wealthy we will be going here as much as we can in person but for now remain in faith and watching virtually. God bless this church!

I’m not a member of this church but I’m the cousin in law of one of the pastors who led my grandmas funeral service not too long ago. I was very close with my grandmother and prepared a beautiful eulogy, one that I hoped speaking aloud would help heal some part of me. And I never got the chance. Two of her siblings spoke for nearly half an hour, they had planned it ahead of time unbeknownst to her immediate family. I found out afterward that the pastor did was ask my grandfather, my grandmas husband, if he had any words to say prior to the service. After her siblings spoke, there was no opportunity for the rest of us to speak, her children, her best childhood friends…then the pastor proceeded to speak about converting our lives to Jesus for approximately 20 minutes, nothing about my grandma. Granted we were at a church, but her service and our opportunity to mourn her was rushed for their own agenda. Save that for church.
So, I asked one of the siblings who spoke why the opportunity was never offered and his response was “there was a strict time limit”. So, part of me is angry at them. But part of me is angry at the church, for lack of communication and their selfishness. I’ll never get that opportunity back, so if you’re thinking about having a service there, maybe think twice.
