On 9/21/2025 I couldn't make it to the 9:00 a.m. service; however, I did watch the live-stream at home. I was shocked and horrified from what I saw and heard from the Lead Pastor and his wife! They were covering the death of Political Conservative Activist to the Congregation in a forceful and non-loving Christian way. Imposing their political beliefs onto the Congregation. The Pastor went as far as to tell the Congregation that if they didn't agree with them they could just leave right there and then and go find another Church! They both used a condescending tone and looked at the Congregation in a hostile manner!
That was definitely not the Christian message that I was expecting to hear from Pastors that I thought I knew. Therefore and sadly, I will no longer be a member of The Rock Church. I  believe that when a door is closed God is the One who holds the key to opening another!
Peace and Blessings to all!!!

I've been attending Calvary Life since the end of May. I wrote a previous review but am changing it because I recently decided to leave Calvary Life and feel the need to share my experience.

When I first attended, Pastor Chet mentioned in his sermon that we need to serve and a small fraction of the church did serve. I felt the Holy Spirit guiding me to start the volunteer process. I met with two members of the church staff and did a quick fingerprint test. When the test cleared, I was contacted to be an online host, a role I chose when I applied.  My first day was good, the person in charge gave me the run down and the need for the service I chose. He then left it up to another man to train me. He sent me a greeting via text and then crickets for three weeks. When I asked questions in the host chat they went unanswered or fellow hosts would try to guess the best they could. I felt left to die. After 3 weeks I quit the position as well as volunteering.

Within the first couple weeks I put a request in for counselling. It went completely ignored. A few weeks later, I called and the woman took my name and number. They never got back to me. I felt left to die.

Not everyone at Calvary Life is bad though. One of the staff members sat with me on Sundays and helped disciple me. The women at the church are great but this church is an example of how men have been deprioritized by the church overall. The men of this church show little signs of spiritual life.

Mostly, I have found Calvary Life to be a church to make converts not disciples.

A Transformative Worship Community at the Heart of Hollywood

My experience at First Presbyterian Church Hollywood has been nothing short of remarkable. This beautiful, historic campus offers a sanctuary where spiritual roots are deeply anchored in traditional Presbyterian heritage, yet gracefully infused with modern touches that resonate across generations. The music is a testament to this blend—a soulful mix of choir harmonies and contemporary melodies that elevate worship at every point in the service, touching the heart on both nostalgic and innovative levels.

Pastor JT’s leadership shines brightly, guiding the congregation with motivational and heartfelt messages that inspire introspection and communal growth. His sermons are thoughtfully crafted, consistently delivering warmth and purpose, truly ministering to both individuals and families alike.

One of the church’s many strengths is its dedication to serving all ages. During Sunday congregation services, children experience their own nurturing environment through engaging Bible School programs. This focus on youth and family creates a multi-layered worship experience—where the spiritual growth of children is prioritized alongside that of adults—fostering a community that truly nurtures all generations in faith.

The church’s commitment to fostering a multi-generational community is further reflected in its diverse programming. From engaging children’s Bible studies and Sunday School to vibrant services for teens and young adults, First Presbyterian Hollywood creates spaces where everyone can encounter God’s love and truth. Additionally, morning Bible studies prior to worship further deepen spiritual roots, making it a place of continuous learning and connection.

Nestled in a prime location in Hollywood, California, the campus radiates history and love—an inviting haven for visitors and members alike. The staff’s warm hospitality makes every visit feel like coming home, embracing all with open arms. Whether you're a local, a visitor, or seeking a spiritual community to root yourself in, this church provides a genuine sense of belonging and purpose.

Beyond Sunday services, the church is actively engaged in meaningful outreach—feeding the homeless through the Lighthouse program and participating in global missions—demonstrating a heartfelt commitment to living out Christ’s love in action. The campus even hosts a vibrant Hispanic Chapel at the same time, ensuring a rich cultural tapestry and worship experience for Spanish-speaking communities.

First Presbyterian Church Hollywood is more than a church; it’s a beacon of purpose, love, and spiritual breadth. I wholeheartedly invite anyone seeking a place of worship filled with beautiful music, powerful messages, and authentic community to come and experience what makes this landmark in Hollywood so extraordinary.

reviews.text:
Upon entering the Orthodox Church, I was immediately enveloped by an atmosphere that felt both ancient and sacred. The heavy scent of incense and the soft flicker of candlelight set the tone for a deeply spiritual encounter. The first thing I noticed was the architecture. The domes, arches, and iconostasis drew my eyes upward and inward, encouraging contemplation and reverence.

The iconography throughout the church was breathtaking. Each icon told a story, serving as a visual theology that invites the faithful into a sacred narrative. Unlike the more minimalist aesthetics of many Western churches, the Orthodox Church embraces beauty as a form of worship. The colors, gold leaf, and rich symbolism reflect the glory of heaven. I was particularly struck by the quiet reverence of those present. Many stood silently in prayer or made the sign of the cross with solemnity and intention.

The Liturgy, which I later learned is called the Divine Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom, began with chanting that seemed to suspend time. The chanting was done a cappella and in unison. Its mystical and meditative tone moved me in a way I wasn’t expecting. The language used was not entirely in English, which added to the sense of timelessness and mystery. I later discovered it was a combination of Greek and Church Slavonic.

A deacon led the prayers in a chant-like tone, alternating with responses from the choir. The rhythm created a spiritual cadence that guided the mind and soul. I appreciated how every action, from the lighting of candles to the movement of the clergy, felt intentional and meaningful. The priest’s vestments were ornate and beautiful, not for vanity, but to reflect the glory of God and the sacred role he embodies during the Liturgy.

The homily was surprisingly accessible. It connected the Gospel reading to daily life, while still rooted deeply in tradition. One of the most striking aspects of the service was the sense of continuity. It felt like stepping into a worship that had been ongoing for centuries. There was no rush. Time in the Orthodox Church seems to flow differently, focusing not on efficiency but on eternity.

The Eucharist, or Holy Communion, was treated with profound respect. Only baptized Orthodox Christians may partake, emphasizing the sacredness of the mystery. Observing the faithful receive Communion with such reverence reminded me of the depth of their commitment and the seriousness with which they approach the sacraments. After the Liturgy, many congregants remained in prayer. There was no hurried exodus, just a gentle transition from the sacred to the secular.

The community was welcoming. Though I was clearly a visitor, several people greeted me warmly and asked if I had questions. I was invited to the coffee hour afterward, where I had the chance to speak with the priest. He was kind, humble, and eager to share the richness of the Orthodox tradition. The conversation revealed how deeply rooted the church’s teachings are, yet how relevant they remain for today’s challenges.

The priest explained the significance of icons, the role of fasting, and the importance of the liturgical calendar in forming the spiritual life of the believer. I was fascinated by how much of Orthodox worship is experiential—meant to engage all the senses. The incense, the music, the visual art, and the physical gestures all serve to create a holistic encounter with the divine.

I also learned about the fasting cycles, the importance of confession, and the theology of theosis—the idea that the purpose of life is union with God. This spiritual vision was both humbling and inspiring. The church wasn’t just a building or a Sunday gathering place. It was a living body, bound together by faith, tradition, and the pursuit of holiness.

What impressed me most was the seriousness with which Orthodox Christians approach their spiritual life.

reviews.text: Iconic historic church in Bronzeville built in 1899 with many preserved elements. The stained glass windows are a standout. Neighborhood gem. Friendly and informative congregants.

Yet another of my favorite splendid church edifice's in the City of Chicago. Ebenezer Baptist Church began its long storied life in 1899. Designed by famed Chicago architect Dankmar Adler (Louis Sullivan's partner). Originally a synagogue, the building was purchased by the black Ebenezer Missionary Baptist Church congregation in 1921.
————————————
"During the Great Migration of the 1900s, scores of blacks who transferred to Chicago from the South settled in Bronzeville and made Ebenezer their church home.
Throughout the years, Ebenezer developed a reputation as a center for gospel music. Thomas Dorsey, the father of gospel music, introduced his blend of Christian praise and blues at Ebenezer and started the first gospel choir here.
The pulpit and pews of Ebenezer have hosted its share of historical politicians, ministers and vocal artists. During the 30-year pastorate of Rev. Frank K.Sims, distinguished guests of our church included Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., Ralph Metcalfe, Adam Clayton Powell and Mahalia Jackson." Soul city is a good birth church. Meaning, if you are looking for a church that gets you in the door, this is a solid place to start. ScC is never short of ways to get involved. Between sermons, service, outreach, small groups, Alpha, and foundations, you are offered plenty of ways to help the church.

If you are genuinely looking for transformation and strengthening your relationship with God, SCC might not be the church for you. The services are inconsistently connected to actual scripture. Some Pastors will rattle of a list of scripture whilst others will connect a story with modern day life.

House of Hope services have about 1.5 month lead time. Small groups discuss the previous week sermon. If you miss Sunday service, small group will recap for you.

Pastors will tell you church is like a hospital. There is a fine line between tolerance of those hurting and and shepherding those causing harm. The community leans into tolerance, not shepherding.

Again, very social church and a good place to start but if looking to deepen your faith, other churches are more effective to help you with your transformation and heart posture. SCC nourishes your flesh but has limits to how it is willing to nourish your spirit. ❤️🙏

Then the lead pastor came on stage. Not bad, a couple reference to scripture, but more of his opinion and not the true meaning of the verses.
Then it got weird...
The pastor started justifying and advocating for the next speaker, known only as "prophet k" ... And the lead pastor kept telling us this guy was a "prophet" and we should be prepared to hear him speak in tongues. The weirdest part about it is they gave no backstory on who he was, where he was from, or even his real name. Weird right?
Enter "prophet k"
Started with 2.5 minutes of incoherent ramblings of hallelujahs and "tongues" (ya, I timed it because it was so odd) I tried to give him the benefit of the doubt, but after 10 minutes, I felt uncomfortable and my gut told me to remove myself from the space. Long story short, I would never go back, nor recommend this church to any fellow believer.

name: Urban Village Church (Wicker Park)

reviews.text:
I love this church, and how it became a safe, inclusive, and empowering home for me during the pandemic. They truly do celebrate people of all backgrounds (i.e. they don't just give the LGBTQIA community a "seat on the pew", but actual voices and leadership roles). The people here are caring, honest, and supportive of each other, wherever you are on your life journey - even if you have doubts, trauma and uncertainty. Truly all are welcome here. UVC lives their mission of being bold, inclusive, and relevant by doing work in the local communities, and providing interactive ways to learn and give back during Black History Month, Pride Month, etc. with history walks and celebrations and hearing stories from the community lifted up.

I've especially loved Pastor D'Angelo's creativity when it comes to services and community-building at Wicker Park; we've had breakout discussion groups during the service, creative use of the stage setup and props, we've heard testimonies, and listened to music together, and even ended the sermon early for a surprise coffee hour when Pastor D said "You know what? I can preach about community, or we can go do it right now," recognizing that coming out of the pandemic many of us don't know each other and haven't had real conversations together. Those conversations and laughter were much needed.

It is wonderful to be a part of a church that follows the Gospel just as Jesus would.  Jesus welcomed all and left no one out.  It's easy to get caught up in religious practices but this is not the case at this church.  I like that the sermons focus on 1 verse st a time. It gives me an opportunity to really focus on that verse, not just during the sermon but during the week as well.  I believe we are the living church and im glad to see it brought to fruition.

reviews.text:
From out of town and needed a place to attend Sunday Mass
The church Is beautiful, the Mass itself was good

It is not very handicap accessible. I didn’t realize there was a lift until I left. I was able to ask someone for help getting my stroller inside.
When I was leaving, one of the guys that worked there was so rude to me, I thought I had done something wrong. But I was just trying to find a way out. He was so aggressive in his tone and choice of words, I actually said to him “I’m sorry if I have done something to upset you” and he then he responded “i know this church better than you do and you’re bantering with me”

Once I went upstairs, someone did help me with the lift. But he was also extremely rude, when I tried to go through the door, he said “I said I would open the door and you’re not listening to me”
What he meant was that he needed to open both doors, not just one door, for us to fit out of it with the stroller.

As a mother traveling alone, especially during the Christmas season, it really took the grace and happiness away from the Mass service I had just attended.

I won’t remember the beauty or happiness of the service. I’ll remember how I was treated by people that work there.

I’m sure it’s difficult to have strangers in the church where you work, but if you’re men of God, and can’t be Christ like to those around you, maybe don’t be a face of the church.

Beautiful stations of the cross and stained glass. The gift shop is on the lower floor with rosaries, cards. Books and more
Accessible venue with heavy door.

Only considering the architecture, pomp.  Epic setting.  Nice that they have the doors open to the public.

My husband and I just went to mass today for my birthday. The priest who presided forced us to take Jesus (Communion) with our hands. I have taken the communion kneeling down with my tongue for years now. This is exactly how it happened. I knelt down, the priest said “Please stand up because my back is bad.” I pray that he was not lying. I stood up, and then he said “USE YOUR HANDS”. In my understanding, PRIESTS SHOULD NOT force anyone how to receive Jesus in the Eucharist. Don’t force your preference to ours. If you are worried that you will be contaminated or infected with something if you are to give us Jesus through our tongue then maybe you shouldn’t be a priest. This church feels like a business building.

There are drinks and breakfast served in their cafe are which is serviced by the sweetest people. As you wait for the doors to open and the service to start you get to see the interactions of the people and their children. The children are excited to go to what is called the MKIDZ (which is the children’s church portion. Kids have their classes and activities while the parents enjoy their service. Just the excitement and smiles on their faces really show how much fun it is for them.
So far i thought it was too good to be true, but when the doors opened not only did you experience the kindness of the greeters at the sanctuary doors, but you felt such a great presence of God.
Everything was set for an atmosphere to receive and to have an expectancy for something great. I for one was excited and ready. The worship and music was definitely a win for me. It reached to my heart and soul and I honestly felt the presence of God overwhelm me. It is very few churches out there that help you feel the glory of God. I definitely felt the glory of God through worship. The amazing thing was that even when the Pastor brought his message, there was a flow from worship to his message. It coincided with his words. They were all in the same spirit.
The structure and the organization of the church was amazing. Everything has its time and its place. Everything was clean, the air was fresh, the people were surrendered to the spirit  and the presence was evident.
The same greeting and smiles you get when you walk in, is the same when you walk out, with a “God Loves you” and a “see you next Sunday”.
Not once did i feel judged, looked at or felt uncomfortable. I didn’t feel pressure during offering time. I didn’t feel alone and I felt like I was being heard. I existed. I felt at home.
Thank you Maranatha.

Fourth Presbyterian Church is a historic and influential church located in Chicago, Illinois. Situated on Michigan Avenue, it is a prominent landmark in the city and holds a significant place in Chicago's religious and architectural history.

The church was founded in 1871 and has since become one of the largest Presbyterian churches in the United States. The current building, constructed in the Gothic Revival style, was completed in 1914 and is known for its stunning architecture and intricate details.

Inside the church, visitors are greeted by beautiful stained glass windows, ornate woodwork, and a grand pipe organ. The sanctuary is awe-inspiring, with its high ceilings, intricate stone carvings, and a sense of reverence that fills the space.

Fourth Presbyterian Church is not only a place of worship but also a vibrant community hub. It offers a wide range of programs and activities for people of all ages and backgrounds. From worship services and Bible studies to social justice initiatives and community outreach programs, the church strives to make a positive impact in the lives of its members and the surrounding community.

The church's location on Michigan Avenue, also known as the Magnificent Mile, makes it easily accessible to both residents and tourists. It is surrounded by renowned cultural institutions, shopping destinations, and iconic landmarks, adding to its allure as a must-visit destination in Chicago.

Whether you are looking for a place to worship, explore architectural beauty, or engage in community activities, Fourth Presbyterian Church offers a welcoming and enriching experience. Its rich history, stunning architecture, and commitment to serving others make it a significant and cherished institution in the heart of Chicago.

reviews.text:
I spent five years in this church, and it remains the most painful experience of my spiritual life.
At first, it appeared loving and familial—but that “love” quickly revealed itself as conditional. The church teaches a works-based form of Christianity, asserting that salvation can be lost at any time. This directly contradicts the assurance of John 10:28: “I give them eternal life, and they shall never perish; no one will snatch them out of my hand.”

Leadership and Culture
The leadership is marked by hypocrisy and moral compromise, frequently condemning others’ sins while excusing their own, including adultery. As Jesus said in Matthew 7:5, “You hypocrite, first take the plank out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.” They manipulate Scripture to control rather than to heal—using the Bible as both sword and shield to justify pride and deflect accountability. Members are often belittled, intimidated, and silenced in the name of “discipleship,” a practice far removed from Ephesians 4:29’s call to “build others up according to their needs.”

Doctrine and Practices
Favoritism and double standards are widespread. The Holy Spirit’s guidance is routinely replaced with the opinions of “disciplers,” whose authority outweighs Christ’s commands. Services resemble motivational rallies more than reverent worship. As Colossians 2:8 warns, “See to it that no one takes you captive through hollow and deceptive philosophy, which depends on human tradition rather than on Christ.”

Finances and Family Values
Members are pressured to give financially far beyond their means, under the guise of “building churches,” though much of it seems to enrich leadership. Scripture cautions in 1 Timothy 6:10, “For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.” Even family duties are neglected, as members are urged to prioritize ministry over their loved ones—contrary to 1 Timothy 5:8, “Anyone who does not provide for their relatives...has denied the faith.”

Final Experience
When I finally left, leaders told me, “We don’t need you, we won’t miss you, and the church will move on without you.” That arrogance speaks volumes. Proverbs 16:18 reminds us, “Pride goes before destruction, a haughty spirit before a fall.”

Conclusion
Avoid this organization at all costs. It masquerades as a church but operates more like a cult, spiritually abusing and exploiting those who genuinely seek God. There are many Christ-centered congregations that truly love, disciple, and restore people in truth and grace. As Jesus warned in Matthew 7:15, “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves.”

reviews.text:
Over the past year, I’ve felt God opening my eyes and heart and opening doors for me to explore my faith.  I found Trinity Church in the Edgewater neighborhood of Chicago through a Google search.  I knew I wanted a nondenominational church that focused on biblically accurate teaching.

As I had not been in a church in the 27 years since leaving the Catholic church I grew up in, I was a little intimidated by the idea of walking into a completely new place where I didn’t know anyone. For the first few months I would attend by joining the online livestreams. I enjoyed pastor Matt’s heartfelt, inspirational, and motivating sermons. I was encouraged to join a small group, which seems odd considering I still had not attended church in person.

On the first day of that small group, I was warmly welcomed by pastor Matt and his family.  I was immediately put at ease, and I found everyone there to be so warm, friendly, and passionate about Jesus. I committed to attending the following Sunday in person at the church.

I don’t know why I waited so long. Everyone was beyond friendly, helpful, and genuinely interested in getting to know me and help me get back on track with following Jesus.   I was eventually baptized at Trinity Church on Easter Sunday, which I think was very special that it ocurred on that day.  I also completed the church’s Growth Track to become an official member of the church.

I’ve continued to attend Sundays and small groups each semester.  I have learned from and shared with so many amazing people here. The worship is incredible as well. There are a number of regular events the church hosts for you to be a part of the community - from volunteering to hot dog fundraisers to men’s and women’s retreats. Plenty of opportunities to fellowship with other believers.

Jesus, through using Trinity Church, has changed my life in so many positive ways. I really do love this place.

Like most people, I found Trinity Church Chicago by doing an online search. I thought I would finally leave my own review after 7 years. Overall, if you’re looking for a true, Jesus-seeking, Bible-teaching, non-denominational church in Chicago, I highly recommend checking out Trinity Church. No church is perfect, but Trinity seeks to follow Jesus unapologetically. It’s a church to call home, a church that will challenge you to grow, a church that is a deeper community, and a church that wants to welcome all but challenge everyone to live like Jesus.

If you’re looking for a church environment where you can slip in and slip out unnoticed every week, you won’t find that at Trinity. You can maybe manage that for a few weeks if you purposefully avoid eye contact with people, but eventually someone will get your attention and want to welcome you into conversation. Give in! You will love the community here. I still remember the first person I met when I walked in the door 7 years ago. (Thanks, Dom!) Also, I met my wife at Trinity, got married at Trinity, experienced many of life’s ups and downs with the community here, and I made many lifelong friends at Trinity. I’m so glad I found this church. Please visit in person if you’re interested in finding a Chicago church!

Trinity is also a charismatic church, if that is something that you’re looking for. If you’re not sure what that means exactly in the church context, don’t let that keep you away, just ask the pastor or one of the church members and they’d be happy to explain what they mean by charismatic.

Finding a place of worship where one feels truly welcomed and loved can be a daunting task, but my experience at New Life Norwood Park [NLNP] has been nothing short of heartwarming and fulfilling. From the moment I walked through the doors, I was greeted with genuine smiles and open arms.

The sense of community at NLNP is palpable. The congregation is diverse, spanning all ages and backgrounds, yet everyone is united by a common spirit of kindness and acceptance. The warmth extends beyond the weekly services; it’s evident in the numerous fellowship events, support groups, and community outreach programs the church offers.

One of the standout features of NLNP is its leadership. The pastoral team is not only deeply knowledgeable and passionate about their faith, but they also make it a point to connect with each member personally. Their sermons are thought-provoking, relevant, and delivered with a heartfelt sincerity that resonates with everyone in attendance.

The worship experience at NLNP is both uplifting and inclusive. The music is a beautiful blend of older Christian contemporary worship songs, and newer ones, ensuring that there is something for everyone. The atmosphere during services is one of reverence and joy, encouraging both reflection and active participation.

Moreover, New Life community church is dedicated to serving the broader community. Their outreach programs are extensive, addressing local needs through food drives, clothing donations, and various support services. This commitment to social justice and compassion is inspiring and exemplifies the church’s mission to be a beacon of hope and love.

In conclusion, NLNP is more than just a place of worship; it is a family. Whether you are a lifelong believer or someone exploring your faith, you will find a welcoming and loving environment here. My experience has been overwhelmingly positive, and I would highly recommend NLNP to anyone seeking a nurturing spiritual home. reviews.text:
My family and I have been part of this church for over 30 years. I started attending as a teenager with my parents and brother, and this church has played a huge role in my spiritual growth and my walk with Christ Jesus.

My wife and I were also blessed to raise our children here. The Sunday School program for children and youth is well organized and has provided a strong foundation for them. The pastor’s Bible teaching is very in-depth but easy to understand—it honestly feels like a Bible school experience that helps you apply Scripture to everyday life.

What really stands out is how much the pastor and his wife genuinely care about each person’s spiritual and personal growth. I’ll never forget when the pastor visited our home while I was a teenager and personally took the time to explain the importance of accepting Jesus Christ, making sure I understood and made that decision that same night. That kind of care and commitment has stayed with me ever since.

The church community is warm, loving, and welcoming. There are weekly services, meetings, and activities for both adults and youth, and the weekly prayer line is especially meaningful. It’s a place where people truly support one another and faithfully pray together.

Spiritual growth is ultimately a personal responsibility, but I’m very grateful for the many opportunities this church has provided for our family to grow in faith and raise our children in a Christ-centered environment. If you’re new to the Chicago area or looking for a church where your family can truly feel at home, I highly recommend visiting a service.

I’ve had a really disappointing experience with this church. It feels more like a place for show than a place for spiritual growth. A lot of people seem more focused on being on stage or showing off their money than actually living out the Word of God.

There’s a lot of gossip, criticism, and backbiting. It’s hard to feel supported or loved here. People are treated differently based on how much money they have, those with more are respected, and others often get looked down on.

What’s worse is the church feels very controlled. Pastor John and some of his family run everything, and that creates a tense, closed-off environment. It doesn’t feel open or welcoming.

I really hoped for a community that’s humble, kind, and centered on Christ but sadly, this church isn’t that. I don’t recommend it to anyone looking for real spiritual growth or genuine fellowship.

reviews.text:
Hope is usually in the future, something you look forward to or desire in front of you. It’s a picture or an image of a desired future; a picture of a future accomplishment, possession or fulfilment. Faith, however, is the essence of hope. In other words, until you hope, that image or picture has no life. That's why hope is so important.

Hope is powerful. When people become hopeless, they could give up, and die. But once you have hope, then the thing you’re hoping for suddenly becomes a possibility; you see that it exists.

Hope is like *“potential energy”;* which means it’s a possibility that could be realized if you could *“look”* at it with your spirit, because that's when it becomes real. This is why hope must translate to faith for it to produce results. With hope, you see the blessings that could result from acting on God’s Word. But with faith, you take possession, you walk in the blessing. Hallelujah!

Temple Head Start was the start of both of my children’s education. Both have graduated a long time ago.

My son is now 26, graduated from Western Illinois University with a degree in Mechanical Engineering with a GPA 3.6, and now is a Engineering Manager at Wahl’s Clipper Corporation.

My son was born prematurely 3 months early. The staff was wonderful with him and he never missed a beat. The doctors said he would never thrive with his class but with the help of Temple Head Start we made sure he thrived with his class!

My Daughter is now 20, a student at Howard University majoring in Media Broadcasting Journalism with a GPA 4.0. My daughter was 2 months prematurely. Like my son they said she would not thrive with her class. Again with the help of Temple Head Start we made sure she thrives with her class.

I want to give thanks to the entire staff from 1998 - 2008. I truly appreciate you all.

If you are looking for a head start for your child where the staff loves and cares for your child as if they are their own. Then stop looking because you have found your head start program Salvation Army Temple Head Start!!!

reviews.text:
My family and I started going to The House about 5 years ago in a really big scary transitional time for us. More than anything at that time we were yearning for a home, a community, a place where we could be at the table with Jesus and His people and know that we were loved. I mean this with all my heart: The House has been exactly this.

My favorite things about our church family are the clear love for the Rock Island community (and active volunteerism and prayer within said community), the prioritization of justice and equality amongst all God’s people, the way we frequently dive into biblical exegesis in sermons, and the passion for worship that I think shows in our worship team as well as our congregation. Nobody worships in exactly same way, but there’s no pressure to do so here: I have always felt like I can come before God and this church as exactly who I am, with all my quirks and questions. We challenge each other to grow, change, and learn more about how God calls us to live, but we do not judge one another.

If you’re looking for a church home, come hang out with these people. Come worship, come pray, come learn with us! You have a place here, you have a seat at the table.

I have been attending The House for about a year and have been so blessed in my walk with the Lord. The praise music is great, fellowship with others is welcoming, and the messages are based on God’s word! Everyone there made me feel at home when I was a newbie!!! If you want to find a church home where you will be led to be a “Jesus Follower” come check out The House❤️✝️❤️

This is a Church that models, authentic spirit lead teaching and worship. The focus is following The Way, and knowing Jesus more rather than some façade of religiosity. I have been attending intermittently for several months and though I find the atmosphere stretching at times, The Word and worship are always brought forth in love and truth… the church is diverse and welcoming yet small compared to where I have been for years. This is a place worth visiting!

My girls and I have been a part of The House from the beginning, and it’s been such a wonderful community for us. We have been through big changes over the years as a family, and this church fam has been pivotal in the healing and growing process. I appreciate the warm & welcoming environment so much, especially in a world that has excluded so many beautiful souls.

My wife and I visited several churches in the area before finding The House. We’ve now been going there for over 5 years, and would highly recommend checking it out! It’s a church community that is truly welcome to all, and the music, messages and opportunities to serve and grow in your faith are impressive for a church its size.

reviews.text: This chapel constitutes one of the great neogothic buildings in the United States and one of the last great examples of the style before a mix of Depression financial problems and changing trends in architecture led to the abandonment of this style, unfortunately. I will try not to be too elegiac and instead simply say that structures like these elevate the spirit, with their lavish artistry and deep reverence. They are buildings that call the individual out of mundane routine and force a heightened awareness of space and movement through space. The tower is the equal of most any in Europe, and people will still be admiring it centuries in the future.

The majestic Rockefeller Memorial Chapel, at 200 feet, is the tallest building at the University of Chicago. The lavender garden is beautiful as are the many wood and stone carvings and the intricate ceiling. Come hear one of the largest carillons in the world.

The chapel's serene atmosphere promotes introspection and reflection. Whether attending a religious service, a wedding, or simply seeking a peaceful escape, the Rockefeller Chapel offers a sanctuary of tranquility in the bustling city.

In my visits and in what they openly share online, I witnessed things that are deeply concerning for a Catholic parish: individuals who were not Catholic being invited to receive Holy Communion, parish representatives promoting views that conflict with Catholic teaching, and public honors given to politicians whose positions are strongly opposed to the Catholic faith.

As someone seeking an authentically Catholic parish, I was saddened that Old St. Pat’s does not uphold the reverence, orthodoxy, or clarity of teaching I expect in the Church. This left me with the impression that the community prioritizes fitting into cultural trends rather than maintaining fidelity to Catholic doctrine.

Holy Covenant is exactly what worship should be. It's exciting, dynamic, inclusive, friendly, charming, uplifting, diverse, messy, flexible, warm

Growing up Catholic shaped the way I viewed religion/Christianity for a very long time. Upon moving to Chicago from Michigan (and starting a "new life") I began looking for a church that was GLBT inclusive. For some reason I never found Holy Covenant and after a few attempts. There are many progressive and inclusive churches in Chicago, but not one that I felt truly connected with.

In January of 2009, at the recommendation of a friend, I walked into Holy Covenant as Pastor Trey Hall was preaching on Christianity and Homosexuality. I had invited a friend of mine who was running late. I decided to head in, terrified of sitting by myself and waiting for him. I was warmly greeted by a woman and her husband who quickly identified that I was new. They weren't overwhelming but made sure I knew everything I needed to know and also introduced me to a few people. While terrifying at first, this first impression proved to be lasting. I would be lying if I said I wasn't immediately connected to this community. I felt overwhelmed but joyous at the possibility of worshipping in a community like Holy Covenant. The music was a perfect blend of traditional and contemporary and Pastor Hall was terrific. The space is quaint and charming while still feeling very much like "church." I left that day feeling as if my life had changed, cliché or not.

Over the next 6 months, my attendance increased and I began finding myself feeling as if I was missing something on a Sunday I didn't attend. In July of 2009, Holy Covenant welcomed Pastor Kate Floyd to the community. She is absolutely wonderful and has taken the reigns in perfect fashion. In September I approached Pastor Kate about joining the church and becoming a United Methodist. I completed that journey on October 18, 2009 and have never felt more excited to be a part of a faith community.

Holy Covenant offers 3 services. The 9:30 and 11:15 are more traditional services with contemporary music, while the 7pm is all acoustic, candlelit and contemplative filled with traditional hymns. They have endless small groups and ways for members to feel connected to the church. They are very active in promoting justice and equality and also house Dignity Diner, a restaurant-style dinner night for the homeless and hungry.

Holy Covenant has changed my life, something many people at HC say. If you're looking for a hip church that is socially active and filled with amazing people...this is your place.

⭐☆☆☆☆ Honest Experience at Fallbrook Church

I visited Fallbrook Church for a few weeks hoping to find a good church home for my family, but my experience wasn’t what I expected.

On my first visit, I tried to greet a choir member and ask where the children’s church was, but they walked right past me and didn’t respond. It felt uncomfortable and not very welcoming, especially for a first-time guest.

A few days later, I got a call from Minister Tardy about marital counseling. My husband and I went, but from the start, the conversation felt judgmental. She made personal comments about how many children I have and even said we shouldn’t have any more. That was hard to hear — especially in a setting that’s supposed to offer support and understanding.

When we went back another time, she seemed distracted and unprepared, watching a video and telling us to “go downstairs” because she didn’t think we were showing up. It felt like our time and situation weren’t taken seriously.

Then, during a Wednesday family night check-out, a lady named Nettaya Keeton almost refused to give me my child and took a photo of my ID because one of my kids didn’t have a sticker. I understand safety policies, but the way it was handled felt harsh and unprofessional.

I’ve felt increasingly frustrated and disappointed with my recent experiences at this church. My first visit was truly encouraging, Pastor Abe delivered a powerful message in person, and it left a strong impression. However, my second visit, which happened to be on Easter weekend, was quite the opposite. Instead of a live sermon, a large screen was lowered, and the service was broadcast remotely.

This was especially disheartening because I had brought a guest with me, having spoken highly of the previous week’s service. Unfortunately, the following two services were the same, sermons projected on a screen. 1 live sermon out of 4 Sundays attended in a row.

If the intention is to offer a remote experience, it defeats the purpose of physically attending. Watching a service on a screen in a church building feels no different than watching from home, just with added commute and inconvenience.

Additionally, I was disappointed to learn that although the church advertises a singles group, there doesn’t appear to be an active group available. This was another area of interest for me, and the lack of follow-through was discouraging.

I hope the church takes these concerns into consideration and works toward offering more consistent live teaching and reliable, accessible ministries for the community

All praises to the Most High! I’m sharing this review and testimony because God’s people are being misled, and I feel it's important to speak up. It’s easy to testify in church, where everyone already has some idea of how good God is, but this review is for those who are seeking Him and don’t know where to turn.

As many churches as I’ve joined and left, I’ve never seen the body of Christ turn from God at the rate we’re seeing now. I couldn’t take anymore prosperity preaching because I knew my life wasn’t right. These churches prosperity preached me to a point of confusion. I was asking God “where were my good things?” Joining this church taught me that if God woke you up that morning that in itself was your good thing. If you’re looking for a church home that is chasing after God with everything they’ve got—not trying to please the congregation or put on a show—then this is the place for you! I came to this church thinking I was a “baby Christian,” but honestly, I can’t even call myself that. I thought I knew God, but the truth is, I really didn’t. I’d leave church feeling convicted and empowered at the same time because the Word is revealed—just the Word.

I was raised in a Christian home, going to church Sunday through Saturday, and though I had a lot of experience in church, I didn’t realize I wasn’t actually walking with God. I was just going through the motions, pretending to be a Christian, but not living the true life of one. Joining this church completely changed my perspective. It helped me see what true Christianity is all about and showed me the right path to Jesus.

For anyone out there truly seeking God, this is the church for you. They preach straight from the Bible, not their own opinions, and they let the Word speak for itself. There’s no performance here, no fluff—just the real thing. It’s refreshing to be part of a church that’s serious about their mission and committed to living out God’s Word.

I mention that I’m a born and raised American because some might feel out of place or discouraged, but don’t let that hold you back from receiving the Good Word. We are all working pieces of God, and no matter where we come from, we need good shepherds to guide us. This church is exactly that—shepherds who are leading us toward Jesus.

To God be the glory! I pray this review reaches those who are truly seeking Him and know deep down they need a Father who will never leave nor forsake them.

P.S. Don’t let circumstances or situations discourage your walk. Remember, the people in church aren’t Jesus Himself. Have grace and pray through it. Keep going!

During a time filled with tragedy and unimaginable sadness, St. Paul AME Church stood as a beacon of comfort and love for our family. I am profoundly grateful to Ms. Betty, whose kindness and readiness to assist us went above and beyond. When we unexpectedly visited to plan the funeral, she opened the church doors, allowing family members who weren’t members themselves to feel the welcoming spirit and assurance that it was the perfect place for our loved one’s homegoing celebration.

A special thank you to Pastor Dawson, whose presence and warm smile provided a glimmer of hope in our darkest hour. The entire church, from the beautifully maintained facility that welcomed us without rush, to the media team that prepared everything, and the facilities crew who made sure we stayed cool in Houston’s heat, showed us nothing but patience and grace.

The parking team also deserves a mention for making access so effortless, which was a huge help to us during such a stressful time. The dove release was a beautiful touch, perfectly executed by the church, encapsulating the love and care we wanted to honor our loved one with.

To everyone at St. Paul Church - thank you from the bottom of our hearts. You have made an indelible impact on our lives during this difficult moment. And I want the world to know that at Green's Point, it’s truly God’s point. Thank you, thank you, thank you.

I’m writing this with a heavy heart. My wife and I have been attending Grace Church in Southeast Houston for some time now. We’ve supported the church, given our tithes, and truly believed it was a place where everyone was welcome — a place where God’s love was shared without judgment.

Recently, my wife simply asked for a prayer request — for her wife. Instead of compassion, she was met with rudeness and rejection. The person she spoke to was extremely disrespectful and unkind because of our marriage. It was a moment that shattered something inside us.

We walked into Grace Church believing we were part of a family. We walked out feeling humiliated and heartbroken. God’s love is for everyone, no matter who they are or who they love. To be treated as less than in a place that preaches love and grace is devastating.

We’re not sharing this to attack anyone — we’re sharing it because we believe people deserve to know. Churches should be a safe place for all, especially for those seeking prayer, healing, and connection with God. No one should ever be made to feel unwelcome in His house

Our hearts are broken, but our faith remains. We still believe in a loving God who embraces all His children. We just hope this opens hearts and eyes within the church community — because love, not judgment, is what truly changes lives.

With deep sadness and hope for change,
Celeste Baldwin

I've been challenged to grow, to think differently, and to find a deeper purpose in my work and relationships. This church has truly been instrumental in helping me navigate some of the toughest seasons of my life. This has been weighing on my heart to discuss. When I was in high school, I volunteered for all three services in the children’s ministry, and I volunteered once at VBS too. Last year, I was going through personal hardships while also being unemployed from August 2024-April 2025.  I used up all my savings and had no luck with any employment opportunities. I even sold my salvaged car to help make ends meet and lost a lot of personal belongings due to a mold infestation in my apartment that my renters insurance refused to cover. I applied for One Need and opened up about everything I was struggling with, and I asked for rental assistance for one month (I also struggled with government assistance as I am not a veteran or mother). I was asked by the person on the other line if I was a member and I said I wasn’t sure. I’ve been going since I was young and I just felt that I belonged so I don’t know if my mom registered me or not. I hadn’t heard back so I reached out to the director of the program and I was told that my need was not “alerted”, whatever that means. Nobody reached out to me to tell me no, and I wasn’t even given referrals to other churches or programs that could help me. Though I haven’t given monetary value, I have volunteered many hours for children’s programs here and I thought that my commitment and devotion would have at least given me the opportunity for guidance/referrals. I’ve been struggling with religion as of late and I feel like me being deemed unworthy of help only makes it harder for me to find comfort in a church. I thought/hoped that maybe I deserved the decency of compassion and redirection. I don’t know if I was denied because I was possibly listed as a non-member, but I believe God would want everyone to treat their neighbors with kindness. I ended up getting some help from a Catholic Church (St. Vincent du Paul) instead where three ladies came to my apartment, heard my story, shed tears with me, prayed over me, and left me with a small goodie bag as well as a check they provided to my apartment complex. Maybe I’m just not meant to go back to the met.

I must take a few moments to address Loralee.  I am so sorry that you came by at such a time that financial assistance was not available. I have personally been at the church offices during office hours for over six years. We have help many poor souls. When our funds were low, I have taken money out of my own wallet to help some one along. We are a charitable organization that depends upon the generosity of our members to give. Many folks believe that a large church building equates to constant supply of money...sadly not true.
After hurricane's Rita and Katrina, we "gave" free gas cards, food, clothing, household items...and yes, occasionally money.
Currently, we distribute food and clothing to underprivileged families in an entire apartment project close by. We distribute free food to "at risk" children in several of our community elementary schools. We have paid house notes, electrical bills, car notes and medical expenses for many families. We do not have an unending supply of funds at our disposal {would that we did :-) }.
Concerning your car...for many years we conducted a ministry to single women called "Car Clinic" which involved men volunteers from our church providing free automobile maintenance on  a regular basis.
Reluctantly, we must admit that we are unable to meet every need that enters our doors, but it is our utmost desire to continually do more. I pray God protected you and brought you to a place of safety.

reviews.text:
Today was my 3rd visit to City Life Church.
I am new in pursuing a relationship with God. I was raised in the church but never practiced. First off, the atmosphere is so welcoming and there is so much diversity, it just feels like home. The pastor was not preaching that day but the gentleman who gave the message spoke about Leah and I truly resonated with that. After the service I went to the front and weeped to one of the women and she prayed over me. My life has never been the same since I left that day. I still struggle with my relationship with God but I actually understand the Bible now. God is working through me because of City Life church. I highly recommend this church. You are also struck by the incredible diversity present. Everywhere you look you see people who come from different ethnic, socio-economic, and cultural backgrounds that are simultaneously celebrating their differences and striving and experiencing unity together. If you are looking for a church do yourself a favor and come visit City Life Church.

reviews.text: I remember visiting this church circa 2017 or 2018 or maybe 2019. There were maybe fifteen people in attendance. Two of us were visiting, we both stood at the call for first time guests. The pastor said thank you for coming and to I want to pray for ya’ll, she walked up to the other guest but didn’t approach me. Odd and performative. I should have walk out at that moment but I sat through the rest of the sermon. At the end of the service the person ushering, a sweet girl was trying to stall me as I was walking out. She told me the pastor usually speaks to our visitors after church welcoming them. She signaled the pastor to us as she was talking to the other guest. The usher continued to small talk and the pastor looked our way and then turned her back to slowly greet another family. Signaling she had no intention of speaking with me. The poor usher tried she apologized for “Shepard” of the church getting “caught up” which was really intentional. Remember there were twelve members in attendance, I counted. She dismissed and excluded me on purpose. The usher thank me for coming and invited me back. That would be an absolutely not! Thank God for protecting evil hand laying. Here it is 2026 I never thought I would still think of this negative feeling leaving a church but it was so distinct. It’s been years since I lived in the state. The feelings never go away. You never know what’s behind the veil of the pool pit. And as far as women pastoring…true nature is always revealed, jealousy is an illness that must be cut off at the root. As a women I always gravitate to women as leaders especially in spiritual matters but that day made me reconsider 1 Timothy 2:12. There are many reasons why God only lets some tend to a small flock because others could be led astray. Others like one who walks in to a “sanctuary” with a generous spirit and years of service looking for a new home to devote to but took her blessings right out of the door. I will say the worship leader was anointed an amazing singer and drummer. Peach and blessings to you all in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ who is coming back soon.

More than 100 INTERNATIONAL ADULTS come to practice and improve their CONVERSATIONAL ENGLISH in classes throughout the week, from BEGINNER to ADVANCED.

I’ve been going to this church for about 6 years.  There are two campuses:  Crosspoint and WestU.  I go to the WestU campus. This church also has a fantastic MISSIONS PROGRAM, here in Houston and Internationally.  In addition to the ESL classes and ESL Bible studies in Houston, the church offers many different types of International mission trips every year.  The church has helped start other churches Internationally and partners with Christian churches and organizations in other countries.  Here at home, West University Baptist Church deployed many church volunteers after hurricane Harvey to anyone who signed up, saying they needed help with house clean up.  The church also has several houses where families can stay when they travel to Houston for Cancer treatment.  Church volunteers pray with them and often provides food and visits. reviews.text: My husband and I were in search of a church where we could nurture our little one and she could grow up in a community that aligns with our values. The worship experience is wonderful and refreshing, and Ministry and a Meal is such a unique approach to Bible Study. I always look forward to coming to church here!

If you're searching for a church that truly immerses you in the teachings of the Bible, look no further than the R.O.C.K. Church! Under the guidance of Dr. Dana Carson, a master wordsmith and inspiring leader, this faith community has transformed my life and the lives of my entire family.

From the moment you step through the doors, you'll feel welcomed and embraced by the warmth of the congregation. Dr. Carson's powerful, insightful sermons will challenge you to deepen your understanding of Scripture and apply its timeless truths to your daily life. His unique ability to break down complex concepts and make them accessible to all has helped me grow in my faith and connect with God on a profound level.

The R.O.C.K. Church offers a wide range of ministries, programs, and events that cater to people of all ages and backgrounds. You'll find countless opportunities for spiritual growth, connection, and fellowship, all centered around the transformative power of God's Word.

I can't recommend the R.O.C.K. Church highly enough! If you're seeking a faith community that will support you on your spiritual journey, encourage you to ask tough questions, and inspire you to live a life rooted in Biblical teachings, this is the place for you. Come and experience the difference that Dr. Carson and the R.O.C.K. Church can make in your life!

The people were very welcoming and helped me get situated into the environment because it was my first time participating in an Orthodox liturgy. The Icons were beautifully painted and the use of TVs to help dictate the liturgy was a great help. I hope more African Americans will come to embrace Orthdoxy and grow closer to our Christian and African brother and sister in the Ethiopian Orthodox Church.

reviews.text:
The history of this beautiful house of worship alone was awe inspiring, but the actual house and grounds were so beautiful. As an African American, I felt a sense of pride and of reverence for the brothers and sisters who gave their lives so that I could have an opportunity to live in peace and equity in this country that promised it to all citizens.
The fact that the site survives and thrives warms my heart.
I purpose in my heart to return for an actual worship service.

Been following church service since April, had the opportunity to visit in person for the first time today- overwhelmed by everything, Reverend Warnock incredible sermon as always, the music impeccable so uplifting, and the staff and parishioners truly and sincerely welcoming. Many blessings to all at Ebenezer our new church. 🙏

I visited the center several years ago and remember sitting in the pews listening to one of Dr. King’s recorded sermons—it was incredibly moving. On this visit, I had the opportunity to attend a formal presentation that shared the history of the church, the five pastors who have led the congregation, and Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s connection to this sacred place.

The park ranger who delivered the presentation was exceptionally knowledgeable and engaging. His passion for the history was clear, and we truly soaked in every detail he shared. The presentation added depth and context to a space that already carries so much meaning and significance.

Overall, it was an excellent and enriching experience that I would highly recommend. Note: Presentations are offered at specific times, so plan ahead. We attended the first session at 11:00 a.m., and it was well worth it.
This was a great experience to actually see and to learn as I found out things I needed to learn it made me feel good to be here

I had an opportunity to serve the “Ebenezer Everywhere” family as a Minstrel for their Mother’s Day celebration and, as always, it’s a distinct honor serving their house of worship. During this bout ministry support, I was especially privileged to experience the exceptional ministry of a legendary trailblazer for women in Ministry—Bishop Vashti McKinsey and also meet her in person! It was humbling to meet one of my personal heroes of the Black Church—one I had only read about and studied in books—while also serving the same hallowed ministry where Dr. Martin Luther King and his father once served, and where the current sitting U.S. Senator of Georgia also pastors. This was a powerful, intersecting moment for me and one I will never forget. 🙏🏾

reviews.text: Went to a concert last night in Grand prairie. There was a time when churches were known for humility and service. Passion City, for all its lights and lasers, feels more like a marketing agency than a movement of faith. The message of Jesus has been replaced by motivational speeches wrapped in LED screens. It’s performance-driven worship — high on emotion, low on introspection.

The music is flawless, the production stunning, and yet somehow, it feels hollow. The sermons often circle back to the same talking points — inspiration without confrontation, hope without repentance. The focus on celebrity pastors, book deals, and social media virality blurs the line between ministry and branding.

People come searching for peace, but too often, they find production. They come thirsty, but the water feels filtered through sponsorship.

Faith doesn’t need a fog machine. It needs authenticity.

My favorite church is a place where people of all races can attend comfortably. The teachings focus solely on Jesus, and there are many opportunities for Bible study. It also offers various programs tailored to different age groups. This is the church I love the most.❤️

reviews.text:
This was my first time visiting Victory, and overall, I really enjoyed myself. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and I could definitely feel a strong sense of community among the members. The message was inspiring, and the worship experience was uplifting — I can tell this is a place that truly values faith and connection.

I didn’t realize that children aren’t allowed in the main sanctuary, so my son and I were directed to the family sanctuary instead. He usually does very well during services at other churches we’ve attended, so it caught me a little off guard. One usher came across a bit rude when I opened the door after service had already begun, telling me I needed to go to the chapel. Thankfully, another usher took the time to kindly explain how Victory operates when it comes to families and where we could sit together. I really appreciated that clarification and their understanding.

Despite that small misunderstanding, I still had a great experience and felt spiritually encouraged. I definitely plan to visit again — now that I understand the setup better, I’m looking forward to being able to enjoy the service more fully next time.

Online service, in person, community involvement, small groups, vibrant youth ministry, and soooooo much more. Victory has been my home  church for 10 years, and I couldn’t imagine my life without the community of Victory - Norcross

Love My church Family been here for seven years when I was homeless 2017 victory took me and my two boys in, one with autism and God is so amazing when placing me here he already knew that they had a sensory room for Special Needs. If you seeking a church home, that’s a welcoming home. This is it.

I've observed a profound spiritual disconnect, particularly within the leadership. This absence is disappointing and creates a sense of spiritual emptiness. It often feels like the rules, the efficiency, and the organizational metrics have taken precedence over genuine empathy, compassion, and the actual spiritual nourishment the congregation needs.

reviews.text:

name: Second-Ponce de Leon Baptist Church

reviews.text: I visited one time, and I felt very welcome. I grew up in Atlanta and attended a moderate Baptist church. I get the impression that "all are welcome", but it's not their entire personality. They seem to have lots of events for youth and kids. We will be returning. I am leaving a review because I did not know where to begin to find the kind of church we were looking for, and visiting all the churches in our area seemed daunting. If you grew up in a middle of the road protestant church with a great youth group or you are new to church, I'd give it a try. It seems to be good for families. They also send a devotional email that I find uplifting.

Wonderful worship experience. Friendly people. My beloved traditional worship style, complete with choral music (if you’re weary of shallow contemporary Christian music). You will not be disappointed.

This church has maintained a tradition of excellence in music and worship for a long time.  The senior pastor and the associate pastors are all excellent preachers.  The music is always done well and is an integral part of worship.  The 11 AM service on Sundays is a traditional service.  This service is streamed live and you can also watch it on YouTube.  There is also have a new, more contemporary service at 4 PM on Sundays.  This service attracts a diverse group that includes students and young adults.

This church has always reminded me of the small-town church I grew up in.  Everyone is welcomed and cared for.  A great place to worship and grow.

Great community support based on their commitment to their faith.

Second-Ponce has been rooted as more traditional Baptist Church belonging to both the southern baptist and Cooperative Baptist Fellowship. The 11:00 is a more traditional service with a great music program. They also have a more relaxed service with a band on Sunday afternoon. They have a live stream for those who want to "tele-worship."

They have a number of community outreach programs but I am particular impressed with their efforts to help others that are not of their faith like the hungry, homeless and underprivileged.

They do great work with youth. Like many churches, they have a preschool and kids programs around worship. They also reach out to the youth of other communities. They are very supportive of Garden Hills elementary by supplying people and equipment for things like the school festival as well as helping to upgrade the playground. They have a mission program that makes a real difference in the community of underprivileged children in Miami.

I applaud them for being clear that their actions aren't just about being "good people" but are a reflection of a commitment to knowing Christ and doing his work.

The  presence of the Holy Spirit was felt in this church. I was a visitor from Ohio and I felt welcomed.   Rob was the Sunday school leader, very interesting and easy to follow.  The Choir and orchestra was fantastic.  Historical Church and very well kept, you can tell the members really appreciate their time together.  Expect a huge welcome.

reviews.text: My daughter's and son got baptized, 4 person praise and worship tore it down I almost jumped in the water. God gets the glory that place is full of the spirit of God. 18-26 year old praising God in a great way, great guidance, awesome, and excited about the word of God.
First time this past Sunday. The Spirit of God was definitely in the house. People actually speak to you🥲my babies and I felt welcomed. Thinking of visiting again
I met a friend that attends. It was a beautiful Worship service and the Word by the Choir Director/ Minister was just what I needed. I will definitely be back again soon.

Today was the first day that I attended service at the faith center. I was supposed to be visiting this church along with 2 others over the course of the next 3 weeks. Well, i have to admit that after coming today in my heart, soul, and spirit, i feel like i found a new church home.
I have been praying and asking God to lead me toward what i needed while i am in the process of getting my life and my family back on track. The faith center had been coming up on my timeline for about a month, and last night, i finally made a plan to go in person.
From the moment i touched the parking lot, i felt welcomed, i felt genuine kindness, heartfelt assitance, and just peaceful. As i was walking in the door, i was greeted with hugs ((literally)). I advised the usher that it was my first time. She stopped what she was doing and walked my children and I to the information desk, and from there, it was just a blessing.
My 9 year old wanted to go to the children's center. He wasn't too happy when i picked him up only because he was grouped with younger kids. He wanted to be with children his age, but i think because of his height, maybe they thought he was younger. He wants to go back and try again. So that was good to hear. He also felt comfortable being able to wear what he wanted to. Ive always taught my children that Jesus says come as you are. In every sense of the phrase.
My teenage daughter sat with me in the main sanctuary, although they had a group for teens she wanted to stay with me. I am glad she did. She was taking notes and was fully engaged.
The choir was awesome, and the sermmon that was preched was truly a WORD. I will definitely be back with the rest of my family. I feel blessed to testify that i feel like I have found my church home❤️

I love my ministry. I have been a member for less than a year and so thankful my Heavenly Father sent me here. I am home… ☺️. I see and feel the anointing in the atmosphere. He gives back to the community. Just come and visit. You will not be the same. You will have alonging to come back. I promise you. God bless.

My daughter LOVES attending here regularly and I feel comforted knowing she's in good hands with God and his people here while I serve on the other side of town. Thanks ACC!

We look forward to more visits in the future when we are in town.   Thank you to everyone at ACC.

Sermons are packed with knowledge and truth, but delivered in a way where you feel like you're just grabbing coffee with a friend. I have attended this church off and on for about 20yrs have attended conferences women’s trips etc. I have truly been blessed and in the past 6years the Founders Theodore McNair and his wife Anna McNair have passed on to the glory of God, however their children have taken over the leadership and have really elevated this church. Members of this church are very friendly and welcoming to guests. The pastor even offers a full breakfast to visitors on their next visit to sit eat and fellowship w/him.

Pastor Theo McNair Jr and his wife First Lady Octavia McNair are wonderful people of God and even though I’m not an official member, due to fact that I don’t live in Atlanta full time,  I consider myself an honorary one, b/c I have attended for so long throughout the last 20 years and plus my mom is a member of this church. Their praise team is amazing I love Courtney who usually sings lead her voice alone delights my spirit and lifts me. If your are visiting in the Southwest Atlanta area around or live in ATL I recommend this church if you believe in the WORD of God, this is where you should be or at least visit. You won’t regret it.

formatted_address: 1580 Peachtree St NE, Atlanta, GA 30309, United States
name: Peachtree Christian Church

reviews.text:
Peachtree Christian Church was the perfect venue for my wedding ceremony! The church is stunning, reverent, and needed very little decoration on our part. There is much history in this church. It was such an honor to be wed here.

Sylvie, the wedding coordinator, made everything go so smoothly that my wedding planner didn’t even need to be there and could focus on setting up my reception. She and her team have done many, many weddings and have it down to a science. They are so kind and were a pleasure to work with!

The organ and talented organist is something I will never forget. Just fantastic beyond words.

If you want a classic, traditional, timeless wedding, Peachtree Christian Church is the place!

I have had the honor of photographing several weddings at the HISTORIC Peachtree Christian Church and it is simply breathtaking!  The staff and clergy are so very kind and it is a stunning church for a wedding ceremony.  Understanding and abiding by the Church's decorum is a must.

As a pastor, I have the opportunity to do funerals all over the state of Georgia. Peachtree Christian Church is one of the most beautiful sanctuaries to host, and in my case, officiate a wedding. The pastors and staff at the church are very kind and organized people. I highly recommend anyone considering getting married in Atlanta and looking at venuesto go tour Peachtree Christian Church. An absolutely wonderful place.
photographed a wedding here and it was gorgeous! great staff as well!

Peachtree Christian Church is absolutely gorgeous! With the beauty of the stained glass, organ pipes, and ornate architecture there is not any need for decorations. The church staff is also great, Sylvie Lansdowne the wedding coordinator, Reverend Gignilliat, and the organist helped make my daughter's wedding day wonderful. Highly recommend!

reviews.text: This is the most holy spirit left church I have ever been to. This isn't just a show up on Sunday kinda church. They offer a wide variety of outside ministries to meet every need, including a healthy network of independent house churches! This church encourages the congregation to be active, just like the early church in the book of acts. Back when church wasn't a time and place, it was a thing you did. Come grasp the next phase in the life God has planned for you with your brothers and sisters in Christ here at Grace

Great church with super welcoming community. Lost of young people and families. All the pastors are great speakers. They also get into the history of the scripture which, has a history buff, I appreciate. Their faith is strong!
My first time here for the Maverick City gathering of worship. Great experience

Cute church with great worship. We were in town visiting for an event at a local all girls college. Our daughter suggested we go to Midtown for service this morning. The service was good but I was taken aback by the fact that no one greeted us. There didn’t seem to be any way to connect. If there were, we were not informed. The message was about the Good Shepherd and was pretty good. The worship was awesome. I just wished we would have felt more welcomed.

I’ve been looking for a new church and a girlfriend invited me to Grace.  It had easy/free parking, short walk to church, intimate/small community, free coffee which they serve in real mugs, music was unreal.  Things I felt could have been better - sermon didn’t feel well prepared, went over an hour (that’s the Catholic in me).  There’s no such thing as a perfect church meaning a church that has everything a person wants but overall, I will definitely go back.  Music is the most important thing to me and this place was phenomenal. From the voices to the audience set up around the stage to less common songs - highly recommend giving them a shot! Young crowd and not a ton of kids.

reviews.text:
Wonderful church Family. We were Blessed by being there this morning.

A big Shout Out to Mrs. Johnson, such a sweet lady. Dr. Heyward fed us a great Spitual meal this morning.

Casual clean appropriate dress seems normal and acceptable. I can imagine some old school members back in Albany speaking on apparel (Deep South vs. Big City). Media, sound, atmosphere, cleanliness, space, gym, kitchen, restrooms, classrooms, gym etc. this Church has all the amenities you can think of. The Pastor’s voice sounds extremely strong when he’s preaching with vigor sharp enough to move you. They didn’t ask visitors to stand and say anything or give ur audio of the message, although the leadership did verbally  acknowledge visitors. A lot of youth and Seasoned Christians here, thriving church. I’ve catered several meals here for events. Great ministry participation. Stop in every Sunday 9am. Renaissance Church of Christ
Got Baptized December 14th Praise God!!
Excellent place to learn, worship and get involved in ministry work. I love it here!

The word of God is in the building, if you want a nice place to go and good service. You want the word of God straight from the Bible, explain to you this is the church home for you. I love my brothers and sisters in the lord everybody is so loving and kind and friendly and authentic

reviews.text: My first experience was September 30, 2025. They had a new event called day of prayer. A buddy of mine and I decided to go and check it out. It was a very ethereal experience. The interaction I received from the people there was very cold. I went on a Wednesday.
To try and get information about their small groups.And no one wanted to sincerely help me. A lot of people just walked right by me.
With no acknowledgement.
Any very cold shoulder. I did not feel the spirit of God at this place.It feels as if this place is only for business.

Passion City is already a wonderful church, but the Cumberland location is beautiful and welcoming. Our daughter goes to the bloom program while we attend regular services, and we always feel so happy and safe dropping her off.
