reviews.text: Went to a repass here, our family is very large & it accommodated us it was very nice

In the area for wedding services and the reception meal was served following a short and simple ceremony.  Not being from the area or member of the church it’s hard saying if much of the immediate decorum was for wedding specifically but there was not much fancy to the actual room used for the event. I’d assume in part to fit the seating and table space for the guest list in attendance. Church was easy to find but there are lots of doors and lots of parking areas to use so it can be intimidating to enter. No mention of the event or signage of any sort on any door or otherwise made it worrisome we had arrived somewhere that regular evening services, church study groups or maybe even other private events that one might not want to crash might be going on. However once inside it is quite spacious and used to promote much more marketing of promotional items than I’ve ever seen in any church setting…not just about God / Faith but also the church itself. Books and mugs and shirts…but it seems school spirit is huge in TX so maybe church affiliation being put on blast is also a norm.?. Forgive my ignorance on the matter. The actual intended or what seemed more likely main entrance was used for my exit but as said I was entered much more cautiously having wondered around the building completely unsure of where to get or where I was going really. My adventures taken were for a bathroom stop and revealed all the wonders mentioned. I must say there was some thought, time and effort put forth in the designing of the furniture and signage upon entry. Not only the main ‘foyer’ area which is wide open and bright….but even as u wonder forward to a central hallway there continues to be a main scheme to the decoration and furnishings. Not so much functional in terms of location per se…but all very well put together. Even the ladies room had many fixtures and quite remarkable seating should one need to take a moment or needed a large mirror area. Not at all public restroom feel…and definitely way to formal for a homey feel to it…i imagine a good portion of the promotional item sales went into the interior budget. But again…the room of the formal event was kind of barren and had not much of any to any ‘sound’ or digital media entertainment system. A few fake ficus trees and some mobile floral with candles item that is quite possibly religion based). The otherwise general theme to the interior had stopped and left this room to fend for itself. The set up and staging area available and used to set up buffet style family pot luck dining was a plus. And again if the tables and chairs there for my friends wedding are always there for those who use the space as functional gathering or venue spot…that would also be a plus. Save much on rental fees and work that is otherwise needed to get.   Not convinced I seen the actual worship room of the church but thank u to my hosts (The new Mr and Mrs….) and a kind thank u to the church itself for having me. God bless

reviews.text:
I visited Lakepointe Church for the first time today, and the experience was… interesting.

First, the greeting and hospitality are next-level. I can’t overstate how nice and welcoming everyone was. Mark met my family at our car, walked us inside, and showed us around. From there, no fewer than a dozen people welcomed us, some even with hugs. Everyone was genuinely kind, but the sheer volume of friendliness bordered on feeling a bit cultish.

The dress code is casual, which I appreciated. The service itself, though, was unlike anything I’ve experienced before. The worship music is contemporary and very well done, the musicians and singers are undeniably talented, but the volume was extremely LOUD. Loud to the point where my ears nearly hurt. It almost felt like the volume was cranked up in hopes of pushing the Holy Spirit into your soul through your ears.

What surprised me most was learning that the satellite campuses are essentially viewing venues; the sermon comes from Rockwall and is shown on three massive screens. To me, this felt impersonal, and it seemed like maybe the church tries to overcompensate for that dynamic with exceptionally warm greeters and staff. I also found all the “Text NEXT to 40177,” “Text WORSHIP to 40177,” “Text BAPTISM to 40177” prompts to be a bit gimmicky.

Despite all of that, I really like Josh Howerton’s teachings, and the people truly were kind. But overall, I don’t think Lakepointe is the right fit for my family. If I’m going to watch the sermon on a screen, I’d rather do that from home—and save my eardrums in the process.

My first time to Lake Point church today for the Easter service.. it was amazing. I felt at peace. Absolutely delighted with my visit today on the holy day of Easter. I loved the word for pastor & The songs were beautiful. Great people and welcoming everybody as a known person. Thanks to my friend Charles Musila who invited me to be part of the service today. I would love to know more about God.

Highly recommend this church if you are looking for a welcoming place! Worship music is contemporary, the pastor preaches directly from the Bible but breaks it down to understand and how it applies today, and there is free coffee! Plenty of parking as well. There’s a nursery and kids ministry so if you have kids, they will be taken care of as well. Services are Sunday at 9:30a and 11a. Then Spanish services are after that! Come check it out!

This church is incredibly LOUD, (even if one steps out from the auditorium)-the decibel level is so loud you have to repeat yourself to check your kids in. The pastor said he gets a lot of comments on how loud it is and the Bible said to yell out the word. I dont think God meant that literally. What about people with infants, the elderly or autistic community who have sensory issues? Lowering the volume just a notch would create a more inclusive space for all people. reviews.text: I’m so incredibly disheartened to make this review. My family and I have been coming to ELC for years, but after last night’s “Christmas at the Cathedral” I will not be back. A service that is supposed to be about the birth of Jesus and giving our lives and fears over to him became a political statement. Condemning democrats and those who do not follow the current conservative administration. But somehow in the same breath “the government won’t control this church” There were many children in attendance, an event for friends and family to celebrate Jesus became about political views. I don’t want to go to a church that believes in telling me and others how they should vote and what to believe. Stick to preaching about the word of the God!

Elevate life has become my family of choice. Since I first walked in the door in May of 2024 my life has transformed completely. I have found Jesus in my life again. I serve in production and prayer team, which has been great and helping me steward my talents for Gods kingdom. Mighty Men and Pastor Keith’s messages have created everlasting impact on me and my new family. If you are reading this and have not attended, do yourself a favor and walk through the doors. 🙏

Very disappointed in Keith Craft. Almost every sermon, he makes it a point to brag about his money, then at the end (or beginning) of the sermon they go on for a good 20 minutes about the church giving THEM money. I understand tithing is Biblical & a good thing, but in times like these, it is triggering for a rich man to brag about his money especially at his big age when the younger generations won’t be able to afford a house. Not very humble like Jesus. If he sold his house or cars, he could have paid off the church instead of, what seems like begging, the Church and live a down to earth life like Jesus. There’s too many corrupt rich pastors in this world. Praying he opens his eyes and get back in touch with reality, for the church. I’ve stopped attending.

Seeker friendly, waterless spring.  If you are seeking God through Jesus Christ, kindly move on from this place.  This is entertainment, worship of wealth and pride, not worship of God as a disciple of Jesus Christ.  It is your job, leaders, to emulate Jesus and His apostles, namely Paul.  Helicopter egg drops, 53ft tall Christmas trees...Santa and live reindeer are not it.  We all must choose wisely...

I guess I’m lost. Why does Pastor Keith feel the need to constantly redefine what Elevate Life Church is supposed to be, and why does it always have to be about being the greatest church out there? What exactly are we competing for?

Shouldn’t the mission be about making disciples and helping people grow in their faith, not just counting how many people we can pack into a building? Jesus said, “Go and make disciples of all nations” (Matthew 28:19), yet it often feels like the focus here is more on attendance than true spiritual growth.

Week after week, messages circle back to giving, or the next big push to make the church “greater,” but very little is said about walking with people through their struggles or teaching them to live like Jesus daily. You shouldn’t have to beg your congregation to give. They should find it in their hearts to give and tithe. Scripture warns us, “Beware of practicing your righteousness before other people in order to be seen by them” (Matthew 6:1). Success in God’s kingdom is not measured in numbers, but in faithfulness and transformed lives.

A church isn’t supposed to feel like a business, but at Elevate Life it often seems like success is measured in dollar signs, attendance, and applause for leadership. That leaves me questioning, are we really elevating Jesus here, or just trying to elevate an image?

For me, church should be a place where people are seen, valued, discipled, and sent out, not pressured into giving more or treated like statistics on a spreadsheet. As Jesus reminded us, “You cannot serve both God and money” (Matthew 6:24).

reviews.text:
Had the pleasure of visiting this Church. Lots to say, but I will share my review. Firstly, for anyone reading this, be aware that as we know, no Church is perfect. No Church will meet all your needs, but the Church is important for us to Gather in with fellow Bretheren and Sisteren.

Now to share my experience. Overall, it wasn't so bad, but some things didn't sit with me personally. I think one thing I noticed is how there weren't people at the front to greet me when I arrived. Its something important that every ministry needs so First Time folks feel welcomed. But observing the Culture of the Church, it seems like their first time welcoming people is at the End of the Service, which was pretty cool. Shaked many people's hands, and got to fill out a card, and there was a men's event coincidentally. This was something I was impressed with as many ministries don't have men's ministries. They were even talking about a Men's event, which was nice.

Worship/The Word: The worship experience for me was really nice. Freedom of the Holy Spirit for sure. Some places will quench the presence of God. Seemed evident at Citadel International Church. People are so joyful here in God's house. In terms of the Word, Dr. Lanre Smith is a great minister of the Gospel. I did notice though that the teachings were not really that expository. The teachings are wonderful and practical, but take a more topical teaching approach in the ministry. To each their own, but I love deep exegetical teaching of the scriptures that dive into chunks of a passage. The speakers too were a little loud for me as I have Tinnitus in my right ear, but still a good word.

Community is something I was praying about. As I filled out my card, Its great that there was something for Men's Ministry, and we need that, but I'm wondering how people in that 30+ group connect in a co-ed way in this kind of ministry. Community would be interesting to explore, and it seems like something which is prioritized. For my age group though, I'm curious where we land in this ministry in terms of belonging.

Overall, I will say it wasn't a bad experience. Once isn't enough, and I'm praying if I will visit again. reviews.text:
I visited Debre Menkirat St. George Ethiopian Orthodox Church in TX this past Sunday on Easter Sunday, hoping to find spiritual peace and connection. Unfortunately, my experience was overshadowed by one individual who acted unethically and without the religious respect expected within such a sacred space.

Upon entering, I took a seat like any other worshiper. A man approached me and, without proper courtesy, insisted I move from where I was sitting. Out of respect for the church environment and to avoid disruption, I quietly moved to the side. However, what followed was truly disappointing—he continued to bother me, pushed the chair against me repeatedly, and disrupted my ability to focus and pray in peace.

Despite the discomfort and frustration, I chose to remain silent, not out of weakness, but out of deep respect for the values I was raised with in the church. I’ve always believed that church is a place of love, humility, and understanding, and I’ve never learned to speak with envy or create conflict, especially in such a setting.

I kindly urge the church administrators and committee to take notice of such behavior. Individuals who cannot treat others with dignity and respect should be reminded of the values this church represents. Everyone deserves to worship in peace, and no one should feel unwelcome or disrespected in the house of God.

reviews.text: This church disappointed me deeply. They go against so much of what Jesus Christ represents. I pulled up to their mostly empty parking lot (except 1 other car) for a moment to collect myself and figure out where I was going. It was extremely hot and the one other car there was next to a shaded spot, and as they were beginning to leave I pulled up to the spot next to them for a moment of shade. That car stopped, the person exited and started yelling at me about how that was church parking. I tried explaining my circumstance, that I'd only be there a moment but it fell on deaf ears. I'm heat sensitive and can be made sick very easily.  They had paid parking available which I did pay for just in case but in that lot the designated church spots were the only ones with shade. Jesus said things shouldn't be sold in front of temples (their parking). Jesus said to be a kind host and offer shelter. I was kicked out of the parking lot. If you want to walk in Christ this is not the place to go.

If you are looking for community and kindness this is not the place. My friend and I paused for a moment in the parking lot to gather our thoughts on where we should go for our next destination as we had traveled a long way. We paid for parking. My friend is disabled and heat sensitive so we thought we’d pull into a spot in the shade for a moment. The lot was completely empty on a Thursday and there was only one spot in the shade. We did not think it would be an issue but the second we pulled in a lady got out of the car and started angrily telling us to leave. We tried to explain that we would only be there a moment because my friend was overheated and then we’d be on our way, but she kept talking over us and just kept saying “read the sign, can you read the sigh?!” Which was honestly hurtful because I’m dyslexic and have gotten that comment a lot growing up. These are the types of interactions that made me leave the church in the first place and this was a reminder of how few people actually walk in Christ that claim to.

I was born in Seattle and this church has been here my entire life. My parents married here, I was baptized here and we had my mother’s funeral here. I’m an omnist but it’s nice to know there’s still family oriented churches in the heart of capitol Hill. Lots of history. I hope this church remains in this location for another 50 years.

But even though Mount Zion isn’t quite like I’m accustomed to it has to ring of home to it. And I like it. I think I will make Mount Zion my home church soon. God bless the Pastor and saint, good word and good singing.

Amazing church, life-giving community. 10/10 recommend. Pastor Tyler and is the real deal!

As a transgender woman, this community has allowed me to continue to thrive in the faith that I have had, ever since I was grown up in it. Everyday I cannot express my level of gratitude and thankfulness for God, and for the amazing Leaders in the ministry of this church congregation. If you’re looking for a place to call home, don’t be shy to enter these doors.
I feel very blessed to have found ASC after moving to Seattle. This church is full of people seeking spiritual growth and guidance from the Lord.

Authentic group of people learning how to follow Jesus together. I’ve been apart of this community for 8 years and have seen the fruits of transformation in real people’s lives. Pastor Tyler is wise and humble, and he does a great job at meeting people where they are at. He brings in a lot of guest speaks too, which helps diversify the folks who are teaching. I will always be rooting for this community’s flourishing in the Spirit!

formatted_address: 2816 1st Ave, Seattle, WA 98121, United States
name: Downtown Cornerstone Church

reviews.text: I have been a member for over 10 years. Its diverse congregation is filled with energetic, personable men and women seeking to grow through God's grace. You are welcome here no matter your socioeconomic status. Doors are open to all, even if you are just curious about Jesus. It doesn't matter what Sunday that you attend; you will always hear a message taught from, about, and through the Word.

If you're looking for a church that preaches the Bible faithfully and expositionally, this is your church! I started attending when I moved to Seattle from the Midwest. - I moved here knowing nobody and already feel like I have a beautiful and rich community through DCC. Please consider coming and witnessing the joy of this body!!

Outstanding church hidden in the heart of Seattle. The elders of this church care deeply about their congregation and teach sermons line by line through the Bible. They make themselves available if you have questions. The first Sunday I visited someone went out to lunch with me after, what a blessing! There are many ways apart from Sunday services to connect such as weekly community groups or Bible studies.
This is a healthy and Jesus-loving church. Amazing expositional teaching and groundedness in the Bible. I have been attending for several years and have found rich community here!
Amazing church with wonderful expository preaching! I think it may have the best Christian bookstore in the PNW! Worth the visit for the nurturing of your soul on any given Sunday.

formatted_address: 801 25th Ave, Seattle, WA 98122, United States
name: Mt Calvary Christian Center

reviews.text: I've attended  Mount Calvary  for over 25 years. Bishop Witherspoon and sister Laura Witherspoon are  very nice people.He is a great preacher/teacher. I enjoy attending service on Sunday. Always a great uplifting message.

I had attended service for the first time there Sunday 7/10 and the service was good singing and preaching and all, but the down side is the parking and also I was never greeted being a first time visitor.  No one has said a word to me when I walked in the door.  The Preacher welcomed one visitor, but it wasn’t me.  I was overlooked by members like I was yesterday’s garbage.  I might come visit again, but probably not no time soon.  I will give them credit for the good singing & preaching, otherwise I really didn’t feel a warm welcome from not one single person.  It is what it is.

Didn't have the best experience there to be honest. A person who walked in who was assumed to be same-gender loving and the preacher began to berate that person. Speaking in a passive aggressive way to try and scare the young man to leave, the preacher began to say things about the man - right from the pulpit. And the gentleman did leave. It's sad, because that guy could have been ready to receive Christ and came to church to change but we'll now never know.
Great, a long time member before moving to New Jersey, home visiting, always attend. A wonderful Pastor and a lovely wife, whom is a great speaker, and beautiful personality.
Outstanding preaching, great music, caring children ministry, welcoming greeters and parking staff. Great planners for outside fellowship.

formatted_address: 7616 Aurora Ave N, Seattle, WA 98103, United States
name: Mosaic Community Church

reviews.text:
I am from Alaska and while visiting Seattle I attended the 7:00pm Easter service. The atmosphere was radiant, the people were welcoming, and the songs were not only beautiful but powerful. The sermon was so moving, it touched my heart and left me in tears. The stories and testimonies shared were inspiring. This church community feels like a family, they treat everyone with love, compassion, grace, and tenderness- nomatter who you are or what you believe. They embody everything I could ever want in a church. I was privileged enough to witness and celebrate someone's baptism. The love, the joy, and the kindness in this church was something I had never felt before. Every interaction I had was sincere and felt personable. They truly made me feel at home.
Thank you Mosaic Community Church for this memorable and joyous experience. I will certainly return here the next time I visit Seattle.

Family of 6 adults from Detroit area visited today - Father’s Day. Great music - Spirit filled singing and preaching that was relevant and comfortably conversational. Message was challenging at the early service. If you get a chance check it out. I believe you will like it. Rodger!

I love Mosaic Eastside!! They are so welcoming and I always feel at home when I’m here. Leadership is so friendly and they want to get to know you! And they have a warm cup of coffee and doughnuts when you walk in the door :) Their sermons are biblical and based on truth.

I have been attending Mosaic Community Church for roughly nine months. From the moment I walked in the doors, I was immediately welcomed into a community of strong believers who have guided me in my faith and helped me strengthen my relationship with Jesus! For two years I was searching for a home church in the Seattle area; Mosaic has made me feel accepted, and they have welcomed me into their church family. If you are curious about Jesus, this is the definitely the church to go to! Every Sunday I wake up excited and full of energy to gather with friends and learn more about our God. I cannot recommend this church enough!

Best church family! These people have intentionally navigated life with me as I've learned how to follow Jesus. Through the celebrations of life and true hardship, these people love one another well because they truly love God. My husband and I met here, we have traveled the world on mission because of this church, and we are excited to have our future family grow up in this church because of the incredible kids ministry! We're in our fifth year at this church and hoping to stay as long as the Lord has us stay because every week that we continue to invest in this community, we find ourselves experiencing more love, more adventure, and more growth. I don't know where we would be without this community cheering us on in the name of Jesus!

formatted_address: 4511 Roosevelt Way NE, Seattle, WA 98105, United States
name: Every Nation Church Seattle

reviews.text:
Beyond grateful for this church and their willingness to stay rooted in Seattle and serve this city. The pastoral care and willingness to shepherd their community through the highs and lows of life is absolutely amazing.

They have a deep and evident love of Jesus and His teachings and is a place where you can be spiritual fed and emotionally cared for as well. One thing we also love about this community is how the name EVERY Nation really is represented by the congregation - we love the diversity and beauty that is represented in the room and in the community! It's a blessing to know this amazing church and be a part of their ministry!

Come on in and check the church out. Pastor Perry and Danielle are awesome and really care about their community and neighborhood. Small to mid-sized church, active community and welcoming to new people. They have a heart for the next generation and loving people well.

Very transparent about their organization, finances, structure, etc. with their church family. Really good about making that stuff available for others to examine.

The location moved from a theater to a building, to their current location now so it’s been a journey but they are still committed to their mission of loving God and loving people no matter when they end up. If you’re looking for community, it’s a good place to start. Thanks cross and crown for hosting, y’all are awesome! The seattle churches really do believe in helping one another in need and they do what they can for each other as a body of Christ.
It's a great church, in the Seattle university district, for anyone who wants to grow in their relationship with God. They have a heart for getting people involved in community.

My family and I have been a part of Every Nation Church Seattle for over 13 years.

Family
Over the years it is obvious that ENCS puts people over place, making anywhere we have met feel homey and welcoming. This family feel extends towards helping each other with practical things.

Finances
For such a small church it is astounding how invested ENCS is in the community and abroad.  The yearly financial report and vision casting/review is a great opportunity to see what ENCS as a whole has been doing.

Fun
There's so much fun involved! From anime clubs, to game nights, to zumba dance parties, to grabbing boba next door, there's always a way to connect with others.

I have called this church family for 8 years now. This church has seen my wife and me go from boyfriend and girlfriend, to fiancé and fiancée, to husband and wife, and now to father and mother.  We have grown and flourished here, and now we get to see our kids do the same. At every turn, the people here have been there for us to celebrate life's wins and to mourn life's losses. It's an understatement to say that the ENCS's people and leadership are warm and generous. They go out of their way to open their hearts to those looking for connection; they preach the Gospel with knowledge, conviction, and passion; and most importantly, they keep Jesus at the center of everything. If you're looking for a solid, Christ-centered church that cares deeply for its members, the local community, and the City of Seattle, then please come to a Sunday service! We would love to welcome you!

formatted_address: 5031 University Wy NE, Seattle, WA 98105, United States
name: SEA Church

reviews.text: This is an awesome church that helped revive my faith in God. A super tight knit community always welcome to new people :) Pastor Aaron and Rachel always have their doors open and I can’t wait to see how this church will grow.

We are grateful to have SEA Church in the U-District neighborhood and serving this community so well! This is a great church to visit, get plugged in with, and be treated like family. They deeply care for their members and the ministries across the city in so many ways, not just on Sunday mornings!

We genuinely believe that they are Kingdom builders and want you to get plugged into church alongside them! Check them out - bet they will have some donuts on Sundays and a chance to hear more of your own story!

We have called this community home for the last couple of years. We found this church shortly after moving to the northwest. The community we found here has been welcoming and supportive. We have made some of our closest friends here. The church has people from every different kind of background. Recently there has been lots of events and opportunities to hang with each other outside of Sunday service. If you looking for a community, a place where you can belong, then stop by one Sunday.

I started attending SEA church in 2018 when I moved back to Seattle. This church has given me lifelong friends and is always a support to me in my faith and life. If you’re looking for a new church home or just want to try something new, I would 10/10 recommend.

I got connected to SEA Church in late 2019. Even though I didn’t know people too well, they’ve always made an effort to stay connected even during the pandemic. The teachings are solid and the community is authentic. I am grateful for SEA Church :)

reviews.text: Hello from Calgary Canada! Our family visited the North Seattle congregation in May 2024 where we heard a sermon from brother Eben. We plan to return to Seattle just to visit this church as soon as we get another opportunity. Thank you again! God bless the brethren there.

Very welcoming and friendly. Great place to worship.

formatted_address: 15415 5th Ave NE, Shoreline, WA 98155, United States
name: Shoreline Full Gospel Fellowship

reviews.text: One of the best churches I have attended in a long time. Trust me we have tried many to fit our growth. We are military so it's hard for us to find a good church before we just give up and move away. I live in Lake Stevens, but it's worth the drive. They teach biblical doctrine, and everyone is friendly. I had many people come up to me just to say hi and introduce themselves. They also pray for one another and care about their congregation. If you ever need prayer they are willing to pray for you without hesitation. I have learned to get out of my comfort box and go out to the street with the pastor and pray for those in the streets. I love this church and would recommend it for all ages. My kids like it too and have become prayer warriors because this church. It's neat to see my 4 year old grow and pray for others and see healing.
I grew up in this church i would recommend going there the pastor is nice. Unfortuantely i moved away but if i was in the area i would still continue to come

I’m a virtual viewer and I’ve enjoyed hearing the wisdom, the truth and anointed Words from Pastor Loud.  The messages have always been uplifting, life changing and spiritually eye opening.  I have watched hundreds of his YouTube videos, and I have benefited by being healed from sicknesses.  Also, I have prayed to heal many others as I have followed Pastor Loud’s modeling and demonstration of the love and power of Jesus!  I hope to see the Pastor in person and continue to learn more…

This has been my church home for four years now. And will be forever. I've never felt so much love, compassion and understanding even in my own family. It may be small, but its mighty!
Pastor Tom Loud is a mighty man of God. Retired Pastor Trevor Harris and Youth Pastor Patrick Wahlmeier as well as Sunday School teacher Paula Loud (not to mention all other leaders), no doubt love Jesus, the word of God and believe in building up the body of Christ. Living the truth 100%, gifts of the Holy Spirit. And so much more.
The Wednesday night bible studies and Sunday morning Sunday School are so empowering and eye opening.
Monthly Healing Service on first Sunday of every month just gets more amazing over time. And has brought us worldwide visitors not to mention the hundreds if not thousands of miraculous healings we've seen with our very own eyes! God is so good!
Just the way we pray for each other and worship together is unlike any place you'll ever experience.
I'd never have imagined how much I'd love a place. Sundays are my favorite day of the week. I cannot wait to get to church. And it's funny how we never want to leave.
When our family found this church we were seeking truth and love. But we could've never imagined having a forever home with so much unconditional love and true family.
I cannot express how much I recommend this church. If you are seeking. Truth, love and strong biblical foundation and teaching. This is it. Thank you Jesus!❤

This church has been my home for over 30 years. Both Pastor Trevor and Pastor Tom teach excellent Bible. My husband, Patrick Wahlmeier, has been the youth Pastor since 2004 and has a passion for young people and spreading the gospel in relevant and practical ways. Our church is small but big in love and solid Biblical teaching.

formatted_address: 1300 E Aloha St, Seattle, WA 98102, United States
name: Grace Church Seattle

reviews.text:
Grace Church has been one of the greatest blessings of my time in Seattle. As an international student far from home, I was looking for a place where faith could feel alive and community could feel genuine. From the first time I stepped in, I was struck by the maturity of this church and the way it carries itself. The teaching is rich and deeply rooted in Scripture, spoken with clarity and honesty in a way that truly meets people where they are.

What makes Grace so special to me is how real it is. People here are open about their struggles and honest about their faith journeys, and that has encouraged me to grow in my own walk with God. The church does not get caught up in appearances or performance. Instead, everything is centered on Christ, and there is a depth and authenticity in the worship and the community that has shaped me in profound ways.

Being here has given me a sense of home even while being so far away from my own. I have found friendships, encouragement, and guidance that have helped me grow spiritually and personally. Grace Church is mature, Christ-centered, and filled with people who truly live out their faith, and I am deeply grateful to be a part of it.

This church is actually a business. We attended for many years and considered them our family. Then they rewrote the vision statement to conveniently fire the music leader and hire someone more subservient. When told the leadership how heartbreaking it was that they'd do this to a family in the worst economy, they told me my intuition was wrong and sat blank-faced as I spoke. My husband then repeated when I had just said and they suddenly acted interested and told him that was interesting insight. That's when I saw how they truly view women and I knew I couldn't raise my kids in this place. They operate from significant social and economic privilege and very little diversity. This is a country club masquerading as a church.

We were very involved with Grace for many years, but recently decided to find a new church. When we broke news of our departure to church leaders, we were massively disrespected, bullied, gossiped about, slandered, and then gaslighted. Unacceptable behavior and totally unprofessional from pastors John and Jason.

If you can't handle gentle criticism, don't ask for it. It seems as though power has gone unchecked for too long at Grace which may explain the leadership's arrogance and church's polarizing culture-led eisegesis.

A saving grace, we did make some lifelong friends at this church whom we cherish dearly.

This church was a good find for me while visiting Seattle.  The liturgy is structured in a traditional format, and I found the music beautiful, the sermon helpful, and the worship touching.  The teaching was spiritual, scriptural, and insightful. Also, I was happy to see the elders and deacons actively and cheerfully serving.

LOVE LOVE LOVE how the pastors talk weekly about important issues pertaining to systems of privilege and levels of oppression as they try to retrain some of the historically problematic ideas out of the church. Unfortunately I can only give 3 stars due to lack of diversity; all upper leadership and pastors are cis-men. Would also love Grace to talk about the T in LBGTQ as many of my marginalized friends don't feel the church is inclusive enough.

formatted_address: 4272 Fremont Ave N, Seattle, WA 98103, United States
name: Church of the Apostles

reviews.text: Completely affirming (marched in Pride with the church after coming out), beautiful music that is primarily composed in house by talented artists, and a healing experience coming out of fundamentalist religion. Episcopalian-ish service format.

I've been attending here for almost 3 years and love the home I've found in this community! The services are beautiful, creative, and contemplative - a great mix of liturgical and modern music and readings. One of my favorite parts of the service is called "Open Space" - it's a time to pray and/or reflect after the sermon. I love the quiet pause it provides for me to connect with God before I begin my work week. There are many opportunities to get involved, as congregational members help choose liturgy, give short sermons, and write and perform music. It's a loving and involved community where we tangibly helps our members through all kinds of life circumstances - deaths, births, illnesses, unemployment, divorce/break-ups, moving etc.

COTA's great! I'd been going to a much larger Episcopal church here in Seattle for awhile and was looking for a church home with a more community feel. My first time at Church of the Apostles, folks I'd met YEARS ago greeted me by name! 😮 I kept going back, Sunday after Sunday, and it's such an enriching experience for me.

My favorite part are the creative liturgies. Week to week, each provides the most beautiful opportunities for reflection. The worship director writes lots of the music, too!

There are small groups each quarter and they're a wonderful way to get (and stay) more connected with folks in the community. There's even an ongoing social justice group.

If you're looking for a welcoming place, where you can engage at whatever level you're comfortable with, from showing up once a month to giving a REVERB (aka sermon/homily), consider Church of the Apostles!

I've been going to COTA (Church of the Apostles) for three years. It's been a wonderful church home. The community is open and accepting of people of different backgrounds and places in their faith journey. Services mix new and old traditions and comprise of music, contemplative time, and community lead sermons. It's been a great place to grow both as a Christian and as a member of a Christian community.

If you've ever been to a show at The Fremont Abbey, it's every bit as creative and inspiring when the church takes over the space on Sunday. The Saturday night Easter vigil and blowout Rise party every year is not to be missed.
When I first showed up more than ten years ago I didn't realize how progressive and "open and affirming" most of the congregation is. I am pretty much conservative, evangelical, and Republican, yet even I am accepted and affirmed here with no expectation of becoming anything different. I would say that takes "open and affirming" to a whole new level. I believe it gives us all a golden opportunity to grow and develop in unexpected ways.
I have found community here like I have not known in years and feel like I have more opportunity than ever to "grow into the image and likeness of Christ". Nothing feels forced, yet expectations are high. I don't drink myself, but the first time I showed up I was invited out to a pub after the service and had a great evening. It felt like Jesus had invited me out to knock back a cold one with his friends -- and did not at all mind if I ordered tea.
COTA is not for everyone, but I encourage anyone to give us a try, and if you feel a little too uncomfortable with some of us, give us another try. It just might be Jesus that you are feeling uncomfortable with.

formatted_address: 2107 3rd Ave, Seattle, WA 98121, United States
name: Coastline Church

reviews.text:
As someone new to the city, I’ve felt extremely blessed to find Coastline Church. From the moment you walk in, there’s a genuine sense of welcome and care. The people are friendly without being overwhelming, and there are many opportunities to get involved, serve, and grow.

The sermons are biblical, the worship is Spirit-filled, and there’s a strong sense of peace throughout the community. It’s clear this church deeply values community and has a real love for both the city and God. A truly warm and inviting church in Seattle.

I’ve been a member of Coastline Church for a long time, and what I love most is how welcoming this community is. The teaching has been relevant, life-giving, and it helps me grow in my faith every day. In my years here, I’ve witnessed firsthand how much this church gives back to the Seattle community and the Belltown neighborhood. I honestly can’t imagine being part of any other because Coastline is home!

This church is truly amazing and a blessing to be part of. From the moment you walk in, you can feel the love and presence of God. The community is warm, welcoming, and full of social interaction — it's easy to connect, grow, and feel supported. The worship is powerful, the message is uplifting, and the people make you feel like family. A place where your spirit is nourished and your heart is filled!

Coastline has been my church community for 2 years now and I could not be more excited and thankful for the wonderful people who are making it possible.

The volunteers and staff are all very friendly and welcoming. And attendees are highly engaged every week.

Given the downtown location, the Coastline community is composed of many younger working professionals, but we are getting new people every week! Our age and cultural diversity is always growing. I love seeing how many people from different backgrounds, countries, and ethnic groups are brought together to worship the same God and love on one another.

I highly recommend coming on Sunday to check out a worship service in our cozy coffee shop setting.

This Church was AMAZING, great worship& energy and the Pastor’s message hit home HARD and was exactly what we as Christians need to hear right now.

This is a majestic cathedral in the heart of Seattle, one that once loomed celestially over the surrounding urban landscape with its two ornate Italian Renaissance style towers. Now, the buildings surrounding it are much taller, these blocky monoliths of steel and glass, but the cathedral is still distinguished by the artistry and deep care of its architecture. This is a building that evokes devotion, the passions of individual hands and individual minds to honor the sublime power of the divine. It is an emblem of a particular time in the history of the nation and the history of Seattle, when the city was young and Italianate architecture styles were extremely popular, in the early decades of the 20th century. Yet it is also an emblem of a kind of reverence and loving, artfully imaginative devotion to the divine that will never age or decay. This is absolutely a building that must be seen by anyone with an appreciation for spirituality or architecture in Seattle.
Nice Catholic Church to visit, it was a 10-minute walk from the Seattle Convention Center or the Westlake LINK/Monorail station. They have a bookstore beside the church too.
As someone who was born and raised in Russia, I’m spoilt with beautiful architecture and it’s hard to impress me. This cathedral is truly one of the most beautiful ones I’ve seen in Washington state!

It was a pleasure visiting St. James Cathedral in Seattle. It is especially beautiful with the spring explosion of flowering trees! This Cathedral was built 1905-07 in the renaissance revival architectural style. The central gnome collapsed in 1916 due to heavy snow, and was replaced with a flat roof featuring a skylight. Renovated in 1950 and 1994, this cathedral is clearly well maintained and cared for. It is rightfully designated as a city landmark and is well worth a visit if you get the chance. This beautiful cathedral is well-known for its community outreach and the services it provides for those in need. Entrance is free, there is plenty of paid parking in the area, and there is no public access to the towers.

reviews.text: Love this church they made me feel at home since day 1. Now it is my home church!!!

I love this church. We had been searching for a church in Seattle for nearly 3 years and decided to visit SCC just to check it out, not anticipating we'd find a place to stay. I cannot say enough about their children's ministry-- my kids used to be resistant about going to church and now cheer to get to go. My husband and I have different faith backgrounds and both of us feel welcome and accepted here. Pastor Fred has created a place that is accepting, it is solid yet open to new viewpoints-- it's really an amazing place. Come for the service, stay for fellowship over breakfast or lunch!

A great church, with a very welcoming membership. Pastor Fred is funny, enthusiastic, and kind. They play lots of energetic music and have a fantastic children's ministry program for the kids. They also have a huge feast in the basement of the church *every week* after the 11am service.

I've been attending Seattle Community Church since 2006, and it's my home! My family and I have formed many friendships there that go well beyond church. Our kids like Sunday School, and the Youth Ministry (GANG) is a blast for my older daughter. I've taught kindergarten age Sunday School (humbling!), did the Welcoming Ministry for a while, but most recently I've been kickin' it with the Praise Band and I think I'll keep doing that! We have participated in several small groups on topics such as marriage, children, and personal transformation. Our family has also done the downtown Feeding Ministry a few times. If you visit SCC, please stay for lunch! It's frequently quite good and this is a great way to catch up with friends.

This is the friendliest church I’ve ever been to in 48 years!  I walked in off the street and was greeted my so many warm people.  I was made to feel like I really belonged and that I was part of an amazing family.  Everyone was a living, breathing example of what Jesus calls Christians to be.

I asked in prayer to see the face of Jesus.

I will always cherish this message and church time. “Ask God for a vision as small as a city and as big as a soul.”

Deborah

name: Queen Anne Christian Church

reviews.text:
The Queen Anne Christian Church is right in my neighborhood, and though I don't go to the Sunday worship--and am not in fact a Christian per see, I have always felt welcome.   It is a wonderful resource for the larger community.  Among the things that makes it special is the occasional recitals of classical music held in the main worship hall.  The last one, I recall, of Mozart's requiem, was graced by the presence of the Austrian consulate.

Even with the doors of the church open on a summer evening, as a neighbor I have never been disturbed.   This kind of respect is dearly appreciated.

The older part of the church has a calming purple-blackish brick neo-Tudor facade, with lovely stained glass windows, that fits in very well with the neighborhood.   I was thrilled to be able to attend a talk on the history of its architecture.

I felt honored to make a small donation at one of the worship services.
A great experience with this church with a nice sermon and good people both in person and on Zoom

God is so good, and so loving, and he's also Just. Whatever I can't control of my own actions and thoughts are out of my hands, and God has shown up every time to provide, to save, to comfort, to prune, to teach, and to humble me.

-Preaching was sound.  I appreciate how they post the Scripture verses up on a screen for you to see.  I was a bit disappointed that few people have Bibles/iphones with them, and there are no Bibles in the pews to refer to. - Worship music was very good, and appeared to be done very humbly and with little focus on the musicians and vocalists.   Great mix of hymns of the faith and temporary pieces.  Musically wonderful.
- NO ONE spoke to me at all on visit one.  I was shocked and saddened.  Everyone seemed to be busy conversing, but no one came up to me, even after I moved around a bit in the sanctuary after the service.  They seemed too busy.  Wow, too busy to speak to a visitor.
- Visit #2 - thankfully, a young couple spoke to me and introduced themselves.  Afterward, a man named Bob (very friendly and kind) spoke to me in the vestibule and I connected with him.  Much better vibe.
- I'm a little concerned about the way they handle Communion.  Not much is said about it, and no Scripture is read concerning Paul's admonitions...which are serious and important.  They also practice intinction here, where congregants simply dip their own bread in one cup and sit down.  No one explains when to partake the elements.  Strange.  They almost seem embarrassed by or uncomfortable with the whole thing.  It should be a thoughtful time of reflection, confession, and prayer.  No one leads you in this at all.  I would suggest the elders really prayerfully examine this part of the service.
Be careful- be sure this church stays true to Scripture and follows the gospel carefully.  Follow Jesus Christ- He is the way the truth, and the life.

name: Heritage Pentecostal Church

reviews.text:
5 stars – A Bible-first church that feels like family (I'm closer to the people of this church than some of my own family!)
First question when searching for a church: Does it follow the Bible above tradition? YES.
Heritage Pentecostal of Tacoma puts Scripture front and center—every sermon, every song, every decision. No watered-down messages or trendy gimmicks; just the uncompromised Word of God preached with boldness and love.
The Pastor is truly anointed, filled with the Holy Ghost, and loves the people like his own family. He knows your name, prays over your struggles, and celebrates your victories. The associate ministers and elders follow suit—humble servants who live what they teach.
This is a vibrant, diverse church bursting with young families, teens, kids, singles, and seniors from every background. You’ll see every generation worshipping together. The youth group is tightknit, woven together with true love of Jesus.  The children’s Sunday School is a highlight: age-graded classes, engaging lessons, and teachers who pray over every child by name. Adult Sunday school is refreshing and relevant.
Worship is genuine and dynamic!  Not performance, but heartfelt ... the congregation sings loud, and the presence of God shows up. Expect clapping, raised hands, tears, and shouts of “Amen!”—all grounded in Scripture.

Outreach is constant: we hand out cards everywhere and sometimes people tell us, "This is the third card I've been given to this church!"
New here? You’ll be greeted with genuine smiles, and have a hard time leaving without a lot of names to remember, but mostly a feeling of belonging and conviction working on bringing you back to the next service.

Service times:

Sunday – 10:30 (Bible Study for all ages) | 1 PM (Worship Service)
Tuesdays & Thursdays (Midweek Bible study/worship – prayer, worship, Bible true teaching and preaching)

If you want a church that loves Jesus, loves people, and lives the Bible out loud—come as you are. You’ll leave changed.

He then mentions something about a "lone black jellybean no one wants to sit with" which I believe was a covert comment for me, a black woman. I felt a very dark energy within the church. All the people playing music like drums and singing were frowning and looked very unhappy same with many of the members of the church. I did not feel welcome and I regret trying to go to a church out of respect for my father who's become a part of the church of christ. I thought churches welcome everyone and to come as you are but this was a big learning lesson that is really not true for all churches. Some churches will turn you away. Jacob then later once again said " I don't really think the church will be a fit for you, not to scare you away". But at the same time lots of fake concern and lots of personal questions asked that really weren't relevant. It just made me feel very uncomfortable. I'm new to billings and I was asked "what brings you to billings" by about 4 members.
It was made clear I wasn't welcome into this church obvious due to my skin color/being poor and nothing to do with my faith or character.
Jacob mentioned "I would love to see you at church Sunday but you may get called in for work, some people gotta work Sunday" and then before leaving more fakes smiles and woman telling me "I will see you next Sunday, if not it's ok....."

I felt a headache the whole time in this church and a worst headache with their prayers. Everything just felt so fake and faked.
I'm giving the extra star because despite being so disrespected and so shocked because I never felt so unwelcome in a church, I learned the truth. I advise you to not go to this church is you are poor or a person of color. You are not welcome and they'll really make it clear. I been turned away from Jesus, by MAN.The Jesus and God that I know wouldnt have screen tvs technology(the devils toys), people using cell phones during service, all this material stuff. Thank you for letting me know that your Jesus doesnt accept me cause my Jesus is the REAL1

reviews.text:
We visited for first time. Took the foster kids with us to visit. "Some" of the staff were friendly, even very friendly. Others not so much. We asked about the welcome gifts and was told we had to wait until after the service. Then after the service, I was asked what size, I said Medium and he insisted I take an XL. I'm not a big guy. It was a little weird TBH. Not offended, just thats not a good first impressions.

The music was really good. It was very loud, but that doesn't bother me. I think the overall thing that stand out to me is that this is a "satellite" church and we aren't going to let another person preach/teach at this location. The head pastor is broadcast live from their main campus.

I see this becoming more and more of a trend. I don't care for it. It's impersonal and disconnected to a degree. It just all felt so structured and cookie cutter. Even if the speaker today would have been at our location, I still wouldn't have cared for it.

As members of the volunteer team, we are dedicated to serving our community and our church. We are a close-knit group and consider each other family. We were baptized at Elevation Church and it is our spiritual home. We are passionate about our faith and love being a part of this church. In short, our experience at Elevation Church has been nothing short of remarkable.

Nice community of people, never felt uncomfortable going here I’ve been going on and off for a couple years. The building itself is always clean and smells nice, the people are friendly and Steven preaches good.
I came out of state to visit.  I felt the spirit of God all around.  Can't wait to come back.

reviews.text: I didn't think I will enjoy a televised ministration/preaching on-site. But I did. Seemed as if the Pastor was in the remote church.  It was aired from the Charlotte headquarters of the church. Service was lively. Friendly people. Energetic. Part of the praise and worship was live while the other part was streaming from the  headquarters. I loved the message from the set man- Pas Steven Furtwick.  Peter from the Bible was sinking when trying to walk to Jesus on waters, and the need for him to stay in sync, so that he does not drown. Message resonated with me - to look up to Jesus, and stay focused, even as the week goes by, and the church effect is not as strong.  Technology was definitely leveraged well. T-shirt gift of your size was given to 1st timers. I was a first timer worshiper.

Super friendly and welcoming for a new comer. Unfortunately the music (though beautifully song) was incredibly loud. My heart rate increased and I felt terrible and had to leave before the sermon started. Almost 40 minutes of music at that level was intense and too long for me.  I guess im too old for it however my teenage daughter felt the same. They did offer ear plugs and even brought us some which was wonderful. Just cannot handle the pain in my chest it caused. Wish we could have stayed for the sermon. I see online attendance in our future.

Good place to worship. Somewhat new and growing church with diverse congregants. Friendly people. Lively, modern, and spirit-filled. However, like one other reviewer pointed out, the music was indeed very loud and I am not a big fan of telecast/livestreamed sermon; but I can understand that given how prominent Pastors Steve and Holly Furtick are within the Elevation church.

It’s the genuine culture and community for me. Pastor Steven and Holly Furtick delivers on sermons that challenge your way of living and each campus creates a community that comes alongside of you in that process. EC Durham has community at its core! From the parking lot to the experience…it’s a 12/10 for me!

I love this location and the campus pastors and staff. They are all very welcoming, even to members of the LGBT community which you don’t always receive in church. The worship is great, although it is quite loud if you’re sensitive to that.

name: Elevation Church - Roanoke

reviews.text:
I was thrilled to find out that Elevation Church was nearby when I moved there. I am somebody that far been following them, especially their music. The messages are crystal clear to me.  I didn't look too far into what they represent and never heard messages from their pastor until recent times. I just knew that I loved their music and what they said! What I didn't really expect was that it is a southern Baptist Christian Church. I prefer non-denominational Christian churches so the pastor's message came off a little too excited (sound )  for me. No matter what, that is an outstanding environment! This is just a place full with true worshipers. They are so kind and loving. It's a spiritually generous atmosphere. It was wonderful to stay after service to have a conversation with a few of them. I've been traveling a lot and all of my belongings are not moved to Virginia. I miss having a Bible but use my YouVersion Bible app. When they asked if there was anything that I needed, I answered  would I able to have a Bible. You get to see this beautiful orange Bible that they gave to me. It is well put together and I'm very excited for it. We prayed before I left and I do intend to go back. A little problem is that I wish that they had more community/groups for women. I am a lady that does not have children and this particular location seems to hyper focus on women's groups that appear to have all children services associated with them. Mostly mom type groups. If you are a mom looking for community, I am sure that this would fit you well.

Overall, I was very happy with my experience. I just was a little overwhelmed with the delivery of the sermon  because I am not Southern Baptist. I tend to lean a little bit more conservative, I like quiet and peaceful yet passionate delivered. This pastor is in a class of his own. He's knowledge and has a great message, just not for me. I love passion but this was very intense for me because I can't tolerate unexpected circumstances with behavior. Nonetheless, this is a total 5 ⭐ experience. The message was excellent and the people were extraordinary, just not my cup of tea. Give it a try! ✨👌

If you have found my review helpful please give me a thumbs up 👍 and feel free to follow me for future reviews.

1130 service Guided parking in large shared lot.some stairs to walk up.
Friendly greeters at door, no hugs. Kids entrance availability. 20's 30's average age attending adults and  plenty of variety of childrens age groups. Youth group. Modern music playing upon entering building. Welcome tent for first time guests. Merchandise table set up for selling CDs shirts and other gifts. Organized and guided seating corral style to theater style seats. Dramatic blue lighting on a black background on stage. Friendly people. Loud concert speakers with good quality sound. First time visitors are considered VIPs and escorted to waiting area for seating. Large emphasis on youth groups and secure kids check in policy.
Guest preacher was cast through on  screen. No bible reference during sermon, however teaching was very relevant to modern daily living. Guest preacher loud at times during sermon. Prayer for salvation at end and all interlocked arms during prayer. Everyone exited in a slow corralled manner as many people attended and left at same time. Overall average experience.
So grateful to have found Elevation Church! It's made such a huge impact on my life this past year and I can't wait to continue growing spiritually with them!

Super disappointed.  People should know you are watching the service online.  We were visiting from Wisconsin.  Ushered to sit in the 2nd row, we said ok maybe they expect a big crowd.  Not so.  The head pastor who didn't preach was a distraction.  I love Elevation church, but this experience was uncomfortable.  I can't imagine how an unbeliever would feel.  We were looking for a church to recommend to our son that lives here.  I should also mention the police presence??  Not sure why they were around, but it was unsettling.

The best worship experience you'll get ANYWHERE! The music is really upbeat and gets you in the right place for worship. Pastor Steven is a PHENOMENAL speaker and even though he's not physically in Roanoke, his words are no less intense. There are so many opportunities to serve the community through this church. You will feel very welcomed as soon as you pull in to the parking lot.

reviews.text:
I've been looking for a church like this my whole life. A wonderful community devoted to God.

UPDATE (1/29/2021): I've been with the church now for three years. I've gone from worshipper to volunteer to volunteer leader to volunteer coordinator for the photography team. It has been an amazing experience! Even with COVID-19 we're able to keep the church open and safe with temperature checks, masks, and social distancing.

We've been attending in-person since 2018 (with the exception of a few months online in 2020 due to covid) and the presence of the Lord is so powerful here when people gather together to worship Him. The honest, caring, diverse community of believers of all ages, ethnicities, & life stages is irreplaceable. The church members go out of their way to help people feel welcomed, encouraged, and taken care of...I mean you can't even walk in the door without like 5 different people greeting you! The leadership has thought of every detail to make the experience better for people...from clean restrooms to mints & coffee, from prayer to  special family-friendly events to earplugs if the sound is too loud for your preference, oh...and they also give every person who gives their life to Jesus a new Bible to grow in their relationship with God. So grateful to God for Elevation RiverWalk! 🧡🧡🧡🧡🧡

We have been coming to Elevation Rock Hill for about a year-and-a-half! The experience is just incredible every single time. All of the greeters and ushers make the experience very pleasant. We have a very diverse crowd at elevation so anybody can come as they are! You don't need to wear a suit and tie. I look forward to seeing you there! If you've gone to other elevation campuses - you will definitely appreciate how easy it is to get in and out of church, there isn't really any traffic getting in or out of elevation Rock Hill.

reviews.text: Elevation Church in Belmont, newly opened, impressively has its logistics well-handled, particularly with parking. Their inviting patios offer an ideal setting for such gatherings. People lined up around the corner waiting in the cold; countless volunteers eagerly welcoming; a darkened worship area misted in fog; not a single seat left empty; heartfelt & impassioned musicians; seamless transition via live-stream to another location; and a great message from a charismatic preacher.  These were my impressions during our first visit to Elevation Church in Belmont.

This is more like a virtual church. No real pastor. You watch a lot on a screen. Makes the parking situation downtown terrible. No respect for local businesses. I can see why downtown businesses are upset. The music here seems more like the type you’d hear in a club than in a church. We like “rock” Christian but the strobing lights etc really??? They are very strict and move you in and out like cattle. Rude when you deviate from the rules like to go to the bathroom. Just not our thing.

Dark and music was so loud,like a nightclub. Bouncers, I mean seat attendant walking up and down the aisle was so visually distracting, made it hard to focus on… what may have been a preacher on a screen (just because you preach doesn’t make you a pastor). reviews.text: This church is full of testimonies! You can feel the love and presence of the Lord in this place! It is my second home and my whole family is blessed to go here and serve! This is more than a church ITS MY FAMILY! ❤️🙏 Come join us today!
I had a great visit to Elevation Church Melbourne this morning. It was a baptism Sunday, and the church baptized 14 new Christians. Very cool! God bless this ministry in Brevard.

I’m new to the Melbourne, FL area and, like many, I’ve known Elevation for its powerful worship songs & strong preaching for years. Attending this campus, however, is a different experience.

The worship and messages are excellent, and there are truly anointed individuals here who love Jesus deeply and serve faithfully. But much of the culture feels built more around the "Elevation brand" than identity in Christ.

The brand is strong, but at times it feels short-lived and surface-level—people can appear enthusiastic yet lack *depth or *fruit of the Spirit when you look closer or try to engage.
This applies across serving teams and even some leadership.💥
Unfortunately.

That said, there are steady, authentic believers here who carry genuine depth in Christ apart from the brand. Encountering them was encouraging, though this will not be my church home. The two stars are for those individuals, who consistently reflect the fruit of the Spirit and serve God faithfully, apart from the machine.

In the end, Elevation is not unique in this struggle—many churches wrestle with the tension between brand and authentic discipleship.
If you visit, be led by the Spirit, not by a name, a brand, or emotion. Jesus is the foundation—not Elevation, nor any other. ✨✝️🕊👑

reviews.text: I have been a member here for about 7 years. I have enjoyed the warm, kind and welcoming people who are a part of this Parish. There are many options for getting involved including Sunday Bible Study, choir, bell ringers, etc, as well as special classes to help deepen one’s faith. The current priest has brought a lot of energy to our 85-year-old church. I love the amount of passion that members have in providing service to our greater community with food collections, clothing drives and other outreach programs. The services are also filled with wonderful music!

This is a community of the kindest, most giving individuals. They do so much good locally through working with Ballard Food Bank, Queen Anne Helpline, Operation Nightwatch, Mission to Seafarers and others. They bring in speakers on social justice speakers. They have great family events. And the priest is phenomenal. She is so down to earth and humble but also energetic and visionary. She is doing great things for the church.

I have been to numerous churches in the Greater Seattle Area.  None have felt as welcoming and safe as Ascension. This is a place my wife and I proudly call our church home.  With a congregation who is always out in the community doing good work, an active music program (Adult and Children's choirs), and an excellent coffee hour, Ascension is truly a special place that welcomes all.

I've been a member of Ascension for four decades and it has been a supportive, loving and faithful community through all of the different phases of my life. Our current rector is thoughtful, personable, kind and nurturing. Her sermons are relevant and ground me to go forth in love and service to others in the week ahead. There are many ways to get involved - come join us!
A welcoming faith community for worshipers of all ages. Lots of opportunities to contribute to outreach missions in the greater Seattle area.

formatted_address: 2004 NW 63rd St, Seattle, WA 98107, United States
name: Sideris Church

reviews.text: I’ve been attending Sideris church for about a year a half and the community there has truly helped me grow in my faith. I really enjoy how pastors Dave and Ryan teach scripture and how deeply they move through whatever Bible passages they have chosen to teach. When I first attended they were moving through the Gospel according to John and illuminated so many truths for me by carefully teaching through each passage. Ty and the worship team provide contemporary music that is performed with both inspiration and humility and often allow me to feel more connected to JESUS. I’m a musician so music is an important part of my prayer life. The congregation is diverse and recently merged with Ballard Baptist Church and moved into a new home in one of Ballard’s oldest church buildings. The sanctuary is comfortable and bright thanks to the incredible stained glass. It feels both historic and contemporary at the same time thanks to some well planned updates. My favorite part of Sideris is the opportunity to gather in small groups during the week. I’ve met genuine and kind people there who have become an important part of my life, both in helping me grow as a Christian but also to have fun, celebrate and support one another. I’m grateful that GOD directed me to Sideris and I love being a part of it.

As a long-time neighbor (over 10 years in this community), I am extremely frustrated by the excessive noise from this church every Sunday. The music and amplified sound begin in the morning and continue loudly through the afternoon without pause. This was never an issue before Sideris moved in.

Everyone has the right to worship, but it should not come at the cost of disturbing the entire neighborhood week after week. Please respect the community by keeping your practices contained within your property. Right now, the disruption is unbearable and makes you very unwelcome as a neighbor.

TL;DR: Sideris Church is a welcoming, Bible-centered community where newcomers feel genuinely connected and empowered to grow in their faith.

From the moment I stepped into Sideris Church, I felt seen and welcomed. A member noticed I was new and took the time to introduce me to others who shared similar backgrounds, making the start of my journey there feel natural and genuine. People here remember your name and make it a point to reach out, creating a sense of belonging that isn't just surface-level. As a newcomer, I appreciated how the church offers a range of ways to connect--whether that means joining a group, volunteering, or simply enjoying meaningful conversations / lunch after the service.

At Sideris, the sermons stay true to the Word of God, delivering messages grounded in biblical teaching. There's a deliberate focus on not just understanding scripture but on actively living it out, making it easy to translate faith into everyday life. It's refreshing to be in a place where the Bible isn't just preached but practiced, with an emphasis on how we can apply God's teachings in our own lives.

Another highlight of Sideris is its diversity. The congregation includes people from all backgrounds, professions, and interests, making it a truly dynamic community. There's always an opportunity to get involved, but it's up to you to take that first step and say "yes." Even something as simple as a four-minute conversation with a stranger has been key in helping me build friendships and find my place in Seattle. Sideris has crafted a space where community is both accessible and intentional, turning Sunday mornings into a genuine time of connection.

Since moving back to Seattle we were looking for a church that would feel like home. Since our first Sunday at this church, we’ve felt the love of God and others in a very real way. Each person I’ve met at Sideris is living out their faith in a humble and honest way and I love that about them. I really feel like the heart of this church and the community that gathers here is how church was meant to be.

I had church hopped 5 times in Seattle area in the span of 6 years and I had never felt I truly belonged. I’m glad I didn’t give up and found Sideris. What a community we have here! I’m not going to hype it up and say it’s a perfect church cuz no churches are, but for the first time in ever, I feel my effort had finally generated lasting fruits. People here are genuine and not “churchy”. Music here are sincere and not overly showy. This community really does focus on relationships and love in a way that isn’t just all talks like the other experiences I’ve had before. I felt growth and progress here. I see changes here, in me and in others. Thank you Sideris. I pray to God almighty that this church will be hitting strong for decades to come and it’ll produce enduring and honest fruits for the kingdom.

reviews.text: The First Baptist Church is a beautiful place to visit, and we felt very welcome 🙏🤗We loved the Nordic Winter concert. It was a lovely time. We highly recommend it!

A true church of Jesus Christ, where the word of the Lord Jesus Christ is preached like it is supposed to be delivered. FBCSF is a very sound and Christ-centered church that exhibits the grace of God in their preaching and practice. Every true church is characterized by people who have placed their faith in Jesus, repented from their sins, bear the fruits of repentance, and desire for others to do the same. God has His hand on this local church.

The church practices kingdom generosity and has people who are characterized by Christian love for believers and people who do not know God. They demonstrate mercy and demonstrate kingdom generosity to the people of the Bay Area and the world, as disciples who have received the great mercy of God.

If you want to find the word of Lord Jesus Christ preached like it is supposed to—not sugar coated or adulterated—then this is the place. The shepherds here are true and do not play games or fool around, demonstrating themselves to be people of the kingdom community who give hope to the hopeless, preparing sinners to meet God, walking down the difficult path that leads to salvation. We are either with God or against Him.

The discussion questions convict me of my sins. The shepherds and disciples are very helpful in helping me deny myself to follow the way of Jesus.

It is continually emphasized that the relationship with God is between the individual and God. We are taught that we the people of God are called to live repentant lives and shine as lights in the darkness everyday in the world, in school, in the workplace, in the home, in services to people, and many different avenues. The Sunday services are intended to equip believers to live out the ways of Jesus practically day by day. The members emphasize that the one true church of God is neither a religious organization nor a building, but the people of God.

I love it when Pastor Benjamin prays: “We pray that our church gatherings will not be empty rituals.” Since our identity is in Christ, we live out the love of God in the community, in the workplace, among or family members, among our unbelieving friends, in the arts, and in any community service organization that helps people. If we have God inside us, we live out the church everywhere. This is what the church leaders teach.

It is taught that our foundation is not in good deeds we do, because no good deeds can merit God’s forgiveness. There is nothing we can do to gain God’s favor and we bring nothing to God that he needs. The church teaches that we are sinners who are adopted into God’s family. The whole Gospel is preached with nothing missed. We are saved through adoption, not through our own efforts. All of our sins, past, present, and future, are forgiven. Jesus paid for our sins on the cross. We have an identity much deeper than ourselves.

The church teaches us to love people in very tangible and real ways, like Jesus did. Sharing the Gospel with people takes many different forms. It is not about parroting facts about the Bible and talking about the doctrines of salvation in abstract theological ways to everyone.

The church emphasizes the importance of accountability to God and worship through a lifestyle of continual repentance, prayer, love for neighbors, and God’s mission to win people to Christ. It is taught to build our relationship with God in have a balance in all the areas of faith.

If you are considering coming, you should totally do it!!!
