reviews.text: I've been coming to this church off and on for a year now, and I like it. Pastor Travis usually does an insightful sermon, and the music is great too. The one thing is that it does sometimes have WASP-y vibes, which doesn't make me feel 100% comfortable

Canvas Church is a welcoming haven where everyone is embraced with open arms. It's more than just a church—it's a community that truly makes you feel like you belong. The sense of togetherness and family that Canvas fosters is unmatched in San Francisco, creating a space where all are invited to come together, support one another, and grow in faith.

We've been attending Canvas Church for a few years now, and it has truly become a meaningful part of our life in San Francisco. We first discovered Canvas when it was still a mobile church, and it's been an incredible journey to see it grow and find its permanent home at 385 Moraga in The Presidio.

Having been raised in the church, I was looking for something a little different—something that felt both grounded and fresh. I found that in Canvas. One of the things that resonated with me most is how Pastor Travis focuses less on life after death, and more on how to live fully, intentionally, and with purpose in the here and now. His messages are thoughtful, relevant, and often challenge me in the best ways.

The community here is genuinely diverse and welcoming—there are young professionals new to SF, families with kids of all ages (our morning kids' classes often have 25-30 children!), and folks who’ve called San Francisco home for decades. In a city that can sometimes feel isolating or hard to break into, Canvas offers a warm, supportive place to build connection.

Whether you're exploring faith for the first time or have been on the journey for a while, Canvas is a place where you're invited to show up just as you are. We're so grateful to be part of it.

Canvas has become my church home, and helped me find purpose when I felt directionless. It offers practical, real-world sermons that can be applied to our modern life. It is free of judgment and has many smiling faces looking to welcome you into their community. Travis and Jena have really worked hard to create something special, and their dedication shows. I highly recommend checking this church out, especially if its been a minute since you and God have spoken, like me.

Canvas is everything I wished for in a church. It has been incredibly healing, and I'm so grateful for this community of heart-centered, honest, and authentic people.

I've always been drawn to Christianity and the teachings of Jesus, but I've struggled with past churches' stances on LGBTQ+ issues, racism, and other social matters. I don't believe true Christians would reject minorities, and that left me guarded.

Something was calling me back to church, so I decided to look for one on Yelp. I wasn't planning to stick around, just wanted to drop in for a Sunday service and see how it felt.

In June 2024, I found Canvas while searching for well-reviewed churches in San Francisco, and I was immediately impressed by their clear, modern website. It was easy to sign up, and by Sunday, I was there.

When I arrived, my first thought was how beautiful the space was--bright, open, and visionary. I was warmly greeted by genuine people, grabbed a coffee and a doughnut, and sat down. The co-lead pastors, Travis and Jena, were discussing Love Week, a week-long service project to partner with local nonprofits in San Francisco. Their passion reminded me of why I was drawn to the teachings of Jesus in the first place.

Over the next several months, I kept going back--even after taking a two-month break for work. I got involved pretty quickly; I was baptized, attended Belong Night, Family Night, joined a volunteer team, participated in Alpha (a growth group), and became part of a women's group. Each time I took a step deeper with Canvas, I felt God's support and confirmation.

Now, after five months, I can confidently say that Travis and Jena are the most authentic and consistent pastors I've met. They truly walk with God and Jesus, and they've created a safe space for people who've been hurt by the church or by issues like racism and prejudice. Their actions speak louder than words.

What stands out about Canvas is the sincerity, transparency, and honesty in everything they do. This isn't just a welcoming church--it's a place actively working to unlearn the harmful practices of the past. It's inclusive to POC, WOC, and queer folks and they're taking steps to address racism, division, and prejudice.

Every interaction I've had with Canvas' leadership and community has been deeply loving, generous, and genuine. They truly care about their members and the people of San Francisco.

One of the key messages Travis has been leading us through recently is to "Love Where You Live." He spoke about how, historically, San Francisco has been a place where people come to take what they can--dating back to the Gold Rush and continuing today with tech and AI. But he challenged us to imagine what it would look like if, instead of taking, we gave, served, and prayed for the city. Hearing this message and seeing it in action has been deeply inspirational and pivotal for me. It's hard to put into words, but it has transformed how I think about and feel toward living in my city.

Canvas is bridging divides and restoring faith in a way I haven't seen in my 30 years of living here as a native. If you're on the fence, I highly recommend trying a Sunday service. Come see for yourself. Like me, you might be surprised by what you find.

Saints Peter and Paul Church in North Beach, San Francisco

I have lived in North Beach, San Francisco, for almost 25 years. One of the most interesting places here is Saints Peter and Paul Church. Whenever I visit Washington Square, I enjoy taking photos of this beautiful church.

Saints Peter and Paul Church is a key part of the North Beach skyline. This Roman Catholic church has a rich history linked to the local community. The church stands on Filbert Street, next to Washington Square Park, but it didn’t always be there.

The original church was built in 1884 at the corner of Filbert Street and Grant Avenue. Sadly, the 1906 San Francisco earthquake and fire destroyed it. However, the community wanted to rebuild. They laid the cornerstone for the new church in 1913, and by 1924, the church we see today, with its stunning twin spires, was completed.

One fascinating part of the church's history is its connection to baseball legend Joe DiMaggio. Joe grew up in North Beach and was baptized here. When he married his first wife, Dorothy Arnold, in 1939, they took their wedding photos on the steps of the church. Later, when he married Marilyn Monroe in 1954, they returned to take photos as well.

The church’s architecture is beautiful. It is designed in the Italian Gothic style, featuring two tall spires. Inside, you will find stunning stained glass windows and intricate details that show great craftsmanship.

Saints Peter and Paul Church means more than just a building; it represents resilience and community. It has been a place of worship, a cultural center, and a source of hope for many generations of North Beach residents. Over the years, it has hosted many weddings, baptisms, and community events.

Visiting Washington Square and seeing Saints Peter and Paul Church is always a special experience for me. There is something timeless about this place that continues to inspire. Whether you are a local or a visitor, I highly recommend stopping by to appreciate this amazing piece of San Francisco’s history.

Next time you are in North Beach, be sure to check out Saints Peter and Paul Church. You might want to snap a few photos to capture its charm!

reviews.text:
This place saved my life... This place offered a light in my time of darkness... I had no business, no invitation, no hint of salvation, yet one Sunday morning I found myself a part of the congregation. Never have I felt so at home, when I walked in a stranger. Never have I felt uplifted and on high.. When I left my own home so afraid and alone.. The human beings that make this place the mecca of a better future did not let me fall to the waist-side, even though my presence did not go unnoticed. If an onlooker would have witnessed, an out-sider i would have been labeled.
However the good, righteous people that I had the grace to integrate into their circle treated me like family. Welcomes and wishes of my return still echo through my soul. The inclusiveness of such an obvious stranger speaks volumes, and I have been in a situation's that fold out on the opposite path...
Maybe it was the obviousness of my imagration to a new congregation. To be wholey honest, I stumbled upon this place of worship looking for a place to please my girlfriend.
She is 100% Macedonian, something that she wears like a badge, adorned with honor at each mention of her parent's homeland. Around easter, the eastern european in her blood was in need of worship. Being an American Mutt, I did not fully understand the gravitation she felt, but as I loved the women to whom I speak, A Macedonian church would be my only solution.

And so we went... With little in our pockets and nothing to our name....

So we saw... A service so powerful, it is now what my soul requires...

The presence of God was palpable, and if I am just feeling the faith of the acting preacher, his faith I mean to carry.

The Macedonian Missionary Baptist Church is the best church in the entire world... It is located Filmore way... San Francisco....

I was always told that God works in mysterious ways.... The Macedonian Missionary Church taught me that God works not only in ways that deem not only mysterious... but, serendipitous... when you need to praise

We have early morning prayer at 8:30a.m. (maybe a little  too early for u lol), Sunday School starts at 9:00a.m. ends at 10:a.m.- u will love it & Morning Worship starts at 10:30a.m. If you are looking for a church home, or confused about who God is or just curious please come to 1 of our services. You might be surprised.
Everyone is very pleasant and courteous. This church engages members to realize and maximize there full potential in Jesus Christ. Macedonia is for the community and has been around for 73 years  .

The people here are genuine, kind, and caring, and the church has a beautiful family-loving atmosphere that makes you feel like you belong. It’s more than just a place of worship—it’s a community where everyone supports and uplifts one another. I’m grateful to have found such an amazing church family.

name: Mission Dolores Basilica

reviews.text: A beautiful mission. Vast and expansive. The services and other programs are great. Easy parking. Attended their Christmas Concert this season where the choir performed Handel’s Messiah. Beautiful concert.
I lived in the Mission but never bothered to stroll in to this historic place of worship. Was reminded by watching Vertigo recently. Open for tours and regular service on the weekends.

The Mission Dolores Basilica offers a fascinating glimpse into history with its stunning architecture and beautiful stained glass windows, some of which date back to the 1700s.
A self-guided tour costs just $10, granting access not only to the basilica itself but also to the adjacent small museum and peaceful cemetery, where you can immerse yourself in the mission’s rich past.

During my visit, the atmosphere was serene, with fewer than a dozen people inside, allowing for quiet reflection and an uninterrupted experience. You’ll enter and exit through the gift shop, which offers a variety of unique souvenirs to commemorate your visit.

The Mission was not on our sightseeing list for San Francisco. We had some extra time though and it was close, so we popped in to check out the cemetery.

I wasn’t prepared for the wealth of history I would be presented with. I needed days worth of time to really take everything in but only had about 20 minutes.

The 2 men working the shop that day were true gems. Not only did they relay the history and tells us colorful stories, they recommended a nearby bakery which as as phenomenal as they said. I could have spent the whole afternoon talking with them.

The basilica was breathtaking.
The cemetery was well maintained and beautifully landscaped.
The displays and artifacts throughout were amazing.

I had such a peaceful walkthrough in one of the busiest cities in the country. What a treasure!

Beautiful church with a rich history. Excellent acoustics for concerts. Features an outstanding concert Steinway grand piano, harpsichord, and organs. High-quality live stream service. Stunning sanctuary and chapel.

Having a strong and healthy community is not always easy or straightforward. Fortunately, this church offers everything our family seeks - a warm and welcoming atmosphere, diverse backgrounds, caring leaders, and excellent fellowship and bonding opportunities. Whether you’re a visitor, a regular member, or a team member, they genuinely care about you and want everyone who walks through their doors to feel like they’ve found a family.

IFGF Bay Area has been our home church since we moved to the U.S., and it holds a special place in our hearts. My husband and I met here, and now we are growing spiritually together with our two sons. The church is a close-knit community where people genuinely care for one another. We love the fellowship, sharing great food, and spending time together outside of church. It truly feels like family!

This church has been such a blessing to our family. From the moment we arrived, we felt the love of Christ through the warmth of the community. It feels like home, a true spiritual family. Our children are growing in their faith, learning about God’s Word and experiencing His presence. Each gathering is filled with joy, fellowship, and a deep sense of God’s love. We’re so thankful God led us here.

IFGF San Francisco is a gem of a church! The intergenerational dynamic here is so refreshing—there’s a beautiful mix of young families, professionals, and older generations, all coming together in a close-knit, family-like setting.

The worship service is truly inspiring, filled with heartfelt praise and an uplifting atmosphere that draws you closer to God. Despite being a small congregation, the community is vibrant, welcoming, and dynamic. You really feel like you belong from the moment you walk through the doors.

If you’re looking for a church that offers genuine connections, meaningful worship, and a strong sense of family, I highly recommend IFGF San Francisco!

name: Citizens Church of San Francisco

reviews.text:
We walked into Citizens post COVID.  In Citizens, our family found a genuine and unforced community that meets you as you are, while lovingly challenges you to deeper faith. Dave’s teaching isn’t afraid to speak to the hard questions, and the faith conversations here make space for doubt and life’s complexity.

One of the things that has transformed me is the church’s commitment to the unhoused community in SF.  I am blessed to know my unhoused neighbors and so grateful for their place in my life.

It’s also a great place for families. My kids are truly cared and loved at Citizens.  It’s a wonderful community for our children with trusted adults and teenage role models.

What sets apart the Citizens community for me is its posture of humility in pursuit of Jesus.

My family and I have been attending Citizens since 2021 during the pandemic. We were immediately drawn to the teaching that is bible-focused and the diverse community who come from all walks of life. For a relatively small church, there are college students, young professionals, married couples, families with young kids and teens, and older adults who have been in SF for years. It is a rare treat to be among this cross-section of SF residents and what I love most about Citizens. We also love that our kids feel loved, known, and comfortable here. If you’re exploring faith, looking for a new church that feels homey and welcoming, or returning to church after a hiatus, I recommend checking out on Sundays at 10am.

My family has been attending Citizens for about a year now, and we couldn’t be happier. It’s a church that has teaching grounded in scripture, and a community that authentically loves the city. We were immediately welcomed by everyone, and quickly felt right at home. We are so thankful that it is a community that our son will grow up feeling known and loved.

Love this church!

I've been at Citizens for many years and it remains a church made up of individuals. The church feels alive with the gifts, affinities, and personalities of the members. There's little pretense. People come as they are and what they bring isn't smoothed out, it's embraced and used! Both in the church and outside; serving our SF neighbors. As a photographer, my interests found an easy home. But it's amazing to see our painters, builders, interior designers, students, parents empowered and welcomed to explore their affinities in a spiritual context. It's also just a cool place. Come through.

Citizens has been such a welcoming and grounding place for me. In a city as busy and transient as San Francisco, finding real community can be hard, but here, I’ve felt genuinely seen and supported. The people are kind, the environment is inviting, and it truly feels like a place to grow and belong. Highly recommend to anyone looking for connection and a meaningful church home.

reviews.text: Good Bible based church. They preach and teach solid bible principles that helps you with your growth in Christ. None of the preachers or teachers stand up there and talk about themselves for an hour.😲 Very good worship. Very good children's ministry on Sunday's & midweek. Also midweek Men & Women's ministry, young mom's ministry. Multi ethnic. Accountability with staff and elders (very important to me). Supports global and local ministries, minister's at a local school, serve's at a Tenderloin ministry, helps support local college ministries. My wife and I have been going here for 6 years. I feel like they really help you to grow in Christ and give opportunities to serve in the body of Christ and community. Pastor Rob is a great pastor. He and his wife have a heart for people and their families. He is an excellent preacher/teacher with heart, NOT ego. The staff preaches too and all are on point. They all work well together. This is a healthy church. Not a perfect church because I attend here 🙃 but a great place to grow in your walk with Christ. I am not an elder or staff leaving this review.

My wife and I have been deeply blessed by this church—from the heartfelt worship to the powerful sermons. We've been attending for the past four to five years, and in that time, we've formed lasting friendships and found a true sense of community. I highly encourage getting involved, whether through volunteering or joining a Community Group (CG); both have been instrumental in helping us grow in our faith and our connection with others. If you're searching for a church home, I wholeheartedly recommend visiting.

I’ve had the pleasure to call New North Church home for almost 10 years now. I was looking for a non-denominational Christian church in SF that would be gospel centered, proper exegetical preaching of the word (even  if it’s counter to today’s culture), and had good worship. I’ve stayed for so long because they have become my family and have supported me through life’s ups and downs, given me resources to grow in my faith, allowed me to serve inside and outside the church, and is led by elders that I admire to be.

It’s hard to list everything, but here are a few more:
- Multi-generational and multi-ethnic
- Mid-week ministries outside of just Sunday service to make church feel like family
- Weekly running group
- Growing young adult group
- Huge focus on growing the children and equipping parents

reviews.text: I attended the church of Epiphany when I was a young child. And also went to the school. It was nice to go back and visit it's been fifty years.

This is a nice church and location, I dont normally go here. I was here for my Uncle funeral,
He was 100 yrs old. Mass started at 11am. The priest who held the prayer service  spoken really well in honoring my Uncle celebration of life and after we went to burial at Holy Cross arranged by The Duggans of Daly City Westlake.

Not sure they know what they’re doing.  Went to mass on Christmas Day in this beautiful and well maintained church.  There were maybe less than 30 worshippers in attendance.  Seating could have been restricted to the front third of the pews and those in attendance would still have been spaced far in excess of what is required for covid.  And you might have been able to hear each other pray.  As it was the 30 people were scattered throughout the grand hall so there was no way a sense of community could possibly develop. Had they done that, you still wouldn’t have been able to hear anyone sing as the organist did everything he could to smother the spirit of those in attendance by playing and singing as loud as possible.  Finally, the sermon was not spoken but read as though someone was afraid that the priest might say something improper, so they required him to read from an approved text.   As I’m perfectly capable of reading myself, they might as well have handed out a flyer for me to take home after mass.  There was nothing of this service that expressed the joy of Christmas but the décor…and the malls do that a whole lot better…as though Christmas means more to them.  It’s true, you do not go to church for the décor…and you do not need to go to church to pray…but you do go for fellowship and on Christmas you go to celebrate with alleluias and glorias and joy to the world.  Just wasn’t happening in this one.  In spite of all that, I was grateful to be at mass that morning.  Somehow the spirit managed to sneak through it all and into my heart.

reviews.text:

We've been there multiple times to watch the San Jose youth chamber orchestra where my daughter performs. The facility is a bit old and the stage is a bit cramped for their orchestra. The rest room facilities are small for the size of the place.

What matters though is the house acoustics which is very nice. And the seating is comfortable. So 4 stars for me.

Updates:

I received a response from the owner that I copied at the end of this post. Nice touch! It shows that they care!

I also like to add a very strong plus that I forgot to mention last time. There's a parking structure conveniently located right across the street. During the events, the parking is free and generally plentiful. For a theatre near downtown San Jose, it's a godsend..

Reply from owner to my previous review:

Thank you for your comments. Trianon Theatre is a historic building. There are two sets of restrooms - one on each floor. It is how the architect designed it. SJCO is driving at the Trianon, and we are glad we can also host the Youth Orchestra.

I went to a stand up comedy show in this theatre. It has 2 floors and has an antique setting. The auditorium in the first floor houses upto 150 people or so. There are restrooms in the first floor. Overall it's a small-medium sized theatre and is maintained neatly. It's also at a walkable distance to the VTA station.

This was probably glorious in its day and the Art Deco decor is still amazing. Antique light fixtures, elaborate pillars out front, and other features make this an historical treasure. However it's somewhat in decline on the exterior and could use a touch up. Inside it's lovely.

On the downside, I was there for a tech conference and the theater promised they could meet our internet needs but it was entirely inadequate. Many presentations were plagued with dropouts and stalls. I don't blame them for that but they shouldn't have promised something that didn't exist. There were other lesser failures to provide as well.

This would be a nice place for a theatre group, a musical ensemble, or perhaps a wedding reception but it wasn't suitable for our needs. They should have been more upfront about that.

reviews.text:
A Christ-centered Biblical church that is zealous of the things of God, with shepherds and men and women of God who desire to bring glory to God, and not to themselves. The disciples of Jesus at Hamilton Square Baptist Church have a sincere desire to walk down the difficult path that leads to salvation. The church’s emphasis on the real relationship between the individual and God rather than association with church institutions, emphasis on Jesus’s teachings on love and compassion for the needy, and emphasis on the severity of God’s judgment are strong points. They preach the whole Gospel, not watered down or sugar-coated.

The church is strong in Bible education through the Wednesday Night Bible Study with very well composed notes, the addiction class known as Freedom That Lasts, the Sunday Schools, and two Sunday services with very helpful notes, that come even with the original Biblical languages.

Many of these services are recorded for the convenience of listeners around the world.

If you want a man-centered, greedy, and Pharisee-like church, look elsewhere.

I add that an elder’s wife is on the board of a Christian charity that helps families and mothers in need, Alpha Pregnancy Center, which the members and leaders support.

Joyful worship, generous community, genuine love for your neighbor, and celebration of a loving God and of human diversity are all to be found here. I love this place, and it is truly special. reviews.text: What an incredibly beautiful treasure the Holy Virgin Cathedral Russian Orthodox Church is, not just to San Francisco, but also to the world! This is one of the six largest Russian Orthodox Churches in the world, outside of Russia. It’s absolutely stunning and you do feel a sense of awe just by walking inside. I haven’t been on a Sunday to attend the liturgy, but I could imagine that it would be very beautiful and touching, given how stunningly gorgeous this church is.

The Holy Virgin Cathedral rises with a quiet majesty, its golden domes catching the light like prayers lifted into the sky. There is a stillness here that feels deliberate, as if time itself slows out of respect for what has been held sacred for generations. The architecture speaks in symbols rather than words crosses, icons, and arches forming a language of faith, memory, and devotion. Even from the outside, the cathedral carries a sense of refuge, a place where reverence lingers in the air. The painted saints gaze outward not as spectators, but as guardians, offering a silent welcome to all who pass. It is a space that invites reflection, humility, and awe in equal measure. Standing before it, one feels not overwhelmed, but gently reminded of something eternal.
Such a beatiful and holy place. One of the most intense experiences I've ever had. A fragment of heaven descends upon this temple during liturgy. Glory to God unto the ages.

reviews.text:
Hidden Gem in Taos History, Faith & Local Flavor 🌄⛪

We came for breakfast at Ranchos Plaza Grill and ended up discovering one of the most beautiful and meaningful landmarks in New Mexico the San Francisco de Asís Catholic Mission Church. Located right in the heart of the historic Ranchos de Taos Plaza, this adobe masterpiece feels like stepping back in time.

The exterior is stunning classic Southwestern architecture with thick adobe walls, soft earthy tones, and twin bell towers against the deep blue sky. Inside, the church is peaceful and full of character: hand-carved wooden beams, traditional altar pieces, colorful candle racks, and warm natural light flowing through the windows.

We took a short self-guided tour, bought a candle, and lit it while saying a small prayer a touching experience even for visitors of different backgrounds. There’s free parking in the plaza (first come, first served) and a small shop nearby selling candles, crosses and local souvenirs.

After visiting the church, we walked right over to Ranchos Plaza Grill next door for a delicious breakfast the perfect combo of culture and local comfort food.
If you’re visiting Taos, this is an absolute must-stop for anyone who appreciates art, history, and authenticity.

📍 Ranchos de Taos, NM
🕊️ Peaceful, historic, and deeply inspiring

There is 2 hour parking on the street, but all taken by residents who have permits.  There is a paid parking garage about three blocks south, but there are many homeless and junkies there.  I would recommend using public transportation or uber and get dropped off right in front of the mission.

Mixed emotions. I love the California missions! I love the history. I love the beauty and the religious experience. But, all things considered; this is one of the smaller missions. It does have a small artifact collection but compared to some of the other missions, especially those in Southern California, it is not … as impressive.

Visiting Mission San Francisco de Asís was a wonderful experience. The historic church is beautifully preserved, and you can really feel the history of the area. The architecture and stained glass windows are impressive, and the peaceful courtyard makes it a perfect spot to reflect and take photos.

The staff were friendly and provided helpful information about the mission’s history and significance. It’s fascinating to learn about the early days of San Francisco and the role the mission played in the community.

I highly recommend visiting if you’re interested in history, architecture, or just want a quiet, beautiful place in the city.

Mission Dolores is a gem.  Much of it is original from 1791, when the church building was completed.  The simplicity of the interior is adorned by beautiful art. reviews.text: Wayman is so full of love. They really care for my family and myself. Lots of fun things for youth of all ages as well as adults. The love of God is all in this place and the anointing of the Holy spirit is definitely present. The people here are very humble. The pastor and his wife are truly a man and woman of God! They lead by example. I also really enjoy how they are able to keep the young people's attention. Right now during this pandemic many churches have not been able to function the same but Wayman A.M.E. Church is strong in the area of creativity. We haven't missed a beat. We have service for the young people on Zoom on Saturdays and boy oh boy! It is such a good time!! The kids get so excited come Friday because they know youth service is the next day. They are able to interact in the zoom and do activities. They sing and dance..... They play fun games, they actually are aloud to pretty much run the service because the leadership has done such an awesome job of teaching them! They work with kids and are so patient. Honestly, even my fiance and I get excited about it. We all attend youth service on Saturdays. It is such a good way to have family time and we really enjoy seeing our church family. When Sunday morning come around, we all rush down to the living room to be on time for service. They do such a great job!! The word of God come forth and you can feel the power of God even online!!! The church even sends out communion kits so you don't even have to miss that! They are so thoughtful!  They also do a lot in the community. We need more churches like this one for sure!! reviews.text: Up front that they consider a large portion of our community to be less than human.  You can verify on the website (carefully review their doctrinal statement, among other areas), other reviews here, reddit, online searches, Nextdoor, etc, so I'd recommend doing your homework.

I attended Bethlehem Baptist Church where Jason Meyer was the Pastor. While I was there I confided in him of my long history of being an abuse survivor. He betrayed my confidence in every way possible. That was proven by the many reports that were written about his resignation from BBC as he was accused of coddling abuse survivors. Namely me. I asked a couple I knew that attended BBC if they felt that Pastor Jason Meyer kept their conversations private. Their response - we believe Pastor Jason is a good guy that likes to make everyone happy. But no. He didn't keep anything we shared with him confidential. I suspected that he had betrayed my confidences and asked him about it, to which he vehemently denied over and over.
But then all the articles re: his resignation appeared and the coddling of abuse survivors was plastered every where. He betrayed my confidence and lied about it. Imagine what that was like for me finding out that way - that I was right about him all along and having to read about it in the newspaper.
While I attended BBC I had three separate surgeries. A hip replacement and two knee replacements. Pastor Jason prayed with me and told me I will not rest until I know you are okay. Those words I found to be heartbreakingly untrue. Pastor Jason after those three surgeries only  called me once after one of those knee replacements because I asked him to. The phone call cold, and abrupt. He prayed with me quickly and then he was gone. It was quite surprising and hurtful for someone who said they wouldn't rest until they knew I was doing after surgery - no visits, no phone calls, not lifting one finger to see how I was doing.  Pastor Jason Meyer's words are beautiful and eloquent and come across as very sincere. But over time his words became a sword.  I found out the hard way his words were filled with lies, betrayed confidences, and when as a Pastor I needed him the most  he would be nowhere to be found. I don't even know how to put into words the heartbreak he has caused me. But now that he is no longer a part of my life . All I can say, is Thank God.

reviews.text: I was just passing through the Twin Cities and visited this church on one Sunday morning. I was very impressed by the message - it was deep, practical and most importantly - it was Biblical. They also practiced open communion so I was able to take part in that. If I lived in the area, I would seriously consider joining this church. It is made up of legit followers of Christ.

This church was such a safe haven for us while we lived in the city. In the midst of the chaos of the world, this was a refreshing, life saving cup of the life saving water of Christ, consistently preaching Christ and the cross and not how we can add to what was already done. The steadiness of the preaching, the open arms of those that attend, and the care of the pastors there are hard to find in the self-focused world we live in. Highly recommend!

We are so grateful for Hiawatha and the impact it has had on our family. The expositional, gospel-centered preaching of the Bible is life-giving and has been life-changing for us. It’s all about Jesus and what He has done for us and never veers to the dangerous works-based theology that is prevalent in Christian churches. And the people…we absolutely LOVE these people! They love each other well, don’t take themselves too seriously, are filled with joy, and are people of integrity.

Love this church! The people are really genuine. They are about exactly what they say they are about: Jesus and what he has done for us. The leaders are humble, the band is talented, and the coffee is surprisingly good.

Hope focuses on emphasizing the importance of scripture and how the Gospel is evident throughout the Bible. Now, almost 7 years in, Hope has become my home and I am so thankful for all that Hope has added to my life! At Hope I am blessed to be a part of a loving community - both in my small group and through the Young Adults Ministry (YAM)! Forever grateful for Hope and the way I have been pointed to Jesus!

I started going to Hope 5 years ago after a quick Google search for churches in my area. What drew me in were the people that welcomed me and the Bible-centered style of sermons. I quickly joined a small group which became and continues to be a wonderful group of Believers who I study the Bible with, learn from, and can call my friends. I've been able to grow a lot in my faith since calling Hope my home church and am excited to see how God continues to use it to disciple other Believers in the Twin Cities area.

If you're looking for a church that is rooted in scripture and is based in theology, this is your place. All of the pastors are great preachers and are always dissecting the bible in ways I never thought to. I love it when preaching is based in strong theology so we have a clear understanding of the whole picture when looking at scripture.

The worship is amazing as well! It's basically all hymns, modernized by their worship leader Tim. It's extremely well done and a joy to worship to.

If you're looking for a new church, you need to come and try Hope Community Church. You won't regret it!

reviews.text: What a wonderful evening at the candle light concert featuring wizard of Oz music! The musicians were beyond talented & played so beautifully!

Came here as part of Doors Open Minneapolis. There wasn't anything going on at the time I went, but the building itself is architecturally fascinating. The two halves of the building were built over a century apart, yet come together relatively seamlessly. The church has an inward looking feel to it with its large dome and circular stained glass windows. The pipe organs you see are for show. The real pipes (nearly 5000 I believe) are beyond the ornamental pipes and some are from as far back as the 1920s. The circular layout is very distinct from the other churches like St. Mary's and St. Mark's in the area.

The newer section of the building has a very sleek modern look with bright naturally lit spaces and modern furniture. Very interesting building.

reviews.text: My home church so I will try to keep this as objective as possible. First, this is a Bible-based church. The pastor, while not using an expository style, cites Scripture extensively to support his points. Second, there is a strong emphasis on multi-generational activities, based on the principles from the book, Sticky Faith. Third, while not advocating the "social Gospel", there is a strong emphasis on community outreach (e.g. good relationships with local elementary schools and neighborhood organizations, hosting police, school, and community meetings and events, hosting an Hispanic church and working alongside them with events and fundraising for their programs). Fourth, a blended contemporary/traditional worship service. Fifth, a high level of lay involvement in ministries such as Vacation Bible Study, Sunday School, Wednesday Night meals and programs, Grief Share, Spice of Life, Kids 2, and other programs. Sixth, a growing young adult segment of the congregation. Seventh, an active small group ministry. Eighth, a friendly and welcoming congregation. Crosstown Covenant Church is a mid-sized  church with about 150 regular-attenders. The smaller size doesn't allow for as many ministries as a large church but because of the high level of volunteerism, there are more programs than similarly-sized churches. If you come, prepare for a conversation and if you join, prepare to become involved in a ministry.

This has been my family's church for 7 years.  We were first attracted to the passion of faith displayed by the members of Crosstown.  It is a very missional church that sends many missionaries overseas but also supports the Nokomis neighborhood association and Keewaydin school.  For the last 5 years, my family has had the opportunity to work with the Eagle's Rock after-school program for Keewaydin.  Crosstown is honored to provide a home for a Spanish church, Verbo En Accion, and any Sunday that we share worship together is a fantastic day!  If you visit, you'll find a multi-generational church family that welcomes you.  That's what I've experienced.

I came to this church after leaving the Catholic Church, hoping I had finally found a place that felt like home. I even brought my family and extended family here because I truly believed this would be the right community for us. But with everything happening in this state—the growing hostility toward brown and colored people, the fear that so many of us are living with—I expected this church to at least acknowledge what we’re going through, or offer some kind of support.

Instead, it’s been the opposite. It was heartbreaking to sit at home watching the service on TV because we were afraid of going out and possibly being targeted or arrested by ICE. With everything happening right here in Bloomington, I kept waiting for a word, a prayer, anything that showed awareness or compassion. But there was nothing.

For a church that calls itself “multigenerational” and “multicultural,” the silence was devastating. We can’t ignore the reality we’re living in. And after all this, we’ve decided we won’t be coming back.

A Heartfelt Commendation for Our Church Community-Rccg Cornerstone Parish, Anoka, Minnesota.

As a co-minister at our beloved church-The Redeemed Christian Church Of God, Cornerstone Parish in Anoka, Minnesota, I am continually inspired and uplifted by the unwavering faith and dedication of our congregation. From the moment I joined this wonderful community, I have been embraced with open arms and hearts full of love. The spirit of fellowship here is truly exceptional and exemplifies the teachings of kindness, compassion, and genuine care for one another.

Our church is more than just a place of worship; it is a sanctuary where individuals and families can find solace, hope, and a sense of belonging.The dedication of our members to serve others, both within our church and in the wider community, is nothing short of remarkable. Through outreach programs, charitable events, and acts of kindness, we embody the essence of Christ’s message to love and support our neighbors.

The leadership and guidance provided by our esteemed Lead Pastor Olayinka Charles-Oni, his wife Pastor Nikky and fellow ministers have been instrumental in nurturing our spiritual growth. Their insightful sermons, thoughtful prayers, and willingness to listen and offer counsel have had a profound impact on our lives. I am grateful to serve alongside such passionate and devoted individuals.

I am also particularly moved by the enthusiasm and energy of our youth in the choir who handled the drum sets and all other musical instruments. Their active participation in church activities and their eagerness to learn and grow in faith is a testimony to the strong foundation we are building for future generations.

Thank you, dear friends, for making our church a beacon of hope and a pillar of strength in Anoka. Your steadfast faith, boundless generosity, and unwavering support make this community feel like home. I look forward to continuing our journey together, growing in faith, and serving our Lord.

With heartfelt appreciation,

Deacon Oludotun Odujole.

reviews.text: I’ve been attending here since 2014. It hasn’t always been my home church, but it feels the most like home. I’ve been attending The House Church since 2021, and it’s been such an incredible blessing in my life! The sense of community here is unmatched—everyone is so welcoming and genuine, which makes it easy to feel at home. The worship is vibrant and uplifting, creating an atmosphere where you can truly connect with God and others.

The preaching is always on point—relatable, inspiring, and grounded in truth. Whether you’re new to faith or looking to deepen your relationship with God, The House Church is a place where you can grow, belong, and make meaningful connections. Come check it out, you won’t leave the same!

House Church offers a unique and enriching worship experience that truly sets it apart from traditional churches. From the moment I stepped in, I was struck by the genuine sense of community and warmth. The atmosphere is incredibly inviting, with a focus on creating personal connections and fostering spiritual growth.

The worship service is a beautiful blend of contemporary music and heartfelt prayer, led by passionate and talented musicians. The sermons are inspiring and thought-provoking, delivered with sincerity and relevance to everyday life. What I particularly appreciate is the emphasis on engaging and interactive discussions, allowing everyone to share their thoughts and experiences.

The leadership at House Church is exceptional. The pastors and volunteers are approachable, caring, and deeply committed to the well-being of the congregation. They make a concerted effort to know each member personally, providing support and encouragement both inside and outside of church activities.

In addition to the uplifting worship services, House Church offers a variety of small groups and community outreach programs. These initiatives provide opportunities for deeper connections, personal growth, and meaningful service to the community.

Overall, House Church is a place where you can truly feel at home. It’s a welcoming and inclusive environment that encourages spiritual exploration and fosters a sense of belonging. I highly recommend House Church to anyone seeking a vibrant and supportive faith.

It is not necessary to be any quantum of Native American Blood, or to have lineage in blood lines. We have a welcoming of all races, religion, sexual preferences. We combine our culture and heritage with how we understand the catechism. We don't have to give up who we are as Native Americans and become richer by being open to hearing gospel messages.  Hymns and many songs have been translated to Ojibwe and we sing in Dakota as well.

Please be respectful and humble when you come to avoid insult. We are open to helping you learn and understand what is happening.

This is a place that you follow your heart and mind to being. If this is a place for you, you will know it when you visit. Even if you visit once or a twice, you will be a better person because of it.

reviews.text: Charis Cornerstone Church is truly a place where you feel God’s presence and genuine love. Being part of Charis Cornerstone Church has honestly been such a great experience for me. I’ve had the chance to serve on the tech crew, and it’s been way more fun than I expected. I’ve learned how to run the slides, set up the music, and help with sound — and even though it was a little intimidating at first, everyone was super encouraging and patient as I figured things out. Now it’s something I really look forward to each week.

I also wanted to shout out the brand new church website — it just launched, and it looks amazing. It really captures the heart of our church. It’s clean, easy to navigate, and has everything someone new would need to know. Whether it’s service times, what we believe, or how to get connected, it’s all laid out in a clear and welcoming way. I’m excited for more people to check it out because it honestly feels like an extension of who we are as a church — warm, Christ-centered, and real.

If you’re thinking about visiting or just want to get a feel for what Charis Cornerstone is all about, the new website is a great place to start. But the best part is still what happens in person — a church full of people who love Jesus and love each other. I’m really grateful to be a part of it. This is Jeremiah

If you’re looking for a place to grow in your faith and be surrounded by people who care, I honestly can’t recommend this church enough.

reviews.text:
My husband and I were married at Saint Olaf, and our ceremony was absolutely beautiful. The church itself is stunning, and our wedding day felt truly special.

We were blessed to work with Father Wehmann, who was fantastic throughout the entire process. He was responsive, supportive, and genuinely wanted the ceremony to feel meaningful and personal. His guidance leading up to the wedding and his message on the day were perfect. We also had a wonderful experience working with Joel Anderson, the music director. He was friendly, welcoming, and incredibly helpful in making sure everything flowed smoothly and stayed connected to our readings. The cantor was also lovely and did a phenomenal job.

We greatly appreciated the livestream and recording of the ceremony. Family members who couldn’t attend were able to watch, and the recording was sent quickly and beautifully captured the day.

The only challenge we experienced was with communication while working with the liturgical director. As an out-of-town couple, it was difficult to schedule meetings, and responses were often delayed, which caused stress as the wedding approached. Some details were finalized very close to the ceremony, and there was inconsistency between what was rehearsed and what occurred on the wedding day. Thankfully, Father Wehmann helped ensure everything came together.

Overall, Saint Olaf is a wonderful church with a beautiful space and many dedicated staff members. With more streamlined communication, the experience could be even better. We would absolutely recommend Saint Olaf for a wedding — the ceremony itself is something we will cherish forever.

reviews.text:
This is a lovely little church! I was here for a meeting, and not yet for Mass. However, I am going to get there soon, and will let you know what that is like also. I was impressed by the fact that they have an elevator and the place is SPOTLESS! However, and this is the best part, is that the church has built in spaces that are big enough for a wheelchair or a walker to fit into within the pews so that a person who has a disability is able to go to Mass WITH their family and friends. St. Leonard of Port Maurice, in Minneapolis, MN exemplifies EXACTLY what the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops (USCCB) mean when they said " If one person is not there, (because of a disability), the church is not complete."  I am extremely used to going to a Catholic church, and seeing the "disability section, in the front, all wheelchairs and walkers together. Or TRYING to get in the section, by the pillars, or the section in the back, (You  KNOW how Catholics bob up and down). You can feel seasick. However, you don't feel part of the Church. I know that others have felt the same way.  Particularly when you came with family or friends, but cannot sit with them.I suppose you could be on your own if you have a medical emergency. However, this one thing, where I am easily able to get into and sit as part of the congregation, is the first Catholic Church in my experience that has done it correctly. If you have a Church that does it"The Right Way", please let me know. I love Good News! I do know that people who sit together in a "Handicap
Section" are friends and care about each other. All I am saying is that I LOVE the space.at St. Leonards of Port Maurice. Next Sunday, wheel yourself speedily to this church!
Next thing I have to work on are the confessionals, everywhere.

A little leaven leavens the whole lump. I know that the right person will see this review as it isn't for everyone-not everyone is truly seeking to honor The Lord. Many, in fact, MOST, are not seeking Him at all as His word has made clear.

I would review their website and then take some time to visit and sit with them, ask questions, lots of questions about their views, about church discipline. Church discipline is not meant to shame just as biblical correction (that we are called to) doesn't and isn't meant to. It is all meant to turn someone who could be straying back from their way.

Anyone who is profiting must be prayed for, prayed over and discipled so that mammon does not begin to compromise their views. Eric Mason makes lots of books and had recently began to try to bring in a 'cool factor' that I prayed on privately. I was sad and surprised to see that weed from a few years ago has grown into posing with known false teachers especially when he could counsel Mike Todd in private. You've now served as an agent of confusion further leading many astray.

With that Dear Christian that The Lord will have to see this post, I would be very careful. A lack of reverence to Our Lord is dangerous, a lack of love for others is as well.

reviews.text:
We were married here a few years ago, and I still think about how magical and seamless our day was thanks to everyone at Gloria Dei. The staff are all true professionals, and they made sure every detail came together perfectly. The wedding coordinator, Amy, was especially wonderful — kind, patient, and incredibly helpful from start to finish. We could not have done it without her!

The church itself is breathtakingly beautiful, with historic charm and romantic grounds that made us feel like we had stepped straight into a Jane Austen novel.

It was an unforgettable, gorgeous day, and we are forever grateful for the kindness, dedication, and care shown to us. I highly, highly recommend Gloria Dei for tying the knot!

PS — I know this review is long overdue, my sincerest apologies, but I didn’t want to miss the chance to share how thankful we are.

Really nice place to take a walk or let your dog run around. Has a lot of charm. It’s interesting to stroll through the graves and read the old headstones. In the front of the church is a brick walk lined with cherry blossoms. Check it out at the end of March to see them in full bloom. We were just a little too late but still got to enjoy a few blooms. I would love to visit this church for service sometime.

There's is a part of me that selfishly wants to keep this church and community to myself. Reverend Chris, Christine and the entire staff and community of Gloria Dei are amazing and made my wedding day perfect. I wanted to be married in a church full of history that was forward thinking and all inclusive (as religion should be). It was absolute perfection. If you are looking for a place to get married that encompasses love, community, history and inclusiveness, along with a stress free environmental....Here is it.

Gloria Dei Old Swedes Episcopal Church holds the performance of St Lucia every Christmas time. In Sweden the celebration is held in homes before dawn on the 13th of the month which is her Saints day.
The church is one of the oldest in the county. This was the 88th anniversary of the pageant honoring St Lucia. It's a great show held in a wonderful place of worship.
The church does have a congregation with weekly services.
There is also a church graveyard with many very old graves including those of original settlers. There is plenty of on street parking.

One of the most peaceful and lovely churches in Philadelphia. It would be perfect if there wasn’t the constant hum of traffic noise from both sides of the church but if you can concentrate on the beautiful structures and grounds and merciful breezes you may be able to block out the noise. The church itself is quaint and well-maintained with slim pews and a modest alter. The grounds are quite large with historic gravesites and a few benches for sitting in quiet contemplation. The grounds seem to be quite safe with a daycare on site and frequent visitors strolling throughout the grounds. The trees are substantial and seemingly very old with plenty of birds chirping and whistling. Close to perfection.

reviews.text: Those people are for real! I felt the Holy Spirit all up & through there.

I usually don't post reviews but today I must share my experience the church is a great place and some people are welcoming not all, the Ushers need more training on respect and how to communicate properly if a person doesn't want to sit down then you should not say to them in a demanding way we're not asking you to sit down we're telling you to sit down here's my thing if a person is not in the aisles and/or in the way causes a scene or not they are grown men and women you don't demand nothing if the person doesn't want to sit down and they way to stand up on the wall or by the door then leave them alone, secondly last I check unless your having a processional you can exit out of any door you don't tell people you can't exit the same door they came in on when entering and exiting the sanctuary then only thing a person can not do is go down the aisle when the rope is up they have to use the side aisles this does not apply to the doors I had no issue with the female Ushers it is the male usher that is unprofessional and did not display Christian couresty if I was a member I would leave and find a new church because how I was raised that was unacceptable the Ushers are the first person that usually greets you and the first impression is always the lasting impression this is why the church is struggling to maintain membership we must always show Christian courtesy and respect to everyone it is my prayer that the Ushers will get the proper training on how to conduct themselves more respectfully my suggestion is to take a page out of the Pennsylvania Baptist Ushers Brotherhood a person should never experience what I did today.

I fail in love with the teachings of pastor Harrison, the motivation to move on and forward in life.  Growing up in the slum of north Philadelphia I didn't no that young brothers like pastor Harrison existed , or sisters at that.  My heart wasn't set on college or school I was fighting demons that I thought only men could cure. I have never seen a young brother so beautiful.   I wanted to experience the life of him and people like him, I had to do better.  I never knew God ,the holy and the body of Christ could be so beautifully wrapped up in a human.  Doctor Harrison is an trend setter for young folks our age and younger folks to follow and for older folks to still believe in Jesus Christ and that he will be there to come get us.  Pastor Harrison is definitely (rev.) Sullivan's hope. I no he wants to travel and spread the gospel all over the world and I wanna be selfis but he is a star to the eye and a bird  🐦 to the ear. He and Zion are truly blessings. I hope pastor Harrison stay forever so we can continue to see hope and keep learning.

I had the pleasure of visiting your church 40 years ago when you were a part of hosting IAOHRA ‘83. Your distinguished spiritual leader, Dr. A. Leon Sullivan, was an influential Christian man who left an indelible print on many global human rights advocates and workers, which included me (a multigenerational Black Canadian). We subsequently invited him to Halifax, Nova Scotia. To this day I am grateful for his agreement to come and share. His philosophy of inclusion in hiring policies and self sufficiency still resounds. Truly he was a trailblazer.
Sincerely,
Dr. Carolyn G. Thomas, (Retired)
Nova Scotia Human Rights Commission

reviews.text: Great little place! The venue outside was a nice-looking church with messages on it of peace and blm. The showroom was small, tight, and rather hot. They did attempt some ac by way of ceiling fans and a larger fan blowing cold air from somewhere else next to stage right, so there was that. The bands were awesome and the crowd was very active. The crowd nearly filled the room completely! I would recommend going to this venue at least once. My only issue is that some of the equipment from the stage is very old and a little dirty, and there are no bathrooms either.

This church is very performative, while it is LGBTQ friendly, it is not community centric. No one in this church is actually getting their hands dirty helping to feed or clothe people. This is definitely a church that will tell you they don’t have any baby formula/can’t help you when you need help. While the rev puts on a pretty smile, she doesn’t respond to requests to meet with visitors to discuss homelessness in the community. I know this because after speaking to her in person, she told me to email her and then never responded to my email, it’s been months now.

Most of the collections go towards building maintenance and salaries- we’re talking 99% of it. A very small portion went to Philabundance during the month of September 2025 but thats it. This church hosts “brunches” with the expectation of members bringing dishes to share, without outwardly asking for members to bring dishes to share, so there will often be a dozen cookies to feed 100 people and thats it.

One pro is that there is childcare available during the service. But I really can’t get over the anti-homeless agenda they carry. While they can say whatever they want during services, the reality is they lock the gates to the only respite from the rain outside - for no good reason! Once we stayed after for an event and found ourselves LOCKED IN! I believe this goes against fire code!!

In conclusion, if you are a do-nothing out of touch emotionally sensitive white person you will fit right in. Good luck trying to get any genuine action or initiative out of this church.

Rating the basement venue where concerts are held. I wish I could like this venue bc it seems to be iconic for punk shows, but this is my least favorite venue. No show lighting and no air conditioning. We were all sweating and breathing is uncomfortable. Weak ceiling fans and one is completely broken. The sound cut out multiple times during the show. There's also no bar obviously, but that's okay—it is nice that the venue is BYOB. Bathrooms are well kept. Parking is difficult if you're figuring it out for the first time. I recommend the lot on the corner of Market and S 22nd (entrance on Market). It would be nice if the church could include info about parking on their website for events other than for exclusive church goers

While our schedule listed breakfast, lunch, and breaks, I was disappointed to learn that, aside from water, they provided no free food whatsoever. I don’t have a car, so I can’t just drive off-site to get meals elsewhere, let alone coffee (the Cafe closed after lunch!!!). It was an expense I hadn’t planned for. Had I known, I would’ve packed something, but nobody informed me. Since they ran out of salads, I had 2 hard-boiled eggs for lunch, with zero breakfast. I wonder how this speaks to the issue of hospitality as Christians? I felt very un-welcome here.

formatted_address: 6391 Church Rd, Philadelphia, PA 19151, United States
name: The Church in Philadelphia

reviews.text:
The movement birthed out of the vision of Witness Lee for the most part is pure.  I have visited the 'Local Church' in both TN and Texas and witnessed a deep unity and love for Christ.

This specific group in the Philadelphia district is odd.  I came to the group with my brother Christ who has done mission work with me for many years. In fact he suffered much for the sake of Christ even among his own family. Eventually like other mission organization we had bought a house, due to coming back to the states empty handed and wanting to be a burden on no one (for instance Overland Missions has a house with a bunch of single guys who travel and save up and have a place to come back to)  When we came to this group we were practically ignored. During the love feast no one talked to us except 2 people who said hi and another person doing an interrogation. In this persons favor Bill went to several people wanting to introduce us and almost every one of them declined, to the point he himself was embarrassed.

Eventually I just decided to overlook the situation, went to the prayer meeting and had a nice welcome, the next prayer meeting we went to it was clear the people were no longer allowed to communicate with us.  The same attitude within the Sunday service caught up with the prayer meeting.  During prophesy time on several Sundays when 'prophesying' it felt as if the words were flowing but being disrupted by someone sowing discord among the brethren, it felt as if a violation of something sacred was happening.

Russell was acting odd (will get back to that).

Eventually we traveled to the other district outside of Philly. The welcome was warm and the Spirit of the Lord flowed so freely. In fact just like the other times we were both invited to eat and to come to bible study. Then something odd happened we were both uninvited.    At this point it was obvious someone was sowing discord.  The problem is no one confronted either of us about the 'Serious sin' committed.  A brother than came to us out of concern and said what we 'felt' in our spirit was correct and should possibly be addressed openly.

When it was almost time to deal with the situation Russell would just toss Bill at us.  Bill is not the problem Russell was the issue. Several times Russell would ask who we knew in Texas.  Once was OK when it kept being asked consistently it became suspicious and odd.

I have ardently defended this movement and got several Youtubers shut down who slandered Witness Lee and the group. I did this using sound theology and in context statements from Witness Lee.
So after defending the movement itself this behavior was very cult like and violated clear scriptural guidelines when dealing with a brother.

We were two straight males on fire and loving Jesus (not gay) who were actually being treated as if we were in some type of sin (maybe someone in the group was jealous and decided to be used of the adversary to pitch an accusation). Being isolated marks a clear problem within the church.   Why were people told to ignore us without us being confronted directly?  This violated anything having to do with holiness.

It is my prayer this church humbly repents for receiving people suspiciously.   Witness Lee himself speaks against this. I have been a Christian since 1998 was healed of a stutter and filled with the Spirit many years ago, never have I been treated this bad by a believing community as this one. I was even kicked out of my home at 16 when leaving to the beach to go pray, so I know what it is like to take on the wounds of Christ.

Unless this church sincerely repents I would not recommend it. The leadership is immature. If someone comes to an elder gossiping it should not be entertained but stopped. In the multitude of words sin is not lacking.  If someone came to me gossiping about another individual I would take the person to that person and work as a mediator to bring peace.  This would shut down the devil from operating in the camp.

Russell I am guessing has sway in the movement. How are elders this immature promoted?

My experience at this location was pretty weird. The other locations I visited seemed to be healthy and spiritually strong. This one was not the same. People ignored my friend and I outright. It does not take ‘discerning of spirits’ to figure this out. At this location (A) things were strange.

All I know is IF a brother sins against you we have an obligation to go to them and confront them especially if you think a mistake was made carelessly. This can’t be done when biblical protocol is outright ignored or worse violated.

It was apparent we were being isolated felt ‘off’ in the Spirit. For this to happen gossip and suspicion had to be at play. It was as if everyone else had been talked with.

There are violations in the Spirit caused by their actions leading to degradation and breeches caused from directly violating Biblical Order on confrontation. I will add Witness Lee in his writings warns against suspicious elders.

(Slight backtracking)
It was my objective after attending in TN due to the unexpected death of my father to get back to PA and fully plug in. Instead I found myself exploring what to do. I had a sincere heart. When attending district A things where awkward & Was blessed & relieved that a brother said hello and let me know there was another location district B that was closer to me. I was able to attend 1 visit it felt lighter in the Spirit - healthier and there was a beautiful time of flowing & prophecy. We were invited to the big blending conference we where going to help pay for rooms but told expenses are covered, ate lunch with everyone, shared more, and was invited to Bible study later in the week. Everything was Great!

(Tuesday) I felt troubled and prayed.
Now it was at the end of the week (Friday) when the Bible study was scheduled. No contact had been made and hadn’t received any addresses of where to meet. I wasnt sure if it was the Sweet lady who gave out info, location changed, or something else occurred.

I inquired with one of the brothers & I could tell was on a gag order. Essentially there’s still a Meeting going on but he doesnt know what is happening or why we weren’t included and that my # was confirmed to be passed.
I felt encouraged to address the issues publicly/also didnt want to get involved in whatever drama is going on in the Philadelphia Church.
I found out Suddenly we were no longer invited to Conference also (was it Russell? At this point who knows) Another brother within the group eventually told us something was wrong and it wasn’t right. This man was a righteous brother in Christ.

Being a missionary, risking my life, and suffering rejection from family to follow the call of God this treatment was disturbing! I’ve never been treated this way in any community.

Thankfully the Lord healed my heart from the wounds inflected, and it caused me to grow and trust my spirit more when something ‘feels’ off.

We are two friends/ brothers in Christ who do missions work that focuses on Jesus. Most missionary societies save on expenses long term & buy a house so we followed example & planned on it being used to help other missionaries who need a place to stay while traveling in U.S. and can’t afford outright cost of living due to giving everything overseas.

At one point my Brother & I thought maybe they thought we were gay? (but quickly dismissed it as that would be ridiculous and that demonic slander would be put to rest if asked) laughed it off but we were treated as if abominable. 😬 and commited some grave sin.

I felt that things needed to be posted again as no apologies where ever made.
This place has potential but the immaturity cast a very dark shade on this location. Everything was done in secret.

When an elder is walking in the light things like this do not need to be said publicly.  Whomever started slander and entertained it None of you knew me I attended 5 times!!  It is my prayer that the Lord shows mercy. without KNOWING Brian nor myself you are forgiven and the Lord loves you greatly. May this strike be a kindness and ointment to you according to Psalm 141:5

Urban Worship is truly a place of worship! I pray that God continues to bless this church. I want to share how I ended up at Urban. I’ve been saved since 2019 and serving faithfully throughout the years. We all go through different seasons, missions, and areas of growth.

Before transitioning to Urban, I was in constant prayer. I wanted more of God and kept asking Him what is my purpose. One morning, as I was getting ready for church, the Lord spoke to me and told me to visit this church. I wrestled with whether it was my own emotions or truly God speaking. I prayed again, and then He used my family to confirm it.

I visited at the end of March of this year, and before walking in, I asked God to show me if this was where I needed to be. From the greeters at the door all the way to leadership, I was welcomed with genuine love. You could feel the love of God. Pastor Ivette embraced me and my daughter and welcomed us as if we had always been part of the family. God is so perfect in all He does, and He knew that in this new season, I needed to simply sit and receive.

Pastor José and Pastor Deb are truly a blessing from God. Every sermon, every conversation, every encounter carries the love and presence of the Lord. My prayer is that as we enter this new year, we come together in community to share God’s love—that it be a season of revival where we witness lives transformed. That we grow as one body and continue to seek the Lord wholeheartedly.

And let me just say… the discipleship class is fire! May the Lord continue to bless this church and pour His blessings over our pastors.

reviews.text:
Come and experience the joy of being filled with the Spirit! As you pull into the parking lot, your ears will delight in the uplifting melodies of the show choir, their harmonies weaving through the air and lifting your spirit even before you enter. Stepping through the church doors, you are met with warm, heartfelt greetings from friendly faces that make you feel like part of the family.
You pass through another set of doors and are welcomed into the vibrant sanctuary. The heart of our community of born-again believers. Here, you will find an atmosphere alive with rejoicing, as we sing, fellowship, worship, and ardently praise the one true living God. The presence of the Holy Spirit is palpable, filling the room with a sense of peace and joy that is truly transformative.
As the Word of God is preached with passion and conviction, it's delivered exactly as it is written, leaving you spiritually enriched and inspired. The sense of belonging is undeniable, and it's clear that this is a place where worship flourishes. I absolutely cherish every moment spent in worship here! My love for the Lord and my brothers and sisters in Christ runs deep as we gather to honor the most High God. Whether you attend in person or connect online, you can partake in this worship experience no matter where you are, the spirit of the service transcends the physical space. Our beloved Pastors, J. Dykeman Brown, and Sandra Brown, as well as the co Pastors, are vessels filled with the Holy Spirit, conveying the Word of God in a way that leaves no doubt of His living presence and boundless worthiness of our praise. Hallelujah! He is truly worthy to be praised! Thank you, Jesus, for the blessing of this church community! Come by and experience it for yourself, you’ll leave with a heart full of gratitude and joy!

I am deeply saddened to share my experience as a former member of this church. During a difficult time in my life, I sought support and community here, but instead I was met with hurt. One Sunday, in the middle of service, the pastor sent a gentleman to tell me that my autistic son was a “distraction” to his audience. My child could not attend the children’s group because of his autism, and we were doing our best to participate respectfully. When I reached out to this church for help during a hard season, it was nearly impossible to get any meaningful assistance or follow-up. In contrast, a local Catholic church not only offered immediate help, but also checked in to ensure my family was doing well. Sadly, I have noticed that some churches focus more on appearances and drawing people in rather than truly living out the love and compassion of Christ.
Thankfully, I have since found another church that welcomed my autistic son with open arms and patiently helped him work through his anxiety until he felt comfortable.

reviews.text: Peaceful.  A calm stop on a busy day. A visit to Christ Church was a welcome bit of down shifting on our tour of American History.  No crowds of kids, no lines, no interactive displays - just peace and quiet and, of course, more history.  I think my favorite thing was sitting in the pews of famous American patriots.

My husband and I go to a lot of cemeteries, but we had no idea that there were vaults in the church. The tour guide was very knowledgeable and gave us a lot of history on the church and the vaults. It also had a beautiful garden.
Really beautiful church and very kind staff. It was free to get in, but they accept donations. You can see where the founding fathered are buried and where they sat in church!

An interesting church and well worth the visit. Well laid out, excellently maintained and full of historical references both inside and out. Whilst the main burial fround for this church is a couple of blocks further down the road, there is also plenty of interest in the burials that surround the chuch, including signatories of the Declaration Of Independence.
The organ inside the main body of the church is magnificent and there are historic bells both inside and outside.
It's worth noting that the church doesn't shy away from it's former parishioners involvement in the slave trade, including the weeping time
I would suggest that it's slightly overpriced if you are just visiting this church without one of the multi-venue tickets.

Beautiful church with a neat and well-maintained surrounding area. The photos were taken on the evening of October 31, 2024. I wanted to go inside and take some beautiful shots of the interior, but unfortunately, the church was closed.

The pastor of the church told the people attending God spoke to him and it was time to be leaving the women were in a uproar crying 😢 and one in particular one row back in the next idle to our right was literally screaming 😱 please pastor don't go.
