Good spot for funeral  just need to clean more
Don't know too much about this place. I went there once for a co-worker's funeral and the church members were very welcoming.

formatted_address: 1195 Centre St, Boston, MA 02132, United States
name: Charles River Church

reviews.text: I am originally from Texas and have had a tough time finding a church home in Boston. I came across Charles River Church while on a run and have loved it! They have an incredible community! They are very welcoming and the teachings are deeply rooted in the Bible.

My family and I started attending CRC last year during their outdoor services and never left. This church is filled with friendly people who are real and willing to share the ugly stuff about who they are, which gives me the freedom to do the same. It's a very caring and supportive community.  It is diverse, with solid biblical teaching, lively heart-felt worship, a strong focus on serving others, and lots of opportunities for people of all ages to connect outside of church. If you're looking for a church in Boston, I highly recommend  you check this one out.

A few years ago, I approached a tough roadblock in life that caused me to sought out God and reconnect with my long abandoned faith. As an androgynous lesbian, it’s hard to find a church that won’t judge me. After sitting in multiple worships and different churches, I found this one. At the time it was just Sunday worship in a Middle school in West Roxbury. Not only was worship held in a middle school auditorium, without glorious Christian decor, but no one dressed in their Sunday best. The longer I sat in that worship the more I realized this church accepts all, just like how God accepts all, no matter where you are, what you’re dressed… he accept you for who you are.

Now the worship that first day, somehow I felt like it was drafted for me. Every word of the sermon and hymn sang, was exactly what I needed to hear. I cried the 75% of the worship.

It’s been 4 years, they finally found an appropriate church building. Still minimalistic, but that’s how it should be. Glad I’m still a member here.

We moved to Boston from the UK a year ago. We received a wonderful welcome at CRC and immediately felt it was a church family we could be part of. We enjoy the heart felt worship and bible centered teaching. The youth and children‘s ministries have also been a huge blessing.

As a college student, I have found this church to be incredibly awesome. We are often guilty of looking for a church that agrees with where we already stand, rather than a church that agrees wholly with the Bible. Charles River Church is the closest thing I have found to an authentic New Testament church. They strive to love the community and preach the Gospel faithfully. However, if you have never been to church, there is no need to be anxious, for the community is warm and welcoming. Everyone looks out for each other and genuine faith is producing an environment of love. You will find people who are following Christ's command of sacrificial love which is what our world could use a lot more of. This is definitely a place where you will can trust that they will preach the truth even when it is hard to take. If you decide to visit, you can be sure you will leave with more of God's word poured into your life.

formatted_address: 1500 Blue Hill Ave, Mattapan, MA 02126, United States
name: Jubilee Christian Church

reviews.text: This is a great place to worship and fellowship with others. The Pastors are amazing there is plenty of parking and good people to direct you. If viking Boston and you need a place to worship this is it 3 services on Sunday and Friday morning prayer in the sanctuary.
It's was a wonderful Home going of a lost one services was something that I never expect at a church. It's worth going back for Sunday Services to hear the word of God.

Atmosphere 2023 has been incredible. ❤️ the presence of the Lord truly is in this place. Also come ready to jump and leap out your chair. From baby to elders everyone screams shouts and jumps for the Lord. It’s so litt!!! That’s how Gods house should be!!!🙌🙌🙌

It's a good family-friendly church with a warm, welcoming atmosphere. The sermons are solid, and the people are friendly and happy. However, I did find the amount of instruction a bit overwhelming for my taste. At every service, you're asked to interact with the person sitting next to you. This can be fine if you're with family, but if you're sitting next to strangers, it can feel uncomfortable, especially in the post-COVID environment.
Outstanding Bible based teaching.  The worship is out of this world

formatted_address: 88 Tremont St, Boston, MA 02108, United States
name: Tremont Temple Baptist Church

reviews.text:
This church is absolutely beautiful and breathtaking. Please understand that only maintenance has been done for upkeep, I don’t believe it’s handicap friendly (didn’t check this sorry!) but wow!

You walk in and kept help but just stare and look up.

Came here for a conference and I’m excited and hopeful to comeback again and explore more!

If you are considering going to church, Tremont Temple Baptist Church, is a biblically faithful congregation grounded on the authority of scripture. The sermons are expository, taught verse by verse, of sound doctrine, avoiding the tickling of ears you are likely to find at so many other ‘churches’ in the local area. We enjoyed warm fellowship with other believers during our visit from New Mexico. The history of the church and building are also fascinating, and worth digging into.

Great church example of all the SOLAS scriptures in one place.
And just like in Revelations, you find people of every tribe and language.

The Pastor is known for being humble and caring.

My family has visited this congregation on various occasions, but our home address is too far for regular attendance. Though we are members of our own local church, if we ever moved to Boston, we’d be blessed to join Tremont. Leadership and laypersons alike have always been warm and welcoming. Their preaching is the definition of excellence as they are faithful to adhere to the scriptures. The same can be said about the worship music. It’s a wonderful multigenerational and diverse group. Check it out if you live in the area!

Highly recommend this church for any believers who love the whole Word of God being preached! Deep theological worship songs, expository sermons, and encouraging fellowship! I was a visitor here for one week and knew this church would be one I’d attend if I lived near the area. Thank you, Pastor Jaime and the family at Tremont Temple for your focus on Christ in everything!

formatted_address: 351 Boylston St, Boston, MA 02116, United States
name: Arlington Street Church

reviews.text:
Absolutely beautiful architecture, amazing history, and a living and breathing spirit within. The musicians are lovely, the Ministers are wonderful to listen to, and the congregation is friendly and happy to be there.

If you ask ahead of time or ask very nicely after worship is over, you may be lucky enough to get a tour of the sanctuary and bell tower, and hear the many historical stories the church has in store. This isn't something that happens very often, but it's not impossible.

The church was okay but I like a livelier setting. The church consisted of older adults and there were no children to have them come up to the front for a quick reading or short activity before being dismissed for religious education. The part I disliked was there was no air conditioning and the seats were pews and they were sectioned off like penalty boxes in ice hockey. The church was large and absolutely beautiful, however. It looked like it was once used for Catholic Mass.

We stopped here to see the Tiffany stained glass windows and they did not disappoint..!

$5 donation per person to experience those - knock on the Boylston Street lower side door to gain entry.

Gives really nice tours and provides lots of information for visitors. Tiffany styled stain glass Windows are its highlight, and its history and that beautiful organ is its star! Very Serene and fills you with satisfaction as you tour through it. People practice music as sound reverberates through the halls.

A beautiful sermon about moving forward. It's so so geourgeos and breathtaking there. I 100% want to go again. We took a tour and got to ring bells in the tower which was amazing. Highly recommend going whoever you are GO.

formatted_address: 15 Newbury St, Boston, MA 02116, United States
name: Emmanuel Church in the City of Boston

reviews.text:
We got married here in late September and had the absolute best experience. Robb who coordinated our wedding day made the process so easy. On our actual day, I remember commenting to my now husband, how organized the church staff was in the wedding proceedings. We walked down the aisle to the organ in which was organized by Robb and we had also hired a bagpiper. I would choose this place to get married over and over again and I highly recommend. Not to mention the space is absolutely breathtaking.
The church itself is a large supporter of the LGBTQ+ community as well as the alcoholics anonymous community in which we are largely involved in. That being said, the fee that we paid to get married here went to causes/communities that we support.!!

Lindsey Chapel at Emmanuel Church is one of the prettiest european style chapels in the city. It feels very English. Long and narrow with soaring ceilings, it is the perfect spot for a Boston wedding ceremony!
I went to the Sunday 10am service mainly to hear the music. The entire service was about 90 minutes. I read that some very famous conductors come every once in a while.

I experienced the true miracle of Easter. I happened to park in front of this church in early morning hours. I was exploring the Newbury street and the commonwealth avenue. As I was approaching my car on my way back, I could have sworn I heard angelic voices in my earphones that weren't part of my audiobook. Apparently I wasn't losing it yet! It was a voice of one of the choral singers practicing in her car. After a bit of chat she invited me into the church for the easter rehearsal.

Wonderful smiling deacon Bob made sure I felt really welcome. After learning that I wasn't going to stay for the 10 o'clock service ( I had to go visit my brother's family and wake up my children at the hotel) Bob offered me a communion. Then he introduced me to the priest and I got a wonderful history tour of the church.

But the miracle doesn't stop there. Bob and Jane convinced me to stay until the beginning of the service to witness a beautiful procession of the animals.

What a spectacular display of human warmth and holiday blessings, this is My favorite place now and forever when I come visit Boston.

Went to their weekly Wednesday art day through Common Cathedral. I was hoping to meet up with people and feel like I had community. Instead all the staff and all the guests ignored me even when I was crying. Maybe it was because my arm was in a brace or I was wearing a rainbow bracelet. Made me feel very lonely, sad and less than. I went on Wednesday April 2,2025. I will not be going back. Jesus loves me even when this group cannot welcome me as I am for whatever reason.

formatted_address: 16 Beech St #1, Cambridge, MA 02140, United States
name: Hope Fellowship Church

reviews.text:
Got connected to this church a couple of decades ago through my home church near Dallas, Tx and it continues to be my church home away from home whenever I can get up to the Boston area.  The church leadership makes a big effort to serve the community so it is not simply about coming to a sermon on a Sunday.  There are many who have come through Hope, serve, and gone on to start other churches or lead in other ways throughout the city.  That is the way it should be!  It is an outward focus about reaching as many with the Gospel as possible.

I always feel so welcomed there and if you are reading this and trying to find a Bible-believing, Bible-teaching church where you can be known and encouraged to you use own gifts and strengths to serve God and the community... I highly recommend giving them a try.  Just a short walk from Porter Square.  If that is too far for you depending on where you live in Boston, they can also gladly help you find somewhere closer to you.  I pray this little review helps you in your journey.

Great Church I was invited there thank you, I enjoyed it because everything was very friend from the time you step in the door you could tell there was a lot of thought put into the service.  People greeting you coffee and snacks to give you energy for the service.  Wow and full band on stage to sing with and all the words on screen.  Last but not least the Pastor was great he explained the sermon so well I felt I learn so much it was great.  Thank You Hope Fellowship Church.
One of my absolute favorite places on the whole entire earth. Wonderful, warm people that love Jesus. Messages are full of grace and truth and very comfortable.
Great place clean great mass

There is a sense of real community here through good times and bad.  The teaching is usually quite good and you can see exactly where the pastor is getting his conclusions from in the Bible, so that you can think through it yourself as well.

name: Mosaic Boston Church

reviews.text: The Longwood Towers residential community has made a disappointing downturn recently since this church bought and took over the event space. Initially, I wanted to keep an open mind given the potential family friendly environment they appear to embody, but after some unpleasant interactions I did research and discovered what they're preaching. I find their ultra conservative platform to be a poorly thought out addition to a residential complex in a historically LGBTQ+ friendly area. I can't help but fear for the safety of some of our community members especially given the pastor self proclaims on the church website that they moved from their old leased location because the building owner displayed a pride flag outside.

I loved this beautiful building. I was told it is the oldest synogogue in Boston. Just beautiful.
The church service was just what I needed. The worship team was great and the sermon was delivered well.

We love this church.
Preaching is Gospel centered, congregation + visitors are welcomed by a wonderful greeting team. Also, MiniMosaic - “Sunday school” for kids is a safe, loving place.

This body of believers has been a gift to our family (of six!) in more ways than one. Before living in Boston, we were encouraged in spirit and in truth through Mosaic's Biblical teaching (we found online). God made a way for our family before we even arrived through the hard work, sacrifice, and heart of the believers in Boston, specifically at this local congregation. Once local, we were warmly loved (prayed for, cared for, looked after) through community. We were unexpectedly blessed ten-fold through the excellence and priority of a strong children's ministry. And we were graced with deep friendships even with the knowledge that our family would only be physically there for a short time. And now, from a geographical distance, we continue to be spurred on through Biblical teaching, sincere friendships, unity of mission, and encouragement from how this body continues to be the hands and feet of Jesus. When a church (a people of God) does works of kindness in Christ's name, rather than in our own name or even in the name of kindness, it is powerful, humble, attractive, and good. My challenge to anyone looking for a body to come alongside in Boston, is to remember that YOU, in fact, are the church. (1st Peter) You have a part to play. You have a responsibility to own. And if you are looking for a people to trust in leadership and heart... stop looking ;) because your google search brought you to Mosaic. Plus it's right at a T stop. ;)

Like other reviewers have mentioned, the building is beautiful. I’m not sure I can say anything else positive, however.

The pastor would hardly read or refer to the Bible during his sermon, choosing to go on rants about Jewish people and how feminism is sinful. I genuinely tried to connect these tirades to the passage which he was supposedly “preaching from” (Nehemiah), but to no luck.

formatted_address: 40 Dalton St, Boston, MA 02115, United States
name: King's Hill Church

reviews.text:
A short story...
We moved my daughter into a new apartment in South Boston on Labor Day Weekend. Arrived at her new 3rd floor apartment with 2 big trucks full of her belongings. We were met at the sidewalk  (7th and I street) by a group of 7 youth members of Kings Hill Church who offered their help. In 20 minutes they emptied both trucks and brought everything to the 3rd floor. They would not accept compensation- even a donation on their behalf! They were truly a Godsend! Thank you Kings Hill Church!

King’s Hill Church was absolutely incredible!
If you live in or around Mission Hill or Back Bay and are looking for gospel centered community, King’s Hill is the place for you! They meet in the Fenway Room at 10:45 AM on Sundays for worship. There are tons of College and university students and young professionals that are a part of this body. It was awesome to see so much diversity among the body of Christ at King’s Hill! If you are looking for a church to connect with in Boston, give King’s Hill a shot!

I loved visiting King's Hill Church during my time in Boston!! This is a beautiful Gospel-centered church and I was thankful to worship Jesus with them this past Sunday! Everyone I met was so kind and welcoming. I can't wait to visit again the next time I am in town. 10/10 would recommend!

I spent a summer in Boston and attended Kings Hill Church every Sunday! The teaching & community at Kings Hill is so life-giving and encouraging. The pastor also really cares for each of the members, and they made me feel so welcome every time i came. I would not trade my time at Kings Hill for the world, and I would recommend this church to anyone. I am so thankful for my time at Kings Hill and I can’t wait to come back!

King's Hill Church is one of the most welcoming and encouraging churches I've ever attended. For students looking for a place to call their home away from home, or for anyone who's looking to set roots down - this is the church you wanna be at. Wonderful hospitality, intentional about relationships and staying connected, and the community is awesome. For meeting in the Fenway room of a hotel they really make do with what they have. Great worship, thought provoking sermons, and plenty of opportunities to get involved. 5 stars.

formatted_address: 645 Boylston St, Boston, MA 02116, United States
name: Old South Church in Boston

reviews.text: Beautiful architecture and glass work,  one section was closed due to renovations but otherwise a very peaceful place to visit, was not crowded at all.

Gorgeous Building it kept your attention from outside !
The building is a landmark and it’s next to the public library.
It’s a must to visit!

This church is a national historic landmark and has been there since 1875. It was spacious and had a few nooks and crannies to explore. Samuel Adams called this his church and Benjamin Franklin was baptized here. There are some pretty areas of stained glass and little bits of history around the church. It can get a little warm inside even in the end of September. It was a nice little stop to explore and worth the visit.
Not big but with lots of details to discover. Christmas decos have more spices of this historical church:)

Boston String Quartet was Amazing. The North Church Venue was a perfect setting
Thank you for an Amazing Evening

name: Trinity Church

reviews.text: It was great to see the beautiful architecture of the old church, inside and outside. The wood carvings were too beautiful to describe. It is not a quick trip. There is so much to see.  Everywhere I looked was amazing 👏

Beautiful church. Beautiful architecture. Came 10 minutes before closing for their last tour. You definitely don't need a lot of time to see everything if you're in a rush, however it's $10 to tour. Very cool visit.

I loved Trinity Church. It's a little gem.
The outside is very gorgeous especially since the church is surrounded by modern skyscrapers.
But it's the inside that it's breathtaking.
The price to enter is $10 for adults. Worth it a visit.

Beautiful and over 100 years old. Father Jean I believe was his name gave us a little bit of information and welcomed us with a smile. He told us there’s bathrooms which we later used and also told us about the throne where Pope JP II sat when he visited the US for the first time and allowed us to seat on it and take pictures.

This was a beautiful place to visit while in Boston. We accepted the audio guide (no extra charge) and this was the right thing to do as we got so much extra information we would have otherwise missed out on and it makes you understand and appreciate what you are looking at so much more.

The price of admission was around 10 dollars and goes towards the upkeep of the  church.

Recommend while in Boston.

The park area directly in front of the church is under redevelopment and should look really good when the work is complete.

An amazing church with incredible pastors/leaders who cultivate an excellent community. Excellent Sunday school for all ages. This church is FAMILY!!!
Amazing Church - great people, great ministry! Great youth ministry for teens and young adults.

Loved hearing Noopy talk!

formatted_address: 193 Salem St, Boston, MA 02113, United States
name: Old North Church

reviews.text: We attended the Sunday church service. No fee to enter. Church staff welcome you at the door and ushers take you to your seat. Beautiful interior and meaningful service. We stayed for a bit to take some photos and to talk with some of the church staff. As to parking, we found a public lot several blocks away, as most on street parking is permit only.

Nice stop to get a couple of tickets to see the Old North Church with its deep historical spot of Paul Reveres famous ride to warn.  The British are coming.

Plenty to read and helpful guides inside to explain histical elements of the church’s heritage.  Nice patio and courtyard when we left via the back door.  I love history!  Boston is loaded with it.

I was really looking forward to visiting this church, as it’s the oldest in Boston. Unfortunately, we couldn’t access it because the backyard and other areas were closed, likely due to maintenance or because it was the 1st of January. From the outside, it looked beautiful, and I would have loved to explore the interior and the catacombs. Looks like I’ll have to come back another time.

We received a wonderful insight from the history of the church and of the Boston from the XVIII century. My first question as soon as we got there was: what are the small cubicles? They are interesting. They were reserved for families. It was a sign of status they explained. I can only imagine the time and the attires, and the wigs. So fascinating. Hear about the famous lanterns and what they meant in the place were it all happened is priceless.

Visiting my son who is stationed near by. This is core American history. Walking the freedom trail, each stop has a ticket price. SOME are free to Active Duty and Veterans. The church is not. Still well worth the admission price to see one of the countries corner stones.

formatted_address: 1 Park St, Boston, MA 02108, United States
name: Park Street Church

reviews.text:
We attended a 4pm Sunday service and was very chill. Lasted until 5:10. You can see the cemetery and the Common from the windows and hear the church bells.
Welcoming environment in a 200+ year old church. The outside is gorgeous. We ended up parking our car several blocks away for free.

Stunning Boston Wedding Venue with history!

We’ve worked in countless venues across New England — Park Street Church is one of the best in Boston. The architecture is timeless, the natural light is incredible for both photography and videography, and the ceremony space is spacious yet intimate.

Captured a beautiful wedding here — the church's iconic red carpet aisle, tall white columns, and historic charm added elegance to every frame. The layout is perfect for smooth processions and guest flow, and the balcony provides excellent angles for wide shots. If you want a Boston wedding venue that’s classic, photogenic, and deeply meaningful, Park Street Church delivers.

Highly recommend for any couple looking for a beautiful church wedding in downtown Boston.

We visited on a Wednesday morning in mid-June 2025. We were doing this as part of the Freedom Trail and we did not actually go inside but we stopped outside to read the signage and take some pictures. They have infographics on display in the windows.

My hubby and I were visiting Boston from Minnesota and wanted to go to church while there.  We would've had to take an expensive uber ride to the nearest church of our denomination, so I just picked a church within walking distance of our rental.  This church was a great choice.  The atmosphere was inviting and the sermon was phenomenal!  This Pentecostal girl was struggling to stay silent!  I was not used to the liturgy, but muddled through, and no one seemed to mind.  If I was ever in the neighborhood again, I'd definitely return!  They also have a historic cemetery which was a fun surprise.   There are so many famous people buried there!  If you're looking for a church this one should definitely make your list (even if its not your denomination).

Delightful, Beautiful & Historical Church!
This is like stop number 3 on the Freedom Trail after Boston Commons and the state house.
it is a beautiful church and very historical (for the USA) as dating back all the way to the 19th Century.
Next door there is the Granary Burying ground where most of the revolutionaries are buried. We really enjoyed this Church but did not have the chance to go in as it was closed the day we were here in summer.

Great concert of my brother -Alex Poliykov

formatted_address: 101 Nightingale St, Boston, MA 02124, United States
name: Greater Love Tabernacle Church

reviews.text: Yesterday was my grandmother’s homegoing service and I must say it was not what my family expected in terms of sending her off. Now I’ve been to plenty of other services here for deaths in the community. Where the service is superb ,but for some reason my grandmother did not get that on Saturday. During the service Pastor Dickerson did not follow the set program and more so free-styled the entire time. There were several electrical malfunctions when speaking and  singing selected songs. We also paid for a projector ,but the pictures were barely shown. After the service away from the guests Pastor Dickerson was approached by family members about our dissatisfaction with the way the service went. During that time Pastor Dickerson became very hostile and confrontational. Stating ” I’m from the hood too and I’m here with just my wife. So I’m not scared “. We as the family could not believe that a pastor in our weakest time would treat us this way. We also knew that our grandmother would not accept this treatment. So we thanked him for his services and left. Our grandmother meant the world to us and to not send her off the right way hurts. Based on this experience, my family will not be asking pastor Dickerson to assist with sending another loved one home.

One of the best churches in Boston. They are a very welcoming place. And pastor Dickerson is definitely good at what he does. Most times it truly feels as if he's literally only talking to me and about my situation. His wife Mrs Dickerson is truly a delightful woman yes she is y'all. Greater Love Tabernacle is truly that, a greater love.

Although the pastor and funeral services were nice, the condition of the church was unacceptable. Although the church body knew a service would be held, there was visable dust and dirt in places there shouldn't have been. Also it is in no way handicap accessible. Lots of stairs and no elevator, not even to the bathroom. I felt so bad for the senior citizens and the physically challenged.

Amazing church. Truly anointed. This church truly cares about the community. The members are so loving and cheerful. It's a family. A church home, with a church family. Every one is genuine. They're nice, welcoming, and inclusive. They help you feel like you're at home.
I know I'm only 17 but I've been going here since I was about 5 or 6 and I absolutely love it. God is the greater love out of all the loves, and in that church they truly have a heart for people.

reviews.text: It's a nice church

reviews.text:
Grace City is an absolutely amazing church. Sunday gatherings are a highlight of the week—from the moment you walk in, you’re welcomed with warmth and genuine friendliness. The people here make you feel right at home instantly.

The music is exceptional. The band features incredibly talented artists, and each week brings fresh arrangements and creative mashups of some of the best worship songs. The rotation of vocalists and musicians keeps things dynamic, yet the quality is consistently outstanding.

The sermons are relevant, practical, and deeply rooted in Scripture. Every message feels thoughtful, meaningful, and truly applicable to daily life.

What stands out even more is how much Grace City does for the community. The church offers numerous outreach opportunities throughout Boston—from supporting those experiencing homelessness to helping at a daycare serving refugee families. If there’s a need, this church steps up with compassion and a willingness to serve.

The children’s ministry is also fantastic. The volunteers are engaging, fun, and incredibly caring. Kids are excited to be there each week, and the teachers intentionally create a safe, joyful environment where children feel known and loved.

Grace City is filled with people who use their gifts to serve in meaningful ways, and it elevates the entire experience of being part of this community. For anyone seeking a welcoming, Christ-centered church with excellent worship, strong teaching, and a heart for the city, you need to check out Grace City Church.

reviews.text: Contemporary, non-denominational church that fully embraced my family for 3 years in Cambridge. The Senior Pastor, Steve Watson, and others from the ministry team consistently prepared a thoughtful and challenging message of faith. I’ve had an amazing experience at this church. Fantastic music, beautiful building, warm and welcoming people, and meaningful messages — truly a gem! My faith has grown immensely here. This church became my new home after I moved up to Cambridge for law school.  I come from an evangelical (charismatic) background and my work is in social justice (currently refugee/immigration law).  Every time I move to a new city, it's difficult to find a new church.  Social justice churches tend to lack a passion for the Holy Spirit.  Holy Spirit-filled churches tend to lack a passion for Social Justice.  I always feel spiritually homeless.  Reservoir does both really well.  They have a passion for prayer, worship, healing (mystical side of God) and they are active players in justice work in Boston & the world.  More important than anything, they are an extremely loving, welcoming, and authentic community.  I've been in churches that do both justice and worship well, but not community.  No fun.  Reservoir is a family of quirky amazing friends you can't get enough of.  Everyone really, truly (I say from experience) cares about you.  Come here!

Church community is hard to do well, and Reservoir accomplishes a deft balancing act of being welcoming, helpful, and growth-inspiring to folks with longtime church experiences and those with none.

My wife and I have been coming here for 8 years and we're sold-out for Reservoir's positive engagement with secular culture, diversity, and welcoming stance to many who may feel out of place at traditional churches in the area (ourselves included).

Disclosure: My wife liked being a part of Reservoir so much, she left teaching to go on pastoral staff almost three years ago! But if this church sucked, I would tell you even if my wife worked there.

reviews.text:
The First Church of Christ, Scientist, located in Boston, is a remarkable place that combines stunning architecture with a peaceful atmosphere. As you approach the building, the intricate details of its facade and the grand entrance immediately capture your attention. The church’s interior is equally impressive, featuring beautiful stained glass windows and a serene ambiance that invites contemplation.

During my visit, I was struck by the sense of tranquility that permeated the space. It’s a perfect spot for reflection or quiet prayer. The church also offers a rich history, with informative displays that provide insight into the Christian Science movement and its founder, Mary Baker Eddy.

One of the highlights of the visit is the Reading Room, where you can explore various resources about Christian Science and its teachings. The staff is welcoming and knowledgeable, always ready to answer questions or provide guidance.

Overall, my experience at The First Church of Christ, Scientist was enlightening and peaceful. Whether you are interested in spirituality, architecture, or simply looking for a quiet place to reflect, this church is a must-visit. I highly recommend taking the time to explore this beautiful location—it truly offers a unique perspective on faith and community.

Visited this Church during free tour on Sunday. You can't just enter there from outside, the tour guides have to take you inside the church by the elevator. Inside of the church is huge and majestic, it was built for a capacity of 5000 people, and the dome itself is not supported by columns, a kind of know how in architecture. The organ is massive, you can listen to it during their masses or online. The church is connected to an old smaller building, it has also organ but it is smaller. They do have their own religion and their own holy book, and as they don't have priests, the book is read during their gatherings by different people from the entire world.

The Christian science museum is undoubtedly one of those historical marvels that have to be preserved at all cost.

It is wheelchair accessible making it accessible to each and every entity on this planet to come and witness how the world which we know today has shaped. I was amongst the fortune ones who had the chance to visit How do you see the world Mapperrium alongside the Church alongside extension as well. The tour facilitators, reception staff and every person working there is unquestionably the sweetest. I had no problem at all in asking and clarifying my doubts.

A must visit place if you like history and the monuments that have survived for nearly a century.

Hugely impressive, monumental. I liked the neo-classical domed church adjacent to the annex that is like a medieval castle and the shallow long reflecting pool outside adjacent to a tree lined walking path.

The Mapparium with the amazing lobby, spherical glass globe mapped from 1935, along with Mary Eddy Baker's teachings is worth a visit. The organization is affiliated to the Christian Science Monitor,  a world renowned news and information agency

reviews.text: Highrock Cambridge Covenant Church, which meets and operates near the intellectual core of Harvard Square, is, in my meaningful estimation and based on the frequent, genuinely moving endorsements from friends and community members I know, a truly welcoming, thoughtful, and highly engaged spiritual community that successfully balances traditional faith with modern, intellectually curious discourse and robust local service. Everyone I’ve spoken with consistently praises the dynamic and relatable teaching, the deep commitment to fostering meaningful connections and small group fellowship, and the sincere, active involvement in serving the needs of the Cambridge community, emphasizing that the church creates a space for both serious contemplation and joyful, practical action. I’ve learned from their narratives that the atmosphere is one of warm, non-judgmental acceptance and shared purpose, making it an exceptional place for students, professionals, and long-time residents seeking both spiritual depth and genuine, lasting friendship. My subjective conclusion is that Highrock is an irreplaceable source of encouragement and community strength - a wonderful place to connect - so I wholeheartedly suggest visiting their service to experience their unique blend of warmth and intellectual vitality.

Churches We Know. Sunday Mass at the Cathedral of the Holy Cross in Boston. It is the cathedral of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Boston in Massachusetts. It is one of the largest Catholic churches in New England. On October 1, 1979, Pope John Paul II held a 38-minute prayer service for 2,000 priests in the cathedral during his first papal visit to the United States. His chair is displayed inside the Cathedral. He celebrated a Mass at Boston Common during his 1979 visit to Boston. This was his first Mass in the United States. The event took place on October 1, 1979, and drew a large crowd despite the rainy weather, visit to Boston in 1979. This was his first Mass in the United States. The event took place on October 1st and drew an estimated 400,000 people, despite a rainstorm. I arrived in the morning to have a good spot to attend this Mass. It was great to see the Pope. Today we remember this historic Mass. We are blessed. #ChurchesWeKnow #abuelosmochileros_boston #abuelosmochileros_churches

reviews.text: This church has changed my life! To come into a community that is so loving, so kind, so open and truly wants to walk alongside you as you walk alongside Jesus has been a game changer. I heard through Pastor Steven’s voice,
the Word of God through the Gospel. The scripture spoke of God’s love and faithfulness me, during a time of suffering. After the service, the members of the church who were in front of me did not just walk out and go their way. They turned around, introduced themselves and engaged with me in conversation. I met many more members of COAH that first day. There is community there. It was truly evident on my first day I attended a service. Now, I understand how incredible the community is there beyond Sundays, with many social events that they participate in, including Baby Showers, Bowling, Holiday parties,  weekly small Community Groups and Church retreats. They also join together to support many organizations in the surrounding Boston neighborhoods, including partnering with English High School down the street. Their mission is to spread the word of God and the hope for salvation. That day that I found City on a Hill was the day my life changed. I love this church. Please come and see for yourself. Come and say hi! I am there praising God every Sunday.

name: Holy Resurrection Orthodox Church

reviews.text: My wife and I have visited our dear friends in Boston who call this parish their spiritual home on several occasions and we absolutely loved attending the services here with them and meeting all the wonderful parishioners. Holy Resurrection is a gem of an Orthodox church, the congregation feels like one big family, and Father Patrick and Father Theodore, the parish priests, are warm, welcoming, love Christ and take their commission to care for His flock very seriously. If you live in the Boston area or are simply visiting, you can't go wrong visiting Holy Resurrection for Orthodox worship and fellowship!

A wonderful  Orthodox community that has the Divine Liturgy and other services in English, and a pot luck coffee hour afterwards.  They have a small bookstore with essential spiritual classics and icons, a school and a soup kitchen every Monday. In addition  to all this, they have catechism classes and othdr classes to help you grow in your spiritual life. If this isn't a true church, I don't know what else is.

If you are looking for an Orthodox Church that is welcoming of everyone look no further. Attend a Sunday liturgy which starts at 9:30 am on Sundays to see for yourself. Make sure you stay for the entire service which goes until 11:30 am and don't miss the Coffee Hour downstairs following every Sunday liturgy.You will find a beautiful and well kept church that is filled with wonderful people of many ethnic and cultural backgrounds tied together by the orthodox faith. You will find families with small children participating in the services as well as some of the original parishioners who have helped found this church. A lot of those that attend regularly are either converted to Orthodoxy or come from Orthodox countries like, Russia, Ukraine, Romania, Bulgaria, etc.

Some of the ministries that make Holy Resurrection Orthodox Church also very special are:

1) Monday's Open Door Free Meal Program, which has operated without interruption for over 20 years
2) Saint Herman of Alaska Orthodox Christian School, grades 1-8, which has also operated for over 20 years
3) Church Book Store which has a nice collection of books, audio & video materials as well as icons and other worship items

In a nutshell this parish is a very active working community that is a great place to begin learning of the Orthodox faith as well as to start and/or raise a family in the same Orthodox faith.

My favorite of the parishes I have attended. The people are very friendly and committed to living an authentic Christian life. The parish also runs a wonderful school for children from kindergarten to about seventh grade, St. Herman of Alaska Christian School.
This Church is the precious Jewel of Boston. We came to visit one day and a year later, we are members.  The hour drive, for us, is well worth it!!!

reviews.text:
Sozo Church has truly become home for us over the past two years. From the moment we first visited, the presence of the Holy Spirit has been undeniable. The pastors here have clearly been placed by God. They lead with humility, passion, and a genuine love for people. They give so much of themselves to the church, its leaders, and the entire community, and it is clear that their hearts burn for Jesus and for seeing lives transformed.

What we love most is their heart to see heaven full. Every message, every outreach, and every moment of ministry shows their desire to truly pour into people and help them grow in faith and purpose. Of course we are all human and we all fall short, but there is only one who is perfect, Jesus, and this church keeps Him at the center of everything.

Pastor’s preaching is powerful and deeply inspired by God. His messages are raw, full of truth, and without unnecessary fluff. Whether you are new to faith or have walked with Christ for years, you will receive something fresh and life changing every time he speaks.

Sozo is deeply committed to growth both spiritually and as a family of believers. The messages are powerful and grounded in God’s Word, the worship is Spirit filled, and the culture feels welcoming and life giving. Our kids absolutely love going to Sozo Kids Church every week, which means the world to us as parents.

If you are looking for a church where God’s presence is real, the leaders truly care, and the mission is to reach and love people well, Sozo is the place to call home.

Grace Church has been my home for the past four years, and I’m incredibly grateful for this gospel-centered community. The preaching is expository, faithfully unpacking God’s Word each week, always pointing to Christ. The elders lead and serve with humility, shepherding the flock with love and care.

Beyond the preaching, the people of this church have made a lasting impact on my life. My wife and I have met some of our closest friends here, and we have truly become part of one big family—united by one thing that is everything: Christ, our only hope. Through this solid, gospel-centered, biblical church, I have grown tremendously in my faith—something I attribute not only to the teaching but also to the relationships, accountability, and love within the body.

Grace Church is a faithful witness in a city that desperately needs more churches like this—rooted in Scripture, committed to sound doctrine, and passionate about making disciples. If you’re looking for a Christ-centered community that will challenge, encourage, and equip you, I highly recommend this church.

The teaching is biblically sound, the worship is deeply Christ-centered, and there’s a sincere, prayerful atmosphere throughout each service. It’s clear that everything done here is rooted in a love for Jesus and a desire to honor Him.

This is an impressive church in that it is young and vibrant and takes its faith seriously. Just one thing bothered me, the pastor during a late 2024 sermon made an offhand comment about DEI, and it felt puzzling at the time, like I didn’t know how he meant it, or why it was relevant. But now with DEI federal jobs and programs being shut down nationally, it seems looking back like a dog whistle to a certain flavor of politics. I don’t like politics in sermons and we don’t see that here really but there is certainly a conservative (culturally) feel to the place, and the pastor seems to be preoccupied with young single people, mentioning dating in almost every sermon, in a way that reminds me of my youth groups (elsewhere, long ago) and the purity culture uncomfortably pushed by youth pastors. Not that it’s NOT an important topic but feels weird sometimes coming from a married middle aged guy (respectfully) instead of another single person.

Cultural conservatism in a church is not unusual- however we live in a diverse multicultural city and the discomfort lies in the doubt that if DEI is scoffed at, for example, what about respect for those cultural differences? And to be fair, the church is diverse and it’s lovely. But I’ve been to a fair amount of churches where the congregation is diverse but the leadership is less so, and it always makes me feel uncomfortable. Are you preaching my salvation but in agreement with my oppression? kind of thing.

Anyway, worth going to see for yourself, the people there are genuine and friendly, and it is big enough that there are multiple members of the ministry to actively lead the congregation and a lot of ways to build community and get involved.

reviews.text:

We've been hooked ever since, tuning in every Sunday for a dose of inspiration and spiritual growth.

Rev. Charles M. Taylor and his assistant Darnetia went above and beyond to ensure our wedding was unforgettable – they should really consider moonlighting as wedding planners! Before we even got engaged, we dipped our toes into some of UTC's introductory courses and met amazing instructors like Myra Terrelonge, Rev Mitchelle Washington, and Deborah Parrott. These folks truly embody UTC's mission of empowering people to awaken their divine potential.

Special shoutout to Prayer Chapel Deborah Donahue – you had us reaching for the tissues! We can't wait to visit again, but in the meantime, we'll be catching the services on YouTube and happily contributing through tithes and offerings.

UTC is more than a community; it's a family that loves unconditionally, a haven for healing, and a powerhouse for growth. Come join us and let's create a world that works for everyone, one God-inspired life at a time!

This is a Jesus the Christ Ministry and a member of the Universal Foundation for Better Living (UFBL), headquartered in Miami Gardens, Florida. The Universal Truth Center For Better Living and all UFBL ministries are spiritually based and their teachings are meant to promote transformation and self-empowerment to awaken one’s spiritual nature to do the good we’ve been brought forth to do and live the good life we’re meant to live. UTC’s practices include ongoing, free and low-cost workshops, presentations, concerts as well as year-round spiritual, self-development classes. These classes include Tai Chi, line dancing, adult and youth Sunday school. There are weekly theme-based Sunday lessons (sermons), spiritual retreats, guest speakers, Senior appreciate days, farm share, prison pen pal and other community activities, all held at the church or sponsored by it, some even  include partnerships with other community organizations. My application of these teachings have helped me experience a better life, one new thought at a time. It was here, that I was re-introduced to God. This remembrance has helped to healed my heart, from the inside out. Beliefs of neglect, abandonment, betrayal, being under-valued during vulnerable phases of my life have melted away with mind thought action. I’ve now learned how to, just like Joseph of Genesis, allow the “bad” to serve as a blessing, a blessing to catapult me to higher spiritual ground. Look at God!!!  I’m now in better shape to mentally do all that which God has sent me here to do, all with God’s ease, grace, wisdom, courage and success. I am so grateful to call this place and space, my spiritual home.

I've been attending this church for the past two years, actively participating in various activities, including church services, prayer meetings, and volunteering for the parking lot and Feeding Miami. Despite my dedication and passing two background checks, I have faced unfair treatment and judgment.

One significant issue is the inconsistency in security checks. I have been repeatedly subjected to bag searches, even after demonstrating that my bag was flat and contains only my phone. I responsibly keep my gun locked in the trunk, as I've shown them and I showed one of the parking attendance on the day they trespass me. However, women’s bags are not searched, and when my mother pointed out that she witnessed a woman carrying a handgun in her purse, the response was dismissive, claiming they trust the "Christian word" of women but not mine, despite my service and background checks.

Furthermore, my mother, who was recently baptized at this church, is trusted more than I am, even though I have been a long-time volunteer. They accuse me of seeking special treatment when all I ask for is fair and equal treatment, similar to that afforded to women.

An additional issue arose with the church’s childcare policy. While I volunteered in the parking lot, my son was expelled from CF Kids because the church stated they only offer childcare for one session, not for volunteers who stay for multiple sessions. They let me know that they do not get paid even though I am also doing volunteer work. This lack of support for volunteers is disheartening.

Moreover, when a distressed person approached me for food, the church refused to help, fearing it would attract more people seeking assistance. This lack of compassion led me to join Feeding Miami to provide help. I discussed this issue with Pastor Alex, and I took it as a calling from God to step in and provide for those in need.

Despite being trespassed from the church, I will continue to host prayer meetings at my home for Christ Fellowship members, treating everyone with the respect and dignity I was denied. This church’s actions have been deeply disappointing, and I hope for a change that aligns more closely with the principles of fellowship and support that a church should embody.

reviews.text:
I’ve been going to Crossbridge Brickell, and it’s honestly one of the friendliest and most down-to-earth churches I’ve been to. The people are warm, welcoming, and really care about building community. What stands out is how seriously they take living with purpose — not just at church, but in everyday life.

The messages on Sundays are focused on the life and teachings of Jesus, and they do a great job of showing how that applies to real life — especially here in Miami. The talks are rooted in the Bible but easy to understand, relatable, and engaging.

They also care a lot about the city — the church regularly supports local nonprofits and encourages people to give back and help those in need. You’ll find a good mix of people here — lots of young professionals (especially in medicine and finance), but also families, kids, and older folks. There’s a great children’s program, and small group meetups during the week help people build friendships and grow personally and spiritually.

On top of that, they host fun events like cookouts and parties where everyone’s welcome, even if you’ve never been to church before. They also occasionally team up with other local churches for worship music nights, cookouts, and community outreach.

If you’re in Brickell and looking for a place that combines meaningful teaching, uplifting music, and a genuine sense of community, I highly recommend checking out Crossbridge Brickell.

reviews.text: I have grown up in this church, raised my family here, and continue to attend, appreciating the ways in which this kind community is open to changing, growing, learning, and being intentional about how the church and its people show up in the world. Calvary is "Open to All; Closed to None" and they truly live up to it, and are willing to listen and transform if not. If you are looking for a safe space as a person in the LGBTQIA+ community, Calvary is officially "Welcoming and Affirming" and will not only welcome you, but affirm and celebrate you- no agenda to change you. We believe all people are created in God's image, just as they are. Calvary is also intentional about justice modeled by the Gospel, and has partnerships and connections, learning and volunteer opportunities in being the hands and feet of Christ in this way. Staff/Clergy are top notch, sermons are thought provoking, relevant, and clearly driven by deep biblical study, and comprehensive knowledge. Staff is wonderfully personable. They truly care about each and every one of CBC's members, and also work to live out a work/life balance and model self care. Understanding that intellectualism/science and faith are not mutually exclusive, embracing complexity and nuance, avoiding binary thinking, taking scripture seriously, using art and creativity, and so much more are found here. The leadership model is great, with transparency and many opportunities and encouragement to get involved. Grief support/memorial services are better here than any others I've seen, done with tenderness, ritual, and detail. Engaging and caring community. The music is phenomenal! Beautiful sanctuary and organ, as well as the chapel and the Foot of The Cross Courtyard which is a sacred space and columbarium/memorial site. Safe and engaging opportunities for children, youth, and every age group. Calvary's statement: "Calvary is a Christ-like community that experiences and shares God's love. Calvary welcomes and affirms all people as children of God from every cultural and religious background, sexual orientation, family composition, physical and mental ability, economic means, race, age, and gender."

Calvary has been "home" to me for several years.  The worship services are thought-provoking and emotionally supportive.  The small groups are varied and welcoming.  The pastoral staff is talented and approachable; the music is really good!  Last night's Good Friday service conducted jointly with New Hope Baptist was one of the best ever!
Beautiful sanctuary and well-kept facility

If you're looking for a church home that provides a nurturing environment for spiritual growth, I highly recommend Calvary Baptist Church. I joined this church three years ago after relocating to to Colorado from the Midwest, and the church body at Calvary has become like family to me. It has helped me to overcome one of the greatest challenges of my life, losing my mother. One thing Calvary specializes in is radiating a warm, heartfelt, welcome that isn't too intrusive. It's a very diverse congregation, with people from different racial and cultural backgrounds. The thing that ties us all together is our focus on being a loving and inclusive community, even for those that are still disparaged by other churches such as gays, lesbians, immigrants, and the disabled. The church's theme is "Open to all, closed to none" and Calvary does a great job of living out this creed. The sermons are always grounded in the Bible, relevant, and taught with a great humility.
Lovely church, sermon, worship, prayer, but seriously, this is the most Methodist church I’ve attended since junior high.

reviews.text: We have been attending this church for 18 months. The teaching is thoughtful and biblical...truly outstanding. The atmosphere is welcoming and loving. With two services and the congregation split between them, it can feel a bit on the small side but I'm not in to mega churches anyway. As with any church I have been a part of, it is important to participate in the small groups. Small group sign-ups are offered twice a year and go a long way in helping you to connect with the others who are a part of this church body.

The warmth and openness of New Denver church impressed my husband and myself on our very first visit. The church is accepting of wherever you are on your faith journey and offers numerous opportunities for growth in our relationships with Jesus and others. Sermons are thought provoking and there are discipleship groups, fellowship opportunities, annual women's and men's retreats, local and international mission experiences, children and teen activities. We have been extremely happy with our decision to be part of New Denver's church family and quickly knew this would be our church home without searchingly further after moving to Denver 3 years ago.

I originally found New Denver because I was searching for a MOPS group after moving several years ago. After attending MOPS, I started attending church services on Sunday and was impressed with the thoughtful sermons and the sense of community. Through the years I have also joined D Groups (small group sessions) and have attended the Women’s Retreat, which have both been great ways to connect with others in a smaller setting. I’m thankful to be part of the NDC community!

New Denver Church is exactly the type of faith community my husband and I were seeking. For anyone seeking a faith community with practical application of traditional biblical values, New Denver Church is a great option!

My wife and I have been going to New Denver for about a year and a half now, and we feel very fortunate to have found it. One thing that I have been impressed with is that the church accomplishes this mission well for people in many different stages and walks of life.

reviews.text: This is our church! I just started coming here with my partner. From day one, everyone was so warm and welcoming. You can really feel the love for Jesus and each other here. We actually just got baptized here today! You can sign up to get baptized during any of the three services held on Sundays. They offer an 8:30 am, 10:00 am and 11:30 am service. The community is so supportive, the topics discussed are heartfelt, relatable and honest. The worship team is great and every single person we've met whether they are staff or just a fellow attendee has been full of love and welcoming. I highly recommend coming here! There is no feeling of judgment, intimidation or awkwardness, just warmth, joy and acceptance. Everyone really comes together to worship here as the family of Jesus and we are so grateful and happy to call Arise our church.

Matthew 25:34-45 reminds us: "For I was hungry, and you gave me food; I was thirsty, and you gave me drink; I was a stranger, and you welcomed me..."

Recently, a well-known member of our community was on his usual walk, highlighting areas neglected by local businesses, community and government. As he passed your church, he was approached by one of your members named Sawyer ( last name unknown)who asked if he needed help.

When he said yes, he invited Sawyer to walk with him to show where assistance was needed. He wanted to understand how the church supports those struggling just steps away from its sanctuary.

Following him, Sawyer was introduced to a homeless person living in a tent, surrounded by trash. The community member asked if they could minister to this individual, but the church member(Sawyer) declined, citing their own issues and expressing concern about being recorded. Instead of helping, Sawyer chose to return to the church.

The community member agreed to turn off the camera to focus on helping. However, about half an hour later, he resumed a live broadcast, seen cleaning the area alone, without support from the church or the member (Sawyer) that he had spoken to earlier

As a woman of faith and a servant of the Lord, I was disheartened by the resistance from the church member and the reluctance to reach out to those in need so close to your place of worship. The principles God instills in us as His servants should compel us to address the needs of all people.

I recognize that the homelessness crisis is significant, especially in Colorado's rising economy, but I would expect the church to take an active role in addressing these challenges. I commend the community member for returning to clean up the area, demonstrating unwavering dedication despite resistance.

As a community, we will advocate for our city and higher officials to address issues of mental health, homelessness, and environmental concerns, even in areas outside our own neighborhoods. Ignoring these needs could lead to larger issues affecting many more.

I hope this serves as a motivation for the church to consider how outreach can extend beyond just Thanksgiving and Christmas. Thank you for taking the time to read this. I pray that your outreach ministry will review its outreach practices  and do more within your own neighborhood.

This church has been my safe place and sanctuary for most of my life. I came to Arise during a time that I was in desperate need of family, and I've found my home at Arise.

The staff here is superb-- they care deeply for the community inside and outside of the church. They've helped myself and the community around me more times than I can count.

I am grateful to go to a church that is ready and willing to respond and care for community needs. I love our passion and dedication to help people follow Jesus through building relationships with the people around us. If you're looking for a Bible- believing church that's Jesus-centered and community- focused, i promise you'll find a home at Arise.

I started attending Arise Church in September of 2022. Before that, I had only been to church a couple of times in my life. I'm so glad I found this church I now call home. I was hesitant to go to church because I feared being judged, but it was also important to me that the church taught sound doctrine straight from the Bible. Arise has surpassed my expectations in every way. I've made genuine friendships here, which has made my walk with Christ even more meaningful. At this point, the only way they'll get rid of me is if I move! Thank you, Arise, for all that you do!

When we found Arise Church on google, I went straight to the reviews and one review caught my attention. The review said that Arise Church had a great kids program. The moment I read this review I mentioned it to my husband and we both agreed Arise Church was the church we were going to visit the following day, which happen to be a Sunday. That Sunday Morning we were a little nervous because it was the first time we were attending church as a family. The moment we walked in to Arise Church we felt welcomed, during the worship time and throughout the sermon we just felt Gods peace and presence. Two years later, I can tell you Arise Church does have a beyond great kids program! My daughters have learned so much and they look forward to attending their youth group and Sunday school every week. Our family’s favorite day of the week is now Sunday because we get to attend Church and learn more about JESUS. Finding Arise Church has been such a blessing to our family and we will forever be grateful to God for Pastor Matt, Pastor Sawyer and their families and everyone who serves at Arise Church.

reviews.text: I am absolutely shocked that this church has any bad reviews to begin with. The place is absolutely flowing with the holy spirit and the message is always something that softens my heart to hear. One thing  I noticed is that this church is not afraid to call out sin as it is. A lot of churches are in active blasphemy by letting people be comfortable in your sin. Not Brave. Its an absolute blessing to be a part of this church, and I tell my friends and family that I found the best church in Denver. Message to the people who called this church political: (If you go to church because you are looking to get told what you want to hear, you are going to church for the wrong reasons). Jesus Christ told the people what they HAD to hear and the Bible is CLEAR on its message. Love is the most prominent message being preached about. Only my second time with the church but so far I am impressed and have experienced the holy spirit working in my heart every time. Can’t wait to get more involved with this church. Keep unapologetically preaching. God bless you!

BRAVE Church is a powerhouse of truth, courage, and transformation. From the first sermon you hear, it’s clear this church isn’t here to entertain—it’s here to equip. The teaching is bold, biblical, and laser-focused on helping men and families stand firm in a culture that’s forgotten what real faith looks like. Every message calls you to rise up, repent, and walk in obedience to Jesus Christ.

What makes BRAVE Church truly special is that it’s only as big as you let it feel. Yes, it’s a thriving, growing church—but when you step in and get connected, it feels like family. Join a small group, serve in a ministry, attend a men’s gathering—whatever it takes, don’t sit on the sidelines. The men and women of BRAVE are real people walking through real struggles and victories together under the authority of God’s Word.

You won’t find shallow teaching or passive faith here. You’ll find strong leadership, accountability, and a community that challenges you to grow into the man or woman God called you to be. The more you pour in, the more you’ll see that this isn’t just a church—it’s a training ground for warriors of the Kingdom.

If you want a church that speaks truth, builds disciples, and pushes you toward godly strength—BRAVE Church is it. Get involved. Be known. Step into the fight and discover how powerful the body of Christ can be when you stop spectating and start participating.

BRAVE Church: where truth is preached, lives are changed, and believers are built to stand strong.  Love this Church!!!!

I attended this church one Sunday out of curiosity, and could genuinely feel the presence of the devil. The hate that came out of the pastor’s mouth made me feel so sad and was so deeply against what Jesus stood for and what kind of man he was, this church does not advocate for loving your neighbor, or spreading kindness to everyone like Jesus would have, and I stand by that. To this day this church is the worst and most hateful church I have attended, and I attend churches around the country regularly. I would not recommend at all unless you wish to take the path of hatred towards others and go against Jesus’s core values and the path of love, genuine kindness, and compassion that god wants for us all.

The First Unitarian Church of Denver restored my faith in what a church is meant to be. It’s a truly welcoming space where everyone—regardless of background, identity, or beliefs—is encouraged to explore, question, and grow. Instead of rigid dogma, this church fosters open-minded discussions, personal reflection, and a deep commitment to social justice. It beautifully blends spirituality with reason, honoring both faith and science. The sense of community is strong, and the focus on equality and action makes it a place where values are truly lived. If you’re searching for a spiritual home that embraces individuality, inclusivity, and the betterment of humanity, I highly recommend visiting and experiencing it for yourself.
