I have been in awe of God working in this church since the day I walked in the doors 14 years ago.  Pastor Craig, the entire staff and volunteers go beyond your dreams on what they do.  The Holy Spirit is alive at every service I attend at this church. I wished the services lasted longer because I don't want to see them end.  I am so inspired by God's hand and what he is doing inside as well as outside the walls of this church.  If I could, I would invite the entire world to attend Mission Hills Church.

What a wonderful church. The pastor Craig is amazing. I was not going to church very often. Maybe a couple times a year. I now attend every Saturday service. We were going to this church for a very short time when he first took the lead about eight years ago. I wasn't sure what to expect but he got me engaged from the first sermon.

Impressive church, great vibe friendly people. You are able to check in your kids for service. Kids are separated by age groups. Kids always seem to have fun and tell us all about what they learned about God and Jesus.

formatted_address: 12455 E Mississippi Ave #101, Aurora, CO 80012, United States
name: Crosswind Community Church of Denver

reviews.text: I didn’t feel welcomed and accepted. The people of the church were rude to me. I’m autistic and had my noise canceling headphones on so I could listen to the service. 2 people ripped them off.
Good people that help the cumminty the most in hood 1040 cafee is the best local coffee I've seen in a long time 🙏🛹🛹

"I've been on a personal journey to strengthen my relationship with God. I recently visited Crosswinds Church and found the people there to be wonderful. The pastor was incredibly friendly and our conversation was very touching."

I never thought being part of a church could look like this. Having grown up as a Christian and raised in different churches my entire life I've been to my fair share of different churches who make church just something that you attend weekly. A year ago my husband and I we're searching for a church that we could be more involved with. I can honestly say I've never been more welcomed and loved on by any other church or Christians my entire life. That's not to say those other churches were bad, but I never felt that connected beyond attending on Sundays or some Wednesdays. I've been to many churches here in Denver growing up, Los Angeles, Seattle, and even Detroit...but this small yet powerful group believers really live out the word of God through their actions and the way they care for others with arms wide open. I could go on and on... but the main thing that I take away from being part of this church is how the main focus is truly ALL about Jesus and LOVING on other people through genuine community. I call this place home because of the authenticity of the members and the servant leadership I've witnessed here Crosswind. Blessings in your search for a church home, would love you to have you join our church family and am happy to answer any questions you may have!

We are truly blessed to be part of this church. Upon joining in 2012, we instantly felt the genuine love of Christ through its members. And now, 6 years after, we can still feel that same genuine love and we are blessed to have members who are faithful in serving and doing God’s work.

formatted_address: 200 S University Blvd, Denver, CO 80209, United States
name: The Pearl Church

reviews.text: We were so blessed to be welcomed for our conference. The little interaction we had with the few members that were present to facilitate the conference were such kind and attentive individuals. Thank You for your heart of Service and the vision for the community.

Absolutely love this church. My husband and I travel for work and try to find a church in each city we go to. We stumbled on this one and still talk about how much we loved it. The passion and love is genuine from the lobby to the worship and sermon. The community here is so kind and welcoming. I’ve never been to a church where I felt like I had friends immediately. People connected with us intentionally on day one and remembered us when we returned. It was such a shock as an east coaster but so endearing and heartwarming. The music was powerful and the message was as well. My heart leapt every service. I only went three times and miss it already. Highly recommend this church!!

I was able to visit The Pearl Church several years ago with the youth group from City Church in Albuquerque, New Mexico.
The people I met were all very friendly and helpful.
We love Pastor Doug and Pastor Donna. They have a phenomenal team who obviously care about being the hands and feet of Jesus.

The Pearl Church is an incredibly special place to worship! If you’re looking for a home church - this is it! Pastor Doug is absolutely hilarious and preaches on messages that are relatable to daily life that inspires personal growth, empathy, goodness and spiritual revival. (Pastors Elliot, Donna, Malia and Kaiya are all pretty great too!) Times when we couldn’t make it in person (which was often for a season), we caught the (YouTube ) online service- it’s super well done and makes you still feel apart of the community. There’s a lot of opportunity to be a part of the church life family too from groups or simply visiting in the lobby with others. Pearl Church is an oikos that makes you feel welcome and loved. And the worship team is so powerful here - when you walk in and hear everyone singing you can truly feel God’s hand at work here. I leave every service feeling so energized and filled with such gratitude! 🙌

formatted_address: 8242 N Pecos St, Denver, CO 80221, United States
name: Kingdom Church Denver

reviews.text: This an amazing church that I am overjoyed to call my second home. Apostle Ryan is an amazing man of God and pastor, who has helped reignite the fire and love that I have for God. His wife, Lady A, is a selfless and beautiful woman of God and I am so blessed to call her my sister in Christ. All of the people within the ministry have become a special part of my life and I am proud to call them family. Everyone in Kingdom Church has a special place reserved for them in Heaven and I cannot wait to be seated next to them, beside the King of Kings. ❤️ All Glory to God for the beautiful people he has created! Hallelujah!

This is a great church!  God is in the building!  The people are super nice.  It's very real.  The worship is so meaningful.  Apostle Ryan is a really great pastor who listens to God, follows the Holy Spirit's leading and is very informative and interesting. This church is NEVER boring.
This church was very nice, the pastor did a great job for my cousin's funeral services.
Great servies ..Come meet Jesus there...

I have been attending this church (off and on) since I was in 5th grade. Not many churches I have been to except you as you are. They expect you to be dressed head to toe in your "Sunday best". Not New Song.
New Song became a home for me and my family. It's hard to feel lost or not connected here. There are a ton of outreaches and outlets you can plug into so you can grow with God more than your one a day Sunday commitment. And the worship?! There are no words strong enough to explain the soul driven power it holds. You should just come check it out.  Even if you can't attend in person you can stream online. It's a real blessing how technology can keep us connect to God. Even more so in these trying times. :)

formatted_address: 660 S Broadway, Denver, CO 80209, United States
name: Denver United Church

reviews.text: Amazing church in the Denver area. I've been coming here since March this year. I'm new to Denver, Colorado and I've never felt at home at a church like I do here. I feel so blessed to call this home and the people there my extended family. They make me feel so loved and welcome. With the loss of both of my parents fairly recent this is exactly what I need. Thank you for being the hands and feet of Jesus and I'm thankful I've been given the opportunity to do such as well. Thanks DU Family.
Sweet and warm. They are paper cups free so don't forget to bring your mugs to have some good coffee and tea. :)
Well chosen worship team, theology is solid, free bagels & coffee. Clean, well maintained with free parking. Great people, small groups, and young adult groups.

Except for the lady who rudely asked if she could help me in a very condescending way as though I was not just in the church for three hours. I was in my car for approximately 2 minutes texting my fiance. When a volunteer of the church came up to me in the most non Christian unfriendly unbelievable way possible. Jesus would NEVER do that.
But this is a great church otherwise.

A wonderful Easter service.
I'm from out of town (N.W Florida.  My home in Denver has been established . If your truly seeking the lord daily in your life this part of the family of our God is awesomely awaiting your arrival.

formatted_address: 1075 Park Ave W, Denver, CO 80205, United States
name: Grace City Church

reviews.text: Had a great experience at this church when visiting the city. Welcoming, friendly, God-loving people. Biblically sound worship with just the right blend of reverence and come-as-you-are. Grace filled and gospel centered message. I’d come back for sure.

Grace City Church is a place where the glory of God is felt in every service, bringing peace, hope, and transformation to all who enter. Through powerful worship, inspiring messages, and a strong sense of community, the church helps people grow in their faith. Whether you're seeking spiritual renewal or a welcoming place to connect, Grace City Church offers a space filled with God’s presence. With a heart for serving others and sharing His love, this church is a true home for believers.

Wonderful church sharing the Gospel of Jesus Christ. The people here love God, love Denver, and love each other. I've been attending for over three years since moving to CO from NY and this church has become my family. If you're new to Denver, come check out this church and get connected. This is a place for everyone to come and feel welcomed.

I had a very nice visit on sunday at the church during my recent travel to the city.

Everyone I spoke with was friendly but not overbearing.

The message was biblically sound and very practical.

This is a church focused on making a positive impact in the community.

If I lived in or around downtown Denver I would definitely consider making this my home Church.

We finally found our community. Our people who understand that we too, are just humans who make mistakes and try to learn from them. We serve a God of GRACE and LOVE who will meet us where we’re at and remind us of the power of the cross. So grateful for this church where family and chaotic lives have been welcomed by people who are simply trying to find peace and serve our Creator… just like us.♥️

formatted_address: 1820 Broadway, Denver, CO 80202, United States
name: Trinity United Methodist Church

reviews.text: I surprised my husband with this evening out and we were not disappointed! It was beautiful, delightful and enchanting! #Candlelight Concert (#Fever) wasabout as delightful of an evening we could have hoped for!
What a lovely experience. The venue, the ambiance and quartet were beautiful. Made for a romantic and peaceful evening. A suggestion for future candlelight events and evening of Vavaldi.

Incredible experience! I loved that they told the audience a little bit about the composer and the songs that they were playing. I wish it was a little longer at the 60 minutes flew by! It made classical music super accessible

Stunning. Truly. We all go through life in a very lonely state. Surrounded by likes…but without the energy of warmth and goodness. There is a strength in this church. There is a beauty that will shift you. At this time in our lives it is imperative to find fellowship and hope and unconditional. No matter your beliefs or where you come from- I hope you stop by and feel what I felt today. With love, Lisa
Came here for the Pink Floyd tribute candlelight concert. The music was amazing in this beautiful venue. Gorgeous church.

formatted_address: 3300 Larimer St, Denver, CO 80205, United States
name: The Summit Church

reviews.text: I am from the Bible Belt and was visiting Denver for work.  I found the Summit - Denver on Google.  Upon arrival, I felt very welcomed.  It was refreshing to see so many cultures together in one church.  Pastor Andy noticed me and spent a great deal of time chatting before service.  The people were active participants in worship and not merely spectators.  The message by Pastor Andy was on-point, truth with love.  So much wisdom in a half hour.  If you are searching for a church, this is a Must Try.

We absolutely love this church! I’m honestly surprised by the negative reviews mentioning cliques, because our experience was the complete opposite. We moved from a large church in Denver to The Summit specifically looking for genuine community, and from our very first service we felt welcomed. People came up to introduce themselves. The first two services we even had members of the church come up and ask us about getting coffee or breakfast afterwards.  We quickly got plugged into a wonderful city group, and it was clear this wasn’t a “sit, worship, listen, and leave” kind of church. Summit is all about doing life together in community. Beyond that, Pastor Andy is deeply grounded in Scripture. His sermons aren’t about feelings or cultural trends; they’re about faithfully teaching the word of God. Although we recently moved to another state, we’re hopeful to find a church like Summit again. We can’t say enough good things about our time there! It truly shaped our lives and faith in such a positive way
If you are looking for a great church to get connected with look no further, they have great community and are teaching straight from the Bible.

I'm leaving this review on past experiences here, talking like 10 years ago past. We came to this church after our home church folded. It was hard to go from somewhere where the congregation was like family to a place where we knew nobody. However, I made friends quickly and joined 2 groups, one was the younger single crowd, the other older (30-50s) with kids (I had a daughter). I never felt unwelcome or unwanted either. Granted, I put effort into meeting people, didn't just sit there and do nothing. Sometimes it takes work people.....
Seeing the reviews here though for the time since then,  makes me wonder if I'd have the same experience if I showed up again.

I attended this church for about a year. I liked the music and sermons but this church is missing the mark on what it means to be a true Jesus follower. As a lot of other reviewers also stated, this church is very very cliquey and does not like newcomers which is very strange for "Jesus followers". After a whole year of attending this church, I knew no one here (and I am extroverted). This is a come on Sunday, sing, listen to a sermon, and leave kind of church.

They make it so incredibly hard to join a city group (small group)... you have to attend one of their classes that are rarely offered and then the girl who teaches it (a dark curly haired 20-something) stated, "Don't expect your city group members to be your friends or your social circle". I found that comment very strange and counter to Jesus' example of building community. I went to one city group meeting but it was really inauthentic and awkward so I never went back.

There are much better churches in Denver to attend. I'm sad churches like this exist because this may be the only church some people ever attend and it may turn them away from continuing to seek God. I do hope this one chooses to change their cliquey ways and actually practices what Jesus taught and lived as an example.

formatted_address: 3000 S Wadsworth Blvd, Denver, CO 80227, United States
name: Colorado Church

reviews.text:
Visited Sunday, August 31, 2025
Appreciated a humble, lovely worship time! The pastor sermon gave me a concept to chew on all week and for the rest of my life. Thank you, Four substituting a visitor away from her home Church and encouraging me.

Friendly people and a diverse congregation from across western Denver and Littleton. The experienced lead pastor delivers very strong sermons that are consistently well-researched, Bible-based and practically applied. Contemporary worship music. Colorado Church is a newer non-denominational church, with a personal size and style. My family went from visitors (and didn't feel claustrophobic) to regulars (known by name) in just a couple months.

Best Church in Colorado. If you are looking for a place to grow your relationship with Jesus in an environment where you will feel loved and valued, look no further.

Everything about this place is incredible. Pastor Evan is incredible. The worship is incredible. The kids program is incredible. The congregation is warm, welcoming and kind. There are many small groups available to help you get connected.

The Holy Spirit is alive and well in Colorado Church. If you are on the fence about coming to church, I dare you to stop by. You won’t regret it. This place is unlike any place of worship I have experienced.

So thankful that I found Colorado Church. I urge you to walk through our doors and experience this for yourself.

Blessed to be part of this life-giving community! My family felt welcomed the moment stepped foot in the parking lot three years ago. Our three kids are plugged into youth and eager to come each and every week. My husband and I have found authentic friendships here too! Our pastor knows his congregation by name and welcomes you at any point in your spiritual journey!

Colorado Church has dramatically changed my life. My wife and I have found not just a home, but a family here. The worship leader is beyond talented and leads everybody so well into the true heart of worship. Sermons always speak right to my situation and challenge me in mercy. We love this church!

formatted_address: 1801 S Logan St, Denver, CO 80210, United States
name: Hope Church

reviews.text: Hope community Church is a true staple of what Denver has to offer. Hope is as it's name's sake a community! One filled with Joy, love, kindness, compassion and integrity! There welcoming atmosphere and love for there neighbors is a true blessing in it's self. But the best part of hope is there deep connection to our savior himself. I'm truly grateful for the experiences that'll last a lifetime from hope. I'd recommend everyone to give them a try because I promise you won't regret it.

Whenever we are in Denver we make it a point to attend Hope Community Church.  The Holy Spirit always speaks to us through the Sermons & Song.  God is alive in this congregation!
We continue to daily pray for Pastor Dean Wirz and his staff.
My wife and I joined this church a couple years ago and have been welcomed into the community. It was easy to get plugged in. The worship and teaching is great!
Great place really gives you hope

formatted_address: 3690 Cherry Creek S Dr, Denver, CO 80209, United States
name: Central Christian Church of Denver

reviews.text: Went there to pick up my grand baby. Staff was very friendly.  The main thing that impressed me was the security and keeping the kids safe. Awesome 👌.

Central Christian is a very welcoming church that is open to the public. It can be described as a transition from Catholic because they celebrate communion every week without any requirements; it is available to all. They worship and message is always centered on the words of Jesus. The two morning services are slightly different with various bible study groups meeting between the two services. The open lobby / gathering area is a great place and time to meet some very accepting and loving people who are happy to see you. The kids' Sunday school operates for all three time slots and is entertaining. We welcome all, and hope to see you soon!

As a Disciples of Christ denomination member, this church is a gem and an oasis in metropolitan Denver. Went to a service here while on vacation, and the sermon was on point and solid. Service well organized, structured, and had just the right balance of everything one could ask for, on seeking the Lord. Wonderful people, check it out everyone!
My husband and I have found a welcoming and loving church family that we have been blessed to enjoy work 15 years! Callum, heard the good news from our senior pastor Canaan Harris.
They are very kind to host our son's chess tournaments. Thank you!

formatted_address: Hallett Academy, 2950 Jasmine St, Denver, CO 80207, United States
name: The Hills Church

reviews.text: I am so blessed to call this church my home! Each week I’m challenged and encouraged to grow in my walk as a Christ follower and it is so refreshing to be in a community of believers that is diverse racially, socially and economically. I love our people :) Believers and sceptics are welcome. Come as you are, we’d love to meet you!
In an era when the evangelical church is a mixed bag, The Hills is about the things that Christ was about. Love this crowd.
Awesome ways of teaching God's word
As usual, l learned and was loved back to a healthy man.
Friendly church.

formatted_address: 2707 W Mississippi Ave, Denver, CO 80219, United States
name: Victory Outreach Church of Denver

reviews.text: This is a nice place to come and worship. Pastor Tom is very amazing and very closed to God. I hope anyone around the city can come and experience this amazing victory inside of the promise of God.

First and foremost I want to thank God for my salvation. If it had not been for Victory Outreach Denver I would be out in the world lost and in a dark place. Since the first time I walked in the doors I was welcomed with open arms of these lovely people who go here my brother's & sister's. Never once was any one rude to me they made me fell so welcomed, I was 8 months pregnant & have a 5 year old son who loves going into kids G.A.N.G short for God's Annointed Now Generation, and they also have nursery for any infants. At first for me leaving my son with anyone else was difficult but they care so much & also teach my son about Jesus, while my self & husband have the opportunity to be able to focus in service & have our time for worship, prayer & be able to take the word in without worrying that my children are bored. I thank them for providing child care not only for my now 6 year old but also for my now 15 month old he loves nursery, he also gets tough about Jesus, they have books & even play worship music. We have been attending VOD for a year and a half now, we would not suggest any other church. VOD is truly a unique church.
This is my family they make me feel accepted more than my regular family does so I love this church and the congregation here .
Beautiful church, be prepared for a complete change of your life and a stronger walk with Jesus Christ!

Where do I even Begin?? I've been attending this church for at least a year, It seems as if it is a Cult more than a Church.. They are not friendly what so ever, my children feel judged when attending. I have an 8 year old son who absolutely hates going, he says other kids make him feel bad about having glasses. They idolize the pastor WAY too much..Like it's actually creepy.. I just feel straight up judged when going. And the people in this church act as if its a PRIVILEGE to be in the presence of their pastor.I get being appreciative, but they cross the line. 90% of the time during preachings I feel like the pastor screams at us and ridicules us more than guides & Loves us. These people who claim to be followers of Jesus certainly don't act like it. Do better.

name: BridgeWay Church

reviews.text: Would not recommend if you are a young adult. They tend to back evangelicals who have their own set of problems and it will be hard for you. They are a step above confessional churches however. I first came here in 2018 after a ski trip and glad I did. I was able to make the first half before catching my flight out and felt at peace and heart renewed. They changed after the pandemic.
Great to hear Danny Silk as a guest speaker. God does not punish. Let's practice joy.

I am totally biased because I am friends with the church's senior leadership. But I visited them last weekend, and I want to echo what many other reviews have said. You will encounter Jesus and the Holy Spirit here. You will encounter people who love and want to see Jesus transform your lives. You will see all walks of life here, from people who used to be homeless, people of every race and nation, and young and old alike. This is what Jesus meant when he said that he came to call everyone to himself.

I went to this church, They welcomed me, Walked me in made me feel comfortable. Got me a seat. They did a normal praise and worship, A little bit after they came to pray for me, and we joined hands in the largest circles I’ve ever prayed in.

A couple of them came directly to me and asked if They could pray for me. I said yes, and they began to pray for me, and they put their hands on me. All of a sudden I felt my temperature rise.

I was a little bit afraid at first it felt like I took a heavy dose of niacin times 10. The Holy Spirit was on fire one of the people that prayed for me said let the Fire of the Holy Spirit come upon me and it sure did.

I went to a lot of churches in my life, but I never felt like that before. Thank you for everything. I really appreciate that the spirit of our father in heaven and the Lord Jesus Christ is definitely in this place.

This church will transform you and mold you as a spirit filled person. The atmosphere is electric and you will feel the Holy Spirit tangibly in this place. Signs and wonders and miracles and healings are all over the place. It is such a blessing to be part of this church and we are so thankful to the Lord for leading us here.

Pastor Scott and Jackie have a deep rooted heart for the unreached Spanish only speakers in their neighborhood. They work tirelessly to provide spiritual growth and real life opportunities to be supported and engage in tangible ways with Jesus. I have been a witness for 14 years to the connection they have with anyone who walks in their doors. I have been a witness for that same amount of time watching them minister to their neighborhood in passionate ways. Grace is safe, Grace is loving, Grace is connecting.

I have watched the ministry of grace and life Church for some years now. They are doing amazing ministry work with young people. I am personally committed to assisting them financially because of the intentional and positive impact that they have on young people.
Warm and friendly. Christ centered. Great leadership.
Very welcoming place which serves hundreds in the community!
A place where God is praised freely

reviews.text: Third time I visited this year and the vibe is just not good. People are not friendly or engaging. They talk the talk but don't walk the walk. Will not return again. I was hopeful  it would work out as it is close to me, not a fellowship vibe at all.

Gospel-centered church following common Acts 29 community engagement. The small group/broader church community is incredibly strong for the size of church. The whole intention is to live life together. It's powerful to see that ideal working.

Probably the most welcoming church I have ever been to. Great people at the service, awesome people on the staff, outstanding pastors, and most important a great message every week out of the word of God. This church truly teaches the Bible and the actions of the church follow the word of God.

Gosh, it's terrible that I am reviewing a church as if I would a restaurant... But my first visit to this church. Not sure of the man/pastor preaching today... I donno, it was pretty boring. His voice also doesn't carry well at all. So my search for a decent church continues...
We felt so welcomed and appreciated, the moment we walked in the door.  I am grateful for my experience at Fellowship Denver, and plan to continue attending…

Great Pastor's at this Church. They make everyone feel so very welcome. Caring Church community as well. A good Church, doing good things. I  recommend Family Worship Center for all, everyone. God Bless.
My Grandkids And I Felt Very Welcomed Here. Great Atmosphere, Friendly People. Great Service. We Absolutely Loved It!

Aside from all this, the chapel is lovely and peaceful.

I know GOD is everywhere. I could feel HIM here.
I'm 67 and I took my 89 year old deaf mom to this church and we had a wonderful worship time. We / I plan on returning as soon as possible.

Love this church with my heart. I went there when it was a preschool I’ve had some good days there and there’s nothing that can change the way that I see that church because in my eyes it’s “bright stars preschool” and god blesssed it and took it into his hands ❤️🙏

Outgoing, loving congregation. Thanks for all you do for the community.
Such a great message on Sunday as well.
Great teaching and worship. Also shared/potluck breakfast every Sunday before the service is really nice.

reviews.text: God is doing a great work in this ministry.  The words "man of God" have been watered down in this age, but not so with Apostle/ Prophet Leon Emerson!  If you ever wanted to see a powerful woman in God, you must also hear Yvonne Emerson speak a life changing word!

Look no more! Great preaching, Great worship, Great Pastors, Great people. If you are looking LOOK NO MORE and come. You have a choice of early Sunday service 8:30 A.M. or 11:00 A.M with bible study in between. Tuesday bible study with a youth service.
I enjoy going to this church people are loving and friendly and Gods spirit is there also, the pastor is Pastor Leon and Yvonne Emerson preaching Gods word.
Sound  doctrine taught. 🙏🏼
Warm, loving people...

He picks me up and drops me off from church every morning. I believe God does everything for a reason because I attend every morning that he decides to pick me up. Thanks, Pastor Hall, for showing me the light ✝️🙏🤗.

I enjoy attending church here, they treat you like family. Warm and Friendly atmosphere!
Man very good service  and man,th e music was awesome  I'm going back

reviews.text:
This is such an amazing church and worship Center. Pastor Ron and Pastor Pam are amazing spirit-filled believers. The atmosphere is always beautiful the music is beautiful the people the congregation is beautiful. As soon as you walk in the door you feel love.
All of the outreaches to help God's people. The food ministry for people who don't have food to feed their family. The Thanksgiving ministry where they make sure the entire city of Denver has food for the holidays. The Christmas outreach they give food and presents for the entire family.

And this has helped me to draw closer to God and obey Him. I’m very thankful for my church family and I encourage everyone who doesn’t have a church home to come and visit. A very warm, welcoming and friendly environment. Since attending higher level, my life has seen nothing but increase in all areas! It has reignited the fire within me!!!  I encourage everyone who needs a change or a boost in life to attend as it shifted my life in an incredible way! I definitely have went to a higher level in God!

formatted_address: 1650 S Birch St, Denver, CO 80222, United States
name: Celebration Community Church

reviews.text: Our family was introduced to Celebration through one of their "Summer Nights" neighborhood get-togethers. We were warmly welcomed into a vibrant community of people who are genuine in their faith journey and love for others. The worship and teaching focus less on a "flashy/feel-good/go home" experience and more on being grounded in the gospel, fostering an environment of authenticity, reflection, lament, healing, praise, and love. We're grateful to be part of a small group that shares life together, as well as having opportunities to serve alongside organizations like the LoVVe Project in the neighborhood. Celebration has certainly been a fun place for us to get serious about God!
Pastor Jill is kind and caring there’s communion every Sunday and the band is awesome

Never attended this church personally, but the people that go there are courteous, nice, and very earthy. Lol.

Been part of their "trunk or treat" festivals every year for 12 years. It is a time where the neighborhood comes together and kids have fun with candy in their bags. They also have a garden setup for food that is given to charities or food banks from my understanding. I do miss that part of living in Denver, CO. since moving to Minnesota in 2019. :(

Ah, the memories.

I have attended Celebration Community Church since 1998, when it was founded. Our founding pastor retired in 2020 and our new pastor, Jill, started then.
I always think of our main room (sanctuary) as a place where I experience some of my happiest hours. Christmas Eve services, potlucks and parties, prayers, singing, preaching that encourages my faith and heart, summer kid camps,  meeting new people (including international people), game nights, blood drives,  retreats and seminars.
The leadership is earnest, caring and loves Jesus. It is a place to grow in community and faith.
Love being a part of Celebration. I am stretched by God's Word and the community here that is living out the Gospel so beautifully. The children's program is wonderful.

I was visiting from out of town and ran across the "In Christ Fellowship" (Berean) church and their Sunday worship service. They were extremely welcoming, with a very spirited service steeped in the Word, accompanied by deep soulful prayers and an incredible choir/music ensemble. The ICF church is a great blessing!

Pastor Ron Fox is an amazing bible teacher! If you are looking for a fellowship that teaches sound biblical truth, please look no further! What a great experience I've had with this amazing family of believers! I have been looking for a long while for a place to call home and I think I've finally found it! Please make your way to Berean Bible Church
First visit back was a experience of a life time. I didnt get to say much that i really wanted to because i know where i came from. I still feel blessed to be home.

reviews.text: This has been my home church for years!  I wouldn't go anywhere else . I have the best friends here, and get challenged in the places I need to grow. This is a church that does not talk just the talk, but walk the walk. Rooted in Christ's love, this church creates a family like no other. We are all here for each other and carry each other's burdens. We have fun together. Most importantly, we are biblically based and bring God's word into fruition. Come check us out! 😀😁

I really appreciate the work the church does. In my opinion, the most important thing that is being lived out by this church is how the church, or rather God's kingdom is not a building. It is made up of many different people who come from many different backgrounds who all have have the same mentality of having Jesus as Lord. I am trying to keep this brief as possible but if you are looking for a relationship with God, this is a great place to begin your journey.

We love this church!! We’ve been part of this church family for almost 5 years, and it’s so welcoming and diverse - full of people from all walks of life and different backgrounds. We are excited for our kids to grow up with many wonderful people in their lives providing a positive influence.

If I were any of you I would not waste an ounce of your mental health, time, or donations on this place for several reasons. A few years back my family attended this church for 3 years. And it was not 3 years of family, reciprocity, and spreading the true gospel as was sold to us. But 3 years of a small church of mindless self righeteous hypocrites who spreaded misinformation about the very faith they preach. It was not family, but a seperation of cliques like high school, and drama queens who only cared about themselves. I was told a few times by some of the older folks there not to question the pastor or what he said. I was a naturally curious person though and wanted to know to learn how to get saved which they claimed was by works, grace, baptisim and a checklist. A false claim. It was by grace alone. Anyways, when some members of my family cried out for help they were not at all helpfull or welcoming. It only confused the hell out of me when I was 12, 13, and 14 on my Chistian path. They taught things about the very faith they were supposed to represent but clearly did not. This is just another church of man, not Christ, decieving it's members for their own benefit. Not sheep and sheperds but wolves and wolves in sheeps clothing.

formatted_address: 1530 Logan St, Denver, CO 80203, United States
name: Cathedral Basilica of the Immaculate Conception

reviews.text: I was looking for a Catholic Church for Sunday Mass while we were in Colorado for our Grandson's Fight. I came across the Cathedral Basilica and was impressed with the pictures I saw on Google that I wanted to see it for myself. I'm so Happy I went, because it was the most Beautiful Church I have ever seen in person.  The architecture was amazing everything from the outside to the inside was very detailed in design. As soon as I walked in I could feel a special feeling come over me that I began to cry. If you are ever in Denver, Colorado, I suggest you go by this Basílica.

A beautiful cathedral. The craftsmanship is amazing. We spoke with priest who told us of the history of the construction of the cathedral. The stain glass windows are gorgeous. There images of Christs crucifixton carved into the walls. It's worth a visit.

Okay so from the top of the state Capitol this cathedral looked awesome. We took a short walk in the rain to see inside. The front of the structure was amazing. I went inside and my jaw hit the ground. It was the second most beautiful church/cathedral I've been in. I walked in, looked around in awe  and questioned myself if I should take a picture. But I talked to God and asked him to forgive me if I'm doing wrong but it's too beautiful to not share with others. I walked in deeper and sat and prayed for a moment. Turned around and saw where the choir would be and a huge organ setup. Overall this cathedral is phenomenal. I would love to attend mass here one time.

Absolutely beautiful and moving experience.  I mean Mass is always gonna be great, but this was wonderful.

I love the 6:30 pm Sunday Mass.  It's the perfect time I can tuck in my little ones with dad and go.

The Mass is completely in Latin at this Mass.  they have guided but I wish they had more they can be tricky to find. But I mean I know the Mass so I wasnt lost.

Security is amazing.  Bring on Colfax I thought it might be sketchy to park but they had security patrolling.  There were also some in the church.  They were also parishioners so it wasn't contracted company ( idk I just love that)

I like the confession but the priest was a little chatty which I usually don't mind but because of that some people couldn't go.

Twice a month they do Gregorian Chant.  I truly reellike onion a whole different place in a different era.  I also veil and there were a lot of others who do.  I know I shouldn't, but I didn't feel as self conscious.  Usually at other churches I'm the only one.

So if you're looking for a traditional, welcoming, beautiful place this is it.  I love in Littleton and I will definitely be coming here to this Mass

Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception is only a block away from the Colorado Capitol we toured before.
The Cathedral dates back to 19 cent, built in neo Gothic style with two bell towers. Interior is richly decorated with beautiful stained glass

name: Denver Community Church

reviews.text:
This is such a beautiful church. The architecture, the stained glass windows... It is absolutely beautiful.  Great walk but lots of closures on the streets recently due to contractions that seem to be never ending.
The church has to put fencing around the building itself-which is a bummer; Realizing that many of our historical, cultural and religious places of worship are actually under threat from being completely TRASHED, due to lack of respect and possibly proper healthcare to those that walk the streets below. It's saddening.
I pray that someday we find a way to make our streets safer,  we take care of the space we all inhabit, and people start to Love Thy Neighbors otherwise. Great walk and beautiful church- all the while.

My family and I have attended Denver Community Church off and on for about ten years, and we recently decided to return to see if it was still a good fit for us. Unfortunately, it no longer feels like the same church we once knew. In our experience, the messages seem to focus more on promoting certain viewpoints than on teaching directly from God’s word. This may work for some people, but it no longer aligns with what our family is looking for in a church.
Most welcoming and non judgemental churchI have ever attended. Sense of belonging on first visit.

This is a wonderful church that I highly recommend that people attend. They are inclusive and loving. As a blind bisexual man, I felt loved and accepted, and this will be my church home while I am in Denver. Whether you are a conservative or a progressive, they will accept you. Regardless of your sexual orientation, they will accept you. Regardless. If you have any disabilities, they will accept you. The music is really easy to pick up, + it is wonderful and not like one of those churches where it's overly too loud. There are tons of opportunities to serve. There is also an lgbtq group that meets on Wednesdays. The sermons are thought-provoking and insightful. Communion works like this. The bread is gluten free, + you can dip the bread in either wine or juice. On every third Sunday of the month, members who want to participate or even if you're not a member yet, can go to The Green room. And if you have prayer requests or want to pray with the people there, you can join in prayer. Like I said, I highly recommend this church. They are all inclusive, loving and accepting. Services are on Sundays at 10:00. A.m..

My husband and I first starter going to this church before we were married. We had one of the pastors here marry and council us. As time went on it became clear the leadership had an agenda that was not biblical but being warped to fit a certain narrative and the main pastor’s giant ego. That pastor has lone decided to pursue other things because once you thoroughly destroy the truth, there’s not much left to believe in. Don’t waste your time here. Jesus loves you, find a church that respects His Word.

formatted_address: 2950 S University Blvd, Denver, CO 80210, United States
name: Christ Church Denver

reviews.text: Christ Church is an amazing place - I felt at home almost immediately. The congregation is warm, welcoming and diverse. The services in their beautiful chapel are spirit-filled and uplifting with plenty of music and sermons that are inspiring and relevant with a great dash of humor.  Fr Terry greets us by name every time!  Excellent programs for children and teens, too.

Christ Church is filled with love, caring, and the Holy Spirit. This has been my home since fall of 1990. I came broken and this place has healed me, taught me, restored me, and continues to do so. Father Terry is also the most consistently amazing preacher I've ever heard. I've served God, in this place, in a large variety of ways and continually find new ways to grow and experience his love through the Word, the people of this community, and prayer. There is something for everyone, come join us!

When we started looking for a church home in Denver a year ago, we knew our search ended here. We've rarely been in such a welcoming church. The truth of the Bible is preached and taught, people are so warm and welcoming, and Jesus is glorified in and through the ministries here.

I've been at Christ Church for 11 years after church shopping all over Denver.  From the first day we came, we felt loved and welcomed and we knew that something was different here. It celebrates the tradition of the Episcopal Church while embracing the future and the vision of reaching a modern world.  It has been my home, my community, and my family.

My parents (Helen and Bill Cozad) were dedicated members of Christ Church for decades. I live on the East Coast so only ever got to attend when I visited them. It was always a highlight of my trips to Denver. Although I have "defected" to the Lutheran church in my area, if I lived in Denver I would "have" to go to Christ Church. It is warm, inviting and uplifting. The incredible support that church members gave to my parents in their waning years was awesome and still so very much appreciated by me. Five star congregation in every way.

formatted_address: 1700 S Grant St, Denver, CO 80210, United States
name: Highlands Church Denver

reviews.text: So happy to have found this community. This is a group of people who are living out the message to love God and love our neighbors (yes, ALL of our neighbors).
Love everything about the Highlands and I always feel very welcome here!    The co-pastors are great.

Our experience in worship on the Sunday we visited for the first time was particularly positive. We were greeted and welcomed in a warm and friendly manner, and helped to find our way around. We met several friendly and gracious regular attendees who made us feel glad to be there. The music was good, the preaching was spot on, and the atmosphere was worshipful, welcoming, and extremely affirming. There was a very diverse crowd present, with lots of families and children, old and young worshipers, multicultural representation, and a robust LGBTQ population. It was a really terrific and heartwarming worship experience that I would highly recommend.

It is an open and affirming church. They will always state this publicly as their ethos. Communion each Sunday. They preach every scripture from a loving place rather than what most of us grew up with "judgment." Mostly white people that probably consider themselves to be liberal or moderate. They will have their "blindspots" but their sincerity allows for a fairly comfortable experience. They just created a type of "wailing wall" inside the church to leave a note and let whatever it is go!🙏🏾 Housed in an old church building from 1800.
Very cool, open, accepting, loving, no-pressure atmosphere in a beautiful old theater. Love the diversity and friendly, welcoming staff. Free coffee and tea anytime, and small bites after service.

formatted_address: 5555 W Evans Ave, Denver, CO 80227, United States
name: Lighthouse Church

reviews.text: Please  make sure  you are not mixing  grace with law. Jesus  came to set us free from law and religion.  We all need to be built  up in love. Love should  be are only aim. Fruit  comes by abiding  in the vine. Grace and peace be multiplied  to you. The power  of sin is in the law

I've been a member of the Lighthouse community since our early days meeting in the Presbyterian Church, and I have been blessed to witness its growth into our beautiful current campus. Throughout all these years, this church has been more than just a building; it has been a true beacon for me personally, offering guidance, hope, and a profound sense of belonging. I have seen the hand of God move in ways that are hard to express with words, fostering a community where personal transformations are a regular occurrence. The shared history and steadfast faith I've experienced here have been a foundational part of my spiritual journey.

What truly defines Lighthouse is its unwavering commitment to its core mission. We don't claim to be a perfect church, but we are passionate about our calling to shine the light of the Gospel, make disciples of Jesus, and do it all for the glory of God, as inspired by Matthew 5:14-16. In every single gathering, regardless of who is leading worship or preaching the sermon, the name of Jesus is declared boldly and unapologetically. If you are searching for a genuine, Christ-centered community that is passionate about the Gospel and dedicated to authentic worship, I wholeheartedly recommend paying us a visit.

Lighthouse Church is truly amazing! From the moment you walk in, you can feel such a warm, welcoming, and uplifting presence. The church is beautifully diverse, with people from every walk of life worshiping together as one family. The pastor is truly anointed by God, delivering powerful sermons that speak to the heart and inspire growth in faith. You can clearly see how God moves through him, and He is glorified in everything. I feel so blessed to have found such a solid, Spirit-filled church!

Just a few weeks in and really enjoy the sincerity and authenticity of the people here! They remembered my name and included me in immediately. Great worship and teaching as well. Fun that I got to help fix up the new church site too! Great to see it ALL DONE NOW! Woohoo!
My 4 years old love the children ministry.  It's a warm, welcoming church. Adult teaching is also amazing. We had a blessed time worshipping and listening to the sermon.

Chris and the worship team do a great job as well. This church loves Jesus—the one true Son of God, the cornerstone, and the Messiah.
We had my beloved mother in law's memorial here. The people are lovely and the church is so beautiful. Mike and Jane Romberger are really just angels. So greatful for them

Love this Church! Love Pastor John, and his staff! I know so many people that go there!
Loving Jesus and changing the world!
Friendly atmosphere.  Talked with guest services and very welcoming.  Will be back to hear their senior pastor!

Everything was great until the lead pastor came out. He said he didn’t like how some churches use the Bible to beat others down and to promote politics. But then moments later decided to use the Bible to “beat down” people who are gender nonconforming and  promote how he thinks we should vote in the election. Disheartening to experience. Just be aware of this if you are coming as they aren’t transparent on their website that not all people are welcome at this church

name: The Heights Church Denver

Totally packed, sound teaching, good music, pastor was actually funny too at times, but quite serious at others, perfect balance. A vibrant congregation from high schools to 50s and 60s and beyond. Really enjoyed it.

You will encounter God here as the Heights is a radically new testament church. Strong teaching, deep community, and missions focused. Not focused on the seating capacity but the sending capacity with church plants and local and global missions. Leadership is so clearly following what the Lord would have for this church. Come and be a part of what God is doing in Denver through the Heights.

My review is based on one visit. This Church seems as though they definetly herald the Bible. Great community. Everybody was so welcoming and i seen a familar face there who was greeting. God is doing big things at and in The Heights. Look forward to coming next week.

Blessings.
Joshua

O and most importantly they have amazing things going on for kids. Thanks yall

They say hi to me regardless of how bad my outfits are. we don’t get to see the coffee connoisseur’s faces all the time but when you get a good glimpse, it’s a good glimpse. preaching pastors coupled with the woke worship gets me every single time. i know it’s coming. but still.

We have always felt welcome, and the personal touch and family-oriented atmosphere have made our experiences consistently positive. Connecting with people has come naturally here. More importantly, we value the solid biblical teaching in both the main service and the kids’ church, and the worship times have been especially meaningful and uplifting.

My wife and I have attended Victory Church for five years now and we are very happy and blessed there! Spirit led worship! Inspiring messages from the Pastors! Opportunities to serve on the “Dream Team!” Thriving youth ministry! Awesome small groups!

From the staff to every single person I've met, the warmth, love, and genuine hospitality have been overwhelming in the best way. I've never felt more welcomed or more at home anywhere in my life. Every Sunday, I walk in expecting a word, and without
fail, GOD shows up through Pastor Jonathan's preaching. The HOLY SPIRIT moves in that place, and it's impossible not to feel it. As my work takes me elsewhere, I already know I'm going to miss this church more than words can express. If I could choose one church to call home for the rest of my days, it would be VICTORY CHURCH. This church, this pastor, this community they are beyond blessed, and so am I for having been a part of it, even if only for a season.

Visited this church. The place was full and lively. Early in the sermon the pastor declared, “If you plant your seed today, your harvest will come this week.”
That sounded good, but Isaiah 58:6-7 came to mind; God’s idea of devotion is freeing the oppressed and feeding the hungry, not paying for blessing. What I heard felt more like a transaction than worship.
Later the preacher shouted, “Rain is coming on your finances!” The crowd cheered. I remembered 1 Kings 18:29, when Baal’s prophets cried for rain and “no one answered.” That ancient scene was about trying to manipulate heaven through performance. The atmosphere here felt the same, with lots of noise, little surrender.
The message focused almost entirely on wealth and personal promotion. Jesus, when He spoke of following Him, said, “Deny yourself and take up your cross daily” (Luke 9:23). Here the call was to “believe for more” rather than to repent or serve.
The preacher told stories about his own success: “Look how God increased me; He’ll do it for you too.” 1 Corinthians 1:31 reminds us, “Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.” It was hard to find that humility.
Every prophecy promised peace and breakthrough. None warned or corrected. It matched Jeremiah 6:14, where false prophets say, “Peace, peace,” when there is no peace.
As I left, Revelation 3:17 echoed: “You say, I am rich, I have prospered, and I need nothing.” True prosperity is 1 Timothy 6:6; “Godliness with contentment is great gain.”
If Elijah walked into this sanctuary, I think he would repeat 1 Kings 18:21: “If the LORD is God, follow Him; but if Baal, follow him.” The same old desire for control, wealth, and performance, the spirit of Baal still hides behind polished lights and catchy faith slogans.

Great sound system, inspiring crowd energy, but the gospel was replaced by a deal. I left praying that this house would preach Christ crucified instead of cash multiplied.

I was really sad as my daughter has come to previous sermons with other pastors and she enjoyed them, but this one really showed the root of the community and I left with my heart feeling more pained than free. While I understand the interpretations of the Bible can often be different depending on the person I did not care for the use of Bible phrases, and trying to almost guilt me into giving of anything I have even if I were to have almost nothing. To be fair, I cannot say anything about any of the other sermons as this was my first time at this church, but from this experience, I will not be returning, and my daughter will not no longer be attending. We have found ourselves fulfilled at a different house of the Lord and will continue our journey there. I have no ill towards anybody there, including those that work, volunteer and give of their time there it is just not an alignment with our hearts. As a sidenote, I am in agreement that if you are able and willing and your heart, so calls you to it, you should be giving but for me giving is not just to the church, but it’s giving your time to those that may need it. It’s giving money to a family whose benefits are currently not being paid. It’s helping a single mom watch her child when she needs. It comes in all forms not just monetary.

reviews.text: I grew up believing a false gospel for ~25 years. reviews.text:
I loved this church. I loved the worship. I went for years and was pretty involved with the young adult ministry, where I met a lot of friends. For that, I am grateful.

Last year, the church was hosting its annual young adult retreat. I was in college and couldn’t afford to go. But don’t worry—they had an email and a team I could reach out to for funding… or so I thought. I emailed them and asked if I could attend one of the three days and pay around 30% of the actual cost. They declined and said I could only go for one day if I paid in full.

So what is this “funding” email for—just for show?

Mind you, this was a church I had been tithing to for years. A church that will spend thousands on decorations, lights, or whatever else. I had never felt so ashamed of my church. I haven’t been back since.

Amazing church and staff , felt truthfully welcomed and safe as well as the kid program is top notch. Highly recommended you will not be disappointed.  Ryan from Austin based RRC was at this location today and was just amazing. The kids loved it.

Disappointed and Unwelcome at Red Rocks Church

I’ve known about Red Rocks since the early days—I even met Sean years ago when I was teaching and saw him filming a music video. I was curious about the church ever since. Years later, after my divorce, I was struggling as a single mom and needed a safe place. I confided in them about my situation, hoping for support. Sadly, despite all the requests for donations, they offered no real assistance to a family in need.

Over time, I came to learn more about the Lakewood location, and the atmosphere has been consistently unwelcoming. The security team feels unorganized, and the children’s area has been disappointing—diaper changes are rare, and my interactions with staff like Heather have been unfriendly at best. The overall vibe is judgmental and cold, far from the supportive community I had hoped for.

At this point, I dread going. Even walking into the parking lot makes my skin crawl. The experience in person feels fake and disconnected, and they don’t even have a live speaker—everything is on screen. My advice: stay home and watch Sean’s messages online, as he’s the only reason I’d still listen at all.

reviews.text: The most loving and friendly environment I’ve been in in a church in a long time. I felt so welcome and my guest did is well. A great multicultural church great worship and authentic fellowship. This church is alive and growing well!

Living Church of God - we need more churches like this in Denver! Jesus is in the center! It's nice to see how many young people praise the Lord. They prayed for my wife for healing - the Lord healed her at the same service! All glory to God!

I have attended HOUSE since January of this year. I will say it was hard for me to connect, yet that is partly due to my own personal experience, and also not serving  for the first 6 months. I wanted to get a full understanding of how the ministry is had. The worship is free in every sense of what freedom in the Lord means. The young adults are on fire for the Lord! When you see that you can be sure God is in this place. I felt a deep sense of acceptance, in a way that includes all humanity. I could clearly discern the integrity of the leadership, and the soundness of the doctrine. The worship glorifies Jesus, honors the Father, and welcomes in Holy Spirit as they minister to Him. I've been thinking a lot about the choice to be at HOUSE. Just tonight, I sensed the Lord speaking to me about what we all need to feel part of a family. He revealed to me that HOUSE is a family, it is in the core of this church. The staff, the worship team, the pastors ( there are 3 Spirit filled and anointed pastors that alternate each weeks services ), the young adults, the women, and men's groups. The Pastors have a desire to disciple, and they have a prayer school, too. I have witnessed an entire row of young men, linking arms, worshiping God, making Jesus cool again, haha. But, that blessed my heart, and it really drove this Church home for me. Overall, HOUSE is a place where the Spirit of the Lord is, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. The unity, love, and rich kindness of Jesus is so felt and organic. Now that I'm serving in Children's church, which I have never had a desire to do before, I see the great lengths they go to in honoring the Lord and His people. The children's ministry is nurtured with the same intentionality as the Pulpit. Everything is bathed in prayer, even the orientation to serve. It's what I need in my life. It's what this world needs, the hurting, the broken, the unseen, and unknowns... It's truly a FAMILY. There motto is : He comes where He's wanted - I am one to vouch, God is present in this place!

Since we began attending and serving at Red Rocks a little over a year ago, my wife and I (who is currently an intern at Red Rocks) have been enjoying the most healthy and life-giving seasons of our marriage and life in general. Is Red Rocks perfect? Of course not. As Pastor Shawn says we are a bunch of imperfect people pursuing a perfect God. As someone who is a regular attender and volunteer as well as someone who knows a little bit more of what goes on behind the scenes, I can wholeheartedly say the way God is moving here is nothing short of miraculous and the directional leadership at this church is one of the most gifted yet humble teams any church has ever seen. Red Rocks is huge, with over 12,000 attending weekly as of February of 2017. If you are attending for the first time and want to get to know people the best way to do so is by serving in one of the ministries or signing up for a life group. It is easy to be anonymous at this church because many of the worship gatherings have 1,000+ people and you cannot expect the staff to meet everyone. If you want to get plugged in, take initiative to make it happen. If you attend for the first time, I recommend arriving 15 minutes early to find a good parking spot, especially on Saturday evening since that is when the pastors preach live. This is my most long winded google review but I feel strongly about this place because of how much it has impacted my family! You will not regret visiting.

reviews.text: Red Rocks Church! This beautiful church, full of the Lords love, the Lord speaks through all of their staff. A few weeks ago I got baptized for the third time. My first time was when I was a child, unaware of what that commitment meant. And once again when I accepted the Lord as my Savior as a teenager. Still unaware of the meaning of baptism and the relationship that the lord wanted with me. But when I got baptized at red rocks, they explained why, it’s a commitment with the Lord, to walk through the hills and valleys with Him. When they asked me why I wanted to get baptized I said,  “I just want to be free.” I was a prisoner in my own mind. Broken, and full of tears, this man prayed over me and there’s been so much change in my life since then. I stopped going to church when I was a teenager, this is the only church I’ve been going to consistently since then, because I know the Lord is working through them to teach me and grow me closer to Him. Am I the only one who finds it a little strange to give a church a Google review? Should I comment on the coffee? The choice of songs or their volume? The version of the Bible being read? The parking lot size? Or whether the pastor had enough life experience? Do I rate it based on whether I felt the Holy Spirit?

It’s easy to measure church by how well it aligns with me. But the more important question is: Was Christ the focus of the message?

What I’ve found at Red Rocks Church is that the message always comes back to Jesus. The music, the community, the teaching—all of it points people to Him. They often say, “If God is not the focus, then this is just a TED Talk and a concert.”

For me personally, this church has strengthened my walk with Christ and given my family a place to grow in faith together. That’s what matters most to me, and I’m grateful to be part of a church that keeps Christ at the center.

I was in the area and looking for a church to visit. I had a wonderful time at Red Rocks. Friendly faces, beautiful worship, and a biblically based message by Pastor Ryan that was also practical. The pastor also spoke in person not via a stream (someone noted a video screen in a comment but that wasn’t my experience).

I think Christ would once again sit down and fashion a whip because this church has taken the holy and corrupted it by turning it into an entertainment venue complete with singers that behave much like Mexican jumping beans, a celebrity staff they parade out that the congregation is expected to cheer and a million dollar-plus collection of lights, video walls and an  audio system cranked so loud I witnessed several people putting in earplugs. These things are meant to artificially reproduce an experience of the Holy Spirit and it's really sad.  If you're looking for a place to fellowship the way Christ's disciples came together loving each other, this isn't it.

One of the ushers even bumped into me without saying “excuse me.” Even though it wasn’t my fault, I still apologized, and he didn’t acknowledge it. There’s nothing Christ-like about that interaction at all. Community is super important and I didn’t see that yesterday.

Fell in love with this church. After my pastor took a new job out of state. I was hesitant about going to another church let alone looking for another church. Was invite by former church members and I was pleased and surprised. The word was great, the music was very good and the atmosphere was inviting. The pastor was very personable.

Not sure if it’s a Colorado thing or a lifegate thing; the outfits people wear on Sundays it’s crazy. Gym shorts, tshirt and thong sandals? But what’s even worst is EVERYONE shows up as mass is starting or late! 5 mins before mass it’ll be empty! Between the start of mass and 20 mins into is when the most amount of people come in. You might ask why that is? It’s because they know they can show up at 9:15 and someone will find them a seat upfront! So mid worship your being tapped on your shoulder to move over for the late people. I personally think 9:05 close the sanctuary doors and have everyone that shows up late to sit outside in overflow. I bet the following week everyone will show up early! People put on their best outfits for their birthday or wedding but not church? If it was a nuggets game everyone would be there an hour early. Really disappointed by lack of professionalism in Colorado

It feels a little weird reviewing a church but I'm a native here and would really love to see the culture shift in churches and possibly giving a fair and balanced review in love may help.

The teachings I found to be solid, (though too much effort in storytelling and it's hard to connect where the sermon is going) but the gospel IS refreshing for the Denver-Metro area! Many churches here are motivational-speakers, prosperity, half-gospel out of context, or hell and brimstone teachings. I appreciate the gospel-centeredness (made up word lol) of this church. Also, the prayer and worship nights are a blessing!

I would really love to see more churches invest in maturing their sheep as disciples to prepare them to go into the world, AND engage with other believers. It starts in the 'home' first.

I've given my information to the info center a few times so that I can get involved and they say someone will reach out and I haven't yet heard back. I also called and left a vm and didn't hear back, then when I called again the person who answered seemed guarded or uncomfortable to interact with me? I'm not sure what it was but the church has the typical Denver-metro stand-offish feeling and a lack of authentic welcoming and friendliness. During testimonial night, some testimonies were so encouraging! But it was concerning as little children talked about suicide (without fair warning to the parents of children who have never talked about that), and the spotlight went to the church more than praises to the Lord himself. Last thought, some of the stats mentioned in sermons I couldn't find in context. I'm a sociologist and geek out on the topics of culture and research so when data is mentioned I love to learn more about it. Though I appreciate the solid teachings as the pastor points us to the Lord (refreshing!), some of the data is taken out of context, which leads to mistrust.

I guess overall I would say that the body represents its leadership and the leadership is responsible for its body. Leadership is a serious role talked about in the Word and there seems to be a lack of wisdom and maturity. I would love to see the church grow, and it's encouraging to hear the gospel in its entirety! And the worship music is biblical ❤️ and I am excited to see volunteers, leadership, and the church body mature in the Lord, the fruits of the Spirit, and wisdom. Blessings!

I can't speak more highly of this church. Although no church is perfect, my experience here has been life changing, especially as part of the Young Adults ministry. Worship here is like no other - intimate in YA, lively in main services,  unashamedly passionate & life-giving in both. This is a church that will challenge you to get out of your comfort zone. I see people encounter Jesus here like they never have before every week without fail. The love for Jesus is radiant and powerful here across generations and ethnicities. I also love the blend between Catholic traditions (specifically how the reading of the Word goes) and Baptist, as my partner and I were both raised Catholic and Baptist respectively and found a happy non-denominational medium here. Ultimately, if you want to take serious steps forward with your faith, this is the church.

reviews.text: The Filipino Church is the first church that genuinely made me feel accepted. I’ve always struggled with my faith and The Filipino Church not only shares the word of God in a way everyone can understand and relate to, but The Filipino Church makes you feel like you’re a part of a family. A family that helps, supports, and worships God together. I also really love how diverse The Filipino Church is. They not only have a live english translator but they make other regions in the Philippines feel seen by offering services in various dialects. Mabuhay ang The Filipino Church!

Our church is a vibrant, Christ-centered community of faith, deeply rooted in Filipino heritage, yet open to all who seek to know Jesus Christ. Whether you’ve been walking with Christ for years or are just beginning to explore your faith, you’ll find a welcoming place here to grow in love, faith, and fellowship. We are a spiritual home where diversity meets unity, and where each person's journey is respected and embraced.

The Filipino Church (TFC) is blessed to be led by a visionary leader, Pastor Arnold Cubos, whose life is a living testimony of God’s mercy and grace. With a deep passion for shepherding God’s people, Pastor Arnold brings not only strong spiritual guidance but also a personal story of transformation that inspires all who meet him. His journey from humble beginnings to becoming a dedicated servant of God reflects the power of God’s redemptive love.

Having experienced God’s grace firsthand, Pastor Arnold is committed to sharing that same grace with others, guiding people toward a personal relationship with Jesus Christ. Under his leadership, TFC has grown into a community that embraces both spiritual depth and practical outreach. Whether through inspiring sermons, personal mentoring, or leading community initiatives, Pastor Arnold’s life is a powerful example of how God can work through one person to impact many.

At the heart of our ministry is a deep commitment to living out the teachings of Jesus through worship, discipleship, and mission. We draw strength from our Filipino identity, celebrating the rich traditions, language, and cultural values that define who we are. Yet, we are more than just a Filipino church. Our doors are open to everyone in the wider Denver community, as we believe that the love of Christ transcends all boundaries.

We are inspired by the words of Psalm 133:1, "Behold, how good and pleasant it is when brothers dwell in unity!" This spirit of unity and family is central to all we do. Every gathering, service, and outreach is designed to reflect God's inclusive love—a love that knows no limits and welcomes everyone with open arms.

True to our slogan, **Si Hesus lang ang Bida** (Only Jesus is the Focus), our church is fully committed to glorifying Christ in all that we do. This guiding principle motivates us to embark on various activities to spread the good news and serve those around us. From community outreach programs and worship services to Bible studies and fellowship events, everything we do is rooted in our mission to make Jesus known and loved.

As we seek to be a beacon of hope in our community, our church offers opportunities for you to get involved, serve others, and grow spiritually. Whether it's through our local mission projects, worship services, or simply breaking bread together, we strive to live out the love of Christ in practical, meaningful ways.

Come and be part of this journey of faith, as we grow together in the love of God and one another. We invite you to experience the joy, peace, and transformation that come from following Christ and living in fellowship with His people.

Which language do you speak? Actually, you know what, that doesn't matter when you're attending Sunday services at The Filipino Church (TFC).

As soon as you see the sound scriptural references on the monitor, as soon as you see the passion of the pastor (Pastor Arnold Cubos) as he preaches (squeezing in some dad jokes in his sermon), and when you feel the warmth and love from members of the congregation every Sunday, how can you not admit that you were meant to be there, in that exact place and in that exact time where God wanted you to be?

Remember when you put your Netflix movie or Amazon TV show on mute, but you could still understand and feel what was happening? That's how it is at The Filipino Church.

I was at first very hesitant to visit this Tagalog-led Sunday service due to my Tagalog being terrible (my French and Kapampangan are even worse)! And I speak straight up Seattle-PNW-US-Army-cussin'-English. I even tried to sneak away (run) immediately after service to avoid talking and mingling with people. #TrueStory

Unfortunately for me, I wasn't fast enough, and I got caught by Pastor Arnold himself in the parking lot right before I got in my truck lol. And since that Sunday (3 weeks ago), I've been blessed and thankful for the opportunity to serve God at The Filipino Church. Plus, I really like how there's always Filipino food every other Sunday after service lol.

In the beginning of this review I alluded to the notion that language barriers fade away, and anxiety is quieted, all so that I could focus on two things: 1) surrendering my life to a God who is and will always be greater than my worries, and 2) giving my all to a Christ who conquered my tomorrows.

Finally, I wish you (my dear reader) a wonderful day and the joy of God's love! All are welcome to find belonging at TFC. Come stop by and say Hi sometime!

However, I am appalled by the unkind review that was expressed toward your security team.  It was unwarranted and a lack of accountability on their end.   As a Christian, they could have reacted better and been a better example toward their children.  The security team handled it appropriately to ensure the safety of the children and took all measures the best they could to protect the venue, which is completely understandable. If you have children, you should never assume it is safe or ok to allow your children to play in water fountains on private grounds without authorization.  You are not only putting them at risk but also the people who own the property.  We all need to be more accountable and be respectful of other people's property, especially when you are a visitor.  For the 5 seconds it would have taken to ask for permission first (which is a good example for children to learn) it would have saved the unnecessary outcome and misunderstanding that occurred.

Again, I just want to thank everyone for a superb job and for everyone that worked hard and long hours to help make this event a success.

At the singles woman group I felt fortified by other women on the same journey as me and we became true friends. I learned what that proverbs scripture meant iron sharpens iron and met true Godly friendships. I got involved with care ministries realizing I hadn't grieved the passing of my grandmother and involved with other Christian resources like CR that really helped me grow and have accountability in my walk. He asks a popularized question like, on a scale of 1-10 how confident are you that you are going to heaven. Then proceeds to say something along the lines of “if you didn’t say 10, you probably aren’t Christian or have never had a relationship with Jesus”. I’ve heard the question before, but have never heard anyone come to such a critical conclusion like that, especially to youths. He will also ask people to come to the front and submit to God, but if you don’t, you aren’t serious about changing your life, or your relationship with Christ and don’t care (he said something exactly like this). I don’t think he understands people worship Christ differently and are at different places in their spiritual journey. Just because some may not be as far along as he’d like, doesn’t make them unserious about Jesus or Christianity. Tried a couple times, probably won’t be coming back here.
