The table on the edge of the carpet I put the table back ,and the drawers popped open. Then the usher accused us of stealing. The New city church that by our hotel didn't judge us or accused us of anything they prayed for our son of whom is on the street. I.m sorry your church doesn't want us there. Please post here what your dress code or what it takes to attend your church. Yes celebrate recovery acceptanced me,and wife we are here now. Are veterans welcome?. Of whom are struggling?. Won't recommend your church to my battle buddy or my other troops I served with.

Pros:
The volunteer staff at the welcome center was wonderful. They informed me how I could get involved and grow at CalvaryPHX. There are community groups, bible studies, community service outreach, etc., that I thought would be important to be a part of. I enjoyed the people I encountered within the church.

Another pro is the idea of expository preaching and Christ-Centered hermeneutics with some topical teaching at times. It is a nice balance.

Cons:
The execution on welcoming new people from the church staff itself was a let down. After meeting with one of the pastors, we discussed the idea of getting involved within the church and volunteering, perhaps by facilitating a class going through a book of the Bible. The pastor asked for a reference within Calvary Chapel to ensure I could teach and had similar theological beliefs, and I gave him one. I had several other references I could have given from my seminary and former Calvary Chapel church as well. The pastor promised to get in touch with my former pastor and did not. My former pastor is well known at Calvary Chapel and credible in his experience and role. He holds a few important positions within Calvary Chapel Global Network.

I signed up for a class for those wanting to learn more about this particular Calvary Chapel, and once again a pastor said he would get in touch with us all to see how we would like to get involved in the church and if we had further questions. That also never took place. I think it is important in any organization to be a person of your word. My experience told me that this church may be unorganized and I did not feel like a priority as someone wanting to get involved. I want to be a part of a church that empowers people who want to grow in their faith and contribute to the church.

Another thing that bothered me was the extent to which the pastors got political unnecessarily in their sermons. In eight Sundays I attended, politics were brought up seven times. Even though some of my political views actually line up with the church, I think it is the wrong approach to focus too much on politics. It is out of balance in that regard.

After eight weeks attending the church, I realized, at least for now, it is not a good fit.

Summary:
No church is perfect. There are some good things about this church. I think it needs to be more organized and the staff needs to fulfill promises. It is imperative to focus more on edifying the church by pointing people to Jesus, since he is our hope.

It was disheartening to experience a culture that seemed cliquish and indifferent, rather than reflecting the unity and compassion we are called to as the body of Christ (Galatians 6:2, 1 Corinthians 12:12-27).

reviews.text: Vineyard Church North Phoenix has been an incredible blessing for my family. When we fall on hard times it can be difficult to ask for help because if fear of judgement... I was so moved by how truly compassionate and understanding everyone a the compassion center was.  They provided groceries for my family twice. Month when things were at their hardest.  I was raised in the episcopal church, but stopped attending regularly when I went to college.  My fiance was raised by a single mother who had religious trauma and so he never knew Jesus.  Last spring Jesus began calling him and he told me he wanted to try going to church. name: Antioch Phoenix

reviews.text: Beautiful church and property. The people were so welcoming.

We lived in the east valley for a few years searching for a church that loves God, takes scripture seriously, and loves all His people. The first Sunday I visited I came with just my daughter. The worship and message were good - but the people. Oh my gosh, the people of Antioch were so loving and kind. We started attending in late 2019 and drove 35 minutes one way to go because it was just that good. We found our friendships and activities were all closer to the church, so we actually moved in 2021 to be closer. Best decision ever!

Wonderful church. Antioch has a deep heart to make sure we are following Jesus and pursuing him wholeheartedly. I grew up in a more conservative church with solid theology and I love how Pastor Travis always makes sure we go back to the Word to build our foundation. Antioch does a fantastic job of building community through life groups to make sure life-on-life discipleship is happening, which is SO necessary for every Christian in their walk with the Lord. We cannot do this life alone, as Paul clearly states over and over again in scriptures. I am glad to be a part of a body of believers that want to know God personally, and make Him known. Leadership is clear and passionate about making sure our congregation builds a deep, healthy relationship with the Lord. I have been here for almost 4 years now and my relationship with God has flourished. I would not be where I am today without God and this community.

A word to those seeking a church- no church will ever be perfect- if you think you found one then please recognize that we all are on a journey with God on the path to righteousness; nobody is perfect, and no body of believers will be either. Aim to get involved with a church that is working towards being more and more like Jesus. A church with open hands, who has made Jesus Lord,  and is ready to be refined by Christ. I see that happening here at Antioch, a place where we can walk this road together and pursue a deep, healthy relationship with the Lord.

I really hate feeling the need to write this review, but I feel that I have an obligation to those who are searching for a new church and have stumbled upon this one. A warning, specifically to incoming/current college students: myself and several others spent many years of their life as a part of this organization, only to become outcasts for questioning some of the theologies of this church. I started going to this church in my first week of my freshman year at ASU, and was awestruck by the community and purpose they could provide me. Unfortunately it was only surface deep, and I was one of many who blindly walked into their culture. I am still recovering and taking time to retrace my views because of this church’s teachings and how they handled myself and many others asking questions. And that’s all it was: we asked questions, and our church leaders and friends refused to listen or answer. They merely asked if we believed their theology, and if we didn’t, we were discarded. Please, take everything you hear with a grain of salt, and match it to the Bible (with real and true context). Ask other leaders of churches with seminary experience about the things you learn here. Read through Matthew 7. If myself and others had done so when we started attending Antioch, we may not have had to endure the difficulties we have had to. Some have had to go to counseling, many of us are having difficulties trusting the church again as we search for a new church home. 1 John 4:1 (ESV): “Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world.”

*I would also like to add that there was a time when leadership asked church members and student leaders to write a five star review on the different review platforms. That is not the case for all reviews, but many of them.

This church presents itself as a beacon of truth and holiness, but the reality is far different. The culture here is deeply toxic, defined more by who they exclude than who they welcome.

From the pulpit, the pastor repeatedly singles out LGBT individuals with hostility, using slurs and cruel language rather than showing any measure of compassion or understanding. Entire sermons are dedicated to vilifying people instead of teaching the gospel. The message is less about Christ’s love and more about drawing lines in the sand to keep people out.

Equally troubling is how the church treats those with disabilities. Rather than accommodating or including them, the leadership often portrays disability as a sign of weakness or even divine punishment. The building itself reflects this mindset there are no ramps, no accessible seating, and no real effort to make the space welcoming. Members who struggle with health challenges report feeling like burdens instead of valued parts of the body of Christ.

The environment is suffocating, fueled by fear and conformity. Families are pressured to raise their children in rigid, exclusionary ways, and questioning the pastor’s authority is met with public shaming. Outsiders are not viewed as people to reach with kindness but as enemies to condemn.

While the church claims to stand firmly on biblical truth, it seems to ignore the most basic commandment of Christ: to love your neighbor as yourself. This is not a safe or healthy spiritual home. It is a place where prejudice is preached as doctrine, and where the most vulnerable are the most unwelcome.

I am deeply disappointed with this church. One of my neighbors reached out to them asking for help with a single month of rent while she got back on her feet. Instead of offering support, they told her, “We don’t do anything like that,” and recommended that she go to shelters with her children. All she needed was temporary assistance, yet they turned her away.

The Bible teaches us that widows, unsupported women, and children were once taken care of at the house of God until they could find stability. Giving tithes to God’s house was meant to provide for those in need. Today, many of us already contribute through taxes that go toward food stamps and medical assistance, yet we are asked to give another 10% to churches—often funding the luxurious lifestyles of pastors—while they ignore the desperate needs right in front of them.

Do you truly believe Jesus would approve of pastors living in excess while refusing help to a struggling single mother? True faith doesn’t require showing off prayers in a church or paying others to read the Bible for you—it’s about compassion and helping those in need.

Thanks to the generosity of kind-hearted people, most of whom were not even believers, my neighbor was able to pay her rent, find a job, and secure a stable home. It’s sad that the church refused to help when she needed it most. I urge anyone attending this church to reflect on the true meaning of faith, compassion, and service

I hadn't reacted to all that had happened. It was not good. But here I was with my walker and my bag with blankets and a pillow. My drink bag with water and soda. And tears that wouldn't stop. I tried my best to explain my situation. What was clear was I was a homeless woman, who is disabled and elderly too. And my emotional state allowed these Godly men to huddle and find a solution. Which was usually a card with a 9 to 5 number where no one answers the phone. But to my surprise. The men were happy to inform me that I would be staying at a house owned by a church member. The house is being renovated. And there is a mother and her son living there right now. And so they took me there and gave me a room and a mattress blanket and pillow. I had some things of my own. I cried and cried with joy. That this church and these men and Jesus Christ has gave me hope for the future. And I could rest my mind about living in the streets for now. I accepted being at the house for now. And began my journey to a beautiful new relationship with Jesus Christ. And with my eyes wide open to the kindness and generosity of the church members of this church. I found my home church. And I'm forever grateful for Jesus and the family I've always wanted. Amen God bless us all. Dios los bendiga a todos in El hombre de Jesucristo mi dios. Mi to-do. Amen

reviews.text: This is a really great community church! People really come together and help one another at this church the way the early church is described in the Bible! They set a good tone for how Christians should behave. 🥰❤️

I love this church!  I have always felt welcomed and comfortable.  The pastor personally greeted us the first day we attended and then actually remembered us when we returned!  The sermons are Bible based, encouraging, and challenging.  My kids love all their sunday school classes and activities like free, top-notch Vacation Bible School.  There are lots of groups for adults as well.  A great family atmosphere and overall fabulous church!

I have been attending North Hills Church for 5... almost 6 years.  I want to share that this church is unlike any other church I have attended for several reasons.  First, the people are real, which means that they have made mistakes and can relate to where you might be; but they have been forgiven and strive to reflect God's Love.  Secondly, our pastors are down to earth, not acting like they have everything perfectly together in their lives, making it easier to relate with them.  Thirdly, this church will become a great support system, if you let them; meaning you have to get involved, active and become vulnerable yourself.  I remember the first time we came, we waited awkwardly, all alone for service to start and the most genuine man came to welcome us... come to find out later that was Pastor Jim.  I have had the pleasure of getting to know Pastor Jim better through taking classes, premarital counseling and going on a mission trip with him.  He cares so much for his church family, he is passionate about our church making a difference in the community and world wide.  Our other pastors are also excellent!  Pastor Lori is on fire for the Lord!  Pastor Jeff is very entertaining but is very serious about teaching the word and helping people find their purpose!  And honestly, I do not know much about the newest pastor, the youth pastor, but from hearing his sermon, he is committed to helping make disciples for Christ.  The office staff incredible and the volunteers alike.  I know that it is hard to figure out what reviews to believe but after reading my churches reviews I was appalled that anyone would post such untrue, unkind things.  If you try our church out and have a problem, it is only fair that you would bring up your concerns, NOT TRASH TALK..... it is an individuals responsibility to resolve a conflict, not gossip about it!!!!

Many of the regular attendees have amazing redemption stories, where they've turned their lives around completely and found grace and forgiveness from their past mistakes.  I find that inspiring... There are many free events for local families, a food program, and a large number of foster kiddos that participate in activities organized for them by church members. formatted_address: 23335 N 18th Dr A114/116, Phoenix, AZ 85027, United States
name: Standing Stones Community Church

reviews.text:
My wife and I have been attending for over several months now. It's a small congregation which we like, but most of the people tend to seek out those who they know and are not very welcoming to strangers. We do not see much if any growth either. The pastor is great, his messages solid, worship is good and he definitely has a heart for those he leads. Communion is spot on, powerful and gives proper reverence to the finished work of Christ.
In a small church everything is amplified, and unfortunately most of the people do not reflect the pastor's heart for others, at least from our observations these past months. John tells us in 1 John that we should be every increasing in our obedience to His Word, and ever increasing in our love for others. By not doing so one misses out on a possible relationship that God had intended. While there are a small few who do, most do not, and the looks of disapproval my wife (who has tattoos) gets from most of the women there makes us both very uncomfortable, and severely taints what would be a great church. Jesus chose the lowliest in stature and appearance to be his disciples and considered not what they looked like, and it boggles my mind and saddens me to see (for example) someone on stage raising their hands during worship but yet can look with such disdain at someone they've never even taken time to say hello to, and willfully pass by and greet others by us. A powerful indictment. Same with of the older ladies on the side that we sit on. This spirit of judging a book by its cover is ever present and the oneness that Jesus speaks of and what that means is lost on many in attendance.  The heart of a church is reflected in the heart of its people.
We are giving it a few more weeks to see how this new worship leader works out.

I went to Standing Stones Community Church yesterday and I was warmly greeted right from the start. The worship music was great and the pastor had a good, sound, biblical message.  If you want to go to a Bible based church that does not shy away from eschatology and is NOT new age, this is it.

formatted_address: 7342 W Indian School Rd, Phoenix, AZ 85033, United States
name: The Door Christian Fellowship Church

reviews.text:
🛑 FALSE DOCTRINE, BLASPHEMY, AND DECEPTION 🛑

If you’re looking for truth, this is NOT the place. This church is run by a pastor teaching lies, twisting scripture, and leading souls into destruction. Here are just a few examples from a single sermon:

❌ LIE #1: “Ask Jesus into your heart” = Salvation
Nowhere in the Bible does it say this. Salvation comes through repentance and keeping GOD’S commandments (ACTS 3:19, 1 JOHN 5:3), not some emotional “repeat-after-me” prayer.

❌ LIE #2: “You’re not under the Law of Moses if you have the Spirit”
He uses GALATIANS 5:18 to preach LAWLESSNESS. But the Holy Spirit causes us to KEEP GOD’S LAWS (EZEKIEL 36:27, ROMANS 7:14). This is anti-Christ doctrine.

❌ BLASPHEMY: “Lie to your wife to keep the marriage happy”
This man openly taught lying is OK in marriage. But GOD says “Lie not one to another” (COLOSSIANS 3:9). He justifies sin with jokes.

❌ FALSE PROPHECY: Preaching the “rapture” & 7-year tribulation
This doctrine is not in the Bible. CHRIST returns after tribulation (MATTHEW 24:29–31), not before. This rapture teaching is a distraction from real end-time prophecy.

❌ MANIPULATIVE GIVING: “If you keep your money, go to hell.”
GOD doesn’t need your money (PSALM 50:10), but they scare people into giving by threatening hellfire. That’s not love—that’s manipulation.

❌ WORLDLY JOKING: “Let’s party for Jesus.”
No reverence, no order. Just jokes, emotional music, and mocking the scriptures with “party for Jesus” language. That’s not holiness—it’s confusion.

❌ CONTRADICTION: Telling people to “let the Spirit change them over time,” while also saying people go to hell for sin.

My husband, Steve, and I went here today for the 9am service, and it was AMAZING! The people were wonderful and VERY welcoming! Everyone who saw us was introducing themselves and welcoming us and acting like we had been coming for weeks. It made us feel very comfortable and like we belonged. We didn't feel out of place or like outsiders in the least.

I liked that there was no cafe. They offered coffee and cold water for everyone (depending on what you wanted/needed) and offered donuts as well (nice if you hadn't had breakfast before coming). They had a stand that had books, hats, and t-shirts on it. However, the books were free (which was a nice way to spread the word of Our Lord), and they weren't "selling" the t-shirts and hats in a traditional way. What I mean is that there wasn't a vendor there asking for money for the items. All they asked is that you put $5 in their giving box per item you took. (No thoughts of the merchants in the temple and Jesus overturning the tables come to mind here.) It was a nice change because it made you feel like they wanted those payments to go back to helping the church and wanted the church to know it. It was an awesome thing to see!

Just overall a wonderful place and I can't say enough good things about this church and its people! The pastor was amazing and when I spoke to him about my autistic son and youth group, he took my concerns into consideration and made time to speak with me about it. It was awesome. He didn't brush me aside like it was a problem. We will DEFINITELY be going back next week.... I do believe we have finally found our Home Church!

Oh! And the pastor actually reads out of the Bible and it's not like a motivational speech.... he talks about uncomfortable things. But you can tell it comes from a place of Love which makes you think about how it applies to your life and makes you want to do better. Not just for yourself but because that's what God commands of you. It makes you want to be obedient. It was amazing today! Complete turnaround from our trial run at another church last weekend...

formatted_address: 5811 N 20th St, Phoenix, AZ 85016, United States
name: Christ Church Anglican

reviews.text: Beautiful experience. Friendly congregation and beautiful liturgy with a sermon that touched me deeply.

This church is a perfect mix of contemporary worship and Indian elements. The message is in English which is great for my kids.  Pastor Suresh is a natural teacher and has a gift for applying the lessons of the Bible to current day life.  The church is centrally located, close to the I-17 and the I-51 and easy to get to.

A wonderful gem I found in the Valley.  Looking for a more orthodox church, a number of friends recommended Christ Church Anglican.  We found a warm, friendly group of believers who praise and love the Lord reverently.  Fr. Chris Schutte and Fr. Chuck Collins are outstanding teachers of God's Word.

Needless to say, Christ Church Anglican has become my home church.
Welcoming church with clear to follow liturgy.  Robed choir.   Message was thoughtfully presented and rooted in the biblical text.   Made welcome at the adult learning after the service in the hall.
Spirit-filled church. Great prayer & healing team, everyone welcome for prayer.

formatted_address: 7569 W Greenway Rd, Peoria, AZ 85381, United States
name: Pure Heart Church - Peoria

reviews.text:
A friend invited me here and I didn't know what to expect. The worship music was incredible—it had so much energy and it felt very alive mixing contemporary together with black Gospel-style. The guy preaching was named Pat. He has definitely found his calling because he is very good at speaking truth through Scripture so everyone stays awake. He's a funny dude who can skillfully float easily between a serious topic while still causing me to grin ear to ear.
😁😉

It's obvious he has a genuine love for God that shines through no matter what he was preaching on. Pat's message on was on the blessings that God has promised to those who are obedient—and I was really happy that he was quoting Scripture many times, and he was careful to note that the blessings God promises us might not be realized in this life.
👊🤘

When you visit, be ready to say a lot of Amens and gives tons of praise to God—be ready to interact and say hello and raise your arms while singing loud enough for the heavens to hear.
⛪🙏
Amazing church. Amazing people and only good experiences. I have found a church finally that is filled with the holy spirit next to my home

My oldest daughter started going there and I could see God doing a work in her. Then two of my grandkids started going there in God started working on them as well. The growth was amazing. I used to be on staff in Ministry at a church in South Phoenix that ended badly. I had had my fill of churches. I became disabled which made things even more difficult to find a church home. The things God showed me during my search scared me and sick of me at the same time. So I decided to fight from home. I started a Ministry now 3 1/2 years which is really amazing but I began going to Pure Heart Peoria because of the growth I seen in my kids and I felt I needed a spiritual covering for my Ministry. Most of all it's the only day that I get to see my great-granddaughter who was the year and a half old. Pastor Patrick is a tremendous sensitive and transparent man of God which is truly something to appreciate in our church of today. I could not recommend the church higher. The worship is good not exactly my flavor considering it came from more of a black gospel background. But the praise and worship is good and people enter into the presence of the Lord. What makes it more difficult for me as I simply just don't know the songs but I have hours a day of worship so I get plenty of what I need.

Holy Spirit led!  Fresh Manna every Sunday.  Praise  and worship over the top.  Freedom in worship!  Humor, love and sincerity.  This Pastor Pat loves his sheep. Straight gospel preacher.  No ear tickling here, just straight shooting gospel.  HOW REFERESHING.

This church changed everything for me! I’ve been going to the Glendale location since 2021, and the Lord has been putting it on my heart to get more out of my Sundays. I love the Glendale location but Pure Heart Peoria is unapologetically bold with Gods Word & is definitely lead by the Holy Spirit!

They also have weekly refuel prayer on Wednesdays, which is where I went first and immediately I knew this would be where I spend my Sunday mornings! The worship was amazing, I loved how long it went for and I enjoyed being able to greet those around me it felt very community oriented!! The service has no time frame which I also love.

I enjoyed service so much I went home and watched the online recording on their YouTube page! I had the Holy Ghost goosies during the entire service and even when I watch online, that goes to show how powerful the message truly was! This church was far from lukewarm and I am excited to spend my Wednesdays and Sundays here from now on.

formatted_address: 750 E Southern Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85040, United States
name: Wesley United Methodist Church

reviews.text: My family was a founding member of this church back in the sixties and had attended services for decades and today I feel nothing but sorrow for the lack of caring and the absence of love for our fellow man so to speak. Wesley feels cold and lifeless and merely a pile of brick and mortar, once Gods house, no longer a place where the presence of Jesus is felt… it saddens me greatly offering these words but more needs to be said and done to restore the Word Of Christ and to begin to build upon the Rock Christ expects from those who are entrusted to deliver God’s Grace

Wesley UMC has been my primary church home for most of the past 30 years. My faith has been strengthened through the sound teachings of the Word of God and I continue to learn under the leadership of Pastor T. I invite anyone searching to have a rewarding spiritual journey full of miracles and wonders to visit and perhaps stay for a while. This strong faith community is a bright light in a world trying to make darkness real.

I love this church!  Every time that I have visited, I have felt welcomed. Pastor T’s messages are always entertaining and thought provoking. She has truly been blessed with the gift to deliver God’s word. If you are looking for a place to worship, you should consider a visit to Wesley.
Intimate church that appears to be growing.  Service is at 10AM and their fellowship is at 11AM and typically includes food and/or snacks.  Always friendly conversation...
Pastor Towanda Connelly and the congregation at Wesley UMC are welcoming and engaging. The Palm Sunday message served as the reminder to shout your praise for all to hear.

The best beautiful place ever. Blessing tone be there.

reviews.text: The congregation is very inviting.  The choir is small BUT YOU WOULDNT KNOW IT IF YOU  WERE JUST LISTENING.  THEY ARE HIGHLY UPLIFTING AND THE PASTOR IS AWESOME.  DELIVERS EVERY TIME🙌

This has been my church for over 13 years.  I love the bright atmosphere and the friendliness of the people. Although much scaled down since Covid, I enjoy the music ministry --  it's a crucial part of my worship.   I like some of the newer gospel music, but  would prefer more Traditional  Gospel as it is what stirs my soul the most.  I truly miss our old minister,  Pastor Ralph Williamson, whose preaching style really uplifted me, but I have come to love and look forward to hearing Senior Pastor Karen  Anderson too.  She really preaches the Word!  How she and Pastor Michelle Brown are preparing and teaching our youth is just awesome. These children will be well prepared to take their place in running and keeping our church alive - they are our future. You cannot go wrong visiting this church and/or becoming part of this church family.  You'll be glad you did.
The member were friendly and the spitir is here at this church!  The message that was preached was PREACHED!!!

Beautiful Church! Very friendly people and active church.  The services are lively and meaningful.  The pastor is fantastic.  This church practices what it preaches.  Community Service is high on the priority list.  AME has Educational Programs for youth, food bank, outreach to the homeless, youth and senior ministries, wonderful choirs, etc.

Came here in 2022. Service was 1 hour.

Spent 15 minutes talking about tithes

Another 15 minutes talking about voting for politicians.

Preacher brought up Kendrick Lamar lyrics but didn’t even open the Bible for a minute

Also you have to wear a face mask all service long but some members walk around without a mask. What’s the point if everybody doesn’t have one? Best thing to do is let it be optional. If you fear air borne illness then wear a mask but don’t force it upon those who don’t fear air borne illness.

God bless.

formatted_address: 2955 E Russell Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89120, United States
name: Fountain of Hope African Methodist Episcopal Church

reviews.text:
Love my new church family.
Friendly, caring  and about doing Gods work. The worship service is awesome.  Come and visit real soon🙏🏽

Awesome Worship Experience. We visit every year during our Christmas Vacation in Vegas. We are family and friends with Pastor Gregory and 1st Lady Savalla. They have a beautiful family and loving Congregation.

My grandmother and two stepfathers, may they rest in peace, were active in this church when it was just a house. They did a lot for this church. Still, Pastor MacLeod refused to officiate a zoom memorial and backed out after agreeing to officiate it because his deacon misunderstood a man who is not even a member of the congregation, living about a thousand miles away. It doesn't matter all the things my grandmother did for this church. It doesn't even matter that almost a year went by without having anything for a matriarch who died. Because of one man's misunderstanding, a pastor goes back on his word. My grandmother is creating a rumble in her urn at such appalling cowardice and dishonor. Shame on him!

GOD will make all things new. We have a new Pastor and First Family that are on fire for the Lord. Pastor Gregory McLeod and First Lady Savalla McLeod are providing are wonderful examples of a family who loves the Lord and the flock. This is a good fit for our church and new and wonderful changes are taking place. The atmosphere is full of high praise and worship render unto the Most High God. Membership is increasing and the love toward each other is renewed. Our motto: We are the friendliest church in the Valley, but I dare say we are the Friendliest Church in Nevada. Come worship with us and experience for yourself.
Awesome and friendly congregation. I love hearing the word of God, the church is close to home, and I like attending when I'm not working on Sundays

formatted_address: 500 Madison Ave, Las Vegas, NV 89106, United States
name: Second Baptist Church

reviews.text: I became a member of Second Baptist Church and was baptised in 2017. I love worshiping and praising God every Sunday and have been going here ever since.

We are new to Las Vegas and reached out to this church to possibly become members. However, I called to simply ask if there was a Men's Ministry and Women's Ministry and was told by administration "I can have someone reach out to you." She didn't seem to know if they had these ministries. This was a simple yes or no question she couldn't answer. I want to give them the benefit of the doubt that she may be is new and just didn't know but I would think knowing what ministries are available at your church is pretty important. I did go to the website to see if I could find them but for some reason I couldn't get the link to open. The person who answered the phone wasn't very warm or friendly so I hope she isn't an example of what to expect if we decide to visit. I won't count them out on our search for a church but I will say I'm reluctant to even visit but I believe in second chances. Hopefully others that call will have a better experience.
MY CHURCH HOME. MY RECENT VISIT WAS ON THE 79 YEARS ANNIVERSARY! THIS WAS AN AWESOME DAY WITH THE FAMILY OF GOD!

They used to host a monthly hot breakfast the last Sunday of each month, years ago. But I'm sure staff are just keeping any & all donations for themselves. Snack bags most times have a sandwich. The BBQ 🌭 & 🍔 are great! Clothing are awesome. Always closed during Thanksgiving & Christmas holidays. Rather odd. Could be a lot more polite. *Man told everyone to wear a mask. God says "Trust in the Lord!" Ditch the masks!!!

I love the fact that I can visit my church on line, and to know that my health is no longer an issue for not going to church. I grew up in second baptist church in las vegas. going on line was a great idea, because  i don't have a car,  and i can't walk to far. and yes, I Give the glory and honor to God our lord. thanks second baptist for making this possible. and  the lord who is the head of my life. So I will say thank God for technology and thank you second
baptist 🙌🏾

Service was good. Felt welcome 🙏🏽

This place is a beautiful representation of what “go and make disciples” means. Bishop McDonnell, to me is one of the most solid oracles of The Gospel this state has seen. I personally appreciate everything he does for Las Vegas.
Is one of the most amazing churches in Las Vegas, Nevada under the leadership of Overseer Bill McDonnell and First Lady Alma Faye McDonnell.
We love our Wealthy Place Ministries COGIC LV family! We miss having servuce but our Facebook Live onlive services are FIRE!!! JESUS HAS NOT BEEN CANCELED!!!

reviews.text: What an experience! There was so much excitement and joy at this service. My son and I always visit black churches wherever we go. It was such a heart-felt moment to find the same dedication of worshiping God at this church. The music was good, the ushers were attentive, and the music was on point. My favorite, was the availability of interpreters. This set this church apart from most churches we visit, and the fact they had more than one was amazing. I hope Bible Study is as good.

My name is Patricia Barrett. I’ve been with this church 15 years and I wouldn’t change it for nothing in the world. I love my pastor. I love everyone that’s in my church. I really appreciate you all you all are my church family, and I am a child of God Sean Taylor. I love you his wife. She’s a beautiful lady and I am a greater at the 11 o’clock service, God bless.

I visited for the first time today. 1.  The one who did the welcome at 11:00 am walked past me and was very rude and unfriendly 2. Who in their right mind stands on a praise team with a see-thru nightgown on? 3. Your praise team leader Jack smelled of alcohol when I passed him today. The members are very unfriendly and unkind. Get it together Victory.

Victory Baptist has gospel singing that is known to be “Tops” and the Senior Minister is thoughtful and tackles life lessons using the Bible.  The members will greet you & are kind.  What a great Church! Come & Enjoy!
I am a member. The members are very kind and friendly. Pastor Sean Taylor is  a great minister and his wife is a wonderful first Lady. His sermons are very enlightening and uplifting .

name: True Love Missionary Baptist Church

reviews.text: We visited recently and the mics were so loud and they kept screaming in the mic I got a migraine and we left. It don’t take all that. We can hear you without screaming.

Great church and members. When I first visited I was greeted with handshakes and smiles. I love singing so as the choir sang I joined in. One of the Mother’s asked me if I was a choir member. I politely answered no and her response was well you better join. Said I sang good (I never thought so). The activities they do with the children and how they quickly attach to the teen children. I’m a single mom with 3 boys. Them deacons and ushers reached out to me so quickly. I was amazed and so were they. I’m so happy and blessed to call this church and members my new  family.

My God Sister and I attended church today I’ve been there before as a visiting Sister church the Director Stephanie is so awesome just so full of love and joy and grace Mostly filled with the joy and ministry of music 10 toes up definitely a woman of God I love to see her direct the choir today was my first time visiting as just a visitor oh my God Sister and I  loved the message and the way it was delivered as soon as we got in the car we both felt the same thing True love Missionary Baptist Church you definitely  I must say you most definitely feel  Holy Spirit the abundance of family but most importantly the love  so thank you Our Heavenly  Father God for your direction we will definitely be back next Sunday can’t wait may God bless and keep each and everyone of you 😇😇😇😇😇😇😇😇
Today, Easter Sunday we visited. Beautiful service. We will be back.
Loves God's People, God's Word while praising and worshipping him.

formatted_address: 850 E Cactus Ave, Las Vegas, NV 89183, United States
name: Hope Church Las Vegas

reviews.text: My family and I just started attending Hope and we are enjoying it. The messages are great and music is ok but not what we are used to coming from CC, it’s just a different type of worship music. Anyway, I notice two things that were distracting in the sanctuary. One, they seat people during prayer, interrupting people while they have their heads bowed is uncomfortable. I understand that people arrive late and that’s fine but they should be held back in the doorway until prayer is finished. Two, babies should not be allowed in the sanctuary. There are two alternatives for families, day care and family rooms. Last Sunday we were there with a new believer.  He really needed to hear from God and the crying babies all around us was very distracting. I noticed he and others were looking around every time a baby would cry. It was distracting. Other than that, we love it.

This is absolutely the BEST church in all of Las Vegas by far . Pastor Vance is always very good at delivering great sermons on Sundays . I was a part of the choir and loved how awesome Teddy sang and ho cool the music was . Thanks for the awesome memories . If I ever get to Laa Vegas again Rick and I will come to a Sunday service . Have a blessed day 😇

I'm not a fan of the OVER THE TOP "worship" service (or concert 🤷)
But, truly their teaching/preaching team are ON POINT! Their messages always hit home.
First impressions volunteers are super friendly, caring, and helpful.

BEST CHURCH IN LAS VEGAS!!!!!

I’ve been attending this church over a year now.
Not once have I ever heard any of the pastors contradict The Word of God.

If you’ve had bad experiences with what you call “organized religion”,
THIS IS THE CHURCH FOR YOU!!!!

This isn’t organized religion. This church promotes a real relationship with the living Jesus Christ Lord of Heaven and Earth and that relationship is between you and Him.

This church is fully transparent with their finances
They expand the Kingdom by opening churchs and funding missionaries to spread The Word in all parts of the World. (That’s where your tithes and offerings go.)

Can say so much more good about this church, but go experience it for yourself and be blessed!!!!! 🙏🏼
I am a member of this church.  It is my home and every week I attend brings me pure joy.  God is truly in this place.

formatted_address: 6200 W Lone Mountain Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89130, United States
name: Canyon Ridge Christian Church

reviews.text: This has been my church for about 20 years now I’ve seen pastors come and go, but our pastor Drew, who is the current pastor, has such a unique way of touching all of us. I encourage you to go. They have a Womens Bible Study. They have a men’s Bible study they have daycare for children, while you’re attending service. They have a hiking group and many others. This is the best church in Las Vegas aside from Central Christian Church its Sister Property. I do encourage you to come and check it out yourself. God Bless

I visited from out of town with my family today. The kids program was very disappointing. It’s in an old building with several tiny rooms. The doors were all open, but there were no cameras. There were 2 teenage boys that were volunteering in each of my children’s classrooms. At our home church there are men and women volunteering in the kids classes and teenagers including boys, but this was different. I got a bad feeling about leaving my children there. I am not comfortable leaving my kids with people that are acting weird/rude/standoffish. It didn’t feel like the type of people who should be taking care of kids. 2 boys and 1 girl specifically stood out to me as people I wouldn’t never trust alone with my kids. Everyone else I spoke to seemed nice. The man and woman on staff who escorted us to the family room seemed confused as to why we weren’t leaving our kids there. It’s just embarrassing that a church would allow just anyone to volunteer. Especially with the children. We ended up going to the family room and then just leaving shortly after. It’s unfortunate such a large church gives so little attention to the safety of the children.

I went to this church over 25 years ago when I was living in Las Vegas. I had my daughter Emily Thompson baptized there too . The congregation was always super nice and helpful. They really knew how to worship Jesus too . Thanks again for the awesome memories there . I have a complete new life that is better than I ever thought possible thanks to my belief in GOD. I live in Flagstaff now so if Rick and I ever come to Las Vegas we will visit your amazing church . Have a blessed day 😇

Excellent worship center with volunteers eager to assist us with our wheelchair access requirements.  A young man provided us with a movable chair that I could use to sit next to my wife.  Plenty of parking, handicap parking, a small area to get coffee, clean restrooms, and an amazing area to worship Christ.  The lesson/sermon and the references are displayed onto the big screens.  On the back of every few chairs is a bar code that I believe will take you straight to the notes of the service.  We enjoyed their praise and worship team and the pastor's message and will be attending service here again

I’ve been about 5 times and probably about half of the times the whole sermon was about donating.  I get that donations are part of an organization and everything needs $$ to thrive and grow and provide services but it was exhausting.  I’d rather a place spend 5 minutes max at beginning of every sermon than spend an entire hr and half once a month pounding it into our brains.  If people are going to donate they’re going to donate regardless.  The pastor goes on and on like pounding it into our brains for an hr and half and even my teenager was like omg he just keeps saying the same things.  And he says “I’m just gonna take one minute” and then proceeds to spend 20 minutes repeating himself repeating himself the same thing, about giving money, we get it.  To make donating an entire sermon is in bad taste in my opinion.  And people were just trickling trickling up and out of their seats.  I’ve been to other churches where someone will speak about tithe or financial generosity for a 5-10 minute talk but never an entire sermon.  It left a bad taste in my mouth each time and I think the organization needs to re think how they can better get that message across especially right now in the world.

reviews.text: American Missionary Church has been a blessing to me. I was looking for a church to call home. I did!! The first day I stepped foot in this church. I already felt the blessing of God. The welcome I got from congregation was so welcoming. The ministry the fellowship was a blessing. Reverend Francis prayed with me and the Testimony I loved to  share is God is really and is amazing grace that saved my soul. Come and join us Sunday morning service. You don’t want to miss the wonderful word of God. God bless you

Great worship,exciting praise.
Dancing stars are a great experience  on their own.
Choir is something else!!!
The sermons from the pastor are edifying, directing, Guiding, and uplifting!!!
Great Great experience.  Presence of God is TANGIBLE!!! You are welcome...to taste what the Lord has for you!
I truly enjoy the prayertime, praise and worship and most of all the preaching of the word of God. I will definitely advise you to come experience it for yourself.
Great place of worship..unfortunately due to the pandemic, the church staff wasn't able to pick the people up at catholic charities no more for the time being..but God is still good..
Nice people, nice music. Will always worship there.

formatted_address: 6425 W Pebble Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89139, United States
name: Southern Hills Church

reviews.text: Pastor Josh, Pastor Caleb are so personable and wonderful to talk to. The members really make you feel at home. I have gone to many different churches, the Deacons were coming up to me and introducing themselves and shaking my hand which is a first in my book.

Love this church. Have been attending since moving to Vegas. Great pastors all around. Pastor Josh's sermons are so rememberable even years after. He really is passionate about helping everyone to get into Heaven.

Southern Hills Church is a truly God centered church. Pastor Josh and his wife are genuine, caring, and honest people. Our Pastor teaches the truth of the Bible and nothing less.
I absolutely appreciate the children’s ministry for pouring truth and love into the kids and making the path of salvation clear.
I am honored to be a part of Southern Hills, and if anyone is searching please come visit.

We discovered this church by accident in 2019 two months after moving to Las Vegas from California. After speaking to the pastor's wife, we decided to attend the following Sunday.  Immediately we felt comfortable and had no desire to go anywhere else.  Pastor Josh Teis is like no other pastor.  He teaches strictly from the Bible but also adds humor along with his real-life experiences that ties into the sermon of the day.  If you are looking for a church with a Bible-teaching pastor who has a passion for Jesus and winning souls, this is the church.

I have loved getting connected to the church being a college grad now for a whole year. It’s been a great place to meet new friends, enjoy amazing worship music and get filled spiritually. Everyone has been welcoming and I can sense the Spirit of the Lord moving in the church and through His people. I love taking notes with Pastor Josh too! I’ve got a notebook filled with thoughts I go back to and share with friends in discipleship.

formatted_address: 2845 S Lindell Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89146, United States
name: Mountaintop Faith Ministries

reviews.text: Good church service.  Usually in and out in about an hour with a dynamic brief, concise, message to lift you.  Music is okay, but spirit and energy is wonderful.

I came here to visit on Sunday during a vacation. The operations of the service were very efficient and the congregation very welcoming for new guests. The Holy Spirit anointing was strong in the room and was there to heal, save, set free and deliver. Thank you ps. House and First Lady for the word, and Elder Williams for the prayer.

This is a wonderful church with friendly people. The people arrive ready to worship the Lord! It's an amazing church! I really enjoyed visiting.
If you are in Vegas and searching for a church, you should visit Mountaintop. The people will make you feel like family. You will experience God's presence from the moment you step inside.
Don't miss the opportunity to experience what faith on the mountaintop is all about.
It has been over 13 years since I was last in Vegas but I will never forget my visits to Mountaintop. I won't forget when God showed up in the parking lot and healed a woman after a simple prayer.
I encourage everyone to give Mountaintop Faith Ministries a try.
God bless you as we all wait for Jesus.
It's some church up in here! I will be back hallelujah. Whether you go all the time or have not been in a month of Sundays, this is the place to be.

Great worship. The pastor and his wife minister Gods word without sugar coating and I love it. Come on out. You will enjoy and not regret it. Also they start service on time and not a minute late. Lol 😂

formatted_address: 7175 W Oquendo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89113, United States
name: Awaken Church Las Vegas

reviews.text: We love this Church we started going every Sunday when we discovered this but, Been sad of what happened earlier. this Church is too sensitive of small noise from children. Earlier we were ask to go to the other room even thou my kids and some of other kids are not making any noise because prayer is about to start. What’s the purpose of bringing your family to church if very small kids noise are not allowed in the worship center. We walked out. They should have put a sign no children allowed. 😔
I am not historically a very religious person.  I started going here after my daughter started to attend.  I go every week now.  I really like the energy and I always leave feeling good.

My wife and I attended service while on vacation. This place is GREAT! Solid worship and preaching. The congregation is on 🔥 Totally engaged in the worship and message. The first message I can remember with action steps! Love you guys 😀

We love Awaken church and Pastor Derek. Unfortunately, we had to stop going because of an issue in our 3 year olds Sunday school class. There is always a teenage boy there helping out, which my husband and I find to be completely inappropriate for a toddler program. We were not comfortable with it at all, but the final straw was when my husband heard him ask one of the children if they needed to use the restroom. We are unsure if he is taking children to use the restroom by himself or what. A teenage boy in a toddler program is completely inappropriate. He is probably a nice boy and probably won’t do anything to the kids, but we can’t go by probably, we need to be smart. If you choose to go to this church and you have a toddler, be very cautious about the Sunday school program. Bad judgement on Awakens part.
I was an out of town visitor and was welcomed with open arms. It was a warm and friendly atmosphere, worshipping our Lord and Savior. The teaching was good, as well.

formatted_address: 55 E Reno Ave, Las Vegas, NV 89119, United States
name: Roman Catholic Shrine of the Most Holy Redeemer

reviews.text:
We attended the mass during the basketball tournament. The church is big and very artistic. It is the first church where I saw Jesus on the cross with different hand positions. Whenever I’m in Las Vegas for the weekend, I make it a point to visit the Roman Catholic Shrine of the Most Holy Redeemer Church and attend Sunday Mass. This church is beautiful and is calming for my soul.

The Shrine of the Most Holy Redeemer Church is located near the strip and surrounded by views of Mandalay Bay, Luxor, and MGM Grand. It is also near the Harry Reid International Airport (LAS).

There are plenty of parking spaces so that is never an issue. In the summer though, they lack shade. The entrance to the church is easy to spot, as you’ll see a large statue of the Most Holy Redeemer at the front of the church.

Upon entering the building, there is a foyer before entering the doors to the main church. Within the foyer, there are restrooms to the right, and a gift shop and office to the left.

Stepping into the main church, the layout is an open semi-circle. Any place you sit has a great vantage point of the altar and the large wooden crucifix.

The priest had a wonderful homily and the musicians (a cantor and pianist) did a beautiful job accompanying the Mass. As a fellow musician, I enjoy listening to how other music ministers enhance the liturgies.

The walls around the church are adorned with artwork from depictions from the Annunciation, Nativity, Last Supper and Washing of the Feet, Crucifixion, as well as frames of Our Lady of Guadalupe and Divine Mercy, and statues of Saints. They do have on/off switches to light candles and a donation slot for lighting a candle.

After Mass, I spent some time in the gift shop and made a purchase for several items to bring back as gifts.

Overall, it was lovely to sit in the church and peacefully say my prayers and attend Mass. They ministers were also very welcoming. Thank you!

The priest projects his voice pretty well, although sometimes he can be hard to understand because he speaks very rapidly. The pianist/organist is very skilled at both instruments and can sing too, which I admire as a church musician myself.

reviews.text: What i just witnessed today at the 5pm Mass was absolutely appalling. There was a person there who was told by the Security Guard "No Shoes, No shirt, No service." The person was sitting quietly in the last pew, minding thier business,  waiting for Mass to begin when they were told to leave. Jesus would not turn away anyone for what they are wearing. When I asked the parishioners if anyone had a spare pair of shoes so that they could stay, they all stared at me like deer in the headlights. Nobody spoke up for this person. They allowed the church to remove the person and also remove my family from Mass for speaking up. What an abomination to the Catholic Church. Jesus preached to the lowly. Jesus said follow me to anyone who was listening regardless of what they were wearing. This church... and yes church with a lowercase c... is not the place to spend time as they have forgotten the mission of Christ. The Diocese of Las Vegas will be notified of this behavior.

Horrible! I had to pay $15 to park! What a waste of $15! I was told that parking would be validated for Simbang Gabi but I had to pay. NO. I absolutely do not recommend this church. Don’t waste your time and money going here. Please continue going to church, but be warned save extra dollars in donation to save for parking, if you’re driving here.

This is essentially the only church in Las Vegas that looks like a church. Every other one (regardless of the denomination) is a nightmare of ugly modernism.

The only qualms I have is that they blast the bright lights even at the night time services and it hurts my eyes. And the echo makes it hard to understand the homily. Both can be easily fixed, but I suspect that many fear to bring up suggestions like this because they don’t want to appear picky or ungrateful or something.

THIS CHURCH IS ABSOLUTELY APPALLING!
We were visiting from out of state and decided to attend Saturday evening Mass here. Before Mass even began, we witnessed something that broke our hearts. A homeless woman was sitting quietly in the back pew—peaceful, respectful, simply waiting for Mass to start.
A security guard approached her and, in a rude and dismissive tone, told her she had to leave because she wasn’t wearing shoes. His exact words were, “No shoes, no shirt, no service.” Other than her bare feet, she was appropriately dressed and causing no disruption at all.
At that moment, we knew we wanted nothing to do with this church. Have we all forgotten that it’s not our place to judge—that only God can do that? Have we forgotten that Jesus Himself likely walked barefoot and welcomed everyone, especially those most in need of compassion?
This woman already faces unimaginable challenges. To be cast out of the very place that should offer love and refuge was disgraceful. It happened right in front of my children, and I told them, “This is exactly what Joan of Arc would have done—stood up for what’s right.” And that’s what we did.
I can only pray that the woman was an angel, or perhaps Jesus Himself in disguise—testing the hearts of those present. Sadly, most failed that test.
May the day karma comes knocking be a reminder of what faith is truly meant to look like. My family and I will be waving with a smile when it does.

I told them I wanted to go home, because I did not feel safe staying another night with her there. I eventually was able to call my parents and they picked me up ASAP, and before we left, the pastors wife, an asian lady, told me that “maybe if you weren’t so shy and actually tried to talk to people, that wouldn’t have happened to you.” It took a toll on my mental health for over a year and nearly ruined my relationship with God. Very welcoming. Two services on Sunday. This is not a typical atmosphere but there is a lot of music, singing, a band and usually guest speakers weekly. They do an offering but it is not high pressure. They have weekly activities with a few bigger activities that are seasonal outreaches.

See a video on our YouTube channel Coolest Life.

ChurchLV has been such a blessing in not just my heart and life but in my families as well. We moved to Las Vegas a few years ago and have been praying for a local church near us that we can pour into and “rattle these dry bones” sort of speak. We attended a few other churches and they were great but ChurchLV felt like HOME the second we walked through the doors… I mean we felt an amazing presence of community and the Holy Spirit. There’s truly nothing like it. My kids ask to go to church throughout the week and look forward to service. Everyone from the pastors to each serve member are truly special and I cannot praise them enough. I have cried my eyes out during multiple sermons due to being overwhelmed by the Holy Spirit and truly it’s been life changing. I joined Pastor Bennys kingdom first for my birthday gift to myself and my husband and I have been blessed in so many ways from our marriage,  finances, community and to a change of mindset to grow in our walk of faith. We know this is a journey and not a sprint and we are in it for the long haul. I cannot WAIT to pour into our amazing local church for more years to come and I’m so blessed we get to raise our children to do the same. Thank you to the entire ChurchLV fam you guys are amazing! May God continue to answer our God sized prayers of reaching more people in this world to know and love Jesus!

reviews.text:
I’ve been attending this church for about three months now, and it has truly been life-changing. A friend from work invited me to a Friends Night service on a Saturday at 5 PM, and from that moment, I knew I had found something special. I’d been searching for a church home for a long time. I’m originally from California, where I attended La Patria Church in Rancho, and I loved it. After moving to Vegas three years ago, this is the first church I’ve consistently attended—and I am so grateful I did.

This church brings so much peace, clarity, and love. The worship team is incredible—I’ve even added their songs to my Spotify because they bless me so much! Pastor Jabin is an amazing pastor who speaks with genuine love, care, and purpose. Through his messages, I’ve been able to understand and learn more about God and Jesus in a deeper way.

I also want to thank the church for supporting families in need during the holidays and for taking such good care of your community. And Amen to NOT serving coffee—because we need both hands lifted high in worship!

Parking and seating have never been an issue, and everyone is always so kind and helpful.

I’m truly blessed to have found this beautiful church.

A Powerful House of Worship — Grateful for the Invite! 💌

I was invited to City Light Church by a good friend, and from the moment I walked in, I immediately felt the presence of God 😭 The worship music is powerful and anointed—every song lifts your spirit and ushers in the Holy Spirit in such a beautiful way. The sermons are filled with truth, wisdom, and real-life application that deeply speaks to your soul 💗

One of the highlights for me has been the amazing prayer team! 🔥 They are Spirit-led, compassionate, and truly stand in agreement with you in faith. I left feeling encouraged, refreshed, and more connected to the Lord than ever before.

If you're looking for a church that is alive, grounded in the Word, and overflowing with love and purpose—City Light is it! 🙌

“For where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them.” — Matthew 18:20 📖

I am a missionary serving in Prague, Czech Republic, focusing on discipleship and deliverance ministry. Recently, I met a young couple here from your church. They shared a powerful testimony about the impact your congregation has had on their lives. Their deep love for biblical truth and their walk of faith clearly reflect the fruit of your pastor’s teaching and shepherding as he faithfully shares the full gospel.

While visiting family in Las Vegas, I was excited to attend City Light—and I was not disappointed. Your church truly shines the light of Jesus Christ in this city. feel really sad to have to share this review on a blessed sunday.
im a UK doctor, and My first time attending church after 3 years of being estranged to religion, was a month ago while visiting my family here, my parents introduced me to the life church (they are locals here, and i’m moving in two months myself).
my First visit was family day, everyone was amazing and so welcoming.  So i have visited 4x during my visit here. really felt a pull back to God so thank you to everyone.

however today, while we were praising God during worship i felt him tell me to join the church worship team.. my mother has been asking me to join a church choir/ band maybe all of my life and he never wanted to. but today i felt that pull.

after the service i spoke to the lead guitarist (sorry i have forgotten his name), who i have actually had a friendly conversation with a few weeks ago when i attended with my father.
i explained that my mother is sick and has been in the hospital for two weeks due to a collapse, and suffered a spinal fracture, so i will be here indefinitely, delaying my permanent move.
i felt him to be very condescending throughout our conversation when i asked to join even as backup without a microphone (as he told me it’s a 3 month wait and long process to be able to sing with the team), and was almost suggesting that, as i’m just passing through, a lot of people are just trying to be in the lime light as it’s vegas, so he’d like to see me go through the 3 month process to show commitment first, he even suggested i just sing in the audience.

in absolute shock, i headed to my car. called my parents who were appalled and suggested we move churches, as i’ve never experienced such unwelcoming behaviour at church before.
i politely went back in to give him feedback on how the conversation had made me feel and explain that it was my first time ever asking to join the choir, and it was very discouraging.
he kept trying to talk over me while i was explaining myself, instead of listening to what i had to say, which almost turned into childish bickering.

i am very disappointed. as a christian i am trying to not hold any disdain in my heart. but at the moment it looks like we will be attending another church.

like i said everyone else has been amazing. it was just one experience with the band member.

happy sunday

I am so grateful for Pastor John.

reviews.text:
I’ve been attending the Springs since 2016 and I can’t believe I haven’t left a review yet.

One of the other main reasons we love the church was their children's ministry program. We have three young boys and it's so important to us that they are hearing strong biblical principles Sunday mornings and learning valuable lessons. I've been amazed at the things my 6 year old comes home talking about. It's amazing to me what an organized and exciting children's ministry they have for this size church. We are also a part of a small group with people that have become family. I love The Springs!

We had a great Easter surrounded by other like minded people, it was a great time. I'm not a member of any specific church but I've been to a few different churches such as Discovery Church and Destiny Church here in town but wanted something new. I was very happy to visit The Springs Church along with my in-laws and my 16 Month old son. Upon arriving everyone was joyful and pleasant. We checked my son in quickly and got him settled into the 0-2 aged room for care.(they provided 2 tags 1 for him and 1for me to show upon pickup for safety, nice!) It was his first time being cared for by anyone who wasn't family, it was tough to leave him upset in there but I was assured that he would be cared for and within 5 minutes they had calmed him down and he was happily playing with a few other youngsters. I was so happy that the woman who was in there with him seemed so nurturing, she was able to keep him occupied for the hour I needed. They even gave me a beginners Bible book to take home.♥️ The service was to the point and had a wonderful singer for any songs they played. I like when the service is focused on the writing of the Bible and not stories the pastor wants to tell or jokes. I enjoyed it and all the other visitors were very uplifting during the songs it just felt good. The pastors wife was just a doll! After the service we spoke a bit while I picked up my son and unfortunately they'll be moving soon but the new pastor introduced himself to us and seems great! We had plans for breakfast after but the church did have some doughnuts and other items. 🙏  Absolutely no one made us feel uncomfortable and no one was over barring or pushy, just kind like minded people all under gods roof enjoying the feeling of community. They also had the weekly Tithing printed on the pamphlet they handed out which was actually so refreshing to me! The other churches I've been to would never do that and that says something about them that I can't even explain. So thank you for that also. Best wishes to the pastor and his family on their new adventures. God bless!

We were looking for a church that did more than get people in the door and tell them God loves them. The fellowship is amazing because it's a good size to get to know people and the people really make you feel welcome and at home.  This church was an answer to prayer.

Have you been searching for a home church? If so the Springs is for you! You will not meet a bunch of nicer people who understand we are all broken and love on one another! It's truly refreshing to find genuine people who care about one another and truly are a reflection of Jesus! Pastor Brian speaks from the Bible and challenges us weekly to grow in our walk with the Lord. The children's ministry is amazing and understands that these children are our future leaders and that it is important to raise them up in the Word in a fun and interactive way that they are excited to come back each week! This church is a life changing!

Before I write anything, I just want to say, a lot of 1 star reviews somehow disappeared from other people. I’m unsure if the business can delete them or not…but it’s rather strange to me. And pastor ben justifies and defends himself along with low key making people sound like victims in responses, just to prepare you.

I came here for several years. This place used to be more free and more joyful.

I don’t want to call it a church. When I was broken, I wasn’t encouraged. I was more damaged after I went for council, most of the time.

I’ve noticed leadership not being inclusive. I did take it to pastors and they didn’t seem to care.

More of the main reasonings for this, is not that. It’s how the church is being led.

there’s a ton of pride and manipulation here. They want you to serve…A lot. they don’t believe in getting burnt out and they don’t care where you serve-even if it’s not your desired or gifted area.

If you have a problem, they tell you not to be a victim, give you a high 5, let you know you’re a champion and send you on your way.

There’s a lot of gossip, and you can get tainted very easy here. (There are some
Super amazing people I have met, but it’s a remnant)

Ben also didn’t like me going to him if I needed help about any interpersonal advice.

😢quick story-
When we were on a mission trip, I was struggling. I’ve been doing missions for 7 years at the time and it was nearing the end of the trip. Ben gave every person on the trip an opportunity to share a word/testimony to the crowd (multiple people got more than 1 opportunity). There was a day I found out my aunt was dying in the hospital/ and actually passed. So for morning prayer, I stayed in my room, prayed, and made myself ready for the bus. Excited, that maybe I had an opportunity, despite the situation. I was down in the hotel lobby encouraging myself in the Lord when he tapped my shoulder and publicly humiliated me in front of everyone in the lobby, telling me i should’ve been at prayer and there’s no excuse for me not to be there, and I have rejection issues and if I don’t get rid of them it would Damage my future marriage, and not to be a victim. And that if I wanted a microphone that bad, I wasn’t ready for it. (That wasn’t why I was sad, it was my aunt and the unfairness and how I was being treated vs others. Also with his pride)

From that moment I wanted to leave TK but I was under a delusion that TK was the best in SD. (I’m not originally from SD) TK made it seem like they were the best church around.

I stayed, and forgave, it was hard. I saw pastor Ben not really caring about needs. We went to him with troubles that an elder was being rude and he didn’t ever have a sit down convo with us and that elder. I Moved on and forgave..again.

I went to an elder once, I was sick & he didn’t want to pray over me, he was looking around for someone else to pray for me. I pleaded with him and reminded him were supposed to go to elders when sick. He prayed, begrudgingly.

We asked permission to have our wedding there. A week beforehand, I really had my tipping point of the pride in the sermons. I approached a pastor and, again, public humiliation from the pastors and I was the wrong one.

God ended up exposing the leadership and leading us to leave after ben gossiped about us after the wedding. (We wouldn’t have had the wedding there if we knew God was leading us out) -also my husband had a long call with him where he was consistently blame shifting and pointing fingers at us.

Later, Ben blocked me and my husband and refused to get together and talk things through or take any accountability for his actions.

I am no longer under the control and manipulation of the religious spirit.

I cherish the good memories I had, but unfortunately all of this outweighs the good times because character and love is everything. Also, this is just a tidbit of my story.

I hope to reconcile & repentance happens & unity. That’s my heart

reviews.text: I used to love victory outreach but slowly their agenda started showing. They take advantage of those who are willing to be in ministry and manipulate them into thinking if they aren’t loyal to the vision/victory outreach they aren’t loyal to Jesus. One time the pastor said if “ you can’t say you’ll lay down your life for Jesus if you don’t lay down your money”. Nowhere in the Bible does it say that. Yes tithing is important but our salvation isn’t tied with tithing and attending every church conference and event. This ministry gets more than enough faithful others and overcharges for their very pricey events. Then they guilt trip people by saying “ if you’re desperate to be in the presence of God you’ll make a way to attend…”. They limit God to 1 place by saying things like this when God is anywhere and everywhere. The pastor gets treated like celebrity and do does his the founder. I understand yes have respect for the church and the pastor and things like that but not idolize it. I don’t see not one thing about Jesus in that church not one picture nothing, just pastor sony and victory outreach. The pastors all hide away in the what they call the green room as soon as service ends. They don’t offer counseling. A pastor is supposed to teach and make time for people and have compassion , even when Jesus was going through the grief of John the Baptist , when the crowd came to him he was moved with compassion. He didn’t hide away. They have open favoritism that they don’t do anything about. They pick and choose who they want to hold accountable. It’s more like a business than a church. They are only willing to be friends and “disciple” those who are willing to be in the ministry 24/7 besides that forget about being a part of the community there. The leaders are lazy and complain about doing things that anyone with a Christlike mind and true servant mentality wouldn’t mind doing at all. Jesus washed his disciples feet, I don’t see that humility in any of the leaders at victory outreach. It’s actually recommended in the Bible that not a lot of people become leaders because it’s a big thing in the church and especially to God to be a leader. These leaders barely have life experience. They make anyone that is involved in the ministry 24/7 a leader, that’s not how you become a leader. I never see them donating to the homeless, building homes in different countries unless it’s involved in building a Mens or women’s home. Even small churches do stuff like this so there isn’t an excuse. It makes you start to wonder where all this money really goes to. Only God knows and I pray and hope that the leaders and pastors of victory outreach start to remember it’s all about Jesus, not about ministry, not about a vision and not about money. Agree or disagree but look at what the Bible says. They preached 3 times in a row about tithing and it didn’t connect back to Jesus, it connected back to how you can be blessed by being faithful in your tithing. One time for a your service the pastor really said “ she’s for the what ?” While the crowd said the streets. God doesn’t call us to judge anyone especially those with a promiscuous broken lifestyle. This sounded like a word to fit in the world not stand out. I’m not sure what happened to victory outreach. It’s been happening to a lot of churches and it’s reminding me of when Paul had to send letters because so many things were happening within the church that were causing destruction slowly but surely. He corrected them to get them back on the path of what it’s really about which is Jesus and Jesus has morals that we are called to live by and it’s not up for compromise. There is so many things as a outside of the ministry that I know about people heavily involved in VO that they should have been held accountable but because of their position they weren’t. I hope and pray this church goes back to the Bible and stands on its teachings and they find God again. 🙏🏼
