This is a very old church with quite a history in the Orlando area. I was there for a funeral. I was ok until I had to go to the restroom. So I walk out to the hallway to look for it. I couldn't find it so I asked the usher where it was. She said it's up front. I was like, you mean in the front of the church? She said yes, behind the pulpit... I was like, "Oh well, I guess I won't be going to the bathroom until church is over. So I went back to my seat... "After sitting there for over an hour, I was about to bust!" I couldn't take it no more, I just had to get up and walk to the front of the church like I knew where I was going... when you're in a Black church, you have to hold up one finger if you're walking while the preacher is preaching. So I'm  walking with my finger up, all eyes on me, the church is packed, and I really don't know where I'm going... I'm all up in the choir stand, I'm stepping over deacons, I'm just making a scene... when finally I asked one of the deacons, "Where's the bathroom?" He pointed to the door at the end of the row. I ran through the row, stepping on deacons shoes and kicking Mother's ankles all the way to the door, praying that I didn't have an accident along the way. When I got through the door, it was a long hallway going in two directions, there's no sign telling me which way the men's bathroom was, so I ran down the hall to the right. When I get to the end of the hall, I see the sign on the door, "it's the women's restroom!" By this time I know I'm not gonna make the half mile run back to the other end of the hallway, so I just bust in the women's empty bathroom, announce my presence, lock the door and handle my business as quickly as I can. Afterwards, I walk back to my seat. All eyes are on me until I sit down. After another hour goes by... wouldn't you know it, "I had to pee again!" This time, I just got up and went home. 😃

Whether it was through prayer, the little messages that came at just the right time, or the constant reminders of God’s love, I started to feel like I wasn’t alone. They helped me rebuild my faith and reminded me that even in the depths of grief, God’s love never fails.

I’m beyond grateful for the way this church has held me up when I couldn’t stand on my own. It’s more than just a place to worship—it’s a true family, a group of people who don’t just talk about love but show it through their actions. reviews.text: Life Connection Church Orlando has been a true blessing to our family for decades. This is the church where our children grew up, and it has always been our spiritual home. As my husband continues his cancer journey and chemotherapy treatments, we haven't been able to attend church in person, but we have never felt alone. The love, prayers, encouragement, and constant support from our pastor and church family have never stopped. From prayers and encouragement to simply checking in on us, they’ve been walking with us through thick and thin. Even worshiping online, we still feel connected, supported, and uplifted. We are so thankful to be part of a church that truly cares and reflects the love of Christ in action.

I was a member of this church for three years. I’m writing this after careful consideration because of how a recent request for help was handled.

When I was scared about my ex-partner making plans to move out and leaving me with full responsibility, I was told in person that I would have help. Based on that reassurance, I later reached out during a vulnerable time to ask whether the church could help with basic needs such as gas or car insurance so I could get my children to school and medical appointments. Transportation assistance or rides were not possible.

I asked whether this was something the church could help with, or whether I should seek help from other churches so I could plan accordingly. The text I received from the pastor was exactly, “go ask other churches.” My message was then characterized as an “ultimatum,” which did not reflect what was written. I clarified that I was asking for clarity, not making a demand.

I acknowledged that I could see where they were coming from, but that same courtesy was not extended to me. Their focus shifted to defending their response rather than addressing the impact of it.

I was texted phrases such as “Not to judge — but SMH” and “You do not want to be healed,” despite having just explained the steps I was taking and the circumstances involved.

Statements were later made that did not align with my household’s legal or practical reality. When I pointed out factual information, the response became emotional rather than reciprocal.

I understand that not every church can provide assistance in every situation. However, the dismissive tone of the response (including “SMH” while stating “no judgment”) and the reframing of my words left me feeling unsupported and mischaracterized at a critical moment. After three years as a member, this experience was deeply disappointing, and I will not be returning.

reviews.text:
Everything here was my personal experience and my own opinion of this Grace Church.

I recommend and encourage to visit and see it for your own; however, be warned.

I visited this church recently and want to give an honest review so future visitors know what they are walking into.

The building is beautiful inside and out, and the community is warm. Unfortunately, the teaching from the pastor directly contradicts foundational Christian doctrine and biblical truth.

During my visit, the pastor made several statements that are not found anywhere in Scripture and go against the Christian's faith for 2,000+ years. These are not small differences,  they change the entire gospel message which Paul warned the believers about. Here are a few examples of what was taught from the pulpit:

That Satan has physical descendants through Eve.

That Eve, not Christ, brings hope to humanity

That good works create spiritual change before God does

That God was insecure about humans gaining eternal life

That “Let Us make man” referred to God talking to Himself and angels, not just Trinity.

That the soul is not eternal and we do NOT receive eternal life through faith in Jesus.

That God wants people to die so He can fix them.

These teachings are not just “different.” They oppose what the Bible says on essential doctrines like who God is, how salvation works, and the nature of humanity.

Because of this, visitors should be aware that:

The message preached here is not Christian doctrine

Several points directly contradict the gospel

The pastor introduces ideas that are neither biblical nor historically Christian

Anyone grounded in Scripture will notice serious theological errors

The church building is beautiful, and the people are kind. But the message being preached is not aligned with Christianity, and visitors should come prepared with discernment, a Bible which I didn't see a pastor with one, and an awareness that the teaching departs from the faith delivered in Scripture.

reviews.text:
Hi, I regularly attend this church every Sunday morning when I can, and here is my honest review. Very clean, especially the bathrooms. There are two men who will open the door for you as you walk in, they are very welcoming. They serve free donuts and coffee at a cafe-like bar, and in the back there is a section for kids and teens under the age of 18. The music is good and they sometimes experiment with different instruments and solos, and the teachings after are also very well said. The environment is welcoming, and polite. I quite literally have no complaints. I just sat for a good minute trying to think of something that they could fix, and I couldn’t think of anything. Overall it seems as close to perfect as possible.

Side notes:
Specifically about the billboard, that it does NOT mean God does not get angry. Someone left a 1 STAR REVIEW about a billboard, and I don’t think they’ve even attended our church. I attend every Sunday when I can, and I can say confidently we do not teach Christians that God does not get angry. The billboard is a type of advertisement, AKA something to catch the attention of an individual to attend the church. More specifically, many non-Christians feel that they are too deep in a pit of sin to come to Christ, when that is not the case, so the billboard is meant to convey that. God is not angry with you, because no matter what you do, he will ALWAYS love you. The billboard says “God is not angry” not “God does not get angry”. It’s a first impression. Not a whole teaching.

Someone also said that they were not welcomed and to that I have nothing to say because I have no idea what they’re talking about. This is the most welcoming church I’ve ever attended in my life. Their arms are open to anyone, just as the Lord’s are. Whether you are LGBTQ+, have a different style than the ordinary Christian, or even a history of crime, anyone can come in on a Sunday morning, sit down, and peacefully listen to the word of God and they will be accepted by our community, because you took time out of your day to listen to the gospel.

I’m a pastor visiting family for the week and we decided to visit grace church Orlando on Father’s Day 2025.  I’m on sabbatical and have visited several different churches in the last month.

I’ve planted and lead a contemporary non-denominational church myself- so I’m sensitive to how easy it is to criticize a church and don’t do so lightly.

Environmentally, artistically and musically the whole experience was wonderful.

As I sat through the service, I was curious about who the lead pastor is, and what their distinctions are doctrinally. Their website was limited in this information.

Their worship team was excellent and had well prepared. I believed they honored the Lord.

All of those positives melted away as the pastor (well, they call him the team leader) began preaching. The series was called “re think disagreement”. He had 3-4 introductions and I was quite lost as to what he was saying. His bottom line- we need to be ok with disagreement and that it’s actually a good thing. What was his biblical support of this?; In the gospels when the disciples disagreed at who was the greatest and Paul and Peter’s confrontation. That they disagreed. Both of those examples are TERRIBLE examples of unity. A disagreement described is not disagreement prescribed. His premise was biblically faulty from the beginning. His hermeneutics were atrocious, his homiletics equally bad. It was the worse preaching I’ve ever experienced in 20 years.

He spent more time quoting contemporary authors than he did the Bible. In fact,  not once did he use the Bible for instruction or any sort. What was spoken could have existed in an atheist gathering or a Unitarian Universalist church.

His conclusion at the end was “re think” means the same as “repent” - and we need to rethink how we disagree with one another. Then he said you don’t have to change your thinking at all. So basically, you don’t need to repent. This is not the message of the Bible- which says to bring all things into the guidance and authority of Christ. It was relativistic deconstructionism at its peak- reminiscing of the emergent church conversation of the early 2000’s with authors like Brian McLaren (generous orthodoxy) and the like.

There was no charge, no take away. Christ was not mentioned or honored in any way.

I get what he’s trying to do to get people to the table, but he’s not offering them anything of value. It’s a deconstructionist world view that sees through everything. To quote CS Lewis “to see through everything is to see through nothing at all”.

This pastor was a false teacher void of the power or grace of the gospel.

It’s possible there’s more here to the story- like he was addressing a congregational issue- but based off of what I observed- he is a false teacher and the church needs to go another direction, “rethink” and preach Christ crucified. It is the power of God for salvation.

I wonder what message this church is teaching?Their Billboard says "God is not angry" -- No scripture reference.  Because there isn't one.. I'm sure the pastor had the idea of helping people feel like God is not personally angry with them but, loving towards them.  That is true Because by His grace and the blood of Jesus Christ we are redeemed and restored to Him.
But to imply that God has no wrath, no judgment and is not angry at this sin sick world with the abominations against His statutes and commands, paints a very idealistic and untrue view of our One True God.

reviews.text:
Selam:
I have deep love and respect for the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church—its theology, fasting discipline, ancient traditions, and spiritual depth. It is one of Africa’s greatest gifts to Christianity and to the world.

However, I struggle with one aspect that feels deeply painful and contradictory.

As an African tradition rooted in Ethiopian history, it is difficult to understand why sacred images so often fail to reflect African likeness—particularly when it comes to depictions of Mariam, angels, and holy figures. For African children growing up in the Church, the absence of dark-skinned representations quietly sends a message that holiness does not look like them.

This is not a small issue of art preference. Images teach. They shape identity, belonging, and self-worth. When African children never see Mariam or the holy figures resemble them, it risks creating spiritual distance and internalized shame—something the Church has never intended, but should thoughtfully consider.

Ethiopian Christianity is not borrowed; it is ancient, indigenous, and dignified. Our sacred art should reflect that truth. Honoring African features in holy imagery does not diminish faith—it **strengthens it**, grounding spirituality in truth, history, and cultural integrity.

This is shared not in disrespect, but in hope: hope that the Church continues to grow in a way that affirms African identity, uplifts children, and fully honors the beauty of the people who have carried this faith for centuries.

Tabaraki

reviews.text: Very beautiful and nice priest, who is very tall lol I love it

St Stephen's is a beautiful, welcoming parish that serves the regular Sunday Divine Liturgy and vespers on Saturday evening, as well as additional weekday services for select feast days. My family's home parish is another Orthodox church in the Orlando area (St George's Antiochian), but my wife and I love coming to St Stephen's for the weekday Liturgies that they offer as well as for vespers on the rare occasion that it's not being held at our parish due to our priest traveling out of town. The choir sings in the Russian choral style rather than Byzantine chant, which my wife appreciates since it's what she grew up with. This does include singing rather than simply saying the Our Father and the Nicene Creed, which may take a bit of getting used to if you're not familiar with this liturgical practice, as was the case with me. Our toddler loves playing on the church playground after services are over, and there are numerous families with younger children, so this parish is very kid-friendly overall. There are numerous active ministries at this parish, including ongoing educational efforts by the parish priest, Father Daniel, and other theologically-knowledgeable members of the congregation, and they are actively working towards raising a new church building, which is wonderful. If you're in the area visiting or looking for a new church to call your spiritual home, I highly recommend St Stephen's!

reviews.text:
I wanted to speak not on the experience of the fellowship but on the experience of doing business with this church. My wife signed a contract to vend at an outdoor event for this church; she paid a reservation fee for her spot. A day before the event, the weather forecast was showing that there was an extremely high likelihood that there would be severe thunderstorms the day of this church event. When she contacted the church’s organizer to inquire about a contingency plan, they told her they didn’t have a contingency plan and that they planned to proceed with the event.

I myself have a productive side hustle as a musician, and bad weather comes with the territory for outdoor events. Usually, the artist I’m working for has a contract with whoever has booked us, and in the event there is inclement weather on the horizon, someone will notify the artist (who notifies us musicians) if the event will be postponed, cancelled or moved. As I said, the organizers of this church event had no contingency plan.

On the day of the event, let’s say things were  scheduled to start at 1:00 PM. By 1:20 PM, it was raining torrentially, and, ultimately, the event was a total and complete wash-out. My wife inquired about getting her reservation deposit back, and she was told the event would be re-scheduled.  We didn’t hear back from the church. When we went to the church  several weeks later to inquire about our deposit—-because they weren’t returning our phone calls—we were advised that the matter would go before the board. We were told while we were there that the re-scheduled event had taken place, but only “indoor vendors” had been invited back. Ultimately, we never heard back from “the board” or any other member of the church, and my wife’s small business ended up losing upwards of $800. We don’t have any control over Mother Nature, but we had major issues with the way this church handled its business with us. Apparently, my wife’s reservation fee was kept as a “donation”. There was no language suggesting that in the event of cancellation or postponement, that our fees would be non-refundable. We would like that to have been our prerogative.

In any event, we live and learn. We have chalked this up as a learning experience. It was my wife’s first vending event, and it was memorable for all the wrong reasons.

reviews.text: One of the oldest churches in Baltimore, and an important conduit between the German community in the Baltimore Metropolitan Area and their German culture and language. Very interesting monuments and memorials on the church grounds including one to General John Stricker and a piece of the Berlin Wall. what a beautiful church! the architecture is wonderful and it was built in 1755!
What a wonderful church. Full of history and wonderful people. A must visit on a Sunday morning. The Brats and Beer events are a great time as well.

It all started back in 1755 and this wonderful place was built after the original burnt in one of the great fires. German heritage caused them parishioners to face discrimination as they clawed their way up the rungs of society ladders. Forward thinking people made the great hall "religion free" so that people would feel comfortable coming there, and this was in the early 20th century. Language classes are offered on Saturday mornings. The carvings on the furniture are detailed, and lots of fine things have been donated over the years.
If you desire you can even attend a service spoken in German on Sunday mornings.

reviews.text:
As a college student new to the Baltimore area, I was looking for a church to attend and decided to visit this one for two consecutive Sundays. Unfortunately, both services focused heavily on tithing, which was disappointing. During one service, the pastor called 10 people up to the altar to commit to tithing. Once they came forward, he asked for 7 more. The following Sunday, the sermon was again about tithing, and this time, the pastor requested 7 people come forward to give extra tithes for his birthday. After they came up, he asked for 5 more.
It was uncomfortable sitting in the congregation, watching this play out. There was a long pause before anyone responded, and the pastor just waited as people slowly approached the altar. In Matthew 21:12-13, Jesus is upset because the temple, meant to be a house of prayer, had become a marketplace, a place of greed and exploitation. While I understand churches preach about tithes and offerings, it felt wrong to have two consecutive sermons focused on this, with repeated requests for extra money. It created an atmosphere that felt more like exploitation than spiritual nourishment, and it made me uncomfortable. Because of this, I won’t be returning.
Additionally, I had an unpleasant experience with some of the church’s volunteers. Two men, who seemed to be involved in the ministry, made my friend uncomfortable by using inappropriate language like "damn" as she walked past. One even chased my car down as we were driving off to talk to her. It would be beneficial if the church provided better training for its volunteers to ensure they demonstrate more respect and composure.

reviews.text: I've been a member of The Mount for about 7 years, and I'm still extremely satisfied with the teaching and the preaching. we're like one big happy family, very warm and inviting environment. I love my Bishop and first Lady 😍 ALL ARE WELCOME 🙏 🤗

If I could rate this experience separately—the love shown by our family and friends versus the behavior of the pastor—this church would receive one star solely for providing a roof.

I attended my grandmother’s funeral here, expecting a service that honored her life, her legacy, and her transition. Instead, I—and many others—sat through yet another self-aggrandizing monologue by a pastor who has consistently made funerals more about himself than the lives we’ve gathered to celebrate. He spoke longer about his personal salvation story and theological opinions than he did about the woman whose casket was in front of him.

What’s worse—and frankly, unacceptable in this day and age—was the overt spiritual manipulation. The pastor used this sacred occasion to condemn and curse those who don’t align with his particular version of belief, essentially telling mourners that if they didn’t accept Christ his way, they were subject to some sort of divine punishment. That is not ministry. That is coercion cloaked in scripture.

This pattern isn’t new. I’ve attended several funerals here over the years, and the script never changes: self-worship, emotional blackmail, and an utter disregard for the grieving families who just want their loved ones properly honored.

Church is supposed to be a place of healing. This felt like spiritual warfare—with the wrong target.

To anyone considering this venue for a funeral: proceed with caution. If you want your loved one to actually be the center of the service, you may want to look elsewhere.

I selected Mount pleasant as the facility to hold my Son’s funeral because of the size of their main sanctuary. My Son had well over 400 people in attendance and people were standing outside. I advised the person in charge that my family was expecting to receive well over 400 guest.
I was charged $800 plus an additional $250 for the musician.

reviews.text:
St. Moses is a church that feels like a home, and a family. It's also a very safe place to land if you've experienced church hurt - or a safe place to check out if you're skeptical or frustrated by Christianity.

You can expect to be loved (some people jump right in with getting to know you, and others build up relationship more slowly).

You can expect to receive deep discipleship and formation in Scripture, worship, and community (and there's lots of ways to receive more of this, if you want, but even showing up on a Sunday is pretty powerful nourishment for the week).

You can expect diverse perspectives and opinions and theology and practice, but clear and thoughtful leadership that balances these diversities well.

You can expect to be both supported and challenged to grow, at your own pace and in your own way. It's a low-pressure but high-encouragement kinda place.

Also, it's shockingly intergenerational. There's a mixture of retirees, older adults, middle aged, parents of teens, parents of young kids, young adults, college students, high schoolers, middle schoolers, elementary, preschool, toddlers, and newborns. All stages of life - but without idolatry of marriage and kids, either. Every Sunday we all get to hear, after prayer and before kid's are dismissed to kid's ministry, "kids, you are loved..." and that is powerful.

As someone in my mid-20s, coming from a very challenging church experience, early in a marriage, and without much local biological family - this has been a healing, growing, restorative, maturing place for me.

I love it. And I'm so glad to be at a church that I can genuinely and wholeheartedly recommend people check out, and try out, again.

reviews.text: I have attended this church for many years since my early childhood. Overall, I would not recommend this church to others. The church asks for money at any given opportunity and say that it is for the good of the congregation and the building itself. I have tried many times to speak personally to the pastor, however, he would never respond to my inquiries. The church is a toxic environment. reviews.text:
Sunday's at Central make a difference. At the Central Church of Christ you will find a friendly, kind and welcoming congregation. There are plenty of opportunities to study God’s word.

Central’s building is located at the intersection of Edmondson Avenue and Athol Avenue just adjacent to Edmondson Village Shopping Center.  Free parking is available on the lower-level of the shopping center parking lot.  Access entrances for the parking lot are on Edmondson Avenue and Athol Avenue. There is also limited off-street parking for the disabled on Athol Avenue along the south-side of the church building. Public MTA bus service stops at the corner of Athol and Edmondson Avenue. The church offers scheduled transportation services via shuttle bus.

Central’s building is multi-level and has an elevator. Congregation leadership offers worship service every Sunday, as well as Bible classes on Tuesday and Wednesdays.  There are additional events for youth and adults. There is a room to care for babies and small children on-site. Bibles and song books are available in the worship areas.  On-line services are available. Feel free to call for more information.

reviews.text: Incredible Sunday experiences without a disconnected “mega church” vibe. I visited many churches in three neighboring cities before finding the Mix. Small groups and community opportunities are plenty, and connections are there if you’re open to them. Scripture focused and relatable to all who walk in the door, hence “the Mix”. Pastor Marcus does not miss — include The Mix in your search if you’re looking for a church to call home or just want to hear who God is.

If you want to encounter Jesus, visit The Mix Church. I’ve attended three times, and each experience has been excellent. The greeters, kids check-in process, baptism celebrations, and welcome team all create a warm and inviting atmosphere. I deeply appreciate Pastor Marcus and his intentional focus on teaching scripture throughout his sermons. He offers a balanced message, centered more on the Word than on people, which I need, look for, and deem necessary. I'm thankful Baltimore has The Mix Church, it is truly a gem!

Almost a 5 star. Until I was told by the pastors wife I was off putting and she isn’t gonna be interrogated. Context I’m neurodivergent, and have CPTSD which makes crowds and loud noises extremely hard for me to cope with. I asked a very important question that no one can really answer “how do you know you’re called to do this” because where I am at in my own journey of wanted insight. I rushed out after being told by her I’m off putting and am still crying in my car. I really wouldn’t have thought a place i experienced such welcome even being late to and such a beautiful message would be ending with me in tears and feeling ashamed and displaced due to my disability.

I can not speak with experience from the ministries themselves. My experience is one that Jesus himself spoke of in the gospel of Luke. I am a truck driver and had a delivery down the street from the church. When I parked in front of the church, a man came out and told me I had to leave. That it was illegal for me to park there. Their reason was people might miss the parking lot entrance. It was nearly 9pm and I was moving at about 6:30am. Finding legal places to park in a number of cities is something I do on a regular basis, so I knew what the sign I parked behind meant. They ended up calling to police to have me moved, but he told them the same thing I was saying from the beginning.
How does that compare to Jesus teachings you might ask?
In Luke Jesus tells a lawyer about the story of, "The Good Samaritan."

Here is a part of that story:
29 But he wanted to justify himself, so he asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”

30 In reply Jesus said: “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, when he was attacked by robbers. They stripped him of his clothes, beat him and went away, leaving him half dead. 31 A priest happened to be going down the same road, and when he saw the man, he passed by on the other side. 32 So too, a Levite, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side. 33 But a Samaritan, as he traveled, came where the man was; and when he saw him, he took pity on him. 34 He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put the man on his own donkey, brought him to an inn and took care of him. 35 The next day he took out two denarii[c] and gave them to the innkeeper. ‘Look after him,’ he said, ‘and when I return, I will reimburse you for any extra expense you may have.’

36 “Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”

37 The expert in the law replied, “The one who had mercy on him.”

I may have not been attacked, but no matter what part of the world you're from, you are still the neighbor of the people around you. Do not cross the street, or shun them. Help them in any way that you can. I needed a place to rest for the night and I feel as though the actions of this church were not the actions Christ would preach, which is my reason for a one star review.

reviews.text: I have been a member of this congregation of believers for many years. Great place to be if making Heaven is your goal ! If your looking for a new church to expand your identity in Christ there’s always a place for you at Agape.

If that's your sincere desire, I promise that the Power Of God which is present in Agape will overtake you and you will never be the same. Try it and see. No matter what your past is, come onto Jesus and Agape will help you to find Him and continue with him. God bless you.

The Agape Christian Church continually change lives for the better and to the glory of God. Through the Food for Your Soul Ministry, the hungry is fed, the Medical Outreach Ministry’s advisory to the needy, and academic support from college students by providing tutorial support to the elementary, middle and high school children. The power of God working miracles in the Church is an indicative that Jesus is alive and present in the Ministry. Answered prayers from unemployment to full employment, in the midst of scarcity, God made the provision from financial challenges to abundance, and immigration status adjusted. I personally want to thank the Lord for leading me to Agape and for Pastor Nwamoh. Agape is truly God's church and Pastor Nwamoh is God's true messenger.

I became a member of Agape from personally seeing the miracle that the Lord did in a friend's life by turning what was an impossible and hopeless situation to one of victory. I happened to be going through my own trials and tribulations which was unbeknown to my friend and I needed Divine intervention in my situation if just to bring calm to my storm.

So i asked him which church he goes to and he told me Agape. I knew that was the church for me.  Agape is real. My Agape family held my hand through the storm and the reason the storm did not destroy my life was my introduction to our Lord Jesus Christ by Pastor Nwamoh.

Since i became a member of this Church, I have seen the Lord's grace in my life. Through it all, my church family has been there for me and the Lord has never disappointed me. I have experienced miracles upon miracles in my life. My story is impossible without Jesus Christ. Incredible!!

Pastor has been a friend, father, confidant, brother, teacher, comforter and Shepherd. May the Lord Jesus Christ continue to bless him and his family abundantly, give him strength and wisdom to continue the good work.  Amen.

If you really want to know God, come to Agape. The Lord will manifest himself to you. I am a witness. At this church, you feel the Lord's presence.  The church members are very humble and loving. We are all united by our thirst for God's presence in our lives as we navigate the perils of the world we live in today.

We are really a family in every sense of the word. Again, thank you Father Jesus for bringing me to Agape.

reviews.text:
The Covid era truly revealed the heart of the big “C” Church. My family and I moved to North Carolina just about a month before the lockdowns began. As a Christ-centered family seeking a church home, we found it extremely difficult to locate a church that remained open despite mandates and the growing hostility toward the Church.

Freedom House was recommended to us, and after attending one Sunday, we were deeply moved by the overwhelming warmth and genuine hospitality. We’ve been faithful members ever since—going on five years now.

We are so grateful to be planted in a church that stands on sound doctrine, boldly serves the community, and is unafraid to take a firm stance on critical Kingdom issues—especially in a time when such convictions are often met with resistance. Freedom House is unapologetically pro-life and vocal on many cultural matters where the Church is called to be a light.

One of the things I personally appreciate is the tremendous commitment Freedom House has to our youth. It's incredibly encouraging to see intentional investment in the next generation.

It also brings me great joy to witness people of all races, backgrounds, and walks of life worshiping and serving together—as one body with many members—united in Christ. When certain groups or individuals come against Freedom House or our Senior Pastors, it only reaffirms for me that we are standing on the right side of biblical truth.

Freedom House is more than a church—it’s home.

Have Life has an amazing atmosphere but is not a baby friendly church. My family & I relocated to Charlotte, NC in December 2018. I reached out to my FB community asking for church recommendations & “Have Life” came highly recommended, plus with it being 5 minutes from our house we were excited to see if we could make this house our church home. We decided to visit the first weekend in March but my husband had to work so it was just myself & our 9month old daughter. We arrive & we are immediately greeted with several hugs & smiles, we felt very welcomed, however, midway through the sermon my 9month old begins to babble & I was approached by a nice young lady who I’m assuming was an usher who asked me if I mind if she took my daughter to another area so the congregation area could stay quiet & “so no one comes & asks you to leave” were her words verbatim. I never imagined someone asking someone to leave the congregation because of a baby but I guess that’s how it is in today’s time so you can imagine the shocking look on my face but I let her carry my daughter elsewhere so I could continue enjoying the great message. The same usher brought my child back to me during alter-call, we move on to offering time, my 9month old is still babbling & now another usher approaches me & says “Hey. Do you mind leaving or stepping out with the baby? We are recording.” I said “oh sure no problem!” & as I’m attempting to leave, another usher stops me & says I couldn’t leave out right then but to just have a seat in the back. So we sit patiently waiting on the opportunity to leave, the opportunity presents itself & we head out at the same time I’m thinking “we won’t be coming back here” which is very unfortunate because I thoroughly enjoyed praise & worship as well as the message which was so ironic the sermon talked about evangelizing, filling the seats, & here I am a first time visitor being asked to leave because of my baby. I called my husband & parents as soon as we got in the car to share with them my not so good experience & both were shocked & disappointed. I don’t agree with asking people to leave the service because of a baby especially an infant. I understand there was recording going on but if babies aren’t allowed to be babies at “Have Life” that needs to be known. I should have been directed to a nursery upon stepping foot into the building before reaching my seat. I should have been able to see the nursery & care takers for myself & sign my child in/out to ensure she was safe. I hate this happened because I enjoyed myself & I was looking forward to visiting again with my husband but now we won’t be returning at all. I do hope some changes are put in place & the protocol is adjusted for those with interactive/talkative babies.

reviews.text: This is based off my own personal experience and I would never tell anyone how they should feel based off their own experience, but this was mine. I hope that anyone who attends finds everything a church is supposed to be for someone, I just didn’t have that experience.

The pastor condemned the genocide in Congo and Africa , but then went on to call Islam a “religion of hate.” Moments later, he defended the actions of the Israeli government, saying that even though they’re bombing children, they’re still “children of God,” and that anyone who disagrees is horrible.

If the church truly wants to teach God’s love and truth, it should be willing to confront all forms of injustice — not just the ones that are convenient to mention.

Title: Disappointed with Closed Church Gates

Review:
I visited Charlotte today, June 22, 2024, with the intention of seeking solace and connection with God. However, to my dismay, the church I had hoped to visit was closed. The gates were firmly shut, leaving me feeling disheartened and excluded.

I considered sitting outside the church, but even the park nearby, which should have been open, was closed as well. It's disheartening to see a place of worship closing its doors to those who seek spiritual guidance and solace. It feels like the church is making its own rules about when it wants to be open, which goes against the teachings of God.

I understand that churches have their own schedules and reasons for closure, such as maintenance or special events. However, it's disheartening to see a place that should be open and welcoming to all, turning people away.

I believe that serving God should involve creating an environment that embraces and supports those who seek Him. Unfortunately, my experience at this church was not reflective of that. I feel compelled to give a low rating of one star as a result.

I hope that the church administration takes this feedback constructively and reevaluates their approach to ensure that all individuals who come seeking solace and connection with God are welcomed with open arms.

The director assured us after meeting him multiple times that he would be a good fit. We then were told that unless he has an ABA therapist attend classes with him every day that he cannot come. reviews.text: I attended the first of 3 "Grace and Truth" Christmas concerts this morning. Our family visited the church for the first time, and from the moment we arrived, we were deeply moved. The grand, soaring entrance gave the impression of stepping into something sacred—almost like walking into heaven or a magnificent temple.

The sermon was grounded in Scripture and spoke warmly to the heart, bringing a sense of peace and spiritual nourishment. After the service, my husband wanted to greet the pastor, and to our surprise, the lead pastor was personally welcoming all new visitors. He introduced himself with kindness and humility, and even shared a few words about his wife, speaking of her with such love and admiration that it was clear how much he values their marriage.

He took the time to ask each person’s name and why they were visiting, creating a genuine sense of connection. He also shared that the Bible is his shield of faith and the foundation of his life, expressing how deeply he leans on God’s Word for direction.

One of the most beautiful aspects of the church was its diversity—people from all backgrounds coming together in worship. The children’s ministry was another highlight: well-organized, engaging, and led by a caring team. Our kids had a wonderful time and truly enjoyed the experience.

We will definitely be coming back.

reviews.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ St. James Missionary Baptist Church – My Honest Review

St. James Missionary Baptist Church has been my church home for over five years, and even though I drive nearly an hour for, the worship experience makes it worth it almost every Sunday. The various praise and worship teams truly deserve 5 stars. They usher in the Holy Spirit and prepare your heart for God’s Word, just as Psalm 100:2 reminds us to “come before His presence with singing.”

Pastor McClendon does a good job preaching God’s Word and connecting Scripture to the issues of today. I appreciate how he recites passages to support his message, fulfilling 2 Timothy 4:2. At times he uses comedy to make a point—sometimes it lands well, other times it may feel less appropriate for the pulpit. Still, I acknowledge many pastors use humor as part of their style.

One concern is the imbalance in holding men and women accountable. There are many more women in the church, and at times the sermons feel more critical toward men while not offering the same level of accountability to women. Scripture teaches that God shows no partiality (Romans 2:11), and true edification builds up both men and women equally.

Pastor has also acknowledged deacons and members connected to fraternities, sororities, Madon or Eastern Star–type organizations. While I do not believe he is personally involved, I do believe such groups conflict with biblical teachings about oaths and spiritual alignment (Matthew 5:34–37, 2 Corinthians 6:14). These organizations often claim a godly connection, but their pledges and symbolism do not reflect the God of Scripture, and for that reason I believe they should not be honored in the church.

I am also conflicted about the vendor tables set up after service selling goods. While supporting members’ businesses is admirable, Jesus was displeased with buying and selling in the temple (John 2:13–16). If the intention is economic support, I understand—but I personally do not feel that after-service is the right place for commercial activity.

With all of this said, I do not expect perfection from any church or pastor. We all fall short (Romans 3:23), but when we know the Word, we are called to live by it (James 1:22). My hope is that this review is received in truth, love, and patience. St. James has blessed me in many ways, and I pray the church continues growing in alignment with God’s Word so that all who attend—men and women alike—are edified and encouraged.

Grateful for Pastor Brad who reflects Jesus so naturally. His leadership is 1 of the reasons the church has grown so beautifully.  I love how he stands by the entrance both at the beginning and at the end of the service, making time for people in such a personal way.

Today after 12:15pm service, my father and I were waiting to greet him. I dreamed about him last night, so it felt important to at least shake his hand, introduce him to my dad who is visiting from out of country. Pastor Brad was in conversation with someone else, and because of his kindness and desire not to be rude, he continued to give them his full attention. My dad grew a little impatient, and we were about to leave, but just as we were walking away, Pastor Brad noticed us and called out with such warmth: “Hey!” He greeted us so genuinely, as though he had been aware of us the whole time.

That moment carried such light, humility, & thoughtfulness- it reminded me of how Jesus notices people, even in the smallest details. It may seem simple, but it meant a lot to me and my father. Pastor Brad’s example is a true reflection of Christ’s heart.

You can truly feel the presence of God here and the worship team is 10/10. Every service lifts my spirit and the pastors always relate everything back to the Bible, stay on subject, and never make you feel uncomfortable. Their preaching is easy to understand and relatable. This church is wonderful for beginning Christians, especially if you are unsure what to do with the spirit of God or Jesus. There are so many groups you can join and be a part of, making it easy to feel connected. They are very organized with parking. When the main lot fills up, they direct you to park at Burger Stadium or further out, and they have shuttle buses and golf carts running every 2 to 5 minutes. There is a cafe and free coffee, and if you are a first time guest they give you a gift and front parking. They have youth groups and a young adults service every Tuesday with Pastor Sam, who is amazing for that age group, plus services every Wednesday at 7 PM and three services on Sunday. They offer Spanish translation, ASL interpretation, and earplugs and headphones for kids or anyone who needs them. I am part of the LGBTQ community and I feel completely welcomed here. Come as you are. Everyone is very friendly and will do their best to accommodate your needs.
If you're looking for a church, highly suggest to come here. Everyone is welcomed.

Sermon Breakdown
—————————————
60% Decent Sermon
20% About how everyone would rather be watching the cowboys/longhorns.
20% Apologizing for preaching too long.

The ratios have changed since I’ve last been through, with closer to 75% decent sermon (once in a while a great one). The man has 4 services though! You can tell by the 4th service he’s thinking about a nap—understandable.

The events and weekly meetings are where the true fellowship and truly impactful messages are to be found. I benefited a lot from a Men’s group that met several months ago, whereas looking for community during the regular services will get you trampled by all the people rushing out of the church.

We are a warm and welcoming church family that embraces the essence of God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit. Our congregation is a big, loving family that truly cherishes the presence of God in our lives.

Whether you already know Him or are still on your journey of seeking Truth, you will find a place here filled with compassion and understanding. No matter where you are in your walk, we are here to support and love you. If you are earnestly searching for the Lord and the Truth, you will be met with open arms and hearts in our community.

I am truly impressed by this church! No church is perfect and have already ran into some “bumps” but God has used them to grow me. A lot of times “bumps” are areas we need to change.

I had walked away from God and KNEW that the guy moving into our apartment complex that shared a backyard was a believer. So I AVOIDED HIM LIKE THE PLAGUE! 😂

He ended up inviting us to church. And God began to tear us down to our foundation so HE could rebuild everything! My husband was set free from a 10 year pain pill addiction, and I solidified my freedom from clinically diagnosed depression among other things!

The main campus has a lot of wealthier attendees which can be intimidating for some, but if you go to some of the other campuses (meet in gyms and schools) you will find people that are in similar socioeconomic statuses. It didn’t bother me but it was hard for my husband to connect with people at the main campus.

Small groups were amazing within the first 3 months of attending we ended up having to move in with my parents which was SUPER embarrassing but God was rebuilding! Well our small group leader came and helped us move and stayed till 11pm and we had to force him to leave! And some other small group members helped as well!!

The senior pastor Will and Suzi Davis are amazingly kind and remind me of my parents. They are very warm and inviting! Will stayed after service numerous times to pray for us when we were going through all these really hard times! And to this day will give us and our kiddos big hugs when we see him! (we are at the Hutto campus now, started at the main campus, moved to Leander with my parents where we attended Brushy Creek campus, helped launch Round Rock campus and are now helping launch the Hutto campus)

Pastor Will is also very intellectual in his deliverance of his messages and they are always something I needed to hear! Also about 3 years ago he openly admitted he was experiencing depression and the church allowed him to take a sabbatical 😱... I have never seen a church do that! AND when he did he invited local pastors to come and speak!? 😱 That was amazing that he had no fear that he would “loose his congregation” to someone down the road.

Also this church gives away half of what comes in sometimes even to other churches 😱😱😱which is in the millions! The other half goes to the 6 campuses, staff at those campuses, bills for all those campuses etc it doesn’t all pad the pastor’s wallet! And have been at 4 of the campuses I can tell you they run them well and pour a lot of finances into them to operate.

For instance in Round Rock they have a FREE special needs Sumer camp (sometimes winter and fall!) that is a WEEK long they hire paraprofessionals to help with the kids. And then they also have church members help out so the brothers and sisters of the special needs kids can have fun with them too!! AND they send the parents out on date nights every day for 5 days and PAY for their meal or activity!? 😱😱😱😱

Also Suzi Davis the pastor’s wife is AMAZING! She helped inspire If:Gathering and cooperates and attends reconciliation circles with Be the Bridge (a racial reconciliation group). And Pastor Will meets weekly with Austin area pastors to pray and strategize on how to effectively spread the gospel. Which to me is amazing as the past churches I attended we a “us 4 and no more” mentality. And that isn’t how the church should operate in my opinion. But God has healed that hurt.

So to the lady who gave Acf a one star I am so extremely sorry you had a bad experience! I have been in your shoes before but I HOPE AND PRAY God brings healing to you and draws you back to him! And shows you the church you are meant to be at that clicks for you, and inspires you to grow. And that one day you will be able to forgive because when we do it is so freeing to let it go and move on! 😘😘😘

reviews.text: Looking for a home church here in Schertz has been difficult.  We have been watching Life Church with Pastor Craig for 5 years. So with over an hour drive to attend, I think we have found a home church I love!

As a family we started going to this church and everything was great, until I failed as a man, as a significant other, and as a father. Haven’t been there since, it’s been over 2 months or so, but I’m tired of putting myself first. This is a cry for help Lord! It’s currently 10:04pm Saturday night. As many times as I’ve failed you, I will be there tomorrow and put in my part to fully give my life to you! Not for the chance to have my wife back, but for the simple fact that I’m lost in this world without you Lord. I need you and I’m tired of saying, saying, saying with no actions to show for it. Thank you for giving my ex the strength to let me have my son tonight even though I’m not ok, thank you Lord because out of all nights this night is when I needed someone with me so I can cope. I’m eager to be in your house of worship tomorrow, and I’m going to put my pride to the side and ask for help because I sure do need it. I need you Lord!

I was not always big on going to church. We tried this church and really started to feel like home. God has touch my life since I started going. I can tell you the people are awesome, I can speak about the activities. What matters most is God is impacting lives at this church. As he is doing at many other churches. I’m lucky this one is in my back yard
I love the energy and friendly atmosphere here. It energize your whole week. It’s contagious.

My family returned to Austin in 2014, seeking real community. We attended a couple of churches for a decent amount of time. At our first church, we felt loved but always on the outside. Despite serving and even becoming leaders, we were not truly accepted. We reflected on our approach, ensuring we were open and confident, but ultimately, we never felt fully accepted.

We then began attending another church where the community was outstanding. We fit in, served, and loved the people, but the worship and sermons were lacking. I tried to convince myself that the sermons were aimed at new Christians and that I needed to advance my own studies in the Word. However, my daughter's view of God started to change due to the youth pastor's frequent "don't do this, don't do that" messages, making her feel down and unloved. So, we switched churches again. This was a tough choice as we were deeply involved in that community. I explained to our children that we wanted a church that loved us as we were, with great community, messages, and genuine worship.

We started attending Life.Church Austin, which I had requested to come to our city years back after using their resources while leading a youth group in California. Initially, we were hesitant and wondered when the "fakeness" would reveal itself, but it never did. We've been at Life.Church Austin for a couple of years now, and the community, pastors, and leaders are as genuine as they were on our first day. We don't just sing here; we worship as a church family, pouring our hearts out to God. The messages are always scripture-based, relatable, and engaging. Most importantly, it's the people. I've made true, genuine, and lasting friendships. I've had ups and downs this past year, and on days when I came to church feeling terrible, I could be honest, and they would just listen. They hear me and meet me where I am. I can be vulnerable because this church truly is my safe space from the rest of the world.

reviews.text:
This church gave me one of the worst experiences I’ve ever had. Certain people here—!!especially some of the pastors and their families!!—carry themselves as if they’re more privileged than others, and they do not respect boundaries. The way they treat people is 100% judgmental, fake, and unkind. They just hide it behind a smile, so you never really know where you stand until you feel it.
The atmosphere is anything but loving or real. I came in with excitement and high hopes, but I left feeling worse than when I walked in.  never coming back to this church. Everyone is entitled to their own opinion, but this isn’t just opinion—it’s behavior I witnessed firsthand. Some may disagree, and that’s fine, but usually those who disagree are the ones already in the “circle.” If you’re not part of that circle, you’ll be treated like an outsider. I would also like to add, This church is NOT welcoming to ALL  They clearly have a select group they consider “their people,” and if you’re not part of that circle, you’re met with judgment, boundary-crossing, and a very hostile way of pushing people out. Some of the pastors here are the worst offenders—disrespectful, judgmental, and masking it all behind a fake smile. Was looking for a home church and quickly realized this is not that kind of place. A church should be a place of love, acceptance, and community—not a runway where you’re judged by what you wear. If you don’t dress to impress, you’ll feel it here. Sadly, this church has made it clear it is not for everyone, and their treatment of people proves it.

reviews.text: This is a church that puts profit over people. They preach community and taking care of others, but their actions speak louder than words. We were personally impacted by a decision made by the church to close our children’s school with only two weeks notice, 5 days before Christmas, and no support for the staff and families impacted. I will never support this church, and their mission is completely flawed.

The church leadership made the decision to close their Mueller location’s childcare center with only 2 weeks notice of closure. They’ve left families without care and staff without salaries or benefits 5 days before Christmas. After an uproar from the parents at how this situation was handled and the lack of care for dedicated teachers, we received a form response and were told that we would have 1 hour to address concerns with one member of leadership. Additionally, non-leadership staff were tasked with delivering the news to all teachers and parents. They were thrown under the bus. This church does not care for its families and is unwilling to take responsibility for how their rushed timeline affects those involved.

Attempted to close the church affiliated daycare with only two weeks notice for families & staff, leaving staff without jobs right before Christmas and families scrambling to find care during an already hectic time of the year. Poor management.

Great leadership and messages. The church is transparent, giving to not only congregants but also faith-based and non faith-based nonprofits locally and internationally. Along with weekly services, events and small groups give attendees opportunities to connect on deeper levels. Worth checking out!

Where to begin. Beautiful area! The services are really organized and the church offers an app to keep up with your note-taking skills if you want to take advantage of that. Services are typically 9am-10am or 11am-12pm with praise and worship lasting about 30 minutes and sermon another 30 minutes or so. Additional prayer time is always available but it is done in private and without an audience. Services are streamed on fb and YouTube and there is a wide variety of ways to get connected with pastors. Pastor Randy is also a great speaker and I always leave here learning something.

I started coming here about 6 years ago and I haven't regretted it or felt judged by anyone-which is common in other places UNFORTUNATELY. There is no one here to 'kick you out', but instead you are welcomed with open arms. As a Christian, I appreciate that, no one is perfect and it isn't our place to judge.

Btw! YES! The pastor will talk about hard to swallow subjects. He finished last year with a bang about hard to talk about subjects but don't let that turn you away-everyone needs a pastor who is willing to shine a light in the deepest darkest areas of this world-how else is he supposed to be a "shepard" for his "sheep"? I really appreciate that with pastor Randy!

If you don't have a church family, I would definitely recommend this place and finding a new way to build your relationship with God. It isn't like other places.

I’m sure the younger crowd (I’m 28 btw) may love it because it “breaks the norms”, but screaming Jesus every 5 seconds during 20 MINUTES of song worship and playing what would be approximately 10-15 minutes of a movie (did make me want to watch it), are things that should never be present at a church. They get you by appeasing to emotion with the movie, and it makes them “feel something”, and it brings me no pleasure in saying this but the majority of their followers are people I’d call as “lukewarm Christians”, don’t know scripture or respectable church traditions. If you like a spectacle/rock show with no order to their readings to the point that bringing your own bible is entirely useless, then this is the church for you. On the other hand if you like to have true readings, any resemblance of long church history & traditions taught by early church fathers, pastors with a true understanding of that same said history, and just a true overall order to things, then this church is not for you. I’m sure they mean well, but yeah it’s a no for me bud. Remember that our Father is a God of order, and this church completely misses the mark. I’m sure the young folk love it though!

City Reach Church has been truly life-changing for my husband and me. This is the church where my husband first came to faith, and where we were both baptized not long ago. We will always be grateful for that.

Like any church made up of real people, it is not perfect. None are. What we have consistently experienced here is grace, truth, humility, and a genuine desire to love people the way Jesus does. The pastoral team and administrators are some of the kindest, most helpful, and most encouraging people we have ever met. They are genuinely present, approachable, and deeply caring.

The weekly messages often bring a sense of loving conviction in the best way. They regularly speak directly into things happening in our lives, or even situations unfolding that same week. You can truly feel the presence of the Holy Spirit, not just occasionally, but consistently.

It is honestly disheartening to see harsh reviews from one-time attendees making sweeping claims. Deep, meaningful church community takes time. Growth takes time. Relationship takes time.

I would encourage anyone who feels unsure or critical after a single visit to attend more than one themed service and, especially, to join a small group. Those spaces are where we have felt the most connected as Christians outside of Sunday service, and they have truly changed our walk with God and our sense of community.

City Reach has been a place of healing, repentance, learning, and real transformation for us. If you are looking for a church that takes Scripture seriously, loves people sincerely, and understands that we are all sinners walking through a broken world together, this is a beautiful place to be.

Very thankful for this church and the work God is doing through it. ❤️

reviews.text: These so-called pastors are timid, spineless men who crumble under the slightest scrutiny.  I'm talking to you Oscar and DR.  Put them to the test, ask some hard questions and push them a little, and watch how quickly they react like petulant children, defensive, evasive, or outright hostile. I’ve experienced it firsthand, only to be met with immaturity and fragility.  For your own spiritual well-being, I strongly urge you to steer clear of this church entirely.

I visited Shoreline Church in early February 2025 with high hopes. The church has a diverse community, engaging preaching, and a fun kids' play area with a slide. I really wanted to like it. But my experience with the kids' service was disappointing enough that it became my first and last visit.

The first thing you notice when you enter the child care center is the sound of crying children. That alone isn’t necessarily a red flag—kids take time to adjust—but what stood out was the lack of adult intervention. When I picked up my 3-year-old, I found out he had been crying for over an hour and he rarely cries especially for such a long time. Despite providing my contact information, no one reached out. That was concerning.

The kids’ area seemed to be run mostly by older kids, which isn’t necessarily a problem if there is proper supervision or if they are trained to handle upset children. But it was clear that wasn’t the case. Meanwhile, there were plenty of adults at the church entrance, welcoming newcomers, guiding them through sign-ups, and making sure the visitor experience was smooth—an efficient church funnel. But why not place more of those adults in the child care center, preferably ones who actually enjoy working with kids?

After my visit, Jonathan from Shoreline Family Ministries reached out, and I shared my concerns. He assured me he would look into it and follow up. That was back in early February. As of writing this, I have heard nothing. It’s clear they don’t take these concerns seriously. The initial outreach was just a formality—an effort to win over newcomers, not to genuinely address feedback.

This was disappointing because the church has potential. It offers many activities and a welcoming environment. But when a church’s child care service fails at the most basic level—ensuring kids feel safe and cared for—it’s a deal-breaker.

Based on what I have experienced I can see, hypothetically of course, how most people would give it five stars because they love experiencing God but demons would maybe give it one star if they don’t want to be cast out.

We attended the Camp Meeting held here. The facility was gorgeous. Large clean bathrooms, a mother's nursing room with chairs, a changing table, etc. We had a wonderful time, and thoroughly enjoyed this place. ❤️

It’s a beautiful church!!
The fire of Holy Spirit is here in the center!!
It’s an opening door for the power of heaven coming down to revival this city!!
Day and night, put the oil into the lamp, let it burn…
Signs, wonders, miracles…

Praying

Located in Austin TX. We went to a Saturday night service.  The people were very friendly, the service was casual and focused on ministry time, led by the pastor's wife. Sweet Holy Spirit led worship and ministry time. So grateful we went. My friend and I attend Bethel Redding and planned our trip to Austin around attending this church plant! It is great to see it thriving.

I’m so happy we found this church! Today was my first Sunday here. The children’s ministry is really friendly & welcoming my son loved it. I enjoyed the service, the worship is personal and led by the Holy Spirit. The word of God is very practical and understandable ✝️🩷 We will definitely be back!!

formatted_address: 126 W Oltorf St, Austin, TX 78704, United States
name: Saint Ignatius Martyr Catholic Church

reviews.text: Very Novus Ordo.  Some issues I see is a lack of reverence.  Old lady's gossip before service while others are trying to pray.  I see a lot of lady's wearing hats as "head coverings".  The Eucharistic ministers (not a big fan of) do not genuflect when coming onto the alter.  And my biggest issue is a roaring applause after mass is over.  It's not a concert it's a ritual celebration.  However this church has a strong sense of community so that's good.

A beautiful parish demographically balanced, faithful and welcoming.  As visitors we were welcomed and thanked for coming!  The Holy Spirit is alive and well in this parish.  Come discover the beauty.   It was only in the darkness that the stained glass window over the entrance was clearly visible. Stunning.

Come Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful and kindle in them the fire of your love. Send forth your Spirit and they shall be created. And You shall renew the face of the earth.

O, God, who by the light of the Holy Spirit, did instruct the hearts of the faithful, grant that by the same Holy Spirit we may be truly wise and ever enjoy His consolations, Through Christ Our Lord, Amen.
This is a beautiful church with new stain windows that are a must see. Lots of parking outside & sitting inside.

I stopped in today to see the church with my small black cloth wagon that I had with me since I am with out a car and walking. The church is big and beautiful and I saw church going on and felt happy and wanted go in but the security guard KEN said NO wagon allowed inside building. I saw plenty of spots in that large room that the wagon small would have been out of the way if I stayed for church and I was not even allowed in front area room with my little wagon he said put it out side. All my belongings have been stolen non stop as homeless lady and even my car was towed away and robbed all my computer stuff and phone several times and all my cloths. The little wagon is all I have and it was a gift. I felt like since I am homeless let's treat you like dirt and tell you to put it out side. Guess Ken needs a pay raise for this keeping church free of homeless lady with small wagon. I pray the Church treats people better than their security guard.

This church smells Holy. As soon as I walked in my nose inhaled the most exquisite incense. It was welcoming and a heavenly embrace. I love the Resurrected Christ on the Cross. The priest who celebrated Mass reminded me of my dear Jesuit, Don Bahlinger, S.J., a Baton Rouge native who loved his brothers and sisters in the forgotten barrios of El Paso. It is good to leave the noise of busy Austin traffic and frantic drivers and enter into peace that only comes from Christ. No one can take that away. St. Ignatius Church provides rest,encouragement and sincere smiles. We sang the Regina Caeli before Mass. I love that there is a 5 p.m. Sunday Mass. Sometimes I sleep in on Sunday but always make Mass.

formatted_address: 610 N Austin Ave, Georgetown, TX 78626, United States
name: Salvation House Church

formatted_address: 12224 Jourdan Crossing Blvd, Austin, TX 78753, United States
name: The ROCK ATX

reviews.text: One of the best churches I have experienced. You know when you’re trying to find your home church and get close with God, the ppl of the church hinder you from seeking the word. But not at The ROCK ATX. The church is a family, one unit; filled with kingdom citizens and makes everyone feel welcome with no judgement.

My daughter is new to Austin, a student at UT, and currently searching for a local body. We visited the ROCK ATX this past Sunday. We were overwhelmed by the love we were greeted with from the door to our seat. This was definitely much-needed in a new city.

This church has given me a brand new life- literally. I have never experienced love, community, knowledge, and growth like I have in my 2 years being here. Looking at other reviews, it sucks that one experience with an over protective member has turned people away, because that doesn't reflect the spirit of the body. If you are curious about God, Jesus, Christianity at all (I came in an atheist), I highly recommend just stopping in and really listening. Your life will never be the same.
This ministry has changed and saved my life. I’m so grateful to be apart of a community like this!

What can I say, there is no better place of worship than The ROCK ATX! I “grew up” in church and it wasn’t until I attended The ROCK that I was able to finally understand the Bible, have a loving community of Kingdom-minded individuals and truly have a personal relationship with God. If you are missing any of these components in your life, I highly recommend that you pop in for a visit… you won’t regret it!

formatted_address: 2525 W Anderson Ln. #365, Austin, TX 78757, United States
