reviews.text: Love the people. Very authentic. God is moving in this church!

formatted_address: 7521 N Lamar Blvd, Austin, TX 78752, United States
name: Capital City Church

reviews.text: Cap City Church is awesome!! Very welcoming and makes you feel at home. Pastors Blaise and Brandon are very passionate in what they do. I really enjoyed serving and have met some great people at this church!!

When I moved to Austin, TX from Georgia, the first thing my roommate and I wanted to take care of was finding a church that’s unashamed to preach the Gospel in its entirety, only moving on the call and under the guidance of the Holy Spirit, engaged in Holy Spirit worship, and rooted in prayer.

And that’s how I would describe Capital City Church! Pastors Blaise and Brandon are humble leaders with a thirst and fire for Jesus Christ!

Both Pastors are actively involved all facets of the church, and the weekly prayer nights are my favorite to recharge from a busy week.

The church has grown significantly ever since I joined and is just further proof of the work the Lord is doing in Capital City Church.

I unfortunately had to re-locate for work to Dallas, TX but I will always call Capital City Church my home, forever and always!

Churches often reflect the heart of their leadership.  If you are looking for a loving, authentic community that is spirit-filled, spirit-led, compelled to pray and guided by the Truth of the Bible, you may not need to look any further than Capital City Church.  Pastor Blaise Raccuglia is a truly anointed leader and under-shepherd.  He loves Jesus, he loves people, and he loves the city of Austin.  If you are in the Austin metroplex, check out this community of believers if you are looking for a place that you can call home.

I personally know Pastor Blaise, and let me just say this one thing about him… he LOVES and KNOWS the Lord. I’m so so thankful for people like Blaise who have stepped out in faith, to partner with the Holy Spirit in contending for revival in this city! The Lord is moving mightily in Austin, TX and it’s because of bold men and women, such as Blaise and his bride, saying “yes!” to the call of God! If you don’t already have a home church, please pray and consider calling Capital City your home of fellowship!

How I came across Capital City Church... I was at the Texas State
Capital for prayer night back in
May of 2023. Pastor Blaise was
one of the pastors leading the
prayer and acoustic 🎸 worship.
The glory of God consumed the
whole room as we all basked in
the presence of God. At that time
I was looking for a home church,
I knew CCC was the place for me
and my family...and the rest is
history.  Capital City Church is a
Spirit filled church led by two amazing pastors, Pastor Blaise
and Pastor Brandon.

formatted_address: 903 Neal St, Austin, TX 78702, United States
name: The Well Austin Community Church

reviews.text: If you are looking for a place to be ACOUSTICALLY ASSAULTED by a rock show sound system that serves to overpower your voice, the Holy Spirit and discourage fellowship, congratulations, you've stumbled into yet another Austin "church". But fret not, they do provide a bowl of free earplugs! Otherwise most Austinites should feel at home with its orientation  to dance-on-the-line between  Austin's Keep it Weird woke culture and that of a godly one, so I am told by some of the greeters.

Reflecting on my review from two years ago, I remember expressing concerns about representation for the 50+ age group. It’s been a beautiful journey, and I’m thrilled to share that I feel genuinely connected and at home here. My age group is “ well” represented. (see what I did there) 🤓🥰

I have found a community here. I am proud to say there is a place and space for me.

If you’re searching for a sense of belonging, I wholeheartedly encourage you to come and experience it for yourself. I’d love to connect… find me, and I’d happily treat you to a coffee! ☕

Wonderful experience when we were visiting friends in town. Everyone was very friendly and inviting. It is a gospel centered church that strives to practice what they preach and its evident in the different facets of their ministries and services. They love people well and do a great job of teaching and encouraging spiritual growth outside of just sundays as well.

We have attended church there several times when visiting family in Austin. We have felt very welcomed each time. Different people have made it a point to greet and connect with us. The preaching is some of the best we've ever heard- so insightful, interesting and inspiring. The worship teams are talented musicians, the music is fresh and focused on worshipping God!  We now listen to the sermons online each week!
Lovely place to bring my family, the community is supportive and welcoming.

formatted_address: 1006 W Koenig Ln, Austin, TX 78756, United States
name: Celebration Church Central Austin

reviews.text:
Celebration Central Austin is truly a 10-star church experience! From the moment you walk in, you are welcomed with genuine love and community. The Spanish translation team is incredible and makes every service accessible, seamless, and spirit-filled for all families.

Worship is powerful, uplifting, and spirit-led every single week. The messages are rooted in solid biblical truth, and the pastor team is the best—authentic, encouraging, and dedicated to helping people grow in their walk with God.

The Children’s Ministry is amazing! The leaders are caring, organized, and committed to making sure kids learn about Jesus in a fun, safe, and engaging way.

Celebration Central Austin also has a vibrant Radiant Sisters women’s ministry and a strong men’s group, both offering support, prayer, and real community.

If you’re looking for a church that feels like home, where God’s presence is felt, and where you can grow spiritually, this is the place!

This church has been nothing short of a blessing in my life and in my children’s lives. Walking through its doors has truly changed us in ways I never imagined. The love, support, and genuine care we’ve received here have touched my heart so deeply.
I am endlessly grateful for every single person in this church—your compassion, your prayers, and your kindness have lifted us up during some of our hardest moments. This place has become our safe haven, our family, and our source of hope.
I will forever be thankful for this church and the incredible impact it has had on us.

I cannot say enough about how much I love my church! From the moment you walk through the doors, you feel the presence of God and the embrace of a true spiritual family. Pastor Riis leads with wisdom, humility, and a heart overflowing with love for people. His sermons are not only rooted in Scripture but also deeply practical, encouraging us to live out our faith every day.

The worship is uplifting, the community is welcoming, and the atmosphere is filled with grace and joy. This church has been a place of healing, growth, and inspiration for me and my family. If you’re searching for a church home where you’ll be nurtured, challenged, and celebrated, I wholeheartedly recommend joining us here. Pastor Riis and celebration church truly shine the light of Christ!

My husband and I joined Celebration Central Austin after moving to Austin and struggling to find a church that truly felt like home. From the very first Sunday, something was different here—warm, genuine, and Spirit-led. We immediately felt welcomed, seen, and connected in a way we hadn’t experienced anywhere else.

Since becoming part of this community, I’ve grown so much emotionally, spiritually, and in my heart for serving others. The teaching is powerful and practical, the worship is life-giving, and the community is full of people who genuinely love God and each other. Celebration has become our family and a place where we continue to be challenged, encouraged, and supported.

If you’re searching for a church where you can belong, grow, and live out your purpose, Celebration Central Austin is truly home. Highly recommend!

Celebration Church (Central Campus) has been a true blessing for me and my family. From the moment you walk through the doors, you feel welcomed, seen, and valued. The worship is powerful without feeling performative, and the messages are real, practical, and grounded in Scripture. Every week, I leave feeling challenged in the best way and encouraged to live out my faith with purpose.

What sets this campus apart is the heart of its people. The pastors, volunteers, and staff genuinely care. They take the time to connect, pray with you, and make sure you never feel like just another face in the crowd. The children’s ministry is incredible as well—safe, energetic, and focused on building strong foundations for kids.

If you’re looking for a church that is alive, Christ-centered, and deeply committed to community, Celebration Church Central Campus is the place to be. This church has strengthened my walk with God and has become a home for my family. Couldn’t recommend it more.

formatted_address: 9023 Old Lampasas Trail, Austin, TX 78750, United States
name: Central City Austin

reviews.text: I've been a part of Central City Austin since the beginning and absolutely love the way it is going.  The people truly care about the community locally and internationally.  My 2 year old daughter has a blast with her friends in "Little City" nursery, and my wife and I have met our best friends and have a community we cherish and are thankful to be a part of.

First impressions are such a big deal and are usually made within the first 5 min of arriving at a new Church.Today was my first time ever at CCA. Right off the bat I was super impressed and thankful for their "Guest Parking"! We are new to Austin and going ANYWHERE is overwhelming! The first thing you see pulling up, is a special front row parking spot for you! Then before getting to the door we where greeted and shown around by the Youth Pastor. Again, very pleasantly surprised! The service was beautiful, energetic and intimate. Their kids ministry is fantastic and got two thumbs up from our 5th and 6th graders! We also saw the preschool and nursery and they looked fantastic! We where greeted and made to feel welcomed by several members and the Pastors. They have a cool first time guest gift as well! Im currently enjoying mine now! This is a place where a family could grow and feel at home! Great first time! We don't know yet where God is leading our family, but this is definitely a place to keep in mind.

I absolutely love being a part of Central City Austin. Are we perfect? Absolutely NOT! Are we striving to be CHRIST like? Absolutely! We are family...we are better together 💕 Come see us & you will see for your self. 😊

formatted_address: 12110 Menchaca Rd Suite 201, Austin, TX 78748, United States
name: City Chapel Church

reviews.text: We love City Chapel! We love the children’s church. Our daughter has grown so much and has so much fun while there. The worship is genuine and beautiful. We have grown so much as a family. It’s feels like what the church is called to be. They are real, loving and authentic people.

I love this place! I've been coming to City Chapel since the launch in 2015. A friend of mine was on the launch team, and I figured I'd try it out. I've found my home. The people here have become family to me. When I'm gone for long periods (for work or travel), someone always reaches out to tell me how much they've missed me--that's more than a lot of members of my actual family. I'm continually amazed at how much I learn here every week (and on the podcast for weeks I can't be there), and it's exciting. I've grown spiritually and personally in ways that I never thought possible, and I don't know that I've ever felt so spiritually fulfilled or peaceful in a church. This is a place that truly is the hands and feet of God, and truly shows what it means to love God by loving others. I'm thankful to be here and be part of it. Thank you, City Chapel!

This is not a church that preaches to you but learns with you and opens your eyes to so many new experiences that you had no clue about. The wonderful people at City Chapel will become your friends, support system and Family. They always go out of their way to help everyone no matter how big or small. This is not just a church it is a community. They don't judge, they claim no perfection, they're just people and no one is more important than the next. Pastor Harry and Rowena will always be there for you.

If you are looking for an authentic church that will make you feel at home, this is it. If you're looking for a church that will challenge you, this is it.

Church means the people of God, not a building. City Chapel has that figured out.

Pastor Harry breaks things down in a simple way, but doesn't sacrifice the deepness of the word. This is my new church home.

Family friendly!
Come as you are!
Excellent worship and Pastor Harry delivers the message in a gifted way, that you will remember.   The Holy Spirit definitely moves at City Chapel.

formatted_address: 11400 Concordia University Dr, Austin, TX 78726, United States

reviews.text: Really love this church.  The members are loving and the leadership is strong and kind.  My experiences have been wonderful here.  I left a United Methodist church to join up with this church and I know it was the best decision!!!   If you come visit, please find me & sit with me!!

Austin Global Methodist Church is a Spirit-filled, loving church. Everyone here is welcoming and makes you feel like family. There are great Sunday school options, childcare, and fellowship. If you’re looking for a Biblical, friendly church come find your home!
I love this church! The people here are warm, friendly and full of joy. The pastor gives inspiring, Bible-based sermons.
Love this church. The people are very friendly and caring.  A wonderful place to share God’s love and message.
I live a thousand miles away, but "drop in" occasionally via their online stream, and am challenged and encouraged by the powerful, Bible based sermons from their pastor.

formatted_address: 1715 W Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78703, United States
name: The Austin Stone Church

reviews.text: The worship was passionate, sincere, heartfelt and joyful. The preaching was biblical, passionate, convicting. But the people. Oh, the people! Friendly, loving, welcoming, interested in you, genuine, smily. I can't wait to go back. If you don't meet God in the preaching of his word or the singing of his worth, you will meet him in his people.

What a wonderful church! Strong on discipleship. Great worship. Solid teaching from the pulpit. Challenging yet graceful. Full of authentic, yet broken and healing people. Just like the rest of us.

So glad I got to go here while in town!

First time coming,  great bible-based sermon, full of truth,  amazing worship team. Seems good for all sorts of ages, great sized college ministry. Provides earplugs for worship music as well if it’s too loud for your taste (super smart).

Have attended the Austin Stone for over 10 years, they LOVE Jesus! The Word is preached with truth and with no apologies. You will be spiritually fed here whether you are a new Christian or are hungry for depth. And yes, the worship team is phenomenal. Not only are they talented, but they are humble and are servants to the church and care for the congregation. Love all the pastors.

You will find Authentic Christians at this Church who love their neighbors and are genuinely welcoming. It's truly amazing and so encouraging to see how many young people in Austin love and follow Christ.
If you are hurt and struggling and need help from people who will not be judgemental but offer to walk along side you through your healing, reach out to this body of believers. With God's Grace your life can be made new.

formatted_address: 4425 Red River St, Austin, TX 78751, United States
name: Midtown Church Austin

reviews.text: I've been going Midtown for 7 years and really really love it. They preach the Bible, and members are very devout in their faith. The worship is contemporary (and super good). The congregation is diverse, with probably a little less than half being college students. If you want to grow in your faith, I highly recommend coming to midtown. I wouldn't be the man I am today without my midtown community. On another note, I met my wife here. So yeah. It's worth a visit.

Midtown has been my church home for four years. I started going here when I was a sophomore at UT, and it has played a huge role in my faith. The people are so welcoming, kind, and loving. I have learned what it looks like to follow Jesus thru Midtown and my community here. On a day-to-day level the preaching and worship are both awesome. Come join us on Sundays!

The way I explain Midtown to my friends who don't do church or God or whatever is, "we just really love Jesus a lot so we try to be like him and not be pieces of crap." We're a community of mostly central Austin people who do an incredible job loving each other, our neighbors, and our city. We're not super fancy, read: no fog machine, so don't expect a show. The music is still high quality and worshipful, it's just a little more down to earth than some of the bigger places around town. Sundays are really great, but the real magic happens during the week when everyone is hanging out doing life together.

The vision of midtown is what makes it different from any other church I have been a part of: to partner with God to see the day when every man, woman and child hears the gospel from a person who loves them. It's important to me to be a member of a church that emphasizes loving others and building relationships while figuring out what God is all about. While sometimes I fail at this, I am surrounded by people encouraging me to continue to pour into others as we build our faith together. It's pretty cool.

I have been a part of Midtown Church for the last 4 years and I am so glad to call these people family! The beauty of the gospel is evident in the teaching on Sundays and in relationships throughout the week. We are broken people who love Jesus and want to know Him more as we learn to love others the way He does.

formatted_address: 9001 N FM 620, Austin, TX 78726, United States
name: The Austin Stone Northwest

reviews.text: What a remarkable church . Austin is truly fortunate to have a place of immense spirit. I was just driving through Austin and through a little bit of research landed on The Austin Stone NW church. Pastor Ross Lester from The Austin Stone West delivered an exceptional sermon . The musical ministry was also deeply moving. My only regret is that I don't live in Austin Texas. If you live nearby or are just driving thru , I hope you visit . Bring Kleenex , you will likely need some .

The Church at Canyon Creek is a wonderful place!  The church staff is incredibly kind and passionate about sharing God's love.  They have wonderful programs for our children and my husband and I always feel welcome and cared for. We have been attending the church for almost 8 years and it's definitely my favorite place to be on Sunday!

Our family attends The Church at Canyon Creek. This is a multi-generational church where people of any age can find caring relationships with their peers. The pastors teach the Bible and the worship is genuine. It is a great place to grow and serve.

I've been attending the Church at Canyon Creek for nearly two years. It's been a great place for our family. The kids ministry has been engaging for my 8 year old and the youth ministry has been very helpful for my teenager - who actually likes going to church. I've also had a great experience with my ABF (Adult Bible Fellowship). I will always remember how the associate pastor Donnie ministered to me when I was going through a very difficult time. If you're looking for a solid group of believers with good teaching, encouraging people, a counseling ministry, and a place to belong in a not-so-megachurch church, TCaCC is a good place to be.

Bible based, truth teaching in the Fellowship hour as well as in the Service. Fantastic place to grow in your relationship with Jesus and make some friends to encourage you on your journey. Social events for all ages, summer youth programs, a preschool, and so much more.

reviews.text: Beautiful place. Very inviting. Very simplistic space but beautiful in their mission, actions, and words. Lots of support for all people. Missional program, outreach program, therapy support for family, marriage, etc, as well as small communities of social connection and intimate relationships to get to know other and them know you. This is a huge multi campus church with multiple services at each location and still growing. But they have allowed to make it a like a small town church.

A positive and  productive place that contributes to the bettering of the community.  There's a field with some soccer goals setup and a place you can take your dogs also.  I would like to see the soccer goals replaced with better goals since the ones that are there are in bad condition and some doggie bag polls put up.
I like my ATX Stone North location more but the same friendly staff / community. thank you and god bless

This is a Calvinistic church, they are honest about their position, and you can read that on their website. They think their philosophy is maturity and like all reformed it's either that or Arminianism. Both are false teachings, appropriately named after men. For those seeking truth, avoid this place, if you are not saved they are no help, if you are saved, they are no help. The fruit of Calvinism is lordship salvation - a lie -, the uncertainty of salvation and fatalism - which they address intellectually. Per God's word, salvation is for all who will believe God's record about his son but per their teaching, salvation is only for the unconditionally elect. Good news for them because they got elected, too bad for everyone else they were elected for hell. There is no gospel in Calvinism, everything is turned on its head.

I found family here. It’s been the best part of my Christian faith the last 9 years. This church really serves the community well. If you are looking for a family focused church Home check it out.

I love that my kids are learning about Jesus in every class.

I also really love how they care about the world - the nations...with purpose!

formatted_address: 6711 Menchaca Rd, Austin, TX 78745, United States
name: South Austin Church

reviews.text: Great people, very helpful and a good message!

From the first time I walked through the doors the entire congregation has welcomed and loved me! I rely on Celebrate Recovery on Thursday nights for my recovery and fellowship there as well. The Pastors and secretary are all about helping the needs of those less fortunate in our community and that I help personally through my employment. I love this place!

This church is absolutely incredible! Lots of friendly folks and a fantastic pastor. Plenty of ways
to get involved and lots to do for the little ones. Apparently founded in 1948 and is going strong !
If you want to know Jesus, this is the place to be !!

I started attending this Church when what is now the Hispanic worship center was just 2 x 4's (1971).
Our Pastors, staff and members are all great people looking to serve the Lord.  Come join us and find out how friendly we are!

The love of GOD is shown and felt here. Loving church community supporting all those in need. Food pantry, Celebrate Recovery and additional service's. Thank you SAC Serving All in Christ. I love you.

formatted_address: 2700 Northland Dr, Austin, TX 78756, United States
name: Glad Tidings Church - Central Austin

reviews.text: Everyone is kind and loving. From the greeters to checking in the children to the amazing preaching and worship. We love the atmosphere.

Staff is great, until they aren’t. They preach that everyone “belongs there,” but that’s only if you are useful… then it’s not a big deal. You can take me for being bitter, but if what I say if half true… is that a place where everyone belongs?
Awesome praise and worship! The presence of God is always there! Love the atmosphere and great word given every time by Pastor Michael and Tamara Norman.

Everyone I've met in this church is very kind and welcoming. You may walk through the doors feeling like an outsider, but you walk out the doors feeling like family. I love it here. The people are wonderful. The service is sent out with love. If you're in Austin and looking for a church, try GT. I don't think you'll be disappointed.

The people are so sweet and very personal during interactions with you and your family. It's not too crowded and the child area (kid city) is so cute.
It's just a little too quiet for me. But a great experience.

formatted_address: 1201 Payton Gin Rd, Austin, TX 78758, United States
name: Antioch Austin Church

reviews.text: I've found Antioch to be a pretty good church experience. It's non denominational so fairly low church and Baptist leaning, but there's a unique blend of charismatic and Biblical basis where the church focuses highly on relationships; with God, with fellow believers, and with the community around us. A great group of people where everyone is welcome.

I rarely leave reviews online, and I have never left a review for a church, but I feel I must do so after my experience here for the sake of any other church seekers in Austin. This is not a church for the seasoned believer who wants in depth, exegetical teaching straight from scripture.

To start with something positive, we were greeted warmly by the welcome team, and the congregation was kind and friendly.

At my previous church, solid, Biblical, exegetical teaching was of utmost importance. Pastors prioritized teaching verse by verse, taking into account the historical context, original language, author, and audience. The pastor at Antioch Austin was teaching from Joshua 1, specifically doing a topical teaching on “How to step into promise.” It was a classic spiritual milky, prosperity gospel, surface deep, topical sermon, that did not take into account original audience, intention, or context at all. Using verse 8 specifically, “. . .For then you will make your way prosperous, and then you will have good success,” the pastor drew parallels from this scripture to Antioch Austin, insinuating that —based on this passage— a great promise of prosperity and success were on the horizon for this church body.

The worst part was a very unfortunate and embarrassing story about his wife’s first birth experience that he used as a sermon illustration. After his wife “thought she was going into labor a hundred other times,” the pastor said his heart had admittedly “grown cold towards her.” (cue laughter from the congregation.) When she was actually in labor, she said so to him, and instead of believing her this time, he said “Like the loving husband and suitable partner I am for my wife, I denied that she was actually going into labor and left the house to go get coffee.” (more laughter.) When his morning coffee run was interrupted by a phone call from his wife that her water had, in fact, broken, only then did he turn around and go home. The story went on, including embarrassing details about his wife’s profanity during labor that I’m sure she didn’t appreciate being shared from the pulpit, and more snide jokes that reflected very poorly on the pastor.

I hate to knock stars off of a church, but I would like to explain.

Now, why only three stars:

1. The congregation felt judgmental when the pastor mentioned more people come on Easter and then they don't come again. As if to say the people only come on the holidays (which could be true for some, or for others it could be that they're finding a new church home and this wasn't it.)

2. The pastor referred to everyone as 'sinners' (I think probably quoting "for all have fallen short of the glory of God), but as a believer I am redeemed through the blood of Christ, repented, baptized, saved through Grace, no longer a slave to sin, no longer a sinner but a saint. I have a problem with being called a 'sinner' in the context that the pastor used because it takes the power out of the gospel.

3. The kids section was supposed to scan our ticket to get the kids back, but they didn't scan at all and instead let the kids walk out to the parents. I don't feel safe about that, especially downtown.

4. The worship service was well done, but way too loud.

5. And finally, the Easter service wasn't about God's miracle of rising from the dead. His message was 'you're going to die and you don't know when so you better follow Jesus so you know where you're going. Time's running out. I only have today to tell you this.'

reviews.text:
The Cathedral Basilica of the Sacred Heart in Newark is truly breathtaking — a masterpiece of architecture and a place that feels timeless. From the moment you approach its towering spires and intricate stone carvings, you realize you’re standing before one of the most stunning cathedrals in the United States.

The interior is even more inspiring. The stained glass windows flood the space with colorful light, and the soaring vaulted ceilings create a sense of peace and awe. Every detail, from the marble altars to the carved wood and mosaics, reflects extraordinary craftsmanship and devotion.

Whether you’re religious or simply appreciate art, architecture, and history, this cathedral is worth a visit. The atmosphere is calm and spiritual, offering a quiet retreat from the city’s noise. The organ and choir performances are also world-class — the acoustics make every note resonate beautifully.

It’s hard to believe such a magnificent European-style cathedral stands right here in Newark. The Cathedral Basilica of the Sacred Heart is not just a church — it’s an experience of beauty, serenity, and inspiration.

What a stunning holy ground. It was a beautiful morning bidding farewell to my friend’s mum, and also my first time at the renowned Cathedral Basilica of the Sacred Heart. What I thought would be a heavy, mourning heart turned into a moment of awe and quiet peace. The church is the most breathtaking I have ever seen, with its towering arches, intricate stained glass, and a presence that fills you with both reverence and calm.

reviews.text:
I attended One Family Church for years but eventually left after too many red flags: their constant emphasis on being a “diverse” church, their partnership with the St. Louis Racial Reconciliation Network, the Maya Angelou mural, and a race series that leaned on false & misleading examples. These felt like ideological tests, not biblical teaching.

Maya Angelou’s I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings has been banned in schools across the U.S., including the U.S. Naval Academy library, for graphic content and racist themes. Yet the church uses her “caged bird” imagery as a permanent symbol of victimhood—reinforcing a worldview where guilt is demanded endlessly and forgiveness is never part of the process.

The church has chosen to partner with and fund the Racial Reconciliation Network. This program is not biblical reconciliation—it CRT. Marx divided society into oppressors and oppressed. CRT applies that model to race: white people are labeled oppressors, people of color oppressed. Instead of forgiveness, the framework demands permanent guilt and endless penance.

I met with the Network’s leader to understand this process. We agreed the purpose is for Yt people to acknowledge privilege and give it up. When I asked what that looked like in real life, his best example was, “It’s like male privilege, you know, like holding a door open for a woman.” That is not a real example of how to live it out. He called the program a biblical cause, yet provided no Scripture. The central idea—privilege—cannot be defined or measured, yet the entire program rests on condemning people for it.

I also met with the main pastor. At first he declined to discuss CRT, calling it “not useful.” When we did meet, I reminded him that he says he wants a church like the disciples built—open to all nations. But this framework does the opposite: it singles out one group and forces them into endless penance with no forgiveness.

Later, I spoke with the prayer group leader. I warned him that this false teaching puts salvation at risk, since the Bible says when the blind lead the blind, both fall into a pit. His response was, “salvation is guaranteed.” Confidence is misplaced when it defends false teaching.

The curriculum confirms the issue. It combines Multi-Ethnic Conversations with Peggy McIntosh’s Yt Privilege Checklist, a secular exercise from 1989. The book never mentions forgiveness and instead tells participants to repeat reconciliation so injustice “doesn’t happen again.” The checklist assigns guilt by skin color. A secular sociology tool is treated like theology, while forgiveness—the heart of reconciliation—is missing.

True reconciliation in the Bible is completed with forgiveness, not endless cycles of guilt. Once forgiveness is given, it is done. This program denies forgiveness, enforces permanent division, and replaces Christian doctrine with ideology.

reviews.text:
The Cathedral Basilica of St. Louis is an absolute must-visit and easily one of the most breathtaking landmarks I’ve ever stepped into. This place is not just a church—it’s a masterpiece of art, history, and architecture.

What makes it even more extraordinary is its World Record: the Cathedral Basilica of Saint Louis houses the world’s largest collection of mosaics. And you truly feel it the moment you walk in. Every inch of the interior glows with intricate, hand-crafted mosaic artwork that tells powerful stories and leaves you in complete awe.

The atmosphere is peaceful, the craftsmanship is unmatched, and the sheer beauty of the space is unforgettable. Whether you’re into art, architecture, history, or just looking for a moment of serenity, this cathedral delivers an experience like no other.

This church is absolutely stunning! We visited on Christmas Eve so the church was beautifully decorated for the holidays. I honestly came to watch/listen to the choir because they are so good. Would love to come back for a choir concert if there’s any.

I have lived in St Louis for 20 years and have always wanted to visit this building.  Decided to attend Christmas mass.  I am not Catholic, but everyone was very warm and welcoming.  The architecture of this building is amazing.  There is so much to see on the inside and outside.  I spent so much time walking around and gazing at everything on the walls and ceilings.  You should visit if you get a chance.

The Cathedral Basilica of Saint Louis is far beyond comprehension in its beauty. Every inch of the mosaics, the arches, and the towering ceilings feels like a direct reflection of giving our very best for God.

The organ is unlike anything I have ever heard. The sound echoes from every direction, filling the space in a way that is almost overwhelming, yet completely moving.

Attending Mass here was truly heaven on earth. I was deeply honored to receive the Eucharist in such a sacred and breathtaking place.

This cathedral is not just another church to visit. It should be a bucket list item for every Catholic, and honestly for anyone who appreciates art, history, and the divine.

One of the most beautiful churches in St. Louis. Catholic or not you need to come here and to one of the tours just to appreciate the architecture. Everything is hand placed, there are millions of golden stones on the ceiling. Jaw dropping experience.

reviews.text:
I do not recommend donating to The Salvation Army based on a recent and deeply disappointing experience I had with their furniture pickup service.

I scheduled a donation pickup for the day before my move out date and proactively called to confirm details. I spoke with a representative named Chris and specifically asked whether the pickup team would be able to collect furniture from an upper level apartment unit. He informed me that they do not go upstairs and that all items must be placed on the ground floor. I explained that, as a woman, I would need to find assistance to move heavy furniture such as a dining table, and he acknowledged that. Chris also stated that the pickup window would be between 11:00 AM and 4:00 PM. This conversation took place around 9:57 AM.

To my surprise, I received a voicemail from him at 11:59 AM saying the driver would arrive between 12:00 PM and 1:00 PM, significantly narrowing the original time window. I immediately began preparing to move items downstairs. However, by 12:10 PM, the driver had already arrived and refused to wait, stating I would need to reschedule the pickup because he couldn't sit and wait for the furniture to be brought down.

I was truly trying to do something kind by donating nearly new, high quality furniture to those in need. Items such as a dining table I paid over $1,000 for and used for only a year, a brand new queen size bed frame still in the box, nightstands, a TV stand, a desk and chair, a full size bed frame, and two dressers, all in excellent condition. I was motivated by generosity and faith, believing that giving back would bless others and, in time, bring blessings my way.

This experience left me disheartened, not just by the lack of professionalism, but by how difficult it was to give away items that could truly help others.

I love everything about Beulah, especially the undertones of true southern Baptist culture and sermons that remind me of the churches I grew up attending with my parents and grandparents across GA and AL. But the best part is the teaching, dedication, and contemporary approach to church leadership from Pastor Harris. I’m truly grateful for my Beulah community and the meaningful work that is prioritized within and outside the church doors in the Tampa community. It truly lives up to the mantra: We’re a Movement, Not a Monument. I brag on this church constantly. 10/10 would recommend to anyone looking for a solid, spiritually fulfilling church home in Tampa.

I also adore the tremendous community outreach, at Beulah, living by the scripture Matthew 25:40 where Jesus let’s us know that as we assist others in need, we are doing it unto Him. I often get into conversations with others about Beulah and one of the things I like to say is that Pastor Harris doesn’t tell you what you want to hear, but what you need to hear. To God be the glory as He continues to Revive in 2025!!!

For many years, I prayed for a church like Beulah Baptist Institutional Church, and God not only answered my prayers—He far exceeded my expectations. Pastor Harris and Lady J are true servant leaders who lead with compassion, humility, and by example. Pastor Harris preaches with power, clarity, and unwavering commitment to sound biblical doctrine. He challenges us to think critically about the word, but more importantly, apply the word of God to our lives.

Our mantra is that we are a "movement, not a monument" and that is clearly reflected in the many impactful community initiatives BBIC carries out each year. At the heart of Beulah is a deep commitment to social justice, grounded in the Word of God, a sincere passion for transforming lives and uplifting the community.

Pastor Harris, Lady J, and the people of Beulah are some of the most generous individuals I have ever encountered. Their love and kindness are not performative—it is genuinely who they are. If you're looking for a church that lives out its faith in action and love, Beulah Baptist Institutional Church is a place you can call home.

reviews.text: Radiant South Tampa is absolutely life-changing. I’ve been visiting since the very first day it started, and it has been nothing short of amazing. The pastor and leadership team are incredible—always striving to grow, lead well, and point people toward the Kingdom. Every week the word is solid, powerful, and never watered down. Truly a place where you can feel God’s presence and be challenged to grow in your faith.

This “skinny jeans church” is the real deal. Yes the pastor wears jeans and is into CrossFit. But people come to Radiant to hear about, discuss, and be inspired by Jesus and the Bible. Pastor Aaron doesn’t make the church about him but does make it about Him. The premade notecards help me retain what was said and there will always be examples to help you apply the holy Word into your life. Pastor is funny and engaging but unafraid to make you uncomfortable in your sin, always wanting you to become a mature believer, walking in the life God intended for you. You will find all ages here, married and single, black, white, Hispanic. It is a diverse, vibrant Church whose energy is contagious and whose worship leaders feel authentic. You will leave there with anxiety lessened and hope renewed in the God that never changes. And isn’t that what church is all about. ☀️🙏

Radiant Church presents itself as a place of worship, yet increasingly operates with the priorities and language of a business rather than a church. Messaging such as “sponsor me,” “tag me,” and “this deserves a Grammy” detracts from the core mission of ministry and reflects a focus on branding and expansion rather than service and humility. Some sermons are good but Pastor Aaron loves to be negative and call everyone out.

Scripture reminds us: “Freely you have received; freely give.” (Matthew 10:8). Unfortunately, that principle does not appear to guide the church’s operations or culture.

Most concerning was an incident in which the sanctuary doors were closed in my face, despite visible open seating and another individual being allowed entry moments before me, because I was accompanied by my service dog. This constitutes a breach of the ADA. This experience was especially painful given that I had called this church home for over two years and faithfully served in youth ministry 2–10 hours per week during that time.

The exclusion I experienced was deeply disheartening and shattered my trust. While I am grateful for the baptism I received here, it ultimately served as a moment of clarity—awakening me to serious issues within this church that are inconsistent with the values it professes.

I use to love Radiant church but recently I’m disappointed and not sure I want to stay with this church. I started attending Radiant as a teenager with my family. As an adult with a family of my own now I came back to the church and have been attending online for 3years, Since I’m blind and can’t drive. My fiancé reached out to the church for prayer he had an upcoming surgery. He only asked for prayer but the church told him to ask for financial help. So he did what they suggested only to be told that the church won’t help because we don’t attend in person and can’t afford to give financial to the church. This broke my heart that the church told him to ask for help and than so easily dismissed us just because we can’t attend in person and can’t afford to give to the church. My only income is SSI. I use to love Radiant but now I think we may need a new church that doesn’t dismiss me just because I’m blind and can’t give financial to a church.

formatted_address: 4811 George Rd, Tampa, FL 33634, United States
name: Calvary Community Church of Tampa

reviews.text:
Calvary Community Church welcomes all searching for the truth that is found in the Gospel (good news) of Jesus Christ.  Salvation is made clear, you may know that you have eternal life through belief in Jesus Christ‘s redeeming sacrifice on the cross, burial, and resurrection.  “For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: not of works, lest any man should boast” (Ephesians‬ ‭2‬:‭8‬-‭9‬).  With each service of the week offering an individual message, scripture is the foundation for all teaching and regularly referenced through deep study of the text.

Calvary is also committed to growing the spiritual maturity of those who choose to walk in the teachings of Jesus Christ (discipleship).  Change does not always come overnight, and following the Lord presents many challenges from within and without the believer, but by knowing and trusting in God’s Word the process of progressive sanctification, even amongst setbacks, can be filled with victory.

Fellowship is another strength at Calvary.  From various potlucks and community events, to chatting before and after services, to praying for one another in difficult times and at Wednesday night prayer services, to men’s and women’s study groups; Calvary has a strong, knowledgeable, and loving body of believers committed to encouraging and helping each other along this journey.  Tack on the AWANA (children) and Tampa Youth Ranch (teens) ministries where the youth are memorizing Bible verses, learning biblical principles and coming to faith in Jesus Christ.

If you’re looking for clear biblical teaching, a supportive body of believers of all ages, opportunity to grow in your faith, knowledge,  and ability to reach others, then Calvary is a perfect place to call home.  Not yet convinced?  Check out the videos and live services on the BibleLine YouTube channel, Spotify or listen to Calvary Community Church on Sermon Audio.

“But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.”
—  ‭‭1 Corinthians‬ ‭15‬:‭57‬ ‭KJV‬‬

My wife and 5 kids and I had a very pleasant experience visiting Calvary community. The kids enjoyed their classes. If I was living in Tampa then I would definitely be attending here. I highly recommend this church especially since they get the gospel right! PSA 27:4 4 One thing have I desired of the Lord, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the Lord, and to enquire in his temple.

I have felt it and seen His blessings in my life since going to this church. Before I was baptized and filled, I very devastatingly lost my job and I was in such panic, being a young single woman trying to support myself. I kid you not, by Tuesday or Wednesday that next week, I received a call from a prestigious company that wanted to MAKE a position just for me! Not only that, they offered me so much more for a salary than I would have asked for. If that's not The Lord working, I don't know what is. The Lord is so good and I am continuing to flourish in this job. I am seeing His Will come to pass, as I received a raise this year and The Lord has secured my position in this job in many ways. Another testimony I have since coming to this church and living for God is my car was flooded in Helene and not like 2 months later, The Lord provided a new year 2025 vehicle for me at a reasonable price and the color I wanted! reviews.text:
I came to this church seeking spiritual guidance, safety, and belonging. I was encouraged to be vulnerable and confess personal struggles—only to later be shamed, excluded, and effectively blacklisted. What followed was a profound breach of trust that left lasting emotional and spiritual harm.

This experience did not feel rooted in grace, compassion, or unconditional love. Instead, vulnerability was met with judgment and rejection. I wanted a church family. I wanted acceptance. What I received was betrayal.

I share this so others proceed with caution. Do not let your guard down here. Do not assume your openness will be met with care. My relationship with God has been deeply impacted by this experience, and the disappointment and trauma are real. I would not wish this on anyone.

Pastor: Please don’t offer for me to reach out and seek reconciliation when you don’t even respond to my emails. You clearly want me to just go away, and I will. But not without informing others about the dangers here.

The Lord led me to Salvation City Church during a very dark season and they welcomed me with open arms. They prayed with me and for me and poured into me like I had belonged there for years. The leaders of SCC are highly anointed and filled with the Holy Spirit. Their passion for sharing the Gospel and teaching the true word of God cannot be understated. I highly encourage anyone who is searching, new to the faith, or a lifelong Christian to attend a service and check it out for yourself.

This church emphasizes the teaching of God's Word and the demonstration of God's power, bringing hope to those in need of salvation, deliverance, and/or healing. Come prepared to experience God's presence through beautiful worship, communion, the giving of tithes and offerings as part of worship, and rich, relevant instruction on the truths of God's Word. Come prepared to meet authentic people with a desire to "do life" together within a missional community marked by love, support, and frequent fellowship. This ministry has radically changed my life. I'm thankful beyond words that God led me here, and I pray daily that others who are searching for a deeper encounter and walk with God will likewise be drawn to SCC.

reviews.text: When I moved to Tampa a few months ago, I really wanted to find a church that was easy to connect with and passionate about serving the community in impactful ways. From the start, this church welcomed me beyond what I expected. It was an instant genuine sense of home. Building relationships here has never felt like work, because everyone is actively and selflessly investing in each others’ lives. Growing with this church has been an incredible blessing.

We were in Tampa during Easter (Did not realize it was so early this year - we are from Ohio) and we were looking for a Christian (Christ) based church.  Holy Cow!  We found the Church at Channelside in the Embassy Suites across from our hotel.  What a welcoming group of Christian brothers and sisters - young, mid-life, and old.  The message was all about Christ, in this case, about Peter and his take on the resurrection before and after.  What was really great was how at the start, a young woman explained to everyone, in simple terms what Easter and the resurrection as about.  The pastor gave a great sermon that really showed, through the eyes of Peter, how we are forgiven.  I cannot say enough about this wonderful group of believers and the Holy Spirit working through them to deliver the message.  Thank you, Church of Channelside, for delivering God's word on this day of our Savior's rising. Your praise team sang the song "Jesus paid it all" and I will finish with these lyrics that they sang:  "Oh praise the one who paid my debt. And praise this life up from the dead".  May God continue to bless this community of believers.

From the Alpha class that is geared towards new believers or non-believers with questions about faith to church membership and the CORE team for devoted Christian members who want to volunteer their time serving the community and the church family. I have found so much love and peach at the Church at Channelside! It is also right in the heart of the channelside area/Downtown Tampa, making it very easily accessible and walkable.

reviews.text: This church currently has Israeli flags displayed outside their church. I find it repugnant that a Christian church would display the flag of a genocidal state. They’ve been there since 10/7 and with that said two things can be true: you can both express solidarity and empathy towards the innocent victims of October 7th, 2023 and and NOT stand with the genocidal state of Israel. I cannot imagine how a church that is supposed to represent acceptance and love towards all would stand with an oppressive country. Imagine being a Palestinian Christian seeking a church to find refuge in and you stumble upon this church with the flag of your racist oppressor displayed outside. True christianity doesn’t equate to aligning with oppressors and genociders. The message is LOUD and off-putting.

Reach City Church is unapologetically unique. It is a place where you go to an experience and praise a living God through his word. It is a congregation built on the pillars of community, love, respect, and redemption.

Pastor Johnny is truly a good and faithful servant of the Lord. I will forever be grateful for his guidance in my walk with the Father. His love and compassion extend not only to members of his church, but to the world. There have been countless days where the Lord has poured a message into him that speaks to the very core of my soul. He yearns for servitude through grace, mercy, and love. A good pastor teaches you the word, but a great pastor prepares you to enter the Kingdom. Pastor Johnny is an exceptional pastor, a passionate leader, and pours his heart out on the pulpit every Sunday. Most importantly, he has always been loud in leading the church with his love for Jesus. Something the world desperately needs right now is the courage to walk by unwavering, unapologetic, and loud faith.

My life forever changed from the moment I walked into Reach City in 2018. As a broken 25 year-old kid, I opened my heart and gave my life to Jesus in that very church. 11 AM Service
The word today was truly amazing and spoke deeply to my spirit. Dr. Jeffery’s message on grace and truth was powerful, uplifting, and full of substance. Even as a non-member visiting the church, I could feel God’s presence through the worship and sermon.
However, towards the end of service, after the sermon and prayer, something occurred that left me with mixed feelings. As some members of the congregation, including myself and a relative, began to leave, Dr. Jeffery addressed the congregation about church protocol — explaining that this was a time of prayer and not a time to exit. While I understand and even agree with the heart of his message — honoring God’s presence and maintaining reverence during prayer — the delivery and handling of the situation felt harsh and somewhat embarrassing.
Members of the church began blocking the middle doors to stop people from leaving, which created confusion and discomfort. I believe there could have been a more graceful approach, such as kindly asking everyone to remain seated or inviting those who had started to leave to return for a moment of prayer.
Considering the sermon’s very theme — the balance of grace and truth — the moment felt somewhat inconsistent with that message. Correction is necessary, but grace in correction reflects the heart of Christ as well.
Overall, I was blessed by the word and the worship experience, but I hope in the future the leadership and ushers will handle moments like this with a gentler spirit — one that still upholds reverence but also extends grace to visitors and members alike.

reviews.text: Point Church North Raleigh is a great place to worship and be a part of a spiritual family. If you’re not yet attending any church or have been “dechurched,” you can try to attend for 5 Sundays and decide for yourself.

They were beyond compassionate and truly genuine. They learned a lot about our sister and her life in a very short period of  time! Their openness did not go unappreciated and unnoticed.
I  wish I lived closer to their church for I would surely be there every Sunday!

formatted_address: 2721 E Millbrook Rd, Raleigh, NC 27604, United States
name: Crossroads Fellowship - Millbrook Campus

reviews.text:
Been here consistently since 2021 to 2024 and visit inconsistency since 2018/2019. Unfortunately I had to leave for reasons not listed here...

♡The positives♡
- There really is a lot to do & ways to connect outside of just listening to the sermon. I personally loved the apologetics class! 💖💜✨
- Mostly warm community! I’ve made a lot of friends and mentors there that I love dearly.
- Lots of resources (from partners). Front desk people can help find you help with one of their partnered ministries if you have a specific need.
- Solid primary beliefs from what I can tell and they were open to answer questions I had.
- They collectively give financially a lot to local ministries that help the local community. They are pretty transparent about their finances too.
- It’s very contemporary, causal dress, and like a mix between being Baptist and Pentecostal.

♡The Negatives♡
- They follow and have speakers that come from megachurches, are apart of the NAR, and big Eva. Ex: Elevation and Hillsong Church.
- When they make a mistake publicly never make a statement about it publicly… idk it's a bit odd. Ex: teaching the ennagram.
- Some of the secondary theological labels they assign themselves with they don’t always follow which is sus. Ex: saying they’re complementarian when they let women preach sermons and act as a pastor without the label of pastor.
- They have a favoritism problem. “Wolves” tend to be given influence & more 2nd chances for awful things without much real consequences… while others are given more swifter consequences for similar or even less worse actions.
- Very topical sermons and some patsors will blantly copy other pastor’s work like Pastor Daivd Guzik.
- CRF as a whole comes off very “seeker friendly” and isn't super active in helping the community in tangible ways despite having the space and money to do so. Ex: they don't like homeless cause some tend to steal, do drugs, and litter so they build stuff on the their property (like frisbee golf course) to keep people from settling there... 😐
- I don't really like how the senior pastor would sometimes talks about people (without naming) that he disagrees with randomly before the beginning of the sermon. One target, the old Youth Pastor that deconstructed made some good observations but they were completely ignored because he's deconstructed… 🙃

♡Other things to note♡
- It usually is very very cold on Sundays.
- The music is so loud they have earplugs in the back of the worship room.
- They don't seem to have to best communication with each division which makes some sense because it is a big church. It just be like that.
- Feedback can be slow. From when I was there leadership just has a lot on their plate, so I’d give them some grace.🙏🏿

I pray that whatever is going on in darkness would come to light, so CRF can grow in a spiritually healthy way. Leaving was very bittersweet and I kind of felt forgotten, but I also did benefit from being there for a season. After going here I’m a lot more cautious about the churches I attend.

I've been working here this week cleaning up due to a fire so water and smoke damage,  but this is one huge church that is televised every Sunday morning!  They have a thrift store in the church as well. Also children will love it! I'll post a few pictures  so check it out!!! There's a huge room for the service also 2 more overflow rooms with big TV screens.  A chapel,  a kitchen , snack and drink machines,  a library,  meeting rooms a welcome center and many others!
The kids ministry is super fun! We love VBS, Spark nights on Wednesdays, and the friendships.

I attended this church for 5 months until one day the lead pastor got political mid sermon. I do not like a political church so I stopped attending. Other than that, I really enjoyed the worship and the EQUIP discipleship training. Seems like they have a good kids ministry too but I do not have children.

We believe everyone matters to God.... This is a place to find help, healing and hope...  all words posted just yesterday on their Facebook page.  What a joke... My daughter is going through a crisis and is homeless right now. She got a tent and a few things and found what she thought was a safe place to stay a few days in some woods near this church. I help her all I can, but I cant do everything. I saw where she was staying and felt it was as safe as she could get. Unfortunately,  this welcoming church didn't agree and instead of having a conversation with her and seeing if they could help in any way, they call the police. They aren't nearly as concerned about the community as they are about the money some in the community provide.  My daughter said she watched so many people donate to their thrift store for them to throw much of it in the garbage instead of passing it forward. I am highly disappointed in the way they handled this situation and I'm sure God is also. All children matter to God, except at this church. Only those with abundant bank accounts matter.

reviews.text: Pastor Grant and his wife, Michelle, truly practice servant leadership. They follow Jesus daily and have changed my life as a believer. If you are struggling, remember it’s not a breakdown, it’s a break through! Come here to experience Jesus’ love:)

While I have only been coming to Mid-Way for 6 months, I can easily say this church is AWESOME! From the pastoral leadership to the staff to the members of this church... people are warm and welcoming while speaking and teaching the TRUTH!

No one has pressured me to become a member or to give money or to get involved. However, the more I come here, the more I feel compelled to get more and more involved here. This place has a liveliness I haven't seen in a church in a long time.

We've been going to Mid-Way for over a year now and really love it!  The kids programs are amazing!  And I hear the same of the youth and young adult programs, as well.  My husband and I have also enjoyed the services and classes offered for adults.  Though the church a bit on the large side, it has managed to maintain the feel of a smaller family church -- very friendly and inviting!  Most importantly, the staff is focused on God's will for this church and He is present in all they do!

My parents and I have been attending Midway since the late 90's and we would never consider going to another church. We have visited plenty of churches in the Garner/Raleigh area, but nothing compares to Midway. We absolutely the music and the choir because they play both old southern gospel songs, but contemporary songs as well; the blend is awesome. I've been in Sunday school classes from Kindergarten to College & Career and they have always been taught my amazing teachers and I've made so many wonderful life-long friendships with my peers. The church is always offering so many developmental classes, fun activities, and other times to worship and fellowship which is awesome! However, the main reason we love Midway so much is because of Preacher Upchurch. It is very rare that a founding pastor still remains at their church and refuses to quit until he is called up to heaven! Preacher has been at Midway for almost 50 years and I'm so grateful for all the wisdom and advice he's given me each Sunday for 20 years now. He's not afraid to tell it like it is and refuses to preach anything other than God's Word because he stands strong with his beliefs. I'm also very glad that our church is debt-free and that we are able to give back in so many ways: to children, single moms, missionaries, you name it. Our Chest of Joash during November is such a great way to demonstrate what God says about sowing and reaping and the importance of sacrificial giving. It is also a great way for new or non believers to give a tithe if they want. I'm so happy to be member of this church and I would recommend you come join us one Sunday morning at 9:30!
